A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.

Probability.title: A Unifying Framework for Global Optimization: From Theory to Formalization
Probability.summary: We introduce an abstract measure___theoretic framework that serves as a tool to rigorously study stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms as a unified class. The framework is formulated in terms of probability kernels, which, via the Ionescu--Tulcea theorem, induce probability measures on the space of sequences of algorithm iterations, endowed with two intuitive properties. This framework answers the need for a general, implementation___independent formalism in the analysis of such algorithms, providing a starting point for formalizing global optimization results in proof-assistants. To illustrate the relevance of our tool, we show that common algorithms fit naturally in the framework, and we also use it to give a rigorous proof of a general consistency theorem for stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms (Proposition 3 of (Malherbe, et al., 2017). This proof and the entire framework are formalized in the Lean proof assistant. This formalization both ensures the correctness of the definitions and proofs, and provides a basis for future machine-assisted formalizations in the field.

Probability.title: An infinite-dimensional representation of Ray-Knight theorems for the Bass-Burdzy flow
Probability.summary: [Bass and Burdzy 1999] introduced a stochastic flow of homeomorphisms of the real line $\mathcal R_t:x\mapsto \mathcal R_t(x)$, driven by a Brownian motion. Ray-Knight theorems for the process $\mathcal R_t^{-1}(0)$ were later obtained by [Hu and Warren 2000]. We extend their results by proving an integral representation driven by a common white noise for the local times of $\mathcal R_t^{-1}(0)$, in analogy with the case of the standard Ray-Knight theorems [Aïdékon, Hu and Shi 2024]. We generalize this representation to the setting of a Bass-Burdzy flow driven by a drifted Brownian motion perturbed at its maximum, and use this framework to answer a question of [Aïdékon, Hu and Shi 2026] concerning the description of the conditional law of a perturbed reflecting Brownian motion given its occupation measure in terms of Bass-Burdzy flows.

Probability.title: High order integration of stochastic dynamics on Riemannian manifolds with frozen flow methods
Probability.summary: We present a new class of numerical methods for solving stochastic differential equations with additive noise on general Riemannian manifolds with high weak order of accuracy. In opposition to the popular approach with projection methods, the proposed methods are intrinsic: they only rely on geometric operations and avoid coordinates and embeddings. We provide a robust and general convergence analysis and an algebraic formalism of exotic planar Butcher series for the computation of order conditions at any high order. To illustrate the methodology, an explicit method of second weak order is introduced, and several numerical experiments confirm the theoretical findings and extend the approach for the sampling of the invariant measure of Riemannian Langevin dynamics.

Probability.title: $\mathcal{P}(Φ)_2$ Theory from many-body quantum Gibbs states
Probability.summary: We derive the $\mathcal{P}(Φ)_2$ measure on the two-dimensional unit torus as the rigorous limit of many-body quantum Gibbs states. In particular, the quantum model corresponding to the $Φ^{2p}_2$ measure is formulated in the grand-canonical ensemble with a general symmetric $p$-body interaction potential which is not required to have a factorized form. Unlike in the $Φ^4_2$ case investigated by Fröhlich--Knowles--Schlein--Sohinger in \cite{FKSS25}, in the treatment of higher-order interactions, Wick renormalization generates a full hierarchy of lower-order interactions which we organize systematically using a graphical formalism. One key ingredient of our analysis is a logarithmic stability estimate for both the nonlocal Hartree functional and the many-body Hamiltonian that is uniform in the interaction range, allowing us to use the positivity of the leading $p$-body interaction to control all lower-order terms generated by the Wick counterterms.

Probability.title: Stationary Ergodic Mean-field Games of Constrained Singular Controls
Probability.summary: We study a stationary ergodic mean-field game of scalar type where the representative player controls a diffusion through two-sided singular controls exerted only at the jump times of an independent Poisson process. For each mean-field parameter, we solve the novel constrained ergodic singular control problem, proving that the optimal policy is of threshold type: the diffusion is reset at Poisson arrival times to the nearest boundary point of an interval. Our explicit probabilistic derivation of the stationary distributions induced by Poissonian threshold singular controls is a key contribution of independent interest. This distribution is used to construct the mean-field fixed-point map. We prove existence and uniqueness of the stationary mean-field equilibrium by combining the stationary density with the monotonicity and continuity of the optimal thresholds in the mean-field parameter. The model provides a tractable framework for a case study of partially reversible investment with singular adjustments under exogenous intervention constraints.

Probability.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
Probability.summary: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.

Probability.title: On the Kantorovich contraction of Markov semigroups
Probability.summary: We develop an operator-theoretic framework for the contraction properties of Markov semigroups with respect to a general class of Kantorovich semi-distances, which includes Wasserstein distances and weighted total variation norms. The framework is based on Kantorovich contraction coefficients, which extend Dobrushin's ergodic coefficient from the total variation distance to general transport costs. Our main result shows that a geometric drift condition, combined with a local contraction condition on the sub-level sets of the Lyapunov function, implies that the Markov operator is a strict contraction with respect to an explicit modification of the underlying Kantorovich cost. This yields, in a unified way, the existence and uniqueness of invariant measures and exponential decay estimates in Wasserstein distances, for both discrete time and continuous time Markov semigroups, as well as for time-varying semigroups. We illustrate the scope of the framework with (i) Markov transitions on models with boundary states, including bounded domains with entrance boundaries, (ii) operator products of a Markov kernel and its adjoint, including two-block Gibbs samplers, (iii) iterated random functions, including Euler-type schemes, (iv) diffusion models, including overdamped Langevin diffusions with potentials that are convex at infinity, jump-diffusions on compact manifolds, and Jacobi and Riccati matrix diffusions, and (v) time-varying and nonlinear semigroups, including Feynman-Kac distribution flows and Sinkhorn bridges. In several of these settings we obtain new contraction estimates, while in others we recover known results through short and elementary arguments.

Probability.title: On the weak invariance principle for strictly stationary sequences in some Besov spaces
Probability.summary: In this paper, we investigate the weak invariance principle in some Besov spaces for strictly stationary sequences. In particular, we provide sufficient conditions on the moments and the dependence of a strictly stationary sequence to guaranty the weak invariance principle in these Besov spaces. Several dependence structures are considered, including projective conditions, $α$-dependent, $ρ$-mixing, and $τ$ -dependent conditions. The main tools in the proofs are martingale approximation and deviation inequalities for weakly dependent sequences. Our results cover a large range of strictly stationary sequences that were not treated previously in the literature. Moreover, the presented conditions are sharp.

Probability.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
Probability.summary: Semi-Markov networks provide a natural framework for describing stochastic transitions between coarse-grained states with non-exponential dwell times, with applications ranging from biophysics and neuroscience to epidemiology and finance. Here, it is shown that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph. These representations yield asymptotic results, including a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem to semi-Markov networks, in which the rate constants replaced by pseudo-rates given by the inverse mean sojourn time weighted by the exit probability through this channel, as well as the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short proof of the constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to show that weak ergodicity breaking occurs generically for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks.

Probability.title: BKT transition for $\mathsf{Sine}_β$
Probability.summary: We prove the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase transition in the large-distance behaviour of the two-point correlation function of the $\mathsf{Sine}_β$ point process for all $β>0$, confirming the first term of an asymptotic expansion predicted by Forrester.

Probability.title: Exact bounds on the distribution function of isotropic log-concave distributions
Probability.summary: For each real $b$, exact upper and lower bounds on the probability $\mathsf P(X\ge b)$ over all random variables $X$ with log-concave p.d.f.'s such that $\mathsf E X=0$ and $\mathsf E X^2=1$ are obtained, as well as the best constant factor $C$ in the inequality $\mathsf P(X\ge b)\le C e^{-b}$ for all real $b\ge0$. Exact upper and lower bounds on the corresponding exponential moments (Proposition 9.4) and explicit exponentially decreasing upper bounds on the mentioned p.d.f.'s (Propositions 9.2 and 9.3) are given as well. Some general results concerning log-concave p.d.f.'s are also obtained.
Probability.comment: Comments to Version 2: Added a direct link to Supplement B, described on p. 49; mathematical content unchanged. Comments to Version 3: Added exact upper and lower bounds on the exponential moments (Proposition 9.4); mentioned p. 49 has become p. 50

Probability.title: Utility-Based Recovery Risk Measures: Redundancy and Approximation for Portfolio Optimization
Probability.summary: Recovery risk measures incorporate explicit liability-recovery requirements into asset-liability risk assessment. We study their specialization to optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs), allowing the underlying utility specification to vary across recovery levels and encompassing Recovery Average Value at Risk (RecAV@R) as a special case. For finite recovery specifications, we use the dual penalty representation to characterize redundant recovery regimes and derive position-independent screening conditions. For a subfamily of the Cressie-Read power-divergence family, including entropic and truncated-quadratic specifications, we obtain an exact characterization on atomless probability spaces: universal redundancy is equivalent to a two-dimensional convex-hull condition involving recovery levels and divergence-scale parameters. On such spaces, universal redundancy for RecAV@R reduces to pairwise dominance, whereas for power-divergence OCEs it can arise from the joint effect of several recovery regimes. For nonlinear OCE utilities, we develop a certified piecewise-linear approximation framework for portfolio optimization. In finite-scenario models, the approximating problems are finite-dimensional linear programs, while utility approximation errors transfer directly to the Recovery OCE, yielding explicit error bounds and convergence rates. Uniform approximation over the portfolio domain further implies convergence of optimal values and stability of optimal solutions. A numerical asset-liability study illustrates the effects of recovery-dependent risk preferences and the accuracy and convergence of the approximation.

Probability.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
Probability.summary: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.

Probability.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part~1: expectation under the uniform null
Probability.summary: We study the expectation of the discrete total variation statistic $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$ of counts $X_1,\dots,X_n$ over $n$ ordered bins with sample size $N$, under the uniform multinomial null. In the notation used throughout the series, a reference distribution $\mathbf r$ defines $d_{\mathbf r}(x)=\|x-N\mathbf r\|_V$; here $\mathbf r=\mathbf u$ is uniform and we write simply $d$. We obtain an exact single-sum formula, a closed form in central trinomial coefficients valid for every $n\ge2$, with one-term evaluations at $n=2,4$ and a complete D-finite characterization for $n=3$. The per-edge expectation $W_N=E|X_2-X_1|$ satisfies an exact three-term recurrence, from which we derive its complete $1/N$ expansion with the $n$-independent constant $E(d^\circ/\sqrt{Nn})\to 2/\sqrtπ$ for the cyclic statistic $d^\circ=d^\circ_{\mathbf u}$, independent of the number of bins; the complementary sparse regime (fixed $N$, $n\to\infty$) is treated in a separate paper. Conditioning on a two-bin total reduces each edge to a symmetric random walk; as the subsequent parts of the series will show, this method carries the analysis to non-uniform reference laws.

Probability.title: Finite-Sample Bounds for Fréchet Means of Dependent Data in Metric Spaces with Curvature Bounded Above
Probability.summary: We prove finite-sample risk bounds for empirical quadratic and power Fréchet means in geodesic metric spaces with curvature bounded above for observations with arbitrary joint law. We compare the sample with exchangeable copies in which one observation is redrawn independently of the original sample and the others move to preserve the joint law. These displacements control the error, with no entropy or dimension assumptions. For quadratic Fréchet means, this yields a general ``coupling bound'' in any separable complete $CAT(κ)$ space, where for $κ>0$ the observations must lie in a closed convex set of circumradius below $π/(2\sqrtκ)$. This bound is exact on the real line for nonnegatively correlated Gaussian observations and for comonotone functions of a common factor. We apply it in two settings. Under local dependence, the resulting risk bound grows linearly with the average size of the dependency neighborhoods. Under transport sensitivity and for bounded metric variances, summable sensitivities of the conditional laws to a change in one observation preserve the parametric mean squared error rate, while nonsummable polynomial decay gives explicit slower rates. We verify transport sensitivity for stationary reversible Markov chains with Wasserstein-contractive kernels and for bi-Lipschitz images of Gaussian sequences. In the more challenging setting of heavy-tailed, dependent data with possibly infinite variance, we consider power Fréchet means of order $α\in(1,2)$. Under nonpositive curvature, we bound their $L^α$ risk assuming only finite $α$-th moments.

Probability.title: Spectrum of Directed Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
Probability.summary: We study the spectrum of the adjacency matrix $A_n$ of directed inhomogeneous random graphs on $n$ vertices. We assume that $A_n$ has independent entries and diverging average degree scale $s_n$. This framework includes, as special cases, the directed Chung--Lu random graph and directed stochastic block models. Assuming boundedness of the variance profile and that $s_n$ diverges faster than $\log(n)^2$, we show that the rank-one Chung--Lu model satisfies a non-homogeneous version of the circular law, which in some situations allows for an explicit expression. Moreover, under mild conditions, we identify the asymptotic singular value distribution using tools from free probability. Finally, for finite-rank directed models, we establish that eigenvalues outside the bulk have joint Gaussian fluctuations at the scale $\sqrt{s_n/n}$, with an explicit covariance matrix. These results extend the theory of spectral outliers and their fluctuations to directed inhomogeneous random graphs.

Probability.title: Higher-Order Gaussian Approximations on Path Space for the Simple Symmetric Exclusion Process
Probability.summary:
Quantitative Gaussian approximation estimates on path space are established for the nonequilibrium density fluctuations of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) on a $d$-dimensional discrete torus of mesh size $1/n$, started from a product measure with a smooth density profile. A novel $n$-dependent modified Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is constructed that incorporates higher-order lattice information while remaining linear and Gaussian. It is shown that, for sufficiently high modification orders, this modification yields quantitative Gaussian approximation error bounds of order $n^{-\min\{d/2,2\}}$ for a class of smooth functionals of the entire fluctuation trajectory. In addition, it is shown that retaining an explicit microscopic correlation correction leaves a remainder of order $n^{-d/2}$, thereby distinguishing contributions to the bound due to correlations from those due to spatial approximation. For nonconstant initial profiles in dimensions $d\ge3$, a separate argument yields matching upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-2}$ for the direct weak error of suitable quadratic test functionals, provided that the modification orders are sufficiently high.
  The proof is based on a novel path-dependent Trotter formula. Its derivation builds on the introduction of a concept of horizontal absolute continuity for non-anticipative functionals and a corresponding martingale formula for Markov jump processes. This formula is subsequently combined with an integral backward Kolmogorov equation for Gaussian continuation functionals. A second ingredient of the proof is a refinement of the exchangeable-pair argument introduced by the authors in a previous work, thereby improving the central-limit rate $n^{-\min\{d/2,1\}}$ to $n^{-d/2}$ for the initial empirical fluctuations.

Probability.title: Time-changed reflected diffusions: subdiffusion, superdiffusion and explosion
Probability.summary: Motivated by semi-Markov models of anomalous diffusion, we study obliquely reflected diffusions in generalized parabolic domains under independent inverse-subordinator time changes. We focus on infinite-mean subordinators, whose inverse clocks can slow the superdiffusive growth induced by reflection. For domains with cross-sectional radius asymptotic to $a_\infty x^β$, where $-1<β<1$, we strengthen the almost-sure growth laws of [MMW23] to obtain precise second-moment asymptotics when the subordinator's Laplace exponent is regularly varying at zero, and matching bounds more generally. Inverse $α$-stable clocks yield mean-square growth of order $t^{2α/(1+β)}$, giving subdiffusive, diffusive, or superdiffusive regimes. For $β<-1$, explosion persists almost surely, with finite mean explosion time if and only if the subordinator has finite mean. Supporting results establish strong existence, pathwise uniqueness, and a time-change representation, also allowing dependent clocks.

Probability.title: Dense alternating sign matrices and imprecise copulas
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study discrete quasi-copulas and discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range, which naturally correspond to alternating sign matrices. We identify dense alternating sign matrices as a particularly well-behaved subclass. We prove that the associated discrete imprecise copulas are always coherent and hence avoid sure loss. We further show that a particular extension of the corresponding discrete quasi-copulas to the full domain preserves this structure and yields self-dual imprecise copulas. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first general result in the literature showing how properties established for discrete imprecise copulas can be preserved when extending them to their full-domain counterpart. We conclude the paper by showing that, for general alternating sign matrices, the associated discrete imprecise copulas need not avoid sure loss, further emphasizing the special role of the subclass of dense alternating sign matrices. We establish, however, that the class of discrete quasi-copulas of minimal range is invariant under all defect transformations

Probability.title: Robust LassoNet: Enhancing Feature Selection in Neural Networks via Robust Loss Functions
Probability.summary: Feature selection in neural networks remains a challenging problem, particularly in the presence of noisy or contaminated data. LassoNet is a recent approach that addresses this issue by combining neural networks with hierarchical sparsity constraints, enabling simultaneous prediction and variable selection. However, its standard formulation relies on the mean squared error (MSE) loss, which is known to be highly sensitive to outliers. In this paper, we present Robust LassoNet, an extension of LassoNet that incorporates robust loss functions, such as Huber, Cauchy, Tukey's bisquare, and Nonnegative Garrote, to mitigate the effect of extreme observations. The proposed approach preserves the original optimization framework while improving stability under data contamination. Through experiments on synthetic and real datasets, we show that robust LassoNet significantly improves both predictive performance and feature selection accuracy in the presence of outliers or heavy tailed noise, while maintaining comparable performance in clean settings. These results highlight the importance of robustness in neural network based feature selection and suggest practical guidelines for choosing appropriate loss functions.

Probability.title: Existence of ergodic invariant measures for 3D Navier-Stokes eqs with superlinear noise
Probability.summary: We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain $D\subset \mathbb R^3$. It has been proved in arXiv:2609.08284 that these equations have a unique solution - globally defined in time - when a superlinear noise is introduced and the initial velocity belongs to the space $V$ of divergence-free $H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^3)$-vector fields. Here we show that the same result holds when there is also an additive noise and a deterministic forcing term. Moreover, when the deterministic forcing term is time-independent we prove the existence of at least one invariant measure for this stochastic equation. This is obtained by the Krylov-Bogoliubov method, based on tightness and Feller property in $V$. Finally, we show that the set of invariant measures contains one ergodic invariant measure.

Probability.title: Fine asymptotics of the magnetization of the annealed dilute Curie-Weiss model
Probability.summary: We consider the dilute Curie-Weiss model of size $N$, which is a generalization of the classical Curie-Weiss model in which the dependency structure between the spins is encoded not by the complete graph but by the (directed) Erdős-Rényi graph on $N$ vertices in which every edge appears independently with probability $p(N)$. In the high-temperature regime with an external magnetic field ($0<β<1,h\in\mathbb{R}$) we prove for $p^{3}N^{2}\to\infty$ sharp cumulant bounds for the magnetization under the annealed Gibbs measure, which imply a central limit theorem with rate, moderate and large deviation principles, a concentration inequality, a normal approximation with Cramér correction and mod-Gaussian convergence.

Probability.title: Weighted derivative estimates for Kolmogorov equations
Probability.summary: For diffusions whose coefficients are smooth, with at most linear growth and bounded derivatives of higher order, we establish explicit pointwise bounds on the spatial derivatives of the classical solution to the Cauchy problem with polynomially growing initial data. We also obtain explicit growth estimates for the derivatives of the SDE with respect to the initial data. The proofs combine Lyapunov functions and Markov semigroups on weighted spaces with Kunita's theory of the differentiable dependence of SDE solutions on the initial data.

Probability.title: Why does entropy drive evolution equations?
Probability.summary: `Entropy' appears as driving force in many different evolution equations, both deterministic and stochastic, and in these equations this `entropy' also takes different forms. We show how all these examples can be understood as different instances of a common principle: Entropy drives evolutions because it characterizes the invariant measure of an underlying stochastic process. This interpretation explains the appearance of entropy, the different forms that entropy takes in these equations, and how entropy `drives' these evolution equations. We illustrate this common structure with examples from stochastic processes, gradient flows, and GENERIC systems.

Probability.title: Dynamical classical-field limit of Bosonic Gibbs states: Renormalized Hartree NLS correlations in 2D and 3D
Probability.summary: In this paper we derive the time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation on the torus $\mathbb T^d$, $d=2,3$, from the corresponding bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics. In contrast with the 1D problem studied earlier by Fröhlich, Knowles, Schlein and Sohinger, in higher dimensions the scaled quantum particle number is not uniformly bounded and the relevant classical fields require Wick renormalization. Our proof combines convergence of the quantum generators in weighted Hilbert spaces with uniqueness for positive solutions of the limiting Liouville equation that are dominated by the Gibbs measure.

Probability.title: Penalizations of Two-Dimensional Simple Random Walk by Direction-Dependent Excursion Counts and Edge-Crossing Counts
Probability.summary: We study penalizations of the two-dimensional simple random walk by functions of direction-dependent excursion counts and edge-crossing counts. The former record completed excursions with prescribed pairs of departure and return directions at the origin, whereas the latter record crossings of a prescribed set of unoriented edges incident to the origin. We determine the distributions of their almost surely finite terminal values and derive explicit path decomposition formulas involving the random walk conditioned to avoid the origin. Moreover, both families of penalized measures can be represented by weighting and normalizing the same universal $σ$-finite measure associated with local-time penalization at the origin. Thus, direction-dependent excursion counts, edge-crossing counts, and local time at the origin give rise to penalizations belonging to a common universality class.

Probability.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous--Broder Theorem
Probability.summary: Random spanning forests provide probability models for partitions and Monte Carlo methods on graphs. In these applications, the distribution produced by a sampler determines which forest functionals can be estimated. The Aldous--Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but a direct calculation requires summing over all orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered. We evaluate this sum through an identity for rooted forests and real matrices with zero row sums. Under a nonsingularity condition on the principal submatrices encountered during growth, the sum of products of harmonic extension entries equals a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots. With one root, the sum is one. The identity gives a direct proof of the extended Aldous--Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state, without assuming reversibility or bidirectional transition support. It also gives the conditional distribution of the discovery order and the law of the forest obtained by stopping after all nonroot vertices have been visited. A completion weight describes the difference between this stopped-walk law and the weight-proportional forest law, including the support restriction needed for importance correction. Numerical examples illustrate the sampling implications. The identity, the Aldous--Broder theorem, and the stopped-forest law are formalized in Lean4.

Probability.title: Stochastic Policy Gradient Methods in the Uncertain Volatility Model
Probability.summary: The multidimensional Uncertain Volatility Model leads to robust option pricing problems under joint volatility and correlation uncertainty. Their numerical resolution quickly becomes challenging because the associated stochastic control problem is high-dimensional. We propose a backward actor-critic stochastic policy-gradient scheme tailored to this setting. The method combines a discrete dynamic programming principle with Proximal Policy Optimization and one-hidden-layer neural-network approximations of both the value function and the control policy. A key ingredient is the policy parameterization: continuous controls are represented through a squashed Gaussian policy built on a $C$-vine representation of correlation matrices, which enforces positive definiteness by construction. Beyond the robust price itself, the spatial gradient of the trained critic provides an approximation of the associated superhedging strategy. We assess the quality of this learned gradient through a dual formulation, which also yields a numerical dual estimate of the price. Numerical experiments on a range of multidimensional derivatives show that the method yields accurate prices, remains computationally efficient, and compares favorably with existing Monte Carlo and machine-learning-based benchmarks for robust pricing in the Uncertain Volatility Model.

Probability.title: On the First Hitting Time Problems for Diffusion Processes: Local Time-Space Approach
Probability.summary: Using the local time-space calculus of Peskir (2005) and the method developed in Mijatovic (2010), we derive a new integral representation for the backward probability associated with the first-passage time (FPT) of a diffusion process through a time-dependent barrier. We present a complete three-step numerical algorithm: first, the problem is reduced to a Volterra-type integral equation; second, its kernel is approximated by a Markov chain; finally, the resulting equation is solved using a quadrature rule. The method is implemented for several representative examples, and its convergence properties are established. An extension to double barrier problems is carried out

Probability.title: Markovian Random Words, a Gaussian Random Matrix Model and Beyond
Probability.summary: After centering and scaling, the length of the longest weakly increasing subsequence of a finite-state Markov random word converges to a Brownian last-passage functional with dependent components. We investigate when this functional, and more generally the limiting RSK Young-diagram shape, admits a Gaussian random-matrix representation. We introduce Hermitian Gaussian matrices with correlated diagonal entries and show that isotropy of the Brownian covariance on the trace-zero hyperplane yields such a representation. Within this natural class of Hermitian models with independent Gaussian off-diagonal entries, we prove a rigidity theorem showing that isotropy, together with equality of the off-diagonal variances, characterizes the conditional largest-eigenvalue representation. Explicit three-letter non-cyclic Markov chains demonstrate that this representation is not universal: the limiting Brownian functional may fail to have the law of the largest eigenvalue of any centered jointly Gaussian $3\times 3$ Hermitian matrix. Finally, we extend the random-matrix identification to chains with non-uniform stationary distributions and to countable state spaces.

Probability.title: Quantum-assisted rendezvous on hypercubes: a quantum Bernoulli noise approach
Probability.summary: We study quantum-assisted balanced rendezvous on the $d$-dimensional hypercube in a one-step two-agent quantum-walk framework, where the two agents move the same Hamming distance and meet at a common midpoint. The key structure is a projective $t$-sphere resolution, which governs exact finite-dimensional quantum attainment. Its scalar analogue recovers the corresponding classical characterization. We characterize finite-dimensional quantum attainment of the no-signalling benchmark, construct quantum strategies from projective sphere resolutions, and establish a rigidity theorem for optimal finite-dimensional strategies. A marked difference appears between nearest-neighbor and higher-cardinality updates: quantum advantage can occur in the former, whereas in the latter the geometry of the relevant Hamming spheres rules out exact finite-dimensional attainment of the no-signalling value. Together, these results connect quantum-walk dynamics, Hamming-sphere geometry, and quantum rendezvous within the quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN) framework.

Probability.title: On the composition of permutons
Probability.summary:
Permutons can be thought of as "continuum limits" of permutations of diverging size, which encode information about the number of occurrences of any given finite subpattern. We construct a natural composition operation on permutons, analogous to composition of permutations, and explore its properties via a correspondence between permutons, Markov kernels, and Markov operators.
  We show that no extension of permutation composition to permutons can be (jointly) continuous with respect to the usual "weak" topology on permutons, but we construct a "strong" topology with respect to which composition is jointly continuous. Moreover, we characterize strong convergence of sequences of permutations of diverging size: a sequence of permutations converges strongly if and only if it converges weakly and its limit is the transpose of the graph of a measure-preserving function. The key insight behind these results is to apply functional analysis to certain operators associated to permutons; with this shift in perspective, our results have elegant and relatively "soft" proofs.
  As an application, we describe the permuton limit of a product of finitely many independent uniformly sampled separable permutations and give a formula for the expectation of this limit. We also show that in this case, as the number of compositions goes to infinity, the aforementioned expectation tends to the uniform permuton.

Probability.title: Nonlocal Characterizations of Stochastic Completeness on Complete Riemannian Manifolds
Probability.summary:
In this paper, we first prove that the following generalized conservation principle holds on complete Riemannian manifolds: for every \(0<s<1\) and \(t>0\), \[ T_t^{(s)}\mathbf 1+\int_0^t T_τ^{(s)}\mathcal R_s\,dτ=1 \qquad\text{on }M, \] where \(\mathcal R_s\) is the intrinsic killing term measuring the loss of mass of the subordinate semigroup, and the condition \(\mathcal R_s\equiv0\) is equivalent to the stochastic completeness of \(M\).
  We then provide several new nonlocal characterizations of stochastic completeness. In particular, we show that stochastic completeness is equivalent to genuinely nonlocal conditions, including the zero-mean identity \[ \int_M (-Δ)^s\varphi\,dV_g=0 \qquad\forall\,\varphi\in C_c^\infty(M), \] as well as the uniqueness of bounded distributional solutions to the associated fractional elliptic and parabolic equations. We also revisit the equivalent \(L^1\)-core characterization for the generator of the heat semigroup, which plays an important role in our approach.
  In addition, we prove \(L^p\)-contractivity and smoothing properties of the subordinate semigroup, establish both short-time and long-time asymptotic results for the fractional heat kernel, derive the short-time asymptotics of jump probabilities for the associated Markov process, and study the variational characterization and minimality properties of the fractional resolvent. Together, these results provide a unified analytic and probabilistic framework for the fractional Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds.

Probability.title: An efficient stochastic generalized method of moments estimator for nonlinear moment models
Probability.summary: We study the asymptotic properties of the nonlinear stochastic GMM algorithm proposed by Chen, Lee, Liao, Seo, Shin and Song for recursively estimating parameters defined by possibly nonlinear and overidentified moment restrictions $\E[g(X,β^*)]=0$. Each observation updates estimates of the moment Jacobian, inverse covariance matrix and Gauss--Newton preconditioner at a cost independent of sample size. For linear and nonlinear instrumental-variable moments, we derive an exact rank-two Sherman--Morrison--Woodbury update. The algorithm combines preconditioned stochastic approximation with iterate averaging. Under a preconditioned monotonicity condition, satisfied globally in linear models and locally around a consistent pilot estimate in general, we establish almost sure convergence and rates, as well as a functional central limit theorem with the efficient GMM variance. These results require four moments of the moment function and its Jacobian when the step exponent exceeds $2/3$. The inverse Gauss--Newton matrix consistently estimates this variance, and a projected linearised statistic enables online testing of overidentifying restrictions. We extend the results to $L$-dependent data with long-run variance weights under stronger moment assumptions. Simulations show that the averaged estimator approaches offline two-step GMM in accuracy and coverage at $10^6$ observations, while requiring a fraction of its computing time and fixed memory at up to $10^7$ observations. The online test achieves correct size and comparable power. In an application estimating the effect of a third child on weeks worked using $254{,}654$ women from the 1980 US Census, single-pass estimates agree with offline GMM within a fraction of a standard error on average across data orderings, and both methods yield the same overidentification-test conclusion in most orderings.

Differential Geometry.title: The Bernstein problem in higher dimensional Heisenberg groups
Differential Geometry.summary: In every sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$, with $n\geq 2$, we prove the existence of a global perimeter minimizer whose boundary is a smooth, non-characteristic, entire intrinsic graph but it is not a vertical hyperplane.

Differential Geometry.title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
Differential Geometry.summary: We formalize the Hamilton--Perelman Ricci-flow proof of Thurston's geometrization conjecture. The public Lean declaration is reproduced in this paper. Its geometric interpretation follows, and verification is recorded in 4.

Differential Geometry.title: Doubly warped product Einstein metrics on spheres
Differential Geometry.summary: We present a simple computer-assisted procedure to construct $SO(d_1+1)\times SO(d_2+1)$-invariant cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics, and use it to recover known Einstein metrics on $S^{10}$ and $S^{12}$, as well as find new ones on $S^{11}$, $S^{12}$, $S^{13}$ and $S^7\times S^3$.
Differential Geometry.comment: Minor corrections and improvements, 12 pages, to appear in Comm Anal Geom

Differential Geometry.title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a smooth embedded annulus in $R^3$ with negative Gauss curvature in its interior whose boundary consists of two strictly convex curves in planes tangent to the annulus, and which contains two closed asymptotic curves. This gives a counterexample to a 1962 conjecture of Nirenberg. The construction is based on Lelieuvre's formula, which yields a closed curve that is then realized as an asymptotic curve on a ruled annulus. The second asymptotic curve is obtained from the periodic solution of a Riccati equation.

Differential Geometry.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

Differential Geometry.title: Existence and uniqueness of bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves a nonlinear elliptic ODE of the form $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation, on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and nonlinearities $f$. Under mild assumptions, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

Differential Geometry.title: Weighted Lojasiewicz inequalities and regularity of harmonic map flow
Differential Geometry.summary: At a finite-time singularity of harmonic map flow in the critical dimension, we show that a Lojasiewicz inequality between the quantities appearing in Struwe's monotonicity formula implies continuity of the body map and the no-neck property for bubble-tree decompositions. We prove such an inequality when the target is $S^2,$ yielding both properties in this case.
Differential Geometry.comment: 11 pages, small edits following referee report

Differential Geometry.title: Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean. We show that if both of these metrics are lens rigid then, up to boundary fixing diffeomorphisms, each elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensor is uniquely determined by the lens data whenever it has at least one isotropic point. If none of those points exists, then there are exactly two elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensors with the same lens data. Clearly, not all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms preserve the imposed structure of the slowness surface. We show that the set of well-behaved diffeomorphisms is never a subgroup of all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms. Our proofs are based on an interplay of algebra and geometry, and the key of the proofs is a characterization of the elliptic anisotropy via several polynomial conditions.

Differential Geometry.title: Topping's conjecture for solutions of harmonic map flow with isolated bubbles
Differential Geometry.summary: By establishing a weighted Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality for maps which are close to a fixed harmonic map modulo scaling, we prove Topping's conjecture on continuity of the body map in the case of finite time singularities at which only isolated bubbles form.

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
Differential Geometry.summary: We obtain sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products whose bases are compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary and whose fibres are closed Riemannian manifolds. These bounds involve the volume of the warped product and of its boundary, as well as the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on the fibre and the Steklov eigenvalues of the base. After separation of variables, these bounds are obtained by comparison with auxiliary Helmholtz-Steklov problems on the base involving weighted Laplace operators naturally induced by the warping function. We also study the effect of various natural geometric constraints, such as the warping function being identically equal to one on the boundary. The proofs make use of various spectral approximation methods, including homogenisation on manifolds when the fibres are one-dimensional.
Differential Geometry.comment: This work supersedes arXiv:2512.15416 where upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products were obtained for the case where the fibre has dimension at least two. By using different techniques, this work treats the case where fibres have any dimension (including dimension one) and obtains sharp bounds

Differential Geometry.title: Lojasiewicz inequalities for maps of the 2-sphere
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality $$ \left| E(u) - 4πn \right| \leq C \| \mathcal{T}(u) \|^α$$ for maps $u \in W^{2,2}\left( S^2, S^2 \right).$ The inequality holds with $α= 1$ in general and with $α> 1$ unless $u$ is nearly constant on an open set. We obtain polynomial convergence of weak solutions of harmonic map flow $u(t) : S^2 \to S^2$ as $t \to \infty$ on compact domains away from the singular set, assuming that the body map is nonconstant. The proof uses Topping's repulsion estimates together with polynomial lower bounds on the energy density coming from a bubble-tree induction argument.
Differential Geometry.comment: More small edits following Sep '26 referee reports. 40 pages, 1 figure

Differential Geometry.title: Geometry of the Atomic Condition
Differential Geometry.summary:
The class AC of integrands satisfying the atomic condition was introduced by De Philippis, De Rosa, and Ghiraldin in 2018. These integrands give rise to Almgren elliptic geometric functionals as proven by the second author and De Rosa in 2020. Explicit examples in intermediate dimensions include small class 2 perturbations of the area integrand and the recent anisotropies constructed by De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, among them the $\ell^q$ norms in Plücker coordinates for $q$ close to $2$.
  We reinterpret the atomic condition in terms of convex geometry. We also propose variants of AC, related to the SAC and USAC defined by De Rosa and Tione, which we call the exposed condition EC, the strong exposed condition SEC, and the quadratic exposed condition QEC. For integrands of class 2, QEC is equivalent to validity of a Caccioppoli-type inequality and is stable under class 2 perturbations; every such QEC integrand admits Lipschitzian normals. Combining these results with a result of De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, we prove that a Lipschitz graph whose anisotropic mean curvature for a QEC integrand of class 2 is $p$-integrable, with $k < p < \infty$, is of class $\mathscr{C}^{1,α}$ on an open set of full measure. Finally, for all $k \ge 2$ and $n - k \ge 3$ we construct strictly polyconvex integrands - associated to inner-product norms on $\bigwedge_k \mathbf{R}^n$ - which fail the atomic condition, showing that strict polyconvexity is necessary but not sufficient for AC.

Differential Geometry.title: The Renormalized Area--Willmore Relation
Differential Geometry.summary:
In [1, Proposition 8.1], Alexakis and Mazzeo showed that the renormalized area of minimal surfaces in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^3$ approaching the ideal boundary $\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^3$ is the negative of the Willmore energy of their Euclidean conformal compactifications.
  In this paper, we investigate whether there are other geometric surface equations for which these two quantities satisfy a universal proportionality relation. We answer this question in the affirmative by extending the Alexakis--Mazzeo result to a broader class of geometric equations containing, as two distinguished cases, the equations defining generalized singular minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and linear Weingarten surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^3$.
  Moreover, for rotational linear Weingarten surfaces, we express both energies in terms of generalized hyperelliptic integrals and show that their doubles form a family of rotational tori in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose Willmore energies realize all values in $(2π^2,\infty)$, with a particular subfamily converging to the Clifford torus in $\mathcal{W}^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$, as the optimal value $2π^2$ is approached.

Differential Geometry.title: Compact lcK manifolds with Gauduchon parallel vector fields
Differential Geometry.summary:
We prove that on a compact locally conformally Kähler manifold, the existence of a non-trivial parallel vector field with respect to a Gauduchon connection $
abla^t$, for $t
e  rac{1}{3}$, forces the metric to be either Vaisman (for $t=-1$), globally conformally Kähler (for $t=1$), or Kähler for all other values of $t$. As a consequence, we characterize compact Vaisman manifolds in terms of their Bismut holonomy group. Moreover, we show that in complex dimension two, the existence of a non-trivial $
abla^ rac{1}{3}$-parallel vector field forces the metric to be globally conformally Kähler.

Differential Geometry.title: Deformations of Kähler and Balanced Hyperbolicity
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the deformation stability of Kähler and balanced hyperbolicity. We prove that Kähler hyperbolicity is open under arbitrary small holomorphic deformations, but need not be closed, even in families of smooth projective surfaces. By contrast, balanced hyperbolicity is not open in general: in every complex dimension at least five, we construct a balanced hyperbolic central fibre with non-balanced nearby fibres. We establish criteria for the deformation stability of balanced hyperbolicity using Aeppli cohomology and Lefschetz theory. For principal holomorphic torus bundles over products of curves of genus at least two, we compute the relevant hyperbolic cohomology, obtain a numerical characterization of balanced hyperbolicity, and prove its openness under small deformations.
Differential Geometry.comment: 32 pages, improvements including an unrestricted openness and failure of closedness about the Kahler hyperbolicity deformation, comments are welcome!

Differential Geometry.title: Finding the Birman-Series set
Differential Geometry.summary: By a celebrated result of Birman and Series, the set of simple complete geodesics form a nowhere dense subset of a hyperbolic surface. We show that a segment of finite length is in a (small) neighborhood of this set if it can be "extended simply" in both directions for long enough. We deduce that, for large enough genus $g$, there exist surfaces with a Birman-Series set that is roughly $\frac{1}{g^{\sfrac{2}{3}}}$-dense.

Differential Geometry.title: Yet Another Family of Complex Structures on $S^6$
Differential Geometry.summary: Following a similar path as the recent construction of a complex structure on $S^6$ we construct another such family, disjoint from the known ones.

Differential Geometry.title: Isoparametric Hypersurfaces of $\mathbb H^n\times\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R$
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify the isoparametric hypersurfaces and the homogeneous hypersurfaces of $\mathbb H^n\times\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R$, $n\ge 2$, by establishing that any such hypersurface has constant angle function and constant principal curvatures.
Differential Geometry.comment: 28 pages, 1 figure. In this revised version we corrected the proof of Proposition 7, which establishes the constancy of the angle function. Published in Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa

Differential Geometry.title: A Lower Bound for the First Non-zero Basic Eigenvalue on a Singular Riemannian Foliation
Differential Geometry.summary:
In the paper, we provide a lower bound of the first non-zero basic eigenvalue on a closed singular Riemannian manifold $(M^n,\mathcal{F})$ having basic mean curvature that depends on the given lower bound of the Ricci curvature $Ric(M)\geq (n-1)K$ and the diameter of the leaf space $d_{M/\mathcal{F}}$. For foliations given by points, the results cover estimates of the first non-zero eigenvalues lower bounds, which are Zhong-Yang estimate, Yang estimate and Shi-Yang estimate.
  We also show a rigidity result that corresponds to the case of $Ric(M)\geq 0$. This is a generalization of Hang-Wang rigidity, which is the equality case of Zhong-Yang estimate.
Differential Geometry.comment: 29 pages, change the abstract, deleted figures, add Section 4 for negative Ricci lower bound, change the statement and the proof of the rigidity theorem for the nonnegative Ricci case

Differential Geometry.title: Compactly supported instability of Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: On the Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metric of dimension $n\geq 4$, we show that the destabilizing TT tensor of Ozuch lies in the image of the ``TT-tensor machine''. By continuity, it can then be approximated, in suitable weighted Sobolev spaces, by smooth compactly supported TT tensors, on which the stability quadratic form is still negative. This proves instability in the usual sense for noncompact manifolds. To our knowledge, no exact smooth compactly supported destabilizing TT tensor was known before, even in 4D.

Differential Geometry.title: Butcher series for Hamiltonian Poisson integrators through symplectic groupoids
Differential Geometry.summary: We exhibit a new pre-Lie algebra in the framework of symplectic groupoids and, in turn, use Butcher trees to compute the Taylor series of a solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation on any symplectic groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M.$ The impact of this new algebraic approach is twofold. On the geometric side, it yields algebraic operations to approximate Lagrangian bisections of $\mathcal{G}$ using the Butcher-Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra and, in turn, aims at a better understanding of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of $M.$ On the computational side, we define a new class of Poisson integrators for Hamiltonian dynamics on Poisson manifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: Isoperimetry of singular CMC hypersurfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We produce the first examples of singular isoperimetric boundaries with non-zero constant mean curvature in Riemannian manifolds. The main technical ingredient is establishing that, for constant mean curvature hypersurfaces containing isolated singularities modelled on strictly stable, strictly minimising regular tangent cones, weak strict stability implies local unique volume-constrained minimisation.

Differential Geometry.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(π_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the
Differential Geometry.comment: AI was used to streamline and verify some of the proofs

Differential Geometry.title: Ruling out Infinite-Time Bubbling under $SO(4)$-Equivariant Yang--Mills Flow on $\mathbb{S}^4\times SU(2)$
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the Yang--Mills flow on $\mathbb{S}^4$ restricted to $\mathrm{SO}(4)$-equivariant connections on the trivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ bundle. It was expected that antipodal instanton--anti-instanton configurations would lead to infinite-time singularities along the flow. We show that this does not occur. Moreover, for any smooth equivariant initial condition, the flow converges to the trivial flat connection.

Differential Geometry.title: The Riemannian Convex Bundle Method
Differential Geometry.summary: We introduce the convex bundle method to solve convex, non-smooth optimization problems on Riemannian manifolds of bounded sectional curvature. Each step of our method is based on a model that involves the convex hull of previously collected subgradients, parallelly transported into the current serious iterate. This approach generalizes the dual form of classical bundle subproblems in Euclidean space. We prove that, under mild conditions, the convex bundle method converges to a minimizer. Several numerical examples implemented using Manopt$.$jl illustrate the performance of the proposed method and compare it to the subgradient method, the cyclic proximal point algorithm, as well as the proximal bundle method.

Differential Geometry.title: Urysohn width of hypersurfaces and positive macroscopic scalar curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that if a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold with non-trivial codimension 1 homology with $\mathbb{Z}_2$-coefficients or $\mathbb{Z}$-coefficients has positive macroscopic scalar curvature large enough, then it contains a non-nullhomologous hypersurface of small Urysohn $(n-2)$-width. This constitutes a macroscopic analogue of a theorem by Bray--Brendle--Neves on the area of non-contractible 2-spheres in a closed Riemannian 3-manifold with positive scalar curvature. Our proof is based on an adaptation of Guth's macroscopic version of the Schoen-Yau descent argument.
authors: Teo Gil Moreno de Mora Sardà
Differential Geometry.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures. To appear in Journal of Topology and Analysis

Differential Geometry.title: Riemannian Shape Analysis of the Corpus Callosum in Kendall Space: Aging and Alzheimer's Disease
Differential Geometry.summary: The corpus callosum (CC) is a major white-matter structure and a well-established marker of brain aging, but most studies quantify it using scalar summaries that discard its boundary geometry. We present a Riemannian shape-space framework \cite{fletcher2013geodesic-regression} for analyzing age-related morphological change in the midsagittal CC, applied to the OASIS-1 cohort. Each contour is represented by $128$ landmarks and embedded into Kendall shape space, where translation, rotation, and scale are removed. We derive a multivariate geodesic regression with exact Riemannian gradients and use the fitted age-velocity field to localize age-related deformation to five anatomical sub-regions. In the cognitively normal cohort ($n = 252$), geodesic regression outperforms the Euclidean linear benchmark ($R^2 = 0.1355$ vs.\ $0.1216$). Regional energy is anterior-dominant: the Genu carries $46.1\%$ and the Anterior Body $23.3\%$ of total age-related shape change, together accounting for $\sim 69\%$ despite comprising only $\sim 41\%$ of landmarks. Signed projections confirm the ordering (Genu $r = 0.562$; Anterior Body $r = 0.507$). In contrast, age explains less than $0.5\%$ of shape variance in Alzheimer's disease ($n = 88$), indicating that the disease disrupts the healthy aging trajectory. A tangent-space classifier achieves an age-group AUC of $0.791$ from the 2D contour alone, exceeding a recent volumetric benchmark ($0.67$).

Differential Geometry.title: Minimizing tangent maps into complex projective space
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify all nonconstant smooth harmonic maps $\mathbb{S}^2\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ whose 0-homogeneous extensions are minimizing: they are, respectively, isometric embeddings or holomorphic isometric embeddings composed with a Hopf map.

Differential Geometry.title: Oblique boundary value problems for n-1type augmented Hessian equations
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study the global regularity of oblique boundary value problems for n-1 type augmented Hessian equations on a bounded domain, without imposing any convexity condition either on the domain or on the matrix-valued function in the n-1 type augmented Hessian equations. We establish a global existence and uniqueness theory for classical elliptic solutions by deriving global a priori estimates up to second-order derivatives. Besides the known applications for n-1 type Monge-Ampere operators in optimal transportation and geometric optics, the general theory here embraces equations raised by Li-Sheng, Some Dirichlet problems arising from conformal geometry. Pac. J. Math. 251, 2011, 337-359 and Guan-Qiu-Yuan, Fully nonlinear elliptic equations for conformal deformations of Chern-Ricci forms. Adv. Math. 343, 2019, 538-566.

Differential Geometry.title: On Santaló's Problem
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper investigates an isoperimetric-type problem posed by L. A. Santaló, concerning convex surfaces in hyperbolic 3-space that minimize total mean curvature among all convex surfaces with fixed surface area. This problem asks for a characterization of the minimizers and for the optimal form of a Minkowski-type inequality in hyperbolic 3-space. In this work, we propose a conjectural description of the minimizers under certain regularity assumptions. We also construct a new family of convex surfaces as as potential minimizer candidates and establish a property of the singular points of any minimizer.
Differential Geometry.comment: 32 pages, 2 figures. Provided more detailed numerical computation in proof of Theorem 1.2

Differential Geometry.title: Cohomology and multiplicative gaps for quasi-isometries of nilpotent groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct two word metrics on the same seven-dimensional torsion-free nilpotent lattice whose asymptotic cones are isometric, but for which every quasi-isometry has multiplicative constant at least $1+\varepsilon$, for one fixed $\varepsilon>0$. We use a convex invariant of a fixed quasi-isometry $Ψ:N\to M$. The displacement cocycle of $Ψ$ and the right-invariant means on $N$ determine a compact convex set $\mathcal A(Ψ)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(V_N,V_M)$. If $\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(Ψ)$ denotes the first-layer maps of the graded homomorphisms that occur as blow-downs of $Ψ$ with varying basepoints, then $$ \mathcal A(Ψ)=\operatorname{conv}\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(Ψ), \qquad\operatorname{Ext}\mathcal A(Ψ)\subseteq\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(Ψ). $$ For every extreme point $L\in\mathcal A(Ψ)$, the dual map $L^*$ is also the degree-one part of an isomorphism of the full real cohomology rings. This cohomological compatibility, together with the realization of first-layer Pansu differentials by invariant means, yields the multiplicative constant gap stated above.
Differential Geometry.comment: 34 pages. This is split off from the authors' previous submission arXiv:2512.06753. Comments are most welcome!

Differential Geometry.title: Ambient and Poincaré metrics for CR $3$-manifolds associated with the self-dual Einstein ACH metric
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct new ambient and Poincaré metrics for the Fefferman conformal manifold over $3$-dimensional CR manifolds, starting from the associated self-dual Einstein ACH metric. Unlike the classical ambient and Poincaré metrics arising from approximate solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation, these metrics satisfy Einstein-Maxwell-type equations to infinite order rather than the Ricci-flat or Einstein equations. Since these metrics are determined to infinite order without ambiguity, they enable us to construct CR invariant differential operators and local CR invariants involving arbitrarily high order derivatives of the Tanaka-Webster curvature and torsion. As an application, we obtain the ambient metric construction of the CR GJMS (Gover-Graham) operators of all orders in dimension $3$.

Differential Geometry.title: Generalized Gauduchon metrics on compact complex spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $X$ be an irreducible reduced compact complex space of dimension $n$, and let $ω$ be a Hermitian metric on $X$. For each $1\le k\le n-1$, we prove that there exist a constant $c_k$ and a smooth positive function $ρ$ on $X_{\mathrm{reg}}$ such that $\ii\partial\bar\partial(ρω^k)\wedgeω^{n-k-1}=c_kρω^n$. The function $ρ$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero. The constant $c_k$ is unique, and $ρ$ is unique up to a positive multiple among bounded smooth positive solutions. We also prove that the full sign set $\{-1,0,1\}$ of the generalized Gauduchon constants $c_k$ on a compact complex manifold is preserved by finite sequences of blow-ups with smooth centers.

Differential Geometry.title: Nonlocal Characterizations of Stochastic Completeness on Complete Riemannian Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary:
In this paper, we first prove that the following generalized conservation principle holds on complete Riemannian manifolds: for every \(0<s<1\) and \(t>0\), \[ T_t^{(s)}\mathbf 1+\int_0^t T_τ^{(s)}\mathcal R_s\,dτ=1 \qquad\text{on }M, \] where \(\mathcal R_s\) is the intrinsic killing term measuring the loss of mass of the subordinate semigroup, and the condition \(\mathcal R_s\equiv0\) is equivalent to the stochastic completeness of \(M\).
  We then provide several new nonlocal characterizations of stochastic completeness. In particular, we show that stochastic completeness is equivalent to genuinely nonlocal conditions, including the zero-mean identity \[ \int_M (-Δ)^s\varphi\,dV_g=0 \qquad\forall\,\varphi\in C_c^\infty(M), \] as well as the uniqueness of bounded distributional solutions to the associated fractional elliptic and parabolic equations. We also revisit the equivalent \(L^1\)-core characterization for the generator of the heat semigroup, which plays an important role in our approach.
  In addition, we prove \(L^p\)-contractivity and smoothing properties of the subordinate semigroup, establish both short-time and long-time asymptotic results for the fractional heat kernel, derive the short-time asymptotics of jump probabilities for the associated Markov process, and study the variational characterization and minimality properties of the fractional resolvent. Together, these results provide a unified analytic and probabilistic framework for the fractional Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: Direct proofs for spaces with cyclic parallel Ricci tensor
Differential Geometry.summary: We give direct proofs of rigidity results for gradient Ricci solitons, compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, and critical spaces with cyclic parallel Ricci tensor. For solitons and quasi-Einstein manifolds, successive traces of first-order pointwise identities yield quadratic equations for the Ricci tensor and its modification. These equations imply radial flatness and radial $Q$-flatness, respectively, and the corresponding global rigidity theorems apply. For critical spaces, comparison of two expressions for the Laplacian of the Hessian gives a pointwise tensor identity whose scalar contraction yields a weighted divergence formula. Integration then gives the vacuum static, CPE, and Miao--Tam conclusions. The same comparison also proves Ricci parallelism pointwise for solitons and quasi-Einstein manifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp lower bound of the first eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian under integral Ricci curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a sharp Zhong-Yang type lower bound for the first nonzero eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian on closed manifolds with small integral Ricci curvature for $p \geq 2$. The proof combines a global elliptic estimate obtained by Sobolev truncation with strict perturbations of one-dimensional comparison profiles.

Differential Geometry.title: Compactness and Noncompactness for the Positive Yamabe--Escobar Problem with Minimal Boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the Yamabe--Escobar equation prescribing positive constant scalar curvature and minimal boundary. The compactness conjecture asks whether being conformally equivalent to the round hemisphere is the only obstruction for its set of positive solutions to be compact. In this paper we show that this is true for dimensions $3\leq n\leq 14$. We show that this dimensional threshold $n_*=14$ is sharp by constructing in $n\geq 15$ nonumbilic and non-locally-conformally-flat examples of metrics in the hemisphere for which a noncompact sequence of solutions exists. We do the same for the special classes of locally conformally flat metrics, $n_*^{LCF}=18$, and the metrics with umbilic boundary, $n_*^{umb} =20$. In all three settings we also prove that the Weyl--umbilicity vanishing conjecture holds for $4\leq n\leq n_*$ and construct counterexamples in $n>n_*$ by perturbing the noncompactness examples. To the best of the author's knowledge, these are the first locally conformally flat noncompactness constructions for the positive-scalar-curvature, minimal-boundary case of the Yamabe--Escobar equation, outside the conformal class of the round hemisphere.
Differential Geometry.comment: v1: 103 pages; v2: Numerical supplement added (missing in v1 due to submission difficulties). Introduction and bibliography revised, terminology and typos corrected, and some proof details expanded, 107 pages

Differential Geometry.title: Surfaces with nonpositive magnetic curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: For a negatively curved surface, magnetic (or twisted geodesic) flows with nonpositive ''magnetic curvature'' have a large-scale geometry on the universal cover that retains some features associated with geodesic flows: magnetic boundary and visibility, possibly magnetically flat strips. This has dynamical consequences: orbit-equivalence to the geodesic flow, density of periodic points, transitivity, entropy-expansivity, existence of equilibrium states.

Differential Geometry.title: Brane space localization and genus-0 T-duality with $H$-flux
Volume growth and parabolicity for non-symmetric operators
Differential Geometry.summary: The interplay between a weighted volume measure and its naturally associated weighted Laplace operator is fundamental to the geometric analysis of weighted structures governed by gradient vector fields. Beyond the gradient setting, however, the theory has remained considerably less developed, largely because this natural correspondence is lost. In this paper, we identify invariant measures as the appropriate framework for extending the theory to general drifted Laplace operators. This approach yields a systematic treatment of parabolicity in the non-gradient setting, reveals its connection with volume growth, and leads to new volume finiteness results for non-gradient geometric structures.

Differential Geometry.title: Rational curves on toroidal compactifications of Picard modular varieties
Differential Geometry.summary:
It was known that the canonical bundle of a smooth toroidal compactification of a noncompact finite-volume ball quotient is nef in dimension $n\geq3$ and ample in dimension $n\geq6$. We prove that the canonical bundle is ample in dimension $n\geq4$ and show that this dimension bound is sharp. We construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular threefolds whose smooth projective toroidal compactifications have non-ample canonical bundle. Each compactification contains a smooth rational curve meeting the interior and having canonical degree zero.
  More generally, in every dimension $n\geq2$, we construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular varieties whose smooth toroidal compactifications contain smooth rational curves meeting the interior. In particular, such curves persist in arbitrarily high dimension, even when the canonical bundle is ample.

Differential Geometry.title: The Height of Choe's Higher-Dimensional Enneper Surface
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that Choe's higher-dimensional Enneper hypersurfaces in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $3\le n\le6$, cannot be confined between two parallel hyperplanes, disproving his slab confinement conjecture. We further strengthen this conclusion by determining their precise height growth exponent. If $H(R)$ denotes the maximal absolute height above the asymptotic hyperplane within the horizontal ball of radius $R$, then $H(R)=R^{α_1+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$, where $α_1=\frac{\sqrt{(n-2)^2+4λ_1(Ω)}-(n-2)}{2}$, $Ω=S^{n-1}\setminus[0,\infty)^n$, and $λ_1(Ω)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the spherical Laplacian. In particular, $0<α_1<1$, so the height is unbounded but grows sublinearly. The proof combines the blow-down behavior of a fundamental piece of Choe's hypersurface with the rigidity of positive harmonic functions on cones. In dimension two, the formula gives $2/3$, recovering the classical Enneper height-growth exponent.

Differential Geometry.title: Autoregressive Processes on Stiefel and Grassmann Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: System identification methods for autoregressive processes on Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds are presented and studied. We model the system parameters as elements of the orthogonal group and we show that the system can be estimated by averaging over observations. Lastly, we propose an algorithm for computing these system parameters using a conjugate gradient method adapted to Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $°p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=α\,q(βz+h)+k$ or $p(z)=α\,\bar q(βz+h)+k$ for some $α,β,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|α|=|β|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.

Differential Geometry.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We give a planar construction with exponential lower bound with respect to $n$: $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,2)\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}, \quad n\geq3 $.

Differential Geometry.title: Asymptotically conical shrinking ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow: rotational construction and uniqueness
Differential Geometry.summary: For $1\leq r\leq n-1$ we study shrinking self-similar ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow, $S_r=c\langle X,N\rangle$ with $c<0$, that are asymptotic to a cone.
