Once the magnetization is fixed, we can show the convergence of the enriched free energy to the solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The magnetization constraint is also used to show the convexity of the initial condition in this equation, and this yields a variational representation of the solution, as a Hopf formula. Convex duality then turns this formula into an optimization over martingales whose initial values are the prescribed magnetizations.
Probability.comment: 60 pages + 10-page appendix. The results of the appendix are meant to facilitate understanding but are not used in the main text

Probability.title: Scaling limit of boundary random walks: A martingale problem approach
Probability.summary: We establish the scaling limit of a class of boundary random walks to the full spectrum of Brownian-type processes on the half-line. By solving the associated martingale problem and employing weak convergence techniques, we prove that under appropriate scaling, the process converges to the general Brownian motion in the $J_1$-Skorokhod topology. The main novelty of our approach lies in a result on the asymptotic behavior of the local time of the boundary random walks, allowing us to derive a CLT result for several Brownian-type limit processes on the half-line.

Probability.title: Critical oriented percolation enhanced along random supercritical horizontal lines
Probability.summary: We consider the oriented site percolation model in a random environment introduced by Kesten, Sidoravicius and Vares (2022), in which the horizontal lines of the lattice are independently declared bad or good, sites being open with a probability that depends only on the type of their line. We study the boundary case where the bad lines are critical and the good ones supercritical, so that the model is critical oriented site percolation enhanced along a random set of good lines. We prove that percolation occurs for any positive density of the good lines. An arbitrarily sparse set of arbitrarily weakly enhanced lines suffices, the density of good lines and the strength of the enhancement being decoupled. The proof adapts the renormalization scheme of Archer, Hartarsky, Kolesnik, Olesker-Taylor, Schapira and Valesin (2026). We show that the edge of the process travels at a positive speed, which yields crossing estimates for tilted boxes; during runs of bad lines, we rely on the box-crossing property of Duminil-Copin, Tassion and Teixeira (2018); and the renormalized model dominates the oriented percolation with geometric defects of Hilário, Sá, Sanchis and Teixeira (2026).

Probability.title: Random Polyhedral Cones I: Distributional Results via Gale Duality
Probability.summary:
Let $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ be independent random vectors uniformly distributed on the unit sphere $\mathbb S^{d-1}\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, where $n\ge d$, and consider the random polyhedral cone \[ \mathcal W_{n,d}:=\mathop{\mathrm{pos}} (U_1,\ldots,U_n) = \{λ_1 U_1+ \ldots + λ_n U_n: λ_1\geq 0, \ldots, λ_n \geq 0\}. \] We establish several distributional results for $\mathcal W_{n,d}$ and the associated spherical polytope $\mathcal W_{n,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$. Our main contributions include:
  (i) Let $α_d$ denote the solid angle of $\mathcal W_{d,d}$ and write $m(d,k):=\mathbb E[α_d^k]$ for its $k$-th moment. We prove the symmetry $m(d,k)=m(k,d)$. As an application, we compute $\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}[α_d]=2^{-d}(d+1)^{-1}-4^{-d}$ and derive a closed formula for the third moment.
  (ii) For $n=d+1,d+2,d+3$ we determine the probability that $\mathcal W_{n,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$ is a spherical simplex, a spherical analogue of the classical Sylvester problem. In the case $n=d+2$ we also determine the distribution of the number of vertices of $\mathcal W_{d+2,d}\cap\mathbb S^{d-1}$.
  (iii) Let $f_\ell(\mathcal W_{n,d})$ denote the number of $\ell$-dimensional faces of $\mathcal W_{n,d}$. We prove a distributional limit theorem for $f_\ell(\mathcal W_{n,d})$ in the regime $n=d+k$ and $\ell=d-q$, where $k,q\in\mathbb N$ are fixed and $d\to\infty$. The limit law is a weighted sum of independent chi squared variables, with weights given by explicit eigenvalues of a convolution operator on the sphere.
  A unifying ingredient is an explicit coupling producing i.i.d. uniform vectors $U_1,\ldots,U_n\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ together with i.i.d. uniform vectors $V_1,\ldots,V_n\in\mathbb S^{n-d-1}$ whose associated oriented matroids are Gale dual.

Probability.title: Dimension-free Convergence Rate in Sliced Wasserstein Distance for Empirical Measures of Markov Processes
Probability.summary:
To derive dimension-free convergence rates of empirical measures for Markov processes on a Banach space, we adopt the sliced Wasserstein distance (SW distance) induced by a probability measure with full support on the unit ball in the dual space. This distance refers to the convergence in finite dimensions, and is topologically equivalent to the classical Wasserstein distance when the Banach space is finite-dimensional. With the SW distance we derive dimension-free convergence rates for the empirical measures of ergodic Markov processes on Banach space, which can be sharp as illustrated by concrete examples.
  The study provides an efficient way to simulate infinite-dimensional distributions using sample trajectories of Markov processes, avoiding $``$the curse of dimensionality" in the classical Wasserstein distance. The main results apply to a broad class of infinite-dimensional models, and are illustrated by partially dissipative SPDEs in the end of the paper.

Probability.title: Large deviations, gradient flows and fluctuating hydrodynamics for fractional diffusion
Probability.summary: This work is a step towards a general understanding of fluctuations for systems of particles described at large scale by fractional diffusion. First, we derive formally a Large Deviation Principle for the empirical measure of mean-field interacting particles with a L{é}vy-type noise. In the case of independent particles, this unveils a generalized gradient flow structure at large scales. Second, we derive and solve numerically a stochastic Partial Differential Equation describing the fluctuating hydrodynamics of this system. The results compare well with direct numerical integration of the particles' dynamics.

Probability.title: Backward and reflected backward stochastic differential equations under initial enlargement of Brownian filtrations
Probability.summary: We investigate the effect of initially enlarging a Brownian filtration by its terminal value on backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) and reflected BSDEs (RBSDEs). We establish the Brownian innovation representation and the predictable representation property in the enlarged filtration, highlighting the singular information drift arising from the semimartingale decomposition of the original Brownian motion. We derive transfer identities under suitable integrability conditions and provide explicit counterexamples showing that the resulting singular equations may fail to admit unique square-integrable solutions, including in the reflected case. We further develop a conditional parametrization of regular BSDEs and establish a conditional comparison principle for Snell envelopes, illustrating both the strict value of additional information and the failure of general pathwise domination. An exact projection identity is also obtained for zero-driver terminal payoffs. Finally, we discuss possible extensions to irregular obstacles and more general information structures.

Probability.title: An Operator-Theoretic Analysis of Nonlinear Filtering under Model Misspecification
Probability.summary: We study nonlinear filtering with misspecified initial distributions and dynamics, but a correctly specified observation model. Observations are treated as a random process generated by the true model, rather than as fixed realizations, and both the correct filter and the misspecified filter are analyzed under this common observation law. Our main result is a Bayesian total variation balance identity for the expected change in total variation distance under a Bayesian update: a covariance term minus a non-negative remainder. The identity characterizes conditional and averaged update non-expansivity. Combined with prediction contraction, it yields finite-time bounds separating the initialization error from accumulated dynamical discrepancies, while allowing expansive updates. When the averaged updates are non-expansive and a uniform joint prediction--update coefficient is less than one, a persistent dynamical misspecification yields an asymptotic error bound proportional to the one-step discrepancy. When the conditional updates are non-expansive, we characterize an accumulated joint contraction that implies almost-sure and \(L^1\) coalescence of the true and misspecified filters. Finally, we verify update non-expansivity for scalar Gaussian predictive laws under a variance-ordering condition and, separately, derive explicit prediction contraction bounds for truncated kernels and bounded transition functions with elliptically symmetric noise.

Probability.title: Free probability via entropic optimal transport
Probability.summary: Let $μ$ and $ν$ be compactly supported probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $μ\boxplus ν$ denote their additive free convolution. We show that for all sufficiently large real $z$, \begin{equation} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \log(z - x) \, (μ\boxplus ν)(\mathrm{d}x) = \sup_Π \left\{ \mathbf{E}_Π[\log(z - (X+Y))] - H(Π\mid μ\otimes ν) \right\}, \end{equation} where the supremum is taken over all couplings $Π$ of $μ$ and $ν$. Analogous formulas hold for multiplicative free convolution $μ\boxtimes ν$ and free compression $[μ]_τ$. In this way, integrals of a log-potential against free convolutions can be expressed as entropic optimal transport problems. The corresponding optimal couplings admit explicit formulas, from which the standard $R$- and $S$-transform descriptions of additive and multiplicative free convolution are recovered. In particular, the optimizer $Π_z$ encodes the subordination equations via couplings of random variables. Our approach is based on a large deviation principle on the symmetric group, combined with the quadrature method of Marcus--Spielman--Srivastava.
Probability.comment: 40 pages, updated version with improved proof of symmetric group limit and expanded applications

Probability.title: Balls in groups: volume, structure and growth
Probability.summary: We develop a fine-scale structural theory for balls of polynomial volume in finitely generated groups. Our main result shows that a polynomial-volume hypothesis on a single ball implies that every larger ball can, after quotienting by a certain canonical finite normal subgroup, be embedded in a lattice of a Lie group whose connected component is nilpotent with sharply bounded index and dimension. These Lie groups and lattices form chains of successive quotients that are essentially unique, giving a quantitative fine-scale analogue of Losert's strengthening of the Mal'cev completion. This describes the fine structure of the group with sharp algebraic and quantitative precision; for example, it leads to sharp bounds in Breuillard, Green and Tao's finitary version of Gromov's polynomial-growth theorem. These results have a wide range of applications in various aspects of the theory of vertex-transitive graphs, including for instance random walks, percolation, and scaling limits. We obtain some of these applications in the present paper, and treat others in companion papers. Some are due to or joint with other authors.
Probability.comment: 101 pages. V3: improved exposition, strengthened main result

Probability.title: Distribution tail of the distance to infinity in supercritical bond percolation
Probability.summary: We give an estimate for the distribution tail of the passage time between $0$ and $\infty$ in first-passage percolation on $\mathbb Z^d$, when the weight distribution is bounded and has a supercritical atom at $0$. A special case involves the number of disjoint cutsets between $0$ and $\infty$ in supercritical bond percolation. Besides, we show that the rate function for the upper-tail deviations of the point-to-point passage time is asymptotically polynomial near $0$.

Probability.title: Optimal Control of Mean-field FBSDEs and Classical Solutions of the Related Generalized HJB Equations
Probability.summary: In this article, we study optimal control problems driven by mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The aim is two-fold: (i) to provide the unique optimal control; (ii) to establish classical solutions of the associated generalized Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations on the space of probability measures. For (i), we study the coupled system arising from the maximum principle, which involves both the state FBSDEs and the adjoint FBSDEs. This system is non-standard and more complicated than that in standard mean-field type control (MFTC) problems. By extending the method of continuation in the coefficients to our framework, we establish the well-posedness result, and subsequently obtain the differentiability of the value functional with respect to the distribution argument --- thereby extending existing results for MFTC problems. For (ii), since the flow property does not generally hold for control problems of FBSDEs, standard dynamic-programming arguments cannot be applied directly. We therefore develop probabilistic approaches to the classical solvability of generalized HJB equations under three distinct sets of conditions. The auxiliary processes arising in these arguments differ significantly from those in standard MFTC problems. We establish new connections between the value function and the adjoint processes, derive equations for the relevant decoupling field, and obtain first- and second-order generalized HJB equations, including a coupled system on the space of probability measures. The standard HJB equations for MFTC problems are recovered as special cases. Our approach yields classical solutions without requiring non-degeneracy of the diffusion.

Probability.title: Eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem
Probability.summary: We study the eigenvalues of the negative Dirichlet Laplacian $-Δ$ in domain $D_{ε,N}$ obtained by removing $N$ Euclidean balls of radius $ε$ from a bounded open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ ($d\ge2$). It is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $ρ$ and for $N\to\infty$ and $ε\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate Newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $κ>0$, the eigenvalues of $-Δ$ in $D_{ε,N}$ homogenize to those of the Schrödinger operator $-Δ+κρ$ in $D$. Here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate Central Limit Theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. Unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by Figari, Orlandi and Teta and, independently, Ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.

Probability.title: The Brownian bubble tea
Probability.summary:
We use Loewner-Kufarev evolution to decompose the Brownian loop soup into a Poisson point process on Brownian bubbles which we call the Brownian bubble tea driven by $ρ$, where $ρ$ is the driving measure for the Loewner chain. The only assumption on $ρ$ is that the evolving boundaries are locally connected. This generalizes a similar disintegration result of Lawler and Werner to essentially optimal regularity, and includes foliations with finite Loewner-Kufarev energy as well as radial and whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ for all $κ\geqslant 0$.
  As applications, we give Brownian loop interpretations of the conformal distortion formula for Loewner-Kufarev energy and the relationships between the Loewner energy, Loewner-Kufarev energy, and the Schwarzian action.

Probability.title: Optimal scaling and curvature correction for constrained MCMC on spheres
Probability.summary: Sampling Gaussian measures restricted to nonlinear manifolds in high dimensions requires a proposal kernel that respects both geometric constraints and dimensional scaling requirements. We introduce tangent preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN), which combines a manifold projection with a cancellation of the ambient Gaussian contribution, leaving only a geometric residual. Considering a shifted sphere with $\sqrt d$ scaling of radius and centre as a tractable benchmark embedded manifold, we prove that uncorrected tangent pCN results in a proposal noise scale of order $d^{-1/6}$ (compared to $d^{-1/2}$ for a tangent random-walk). We establish asymptotic optimal tuning for the geodesic expected squared jump distance which is maximised at an acceptance probability of 0.574 for the family of drift-corrected tangent proposals containing tangent pCN and tangent MALA. We also prove a joint diffusion limit for the parallel and orthogonal coordinates to the sphere's centre vector of tangent pCN. The orthogonal diffusion speed matches the limiting geodesic expected squared jump distance and is maximised at acceptance probability 0.574, whereas the parallel speed is maximised at 0.712, demonstrating that optimal tuning depends on the observable. We then identify an intrinsic precision correction characterised by potential Hessian and Ricci curvature that yields a proposal kernel with dimension-independent fixed step size limit. We discuss a generalisation to arbitrary hypersurfaces and present nondegenerate scaling of tangent pCN applied to conditioned diffusions under resolution refinement.

Probability.title: Bivariate asymptotics via random walks: application to large genus maps
Probability.summary: We obtain bivariate asymptotics for the number of (unicellular) combinatorial maps (a model of discrete surfaces) as both the size and the genus grow. This work is related to two research topics that have been very active recently: multivariate asymptotics and large genus geometry. Our method consists of studying a linear recurrence for these numbers, and can be applied to many other linear recurrences. In particular, we include a general theorem that yields asymptotics for such recurrences, provided that some assumptions are satisfied.
Probability.comment: 40 pages, 4 figures. Previous version was an extended abstract of this work for FPSAC 2025

Probability.title: $L^2$ convergence rates for singular stochastic wave dynamics
Probability.summary: We establish quantitative hypocoercivity for singular stochastic damped wave equations arising in stochastic quantization. Building on the finite-dimensional argument of Cao, Lu, and Wang [Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. 2023], we derive a dimension-free criterion that replaces uniform semiconvexity by a log-Sobolev inequality together with exponential lower-tail bounds for the bottom of the Hessian spectrum. We verify this criterion for the two-dimensional $Φ^4_2$ and sine-Gordon models and for the three-dimensional $Φ^4_3$ model, through estimates on the lowest eigenvalue of associated singular random Schrödinger operators. Combined with the continuum limit established in a companion paper, this yields exponential $L^2$ convergence to equilibrium for the $Φ^4_2$ dynamics and for sine-Gordon with $β^2<2π$. For $Φ^4_2$, we verify that in a weak-coupling, small-mass regime, optimizing the damping yields a kinetic relaxation rate of at least order $m$. This yields a genuine acceleration over the order-$m^2$ relaxation rate of the overdamped dynamics. The lattice estimates are uniform in the discretization for sine-Gordon throughout $β^2<4π$, and for $Φ^4_3$ at fixed volume, including regimes beyond those for which the continuum dynamics is vpresently constructed.

Probability.title: Cutoff profiles and boundary effects in the Togashi-Kaneko model of autocatalytic reactions with weak mutations
Probability.summary:
We determine explicit bulk and worst-case total variation cutoff profiles for the configuration law of a two-species Togashi--Kaneko model with a fixed population of $n$ particles and weak mutations. Boundary initial conditions introduce an additional logarithmic growth phase and change both the leading mixing-time coefficient and the limiting cutoff profile.
  Let $κ_1,κ_2>0$ be the autocatalytic rate constants and put $λ_*=κ_1κ_2/(κ_1+κ_2)$. For deterministic initial configurations whose density converges to $m\in(0,1)$, the total variation distance to equilibrium at time $t_n(s)=\frac{\log n}{2λ_*}+\frac{s}{λ_*}$ converges to $\mathcal G(r(m)e^{-s})$ for every fixed $s\in\mathbb R$, where $\mathcal G(r)=d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathcal N(r,1),\mathcal N(0,1))$, $r(m)>0$ is explicit, and $\mathcal N(a,b^2)$ denotes the Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and variance $b^2$. For the worst-case distance $\mathscr D_n(t)$ over all initial configurations, we prove $\mathscr D_n(T_n+s/λ_*)\to\mathcal P(s)$, where $T_n=\left(\frac{1}{\min\{κ_1,κ_2\}}+\frac{1}{2λ_*}\right)\log n$.The profile $\mathcal P$ is the total variation distance between the equilibrium Gaussian and a Gaussian mixture whose random displacement is determined by a gamma-distributed amplitude arising from early growth at the boundary. Unlike the bulk profile, $\mathcal P$ depends on the mutation parameters. Both cutoffs have windows of constant order, and we identify the asymptotically worst boundary configurations.

Probability.title: Distribution-Dependent Improvements of McDiarmid's Inequality via Rényi Divergence
Probability.summary: We investigate whether Rényi divergence can sharpen McDiarmid's inequality and its distribution-dependent refinement induced by KL divergence. Starting from Marton's transportation proof, we show that its transport inequality fails in general when KL divergence is replaced by Rényi divergence of order $0<α<1$. For sums of independent bounded random variables, however, the additivity of Rényi divergence allows us to adapt the argument and derive concentration bounds. For Bernoulli sums, these bounds strictly improve on the distribution-dependent bound induced by KL divergence over a range of deviation thresholds. We also establish a distribution-dependent refinement of Gilardoni's inequality relating total variation to Rényi divergence, providing explicit constants for our general concentration bounds.

Probability.title: Sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model up to Criticality
Probability.summary: We prove that the simulated annealing algorithm efficiently samples from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $β< 1$ to an arbitrary inverse polynomial accuracy in total variation.

Probability.title: Large deviation principle for determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study natural determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds defined by canonical sections and plurisubharmonic weight functions. We present a natural condition on the weights under which these processes satisfy a large deviation principle with a good rate function given by the Fenchel--Legendre transform of the pluripotential equilibrium energy. Along the way, we prove some pluripotential theoretic results on Stein manifolds, such as the $C^{1,1}$ regularity of appropriate envelopes. These results are noncompact analogues of results of Berman and Berman--Boucksom on compact Kähler manifolds.

Probability.title: Optimal transportation under McKean-Vlasov dynamics
Probability.summary: We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. In contrast to the classical Schrödinger problem, the reference dynamics depend on the evolving law of the process, leading to nonlinear optimization problems on path space, while the terminal constraint is formulated through weak optimal transport, permitting a flexible treatment of distributional targets. This framework encompasses several problems of current interest, including the mean field Schrödinger problem, martingale optimal transport, and Schrödinger-Bass bridges. We establish three main results. First, we prove the existence of optimal controls under general coercivity, continuity, and convexity assumptions. Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schrödinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schrödinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schrödinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schrödinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.

Probability.title: Probability of Quota Violations in Divisor Apportionment Methods with Nonzero Allocations
Probability.summary:
Apportionment assigns indivisible items among groups. By the Balinski-Young theorem, no method can satisfy both house monotonicity and the quota rule. This paper investigates quota violations caused by nonzero allocation constraints, and derives exact probability formulas for their frequency. Such violations occur in systems like the U.S. House of Representatives, where each state is guaranteed at least one seat. We analyze the three-state case, introduce the $τ$ statistic to parametrize population distributions, and prove an Asymptotic Quota Stabilization theorem: for fixed $τ$, quota behavior stabilizes as populations grow, yielding probability results for quota violations determined by the set of ultimately violatory $τ$ values.
  Applying this framework to the five classical divisor methods, we derive exact probability formulas. Additionally, we show that as the number of seats $M \to \infty$, these probabilities converge to method-specific constants. These results provide a precise, quantitative foundation for evaluating the fairness and frequency of quota violations in constrained apportionment systems.

Probability.title: Simultaneous random polytope approximation characterizes the Euclidean ball
Probability.summary:
In this work, we present a new geometric characterization of the Euclidean ball based on approximation by random polytopes. We investigate when a single boundary sampling density is asymptotically optimal for two random polytope approximation problems, and show that for a convex body in $\R^d$ with $C^2$ boundary and everywhere positive principal curvatures, one fixed density minimizes the leading expected errors for any two distinct intrinsic volume differences of inscribed random polytopes if and only if the body is a Euclidean ball. We show that an analogous characterization holds for the volume and mean width differences of circumscribed random polytopes, and that uniform sampling gives the converse statement in both models.
  We also determine the unique density minimizing the average of two normalized leading errors, and obtain an explicit positive gap for every nonball. The proofs combine classical random polytope asymptotics, Hölder's inequality, and a curvature rigidity argument based on the Hsiung--Minkowski identities and Newton--Maclaurin inequalities.

Probability.title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
Probability.summary: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},μ,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.

Probability.title: Heat Kernel Estimates for Random Walks with Killing on Transient Graphs
Probability.summary: We give matching two-sided estimates for heat kernels obtained from Schrödinger operators $Δ+W$ on weighted graphs. The graphs we consider are transient and admit two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates for the Laplacian $Δ$, and the potentials $W$ decay to zero at infinity. We offer two proofs for one of our main results: one using the Feynman-Kac formula, and one without using it. Our results apply to fractal-type graphs such as graphical Sierpinski carpets, among other examples.

Probability.title: Conditional Fluctuations of Mean-Field Systems with Stable Common Noise
Probability.summary: We study conditional fluctuations of smooth mean-field systems on a torus with endogenous symmetric stable common jumps of index $0<α<1$. A positive-strip estimate makes empirical Poisson acceptance errors negligible at the sampling scale. The conditional laws given the full Poisson master converge in probability to a centered Gaussian kernel in a negative Sobolev path space. In dimension one, quantile coupling preserves this limit for microscopic marks with relative tail remainder $O(x^{-ρ})$, $ρ>α/2$. A quantified second-order tail expansion gives the endogenous rank response: it shifts the conditional Gaussian mean at criticality and, when nonzero, dominates sampling below criticality. We also identify a separate stable-to-Brownian transition for the rank error. Finally, in a translation model, rank and clock couplings give the same microscopic laws. The rank coupling has a functional Gaussian limit. The clock coupling has no diverging additive path normalization at the limiting center.

Probability.title: Second-order Wasserstein response for Lévy laws
Probability.summary: Weak perturbations of the same size can lead to terminal Wasserstein errors of different orders. For infinitely divisible laws smoothed by a Gaussian, we differentiate their distribution functions with respect to variance-weighted Lévy characteristics. This includes distributional directions caused by moving atoms. We obtain first- and second-order expansions that are uniform over Lipschitz test functions. When the first response is nonzero, Gaussian analyticity gives the signed second coefficient of the Wasserstein--1 distance. When the first response vanishes, a finite second displacement moment is enough to obtain a quadratic response. Its coefficient is strictly positive if the displacement dispersion is nonzero. For local balanced remeshing, the error is comparable to the grid-alignment variance. This gives sharp quadratic grid rates for compactly supported densities and nonaligned atomic sequences. We derive metric speed and length along admissible non-atomic curves, and use the response to build a linear program with a proved bound on how much its error exceeds the infimum over the allowed class and consistent quadrature. We also prove a sharp transition as smoothing vanishes and give a multivariate second-order expansion. The appendix gives state-dependent response formulas and further stability estimates.

Probability.title: With Leverage, the Gambler is Not the One Who Gets Ruined
Probability.summary: In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.

Probability.title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
Probability.summary: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $ν>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+ν+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.

Probability.title: $L^p_μ$-Normed Spaces of Bounded Multilinear Operator
Probability.summary: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators $\mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ endowed with $L^p_μ$-norms, where $X,Y$ are normed spaces and $μ$ is a measure with $p$-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for $p=2$; with iterated $γ$-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general $p$.

Probability.title: Anomalous scaling law for the two-dimensional Gaussian free field
Probability.summary: We consider level-set percolation for the Gaussian free field $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ regularised by a mass of order $N^{-2}$, and investigate the probability $θ_N(a)$ that the cluster of the origin in $\{\varphi \geq \sqrt{g_N} a\}$ reaches distance $N$ while remaining finite, where $g_N$ is the variance of $\varphi_0$. We prove a scaling law for $θ_N(a)$ which is quantitative simultaneously in $a$ and $N$. It asserts that $θ_N(a)=θ_ξ(a_*)(N/ξ)^{-\vartheta+o(1)}$ as $N/ξ\to\infty$, where the correlation length $ξ$ diverges exponentially as $a$ approaches the critical level $a_*$, the critical one-arm probability $θ_ξ(a_*)$ decays fractional-logarithmically, and the exponent $\vartheta$ is explicit and given by a variational problem involving the logarithmic energy. Thus $θ_N(a)$ crosses over from fractional logarithmic decay at and near criticality ($N\lesssimξ$) to polynomial decay away from it ($N\ggξ$), in stark contrast with dimension three and higher, where similar observables exhibit polynomial decay at and near criticality and rapid decay away from it. The proof relies on a coarse-graining scheme capturing a polynomial rate with sharp exponent, and on sharp logarithmic capacity estimates for planar "porous" sets.

Probability.title: The odometer in subcritical activated random walk
Probability.summary: We consider the activated random walk particle system, a model of self-organized criticality, on $\mathbb{Z}$ with i.i.d.-Bernoulli initial configuration. We show that at subcritical density, the system's odometer function, which counts the number of actions taken at each site, has a stretched exponential tail. It follows that the expected odometer at each site is finite.
Probability.comment: 12 pages; minor changes; final journal version

Probability.title: Monitoring for a Phase Transition in a Time Series of Wigner Matrices
Probability.summary: We develop methodology and theory for the detection of a phase transition in a time-series of high-dimensional random matrices. In the model we study, at each time point \( t = 1,2,\ldots \), we observe a deformed Wigner matrix \( \mathbf{M}_t \), where the unobservable deformation represents a latent signal. This signal is detectable only in the supercritical regime, and our objective is to detect the transition to this regime in real time, as new matrix--valued observations arrive. Our approach is based on a partial sum process of extremal eigenvalues of $\mathbf{M}_t$, and its theoretical analysis combines state-of-the-art tools from random-matrix-theory and Gaussian approximations. The resulting detector is self-normalized, which ensures appropriate scaling for convergence and a pivotal limit, without any additional parameter estimation. Simulations show excellent performance for varying dimensions. Applications to pollution monitoring and social interactions in primates illustrate the usefulness of our approach.

Probability.title: Sig-DEG for Distillation: Making Diffusion Models Faster and Lighter
Probability.summary: Diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art generative performance but remain computationally expensive at inference, often requiring many discretization steps. We propose Sig-DEG (Signature-based Differential Equation Generator), a generator for distilling pre-trained diffusion models. Inspired by high-order stochastic Taylor expansions, Sig-DEG combines partial signatures that summarize Brownian motion over subintervals with a recurrent structure to approximate stochastic differential equation solutions to achieve universality. We formulate distillation as supervised learning, matching fine-resolution teacher trajectories on a coarse time grid. At inference, Sig-DEG enables fast generation, as the partial signatures can be simulated exactly from their known distributions without requiring fine-grained Brownian paths. Experiments on image and time-series generation demonstrate competitive sample quality with inference speedups of up to several hundred times over the teacher. A Schrödinger bridge example further demonstrates Sig-DEG's applicability beyond diffusion distillation.
Probability.comment: 44 pages. Revised version with expanded theoretical analysis, updated experiments, and revised presentation

Probability.title: Complexity of flows with interactions and stochastic analysis
Probability.summary: We study stochastic flows with interaction through an infinite-dimensional semigroup approach. By means of a kernel lifting procedure, we represent the solution to measure-valued stochastic equation as a Hilbert-valued Markov process. We identify its generator, construct the associated Markov semigroup, and establish a dense range condition using measure polynomial functionals. The results provide a framework for the analysis of stability of stochastic equations with interaction.

Probability.title: On the discrete Fisher information
Probability.summary: We investigate a discrete analogue of the Fisher information. By using a discrete Laplacian operator, we can construct a discrete analogue of the score function and hence of the information. This provides a natural framework for establishing several information-theoretic inequalities in the discrete setting.

Probability.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
Probability.summary: Gaussian processes (GPs) are widely used across machine learning, spatial statistics, time-series analysis, optimization, Bayesian statistics, and scientific applications. A central component of a GP model is its kernel, which is typically specified through a parametric family. Among the most widely used choices is the radial basis function (RBF), also known as the squared exponential or Gaussian kernel, owing to its simple form, smoothness, and flexibility. In practice, the kernel parameters are routinely estimated by the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs), as implemented by standard GP software. Despite this widespread use, the asymptotic behavior of the MLEs remains poorly understood under fixed-domain asymptotics, even for the RBF kernel. The main difficulty arises from the increasingly strong dependence among densely sampled observations and the nonlinear dependence of the covariance matrix on the kernel parameters. In this paper, we address this gap by providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first complete asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE of the spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance under fixed-domain asymptotics. We establish consistency, derive convergence rates for all three parameters, prove joint asymptotic normality, and show that these rates are minimax optimal.

Probability.title: Rare Event Simulation of Quantum Error-Correcting Circuits
Probability.summary: We describe a practical approach for accessing the logical failure rates of quantum error-correcting (QEC) circuits under low physical (component) failure rate regimes. Standard Monte Carlo is often the de facto approach for studying the failure rates of quantum circuits. However, in the study of fault-tolerant error-correcting circuits, the ability to extend this approach to low physical failure rates is limited. In particular, the use of Monte Carlo to access circuits that are relatively large or have high correcting power becomes more difficult as we lower the input failure rates of the individual components (gates) in the circuit. For these reasons, many simulations studying the circuit model go no lower than end-to-end logical failure rates in the 10^{-6} regime. In this report, we outline an approach that borrows from earlier work by Bravyi and Vargo to the more complex circuit noise model. Earlier works studied both the capacity and phenomenological noise models, but the work is insufficient for generating similar simulations in the circuit-noise model. To the best of our knowledge, our team is the first to develop a full prescription of the rare event simulation by splitting technique for the circuit-based noise model. We have also generated promising results that are confirmed by standard Monte Carlo simulation under an accessible regime. This work shows that we can access noise in the circuit-model prescription of quantum error-correcting code to failure rates below 10^{-20} regime.
Probability.comment: Accepted on Sept 29, 2026 for publication in Quantum Journal; 15 pages, 15 figures; includes a new treatment of circuits with leakage noise and post-selection, added author contribution statement

Probability.title: On rigidity of infinite exchangeable sequences
Probability.summary: We ask when the law of an infinite exchangeable sequence is uniquely determined by a finite-dimensional marginal. For mixtures of a probability kernel, a weak localization condition makes three coordinates determine the directing law. Completeness alone makes four coordinates sufficient. Neither order can be lowered in general. For exponential kernels with a nonnegative sufficient statistic, a Müntz-Szász support condition implies three coordinates suffice. In the scalar case, this result is sharp. We also characterize when completeness holds simultaneously for all scalar mixing laws by a weighted Müntz density condition and show that statistic support alone need not decide completeness. These methods yield sharp finite-dimensional refinements of Freedman's theorem on rotatable sequences, namely that spherical symmetry of three coordinates makes an infinite exchangeable sequence rotatable while symmetry of the first two coordinates is in general insufficient. Finally, for energy-radial densities we give a complete-monotonicity criterion for infinite extendibility and determine the exact uniqueness thresholds for $\ell_q$-norm exponential laws.

Probability.title: Wong--Zakai Convergence and FNO Learning for Stochastic Volterra Equations
Probability.summary: This paper studies Wong--Zakai convergence and Fourier neural operator learning for stochastic Volterra integral equations (SVIEs) describing random systems with memory. A Wong--Zakai theorem establishes convergence of pathwise solutions driven by piecewise linear approximations of Brownian motion to the corresponding SVIE solution. This convergence provides a foundation for using mirror-padded Fourier neural operators to learn the solution operator mapping initial conditions and driving noise to entire solution trajectories. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive prediction accuracy and generalization to temporal grids finer than those used for training, while assessing the influence of padding and computational cost. As a follow-up to \citet{LKP:26}, this study extends their operator-learning framework to SVIEs through separate convergence and approximation analyses tailored to convolutional memory.

Probability.title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
Probability.summary: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,θ}μ$, $θ\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}μ$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $μ$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and Hölder images. First, $\dim_{qH}μ$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s\leq n$, $\dim_P^sμ=s$ if and only if $s\leq\dim_{qH}μ$. Second, we prove a lower bound for the profiles in terms of $\dim_Hμ$, $\dim_{P,θ}μ$ and the Assouad dimension of $\operatorname{supp}μ$, which improves the bound of Falconer and Mattila, the best previously known general lower bound for the packing dimension of projected measures. The improvement is strict whenever $\dim_Hμ<\dim_Pμ$ and $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)<n$, and when $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)=n$ it occurs exactly when $\dim_{P,θ}μ$ exceeds an explicit universal lower bound for some $θ$ in an explicit range. We present examples of measures with $\dim_Hμ<\dim_Pμ<\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)=n$ for which our bound gives the exact value $\dim_Pμ_V=\min\{\dim_Pμ,m\}$ for almost every $m$-dimensional subspace $V$, whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random $α$-Hölder maps $f_ω:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, we prove that, for compactly supported $μ$, $\dim_Pμ_{f_ω}=m$ almost surely if and only if $αm\leq\dim_{qH}μ$, and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if $\dim_{qH}μ=\dim_Pμ$. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.
Probability.comment: This manuscript supersedes and substantially extends the results presented in arXiv:2604.18222 and arXiv:2609.11301. It incorporates all the main results of both preprints into a unified and more comprehensive treatment, providing further developments and a deeper analysis

Differential Geometry.title: Exterior free-boundary minimal surfaces of every topological type with at least two ends
Differential Geometry.summary:
An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface in the complement of the open unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. We prove that for all integers $\ell\geq2$, $b\geq1$ and $γ\geq0$ there is a connected, orientable, properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with $\ell$ ends, $b$ boundary components and genus $γ$. Its total curvature is finite, and its ends are parallel catenoidal ends of multiplicity one. By the theorem of Mazet and Mendes, a surface of this kind with one end is a rotational annulus. Hence the topological types of such embedded surfaces are exactly the annulus with one end and all types with at least two ends.
  There are two gluing constructions. For $\ell\geq3$ we stack $\ell$ sheets over a stable catenoidal annulus that meets the sphere along a circle of radius $4/5$, and we join adjacent sheets by half-catenoidal bridges sitting on the sphere. The sheets are small normal graphs over this annulus whose displacements contain different multiples of the Jacobi field of the family of such annuli, so their boundary circles and the logarithmic growth of their ends differ slightly. For $\ell=2$ we double a catenoidal annulus near the critical angle $π/4$, where it acquires a bounded rotationally invariant Jacobi field; the distance to the critical annulus is coupled to the size of the bridges. In gluing constructions inside the unit ball that double or stack a compact surface, the bridges themselves must balance the sheets, which forces many bridges. Here the logarithmic growth of the ends absorbs this balancing. A fixed number of bridges therefore suffices, and every topological type is reached, including the small ones.
Differential Geometry.comment: 39 pages, 4 figures. Interactive versions of the figures and Surface Evolver approximations: https://surfaces.igorkozyrev.com

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp Yamabe Bounds for Spherical Three-Space Forms via Four-Dimensional Poincaré--Einstein Compactness
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $Γ<SO(4)$ be a nontrivial finite group acting freely on $S^3$, and let $M=S^3/Γ$. We prove that every smooth conformal class $C$ on $M$ satisfies \[ Y(M,C)\le |Γ|^{-2/3}Y(S^3), \] with equality for the quotient-round conformal class. Consequently, \[ σ(M)=|Γ|^{-2/3}Y(S^3). \]
  Our approach uses four-dimensional Poincaré--Einstein fillings of the ball. We first establish compactness for fillings whose conformal infinities range over a compact family of positive-scalar-curvature metrics. Since compactness alone does not guarantee continuation through degenerate Einstein metrics, we use equivariant Fredholm parity to obtain a filling with the prescribed boundary conformal class and group action. A common interior fixed point then makes the Li--Qing--Shi boundary test function invariant, and its descent to $M$ gives the sharp covering factor.

Differential Geometry.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product Kähler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $ψ=Bz$ and $φ=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.

Differential Geometry.title: Conformal hyperbolic distances and holonomies of Anosov diffeomorphisms
Differential Geometry.summary: We use conformal hyperbolic distances to analyze the stable/unstable holonomies of Anosov diffeomorphisms. The main result is that the lengths of the stable/unstable curves in a conformal hyperbolic distance are preserved by the stable/unstable holonomies, whenever they are well-defined. In particular, the existence of a conformal hyperbolic distance with well-defined length of stable/unstable curves ensures that the holonomies are globally defined. We exhibit a conformal hyperbolic distance with well-defined length of stable/unstable curves for each real Anosov diffeomorphism, which are Anosov diffeomorphisms with a one-dimensional finest dominated splitting where contraction/expansion in each space is constant along orbits.

Differential Geometry.title: Smooth approximation, Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities and curvature flows for h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
Differential Geometry.summary:
We associate each h-convex body in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}(n\geq 2)$ with a Radon measure valued $(0,2)$-tensor on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ through its horospherical function. Using spherical convolution, we prove that any h-convex body can be approximated by a sequence of smooth strictly h-convex bodies in the Hausdorff sense. This approximation result extends the inequality parts of the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality to general h-convex bodies, but equality rigidity cannot be obtained directly. We prove that the equality holds in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality if and only if the h-convex bodies are geodesic balls. For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which implies the equality rigidity of the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. For the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we introduce a class of globally constrained $k$-th modified quermassintegrals preserving flows with general h-convex initial hypersurfaces to obtain the equality rigidity. Moreover, we prove the flows above preserve h-convexity, make the $(k+1)$-th modified quermassintegrals non-increasing and converge to geodesic spheres.
  We prove a rigidity theorem for modified area measures for h-convex bodies and use this rigidity theorem to characterize the geodesic balls via modified support measures for h-convex bodies, from which we prove that the $(k+1)$-th modified quermassintegrals strictly decrease in a short time along the flows with non-spherical initial hypersurfaces. Then we obtain the equality rigidity of the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.

Differential Geometry.title: A classification result for eternal mean convex flows of finite total curvature type
Differential Geometry.summary: In this article we partially classify the space of eternal mean convex flows in $\mathbb{R}^3$ of finite total curvature type, a condition implied by finite total curvature. In particular we show that topologically nonplanar ones must flow out of a catenoid in a natural sense.
Differential Geometry.comment: Further revisions made (including several new figures). To appear in Ann. Global Anal. Geom

Differential Geometry.title: Generalized minimizers for the capillarity energy outside convex obstacles
Differential Geometry.summary: In general, the capillarity energy outside an unbounded obstacle may fail to admit volume-constrained minimizers, as infimizing sequences may escape to infinity. We study this minimization problem outside a closed convex obstacle $C$. Via a $Γ$-convergence result for the capillarity energies outside sequences of closed convex obstacles converging in the Hausdorff sense, we prove that the infimum of the functional is attained by a generalized minimizer, namely, a finite union of regions, each of which minimizes the capillarity energy outside a limit of translations of $C$ in its volume class, with the total volume satisfying the prescribed constraint. Each generalized minimizer can be suitably approximated by an infimizing sequence, thus providing a description of its asymptotic behaviour. As an application, we study the isoperimetric profile associated with the capillarity energy and investigate how the asymptotic geometry of the obstacle affects both this profile and generalized minimizers and their connectedness.

Differential Geometry.title: Odd-dimensional lens-space Yamabe counterexamples
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $n\ge5$ be odd and let \(L_{3q}^n=S^n/C_{3q}\) be the standard lens space, where $q>3$ is prime. We prove that for all sufficiently large $q$, \[ σ(L_{3q}^n) >
(3q)^{-2/n}Y(S^n)=Y(L_{3q}^n,[g_{\rm rd}]). \] Here \([g_{\rm rd}]\) denotes the quotient-round conformal class. Combining spin bordism with the surgery theorem of Ammann--Dahl--Humbert, we establish \[ σ(L_{3q}^n)\ge \min \{q^{-2/n}Y(S^n),Λ_n\}, \] where $Λ_n>0$ depends only on $n$. For sufficiently large $q$, this exceeds the quotient-round value, showing that the quotient-round conformal class need not maximize the smooth Yamabe invariant in any odd dimension $n\ge5$.

Differential Geometry.title: C'est un petit val qui mousse de fonctions
Differential Geometry.summary: Easy lowering local minima, after introducing valley functions on smooth manifolds gives, without gluing technicities, "M. Morse's lemma's" canonical form, moving critical values and eliminating pair of critical points theorems, reducing the last to its one dimensional case.

Differential Geometry.title: Generic boundary behavior of Dirichlet eigenfunctions
Differential Geometry.summary: We extend Uhlenbeck's classical results on the generic properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions. In particular, we find a residual set of $C^k$ domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $k > n$, such that the nodal set of any Dirichlet eigenfunction intersects the boundary orthogonally along a $C^{k-1}$ embedded submanifold, whenever the intersection is non-empty. This is achieved by analyzing the boundary asymptotics of Dirichlet eigenfunctions via homogeneous harmonic polynomials and comparing their respective nodal sets. Along the way, we give a complete proof that generic Euclidean domains have simple Dirichlet eigenfunctions with zero as a regular value in the interior and zero as a regular value of the boundary normal derivative. In the special case of planar domains, a different argument provides one-parameter families of perturbed domains with the desired properties.

Differential Geometry.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.

Differential Geometry.title: Godbillon-Vey classes of Lie subalgebroids
Differential Geometry.summary: The Godbillon--Vey class is a secondary characteristic class which is defined for regular foliations and has been studied extensively. In this paper, we fix a Lie algebroid and relatively define the Godbillon--Vey class for its Lie subalgebroids, and study their properties. We also present several examples.

Differential Geometry.title: Heat Kernel and Resurgence
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the resurgent structure of short--time heat kernel asymptotics from the viewpoint of Picard--Lefschetz theory. For a real analytic Riemannian manifold, we show the heat kernel admits a 1-- Gevrey small--time expansion whose Borel transform detects complex--geometric data beyond the real geodesic sector. We formulate an infinite--dimensional Picard--Lefschetz problem of Morse--Floer type for the holomorphic energy functional on the complexified path space, and propose a heat--kernel analogue of the Picard--Lefschetz/Alien correspondence. In this framework, pointed alien operators acting on the asymptotic expansion associated with the real geodesic are predicted to produce the formal heat--kernel sectors associated with other holomorphic geodesics, with coefficients given by signed counts of connecting trajectories of the Morse flow. We perform a confirming test of this proposal on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}_{\R}^2$.

Differential Geometry.title: A sharp pinching theorem for closed minimal Legendrian submanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $F:M^n\to\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$ be a minimal Legendrian immersion of a connected closed manifold, where $n\ge3$, and let $B$ be its second fundamental form. We prove that if $|B|^2\le(n-1)(n+2)/n$, then, up to a unitary transformation, $F$ parametrizes a totally geodesic sphere or is a finite covering of the image of the minimal Calabi product of a point and a totally geodesic Legendrian sphere. This proves Conjecture 1 of Luo and Sun [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré C Anal. Non Linéaire 40 (2023), p. 548].

Differential Geometry.title: Codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphisms
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected complex manifold is biholomorphically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of a complex torus. This verifies a conjecture of Ghys in the codimension-one case and, in particular, in complex dimension three.
Differential Geometry.comment: Added a declaration of AI use, a statement on proof formalisation, and acknowledgements. 19 pages

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$. The original proof used the amenability of the images of sufficiently small local fundamental groups. Since that work was written, Kapovitch and Wilking proved Gromov's generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Their theorem gives the stronger conclusion that these local groups are uniformly virtually nilpotent. We explain how their result supplies a direct modern input for the bounded Betti number theorem. We also discuss the topological meaning of the bounded part of ordinary cohomology and its relation to the $\ell^1$-seminorm on homology.

Differential Geometry.title: Linking numbers and special differential characters in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct non-holomorphic Siegel modular forms whose coefficients encode linking numbers in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds of simplest type. Our proofs rely on an improved understanding of the transgression forms appearing in Kudla--Millson theory, and along the way we establish some structural properties including in particular their expected current equations.

Differential Geometry.title: Comparison between renormalized volume and area in the Weil--Petersson topology
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the renormalized volume between the two Epstein surfaces associated with a Weil--Petersson quasicircle is continuous with respect to the Weil--Petersson topology. As a consequence, we establish that the universal Liouville action is proportional to this renormalized volume for every Weil--Petersson quasicircle. We then establish an inequality relating this renormalized volume to the renormalized area introduced by Alexakis--Mazzeo. To this end, we compare both quantities with the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the associated Grunsky operator, which can be expressed in terms of a nonlocal Lagrangian introduced by O'Hara--Solanes.
Differential Geometry.comment: 31 pages. v2: added a comparison between the renormalized area of minimal surfaces and renormalized volume between Epstein surfaces

Differential Geometry.title: A geometric rigidity estimate for codimension-1 immersions into spheres
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a quantitative stability estimate for codimension-one immersions into a round sphere. Let $(M,g)$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold and suppose that a prescribed shape operator is realised by a smooth isometric immersion $θ:(M,g)\to\mathbb S^{n+1}$. We prove that, on every relatively compact strongly Lipschitz domain and for every $1<p<\infty$, any Sobolev immersion $φ$ is close to $θ$ modulo an ambient rotation, with the $W^{1,p}$-distances between both the immersions and their Gauss maps controlled by the $L^p$ stretching-plus-bending energies of $φ$. No {\it a priori} bounds on the fundamental forms of $φ$ are required. The proof proceeds by extending the immersions along normal geodesics and reducing the problem to an equidimensional geometric rigidity estimate on the sphere. A finite localisation and patching argument handles the possible non-injectivity of the normal extension of the reference immersion.
Differential Geometry.comment: 13 pages; V2 added AI declaration which was originally omitted by mistake

Differential Geometry.title: Nahm-Kirchhoff Moduli Spaces, Hyperkähler Quotient and 2D Field theories
Differential Geometry.summary: To an oriented quiver with boundary $Γ$ and a compact connected Lie group $G$ we associate a Nahm-Kirchhoff moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{H}}(Γ)$: solutions of Nahm's equations on the edges with Kirchhoff matching at interior vertices, modulo boundary-trivial gauge transformations. For connected $Γ$, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{H}}(Γ)$ is a smooth manifold of dimension $4(|E|-|Γ_{\mathrm{int}}|)\dim G$ with a hyperkähler structure arising as an infinite-dimensional hyperkähler quotient. Via a Kempf-Ness argument on the Cartan-Hadamard manifold $G_{\mathbb{C}}/G$, we prove a quiver analogue of Donaldson's theorem identifying it with the complex-symplectic quotient $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}(Γ)$ of the complex Nahm equations by the complexified gauge group. This quotient is independent of edge lengths and isomorphic to a finite-dimensional complex-symplectic quotient of $(T^*G_{\mathbb{C}})^E$, while the hyperkähler metric depends on them: uniform rescaling acts by a homothety, and the transported metrics genuinely vary. By cutting and gluing, $Γ\mapsto\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}(Γ)$ is a 2D TQFT valued in complex Hamiltonian manifolds, à la Moore-Tachikawa, whereas the hyperkähler refinement is not functorial on $\mathbf{Cob}_2$: spines of a cylinder with different lengths give non-isomorphic spaces. Retaining lengths, these spaces form a metric field theory, a functor of non-unital monoidal categories from metric cobordisms to hyperkähler manifolds composed by hyperkähler reduction; over each cone of $M_{g,n}^{\mathrm{trop}}$ they give a family with fixed complex-symplectic fibre and varying metric. Finally, harmonic gauge representatives converge as an internal edge collapses, and on a long edge with regular semisimple Higgs field the Kempf-Ness minimizer is exponentially confined near its centralizer; the limiting metrics are left open.

Differential Geometry.title: Counterexamples to prescribed scalar curvature in the null case
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct smooth functions on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{n\ge5}$ that change sign and have negative mean but cannot be realized as the scalar curvature of any metric in the given conformal class.

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature measures and volume preserving flows in h-convex geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we introduce a concept of modified curvature measures for h-convex domains in hyperbolic space and prove a shifted version of the generalized Alexandrov theorem, which characterizes geodesic balls in hyperbolic space via modified curvature measures. This result generalizes the classical work of Kohlmann (1998). We further investigate a volume-preserving shifted $α$-Gauss curvature flow for strictly h-convex hypersurfaces in hyperbolic space and prove that for any $α>0$ the solution exists for all time and converges smoothly to a geodesic sphere. The theory of modified curvature measures developed in the first part serves as a key ingredient in characterizing the Hausdorff limit shape of the flow.
Differential Geometry.comment: 37 pages. The paper was submitted on May 14, 2026

Differential Geometry.title: Scalar curvature rigidity of small spherical caps with arbitrary fill-ins
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove an analogue of Min-Oo's conjecture for sufficiently small spherical caps in the unit round sphere. For every dimension $n\ge3$, there exists $r_*(n)>0$ such that the following holds for every round cap of radius $0<r\le r_*(n)$: any smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian fill-in with the same intrinsic boundary metric and with scalar curvature and outward boundary mean curvature at least those of the cap is isometric to the cap.

Differential Geometry.title: Derived deformation theory of heterotic $G_2$ systems near the standard embedding
Differential Geometry.summary:
We study heterotic $G_2$ structures near a torsion-free standard embedding, to first order in $α'$ and to all orders in formal deformations. The tangent connection is the Hull connection determined by the metric and flux. We construct a locally invertible family of differential operators relating the supersymmetry and instanton $BPS$ equations to the Euler-Lagrange equations of the heterotic superpotential.
  Using this comparison and the physical gauge symmetries, we construct a homological vector field locally formally conjugate to the Hamiltonian vector field of the superpotential. On a closed manifold in the fixed gerbe sector, the torsion equation implies vanishing of the leading flux. We prove ellipticity of the linearized deformation complex with mixed differential-order weights and construct a finite-dimensional cyclic $L_\infty$ model with a formal effective potential.
Differential Geometry.comment: 44 pages. Major v2 revision: recognising the redundancy of the leading-flux condition led to a substantially simpler and shorter construction

Differential Geometry.title: Pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for complete Ricci flows
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove a uniform pseudolocality theorem for smooth complete Ricci flows whose initial metrics have Ricci curvature bounded below and uniformly positive injectivity radius. No a priori curvature bound is assumed on the flow. As a consequence, we obtain strong uniqueness for smooth complete Ricci flows from a complete metric with the above geometric bounds. We also prove that every smooth complete Ricci flow from a complete Ricci-flat metric with uniformly positive injectivity radius is stationary. The same conclusion holds for any complete flat initial metric. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to Chen's question on the strong uniqueness of Ricci flow from Euclidean space in every dimension.
Differential Geometry.comment: 37 pages. The main ideas of the proofs in this paper are due to ChatGPT-6 Astra. The paper is written all by the authors after they absorb the ideas from AI and interact with AI. The authors take full responsibility for the final content of this paper. All comments are welcome

Differential Geometry.title: A diameter gap for irreducible compact symmetric spaces of fixed rank
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that, for every positive integer $r$, the positive normalized diameters of isometric quotients of simply connected irreducible compact Riemannian symmetric spaces of rank $r$ have a uniform positive lower bound. The bound is independent of the dimension and of the acting group, which need not be connected. For the higher-dimensional Grassmannian families, we obtain an explicit bound for positive-dimensional acting groups by constructing nonconstant invariant functions of bounded trigonometric degree. The real and complex cases use moment maps. The quaternionic case follows from a quartic rigidity theorem proved by means of invariant four-forms and the classification of compact quaternionic symmetric spaces. We also give examples showing why the rank and the relative scales of product factors must be controlled.

Differential Geometry.title: Connectedness properties of small minimal clusters in Riemannian or Finsler manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that in a compact Riemannian manifold, the $m$-minimal clusters of sufficiently small total volume are connected and with small diameter, while in a more general Finsler manifold they are done by at most $m$ connected components of small diameter. We apply these results to calculate the asymptotic expansion of the multi-isoperimetric profile at the first nontrivial order, for small volumes.
Differential Geometry.comment: In this second version of the paper we have improved the introduction to be more clear. The mathematics and the proofs have not been changed

Differential Geometry.title: A topological sphere theorem for pinched Legendrian submanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $M^n$ be a closed simply connected Legendrian submanifold of $\mathbb S^{2n+1}$, where $n\geq5$, and let $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{H}=\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{B}$ denote its second fundamental form and mean-curvature vector. We prove that $M$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb S^n$ if \begin{equation*} |\mathbf{B}|^2\leq \frac{(n-1)(n+2)}n+\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|^2-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|\sqrt{|\mathbf{H}|^2+4n}. \end{equation*} The equality can be attained by the Calabi products, so simple connectivity cannot be omitted. For $n\geq4$, we also prove a sphere theorem under an explicit bound and the weaker assumption $b_1(M;\mathbb R)=0$. The proof combines phase-rotated Lawson--Simons variations with a systolic inequality for finite two-complexes. We also give local constructions showing that the pinching condition allows negative isotropic curvature at a point.

Differential Geometry.title: Cohomogeneity-One Ruled Hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and $\mathbb{C}H^2$
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we show how to construct a special class of ruled hypersurfaces in the nonflat complex space forms $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{C}H^n$. This is done by taking an arbitrary smooth curve in a totally geodesic (complex) one-dimensional submanifold and erecting an orthogonal ruling over each of its points. Concentrating on the $n=2$ case, we also examine the special situation in which the base curve has constant geodesic curvature. We show that, in this case, the construction yields precisely the real-analytic hypersurfaces of cohomogeneity one that satisfy a certain transversality condition.
Differential Geometry.comment: 28 pages; revised version, with corrections to main theorems; published in Differential Geometry and its Applications

Differential Geometry.title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. These provide infinite family of Einstein metrics on closed $4$-manifolds with $λ>0$, which are in addition not Hermitian. We further establish the uniqueness of the $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics on $S^4$, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and CP^2#\bar{CP}^2.

Differential Geometry.title: Nonlinear Lebesgue spaces: Curves and geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper is the second in a series by the author and collaborators devoted to the study of geometric and analytic properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces, that is, L^p spaces of mappings taking values in arbitrary metric spaces. The present article formalizes the pointwise description of their geometric properties---their length structure, bounds on their Alexandrov curvature as well as the definition of a velocity for absolutely continuous curves despite the lack of differential structure. To obtain this pointwise description, we first prove a nonlinear analogue of the Fubini--Lebesgue theorem, which yields an identification of L^p curves in nonlinear Lebesgue spaces with mappings taking values in the space of L^p curves. This identification of L^p curves then enables a similar identification for absolutely continuous curves, from which the pointwise description of the geometric properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces follows.

Differential Geometry.title: Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every tangent flow at the first singular time of a smooth, closed, embedded mean curvature flow has smooth support, provided that the total curvature satisfies $\sup_{t\in[0,T)}\int_{M_t}|A|^n\,dμ_t<\infty$. This extends Ilmanen's smoothness result for tangent flows to higher dimensions.

Differential Geometry.title: Tournaments, flags, and spinors
Differential Geometry.summary: It is observed that the dimension of the space of invariant spinors on the manifold $\mathrm{SU}(n)/T^{n-1}$ of full flags in $\mathbb{C}^n$ equals the number $\mathrm{RT}(n)$ of labelled regular tournaments of order $n$, for $n$ odd. This space is decomposed under a double cover of the Weyl group, and realized as a pair of eigenspaces, first for the Dirac operator, then for a twisted version of it which acts equivariantly; this is used to show that multiplicities of irreducible representations are even for $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$.

Differential Geometry.title: Nonexistence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue near the round sphere in low dimensions
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider the problem of minimizing the second conformal eigenvalue of the conformal Laplacian in a conformal class of metrics with renormalized volume. We prove, in dimensions $n\in\left\{3,\dotsc,10\right\}$, that a minimizer for this problem does not exist for metrics sufficiently close to the round metric on the sphere. This is in striking contrast with the situation in dimensions $n \ge 11$, where Ammann and Humbert obtained the existence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue on any smooth closed non-locally conformally flat manifold. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also obtain a lower bound on the energy of sign-changing solutions of the \nobreak Yamabe equation in dimensions 3, 4 and 5, which extends a result obtained by Weth in the case of the round sphere.
Differential Geometry.comment: Final version to appear in Journal of Differential Geometry. Some details have been added following the recommendations of the anonymous referees

Differential Geometry.title: Equivariant analytic torsion forms
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we first construct infinitesimal equivariant analytic torsion forms for Kähler fibrations. We then compare them with Ma's equivariant analytic torsion forms, modulo $\partial$- and $\overline{\partial}$-exact forms, in terms of equivariant Bott--Chern currents and the $I$-genus. Our comparison formula extends that of Bismut and Goette to families.

Differential Geometry.title: A stationary harmonic map with a nonstationary tangent map
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a stationary weakly harmonic map from a domain in \R^5 into a compact Kähler surface for which a tangent map is weakly harmonic but nonstationary. The target manifold is the blow-up of \CP^1\times\CP^1 at four points lying in one fiber and arranged at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. The nonstationarity of the tangent map arises from the break down of the tetrahedral symmetry in the defect measure concentrated on the vertices.

Differential Geometry.title: Metaplectic-c prequantizations and the Einstein--Brillouin--Keller quantizability condition
