Differential Geometry.summary: We show that every symplectic manifold admits a symplectic form whose metaplectic-c prequantizations give quantizability conditions on all its Lagrangian submanifolds. Metaplectic-c prequantizations descend to prequantizations over the Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle that are fibrewise flat with holonomies primitive fourth roots of unity on the generators of the fundamental groups. This fibrewise holonomy is consistently interpreted as that of both Leray two-orientations and normalized Blattner--Kostant--Sternberg half-forms. The prequantizations pull back to flat circle bundles on each Lagrangian submanifold whose holonomy character defines a quantizability condition. The first and second Stiefel--Whitney classes are identified as splitting obstructions to the Lagrangianwise holonomies. These holonomies split into a product of holonomies on any orientable Lagrangian submanifold, and split consistently for all Lagrangian submanifolds of a manifold with metaplectic structure. When the first Chern class vanishes, the holonomy splits into the Bohr--Sommerfeld factor and a quarter phase Maslov correction, recovering the classical Einstein--Brillouin--Keller condition. We develop the underlying obstruction theory for circle extensions associated to general Lie group double coverings with first hypercohomology groupoids.

Differential Geometry.title: Existence and uniqueness of conformal Gauduchon metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove that every Hermitian conformal class on a connected noncompact complex manifold of dimension at least two contains a Gauduchon metric. We give a sufficient condition for uniqueness of such Gauduchon metrics up to scaling in terms of functions bounded from above and their Levi forms. This condition is necessary when the manifold has at least two ends. In that case, uniqueness in a fixed conformal class is equivalent to the assertion that every positive solution of the complex Laplace equation for a metric in that class is constant. For a connected noncompact complex Lie group of dimension $n$, uniqueness in every conformal class is equivalent to the assertion that, for every Hermitian metric, every positive solution of the complex Laplace equation is constant. These properties hold exactly when the complex tangent space of a maximal compact subgroup has dimension $n-1$; such a group is abelian. In a conformal class containing a balanced metric, the same equivalence holds without a restriction on the number of ends. We also prove uniqueness for manifolds with a suitable potential on a compactification with compact fibers over a point, the real line, or a parabolic Riemann surface. The examples include compact pluripolar deletions, partially deleted compact fibers, and semipositive line bundles. We construct conformal Gauduchon metrics which are not related by scaling on Stein manifolds and on the total space of $\mathcal O_{\PP^1}(1)^{\oplus2}$.

Differential Geometry.title: Conformal Killing--Yano Ricci solitons: Structure, compatibility, and rigidity
Differential Geometry.summary: We introduce a geometric structure -- a conformal Killing--Yano Ricci soliton (CKY--RS) -- that couples conformal Ricci soliton (CRS) geometry to conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) 2--forms. The soliton field of the CRS geometry is given by the divergence of the CKY 2--form. We introduce a conserved CKY--Cotton current and derive a compatibility identity relating the Cotton tensor, the CRS obstruction tensor, and the CKY 2--form. In 4--dimensional Lorentzian signature, we show that, under non-degeneracy and closedness assumptions on the CKY form, a CKY--RS structure forces the conformal representative to be locally Kerr--NUT--(A)dS. For a closed non-degenerate CKY on a Kerr--NUT--(A)dS background, the conformal deformation is necessarily trivial. For Einstein backgrounds of arbitrary dimension and signature, the conformal factor satisfies an eigenvalue equation and an Obata--type Hessian equation. If the background is also compact or a CKY orbit is periodic, the conformal factor is an invariant of the CKY--flow and we obtain simple spectral obstructions to non-trivial CKY--RS structures. From the Hessian equation, we obtain obstruction and classification results for the non-trivial conformal sector, including product/Brinkmann geometries and a Weyl--aligned branch. Finally, we give explicit constructions for static spherically symmetric geometries and BTZ backgrounds, including a CKY--RS realization with a time-dependent conformally flat representative. These results provide a geometric framework for studying CRS with hidden symmetry structure, with potential applications to exact geometries in general relativity.

Differential Geometry.title: Hyperquiver varieties
Differential Geometry.summary: We discuss the recently introduced concept of hyperquivers, due to Muller, Nanda, and Seigal, from the point of view of Kähler and hyperkähler quotients. In particular, we show that the Kähler hyperquiver variety ${\mathcal M}$, corresponding to a hyperquiver with a single hyperedge, is a projective variety isomorphic to the geometric quotient of the space of tensors with maximal multilinear rank. Moreover, the hyperkähler hyperquiver variety corresponding to doubling of this hyperquiver can be identified with the linear scheme corresponding to the sheaf of reflexive $1$-forms on ${\mathcal M}$.
Differential Geometry.comment: 6 pages; v.2 - corrected the example in §3

Differential Geometry.title: Constant Rank Theorems under Intermediate Ricci Curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove two constant rank theorems for the Ricci tensor in two geometric settings: manifolds with harmonic curvature and gradient Ricci solitons. In both cases, if the $k$-intermediate Ricci curvature satisfies $\Ric_k\geq0$ for some $1\leq k\leq n-2$, then the Ricci tensor has constant rank and its nullity distribution is parallel. In the complete case, the universal cover splits isometrically along the Ricci-null directions. We also show that the range $1\leq k\leq n-2$ is sharp: in every dimension $n\geq4$, nonnegative Ricci curvature alone does not imply the constant rank property in either setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Higher localised $\widehat{A}$-genera: a note on disconnected fixed-point sets
Differential Geometry.summary: For a proper cocompact action of a finitely generated discrete group $Γ$ on a spin manifold $M$, the higher localised $\widehat{A}$-genera $\widehat{A}_g(M,ω)$ introduced earlier by the author and Mathai were shown to be an obstruction to $Γ$-invariant metrics of positive scalar curvature, for $ω$ arising from the subring of $H^*(\underline{B}Γ,\mathbb{R})$ generated by elements of degree at most $2$, under the assumptions that the fixed-point set $M^g$ is connected and that $g$ is regular with respect to a certain real group $2$-cocycle. We show that both assumptions can be dropped.
Differential Geometry.comment: Small correction in new version. 9 pages

Differential Geometry.title: A Geometric Interpretation of Generalized Hurwitz--Radon Numbers Defined by Kannaka--Tojo
Differential Geometry.summary:
The Hurwitz--Radon number originates in the composition problem of quadratic forms and is related to the maximum number of pointwise linearly independent vector fields on spheres. Kannaka--Tojo [arXiv:2602.04544] reformulated the Hurwitz--Radon number in the setting of a real reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ and its faithful representation $ι$, and introduced two natural numbers $ρ^{(1)}(\mathfrak g,ι)$ and $ρ^{(2)}(\mathfrak g,ι)$. For classical Lie algebras and their standard representations, these two numbers coincide except for a few cases.
  In this paper, fixing a Lie group $G$ and a subspace $\mathfrak{s} $ of $ \mathfrak g = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$ , we define natural numbers $ρ_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,σ)$ and $ρ^{\pm}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,σ,
abla)$ for a $G$-manifold $(M,σ)$ equipped with an affine connection $
abla$. These are defined in terms of fundamental vector fields on $M$. In a special case, we show that $ρ_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,σ)$ coincides with $ρ^{(2)}(\mathfrak g,ι)$, and that $ρ^{-}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,σ,
abla)$ coincides with $ρ^{(1)}(\mathfrak g,ι)$. Furthermore, we show that $ρ^{+}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,σ,
abla)$ is related to Clifford structures on $M$.

Differential Geometry.title: On the existence problem for a double mean field equation and its application to prescribed curvature problems
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemann surface with smooth boundary $\partial M$. Let $K(x)>0$, $h(x)> 0$ or $h(x)\equiv 0$ be two smooth functions on $M$ and $\partial M$ respectively. In this paper, we consider the following double mean field type equation with a nonlinear Neumann boundary condition related to a prescribed curvature problem \begin{equation}\label{equation:01}
  \begin{cases}
  \displaystyle
  -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|}
  =2ρ\frac{Ke^u}{\int_MKe^u\,dv_g},
  & \text{in }M,\\[1.2em]
  \displaystyle
  \partial_νu
  =2ρ'\frac{he^{u/2}}{\int_{\partial M}he^{u/2}\,ds_g},
  & \text{on }\partial M,
  \end{cases}
  \end{equation} where $ρ> 0,\ ρ'\geq 0$ and $ρ+ρ'=2π$, $ν$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial M$. When $h\equiv 0$, the second equation changes to $\partial_νu=0$ on $\partial M$. By introducing a boundary integration constant, we obtain a sufficient condition under which \eqref{equation:01} admits a solution.
  As a geometric application, we solve the prescribed curvature equation for both the Gauss curvature and the geodesic curvature in the case that $M$ is topologically a disk. When $(M,g)$ is the standard hemisphere $\mathbb S^2_+$, let $p\in \partial \mathbb S^2_+$ be a maximum point of $$
  Φ(q)=h(q)+\sqrt{h(q)^2+K(q)},
  \qquad q\in\partial \mathbb S^2_+.
  $$ Suppose
  \begin{equation*}
  K_ν(p)+2Φ(p)(-Δ_{\partial \mathbb S^2_+})^{1/2}h(p)<0.
  \end{equation*} Then the prescribed curvature problem \begin{align*}
  -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|}=2Ke^u,
  \text{in }\mathbb S^2_+,\ \
  \partial_νu=2he^{u/2},
  \text{on }\partial \mathbb S^2_+.
  \end{align*} admits a smooth solution.

Differential Geometry.title: Scalar Curvature in Dimension 4
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every locally conformally flat metric on a closed, oriented hyperbolic $4$-manifold with scalar curvature bounded below by $-12$ satisfies Schoen's conjecture. We also classify all closed, oriented Riemannian $4$-manifolds of positive scalar curvature that arise as total spaces of fiber bundles whose fiber and base are connected and have positive dimension and whose base is orientable. For a closed, locally conformally flat, scalar-flat manifold $(M^4,g)$ with $π_2(M^4) \neq 0$, we show that the universal Riemannian cover $(\widetilde{M},\tilde{g})$ is homothetic to the standard product $\mathbb{H}^2 \times S^2$. This affirmatively answers a question of M.~H.~Noronha.
Differential Geometry.comment: Corrected typos and grammatical errors; updated references; submitted

Differential Geometry.title: Long-Time Behavior of the $α$-Ricci Flow on the 2-Torus
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the $α$-Ricci flow $(g(t),α(t))$, which is a Ricci flow coupled with a harmonic 1-form heat flow, on the 2-torus $M$. We prove global existence for this flow as well as a Type III curvature estimate. The long-time behavior of the $α$-Ricci flow depends on the cohomology class $[α] \in H^1(M,\mathbb{R})$, which is invariant under the flow. If $[α]$ is rational, then as $t\to\infty$, $(M,t^{-1}g(t))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to $S^1$ with length $\ell([α])/\sqrt 2$ where $\ell([α])$ is the primitive length of $[α]$. On the universal cover, the rescaled flow $(s^{-1}\tilde g(st),\tildeα(st))$ smoothly converges to an expander $(g^*(t),α^*(t))$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ as $s\to \infty$ where $α^*(t)$ is nonzero and constant in spacetime and $g^*(t)$ is flat and expanding in the $α^*$ direction. If $[α]$ is irrational, then there is a sequence $s_i\to\infty$ such that $(M,s_i^{-1}g(s_it))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to a point. Moreover, on the universal cover, $(s_i^{-1}\tilde g(s_it),\tildeα(s_it))$ smoothly converges to $(g^*(t),α^*(t))$.

Differential Geometry.title: Existence of exhaustions with controlled sign of mean curvature in noncompact manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Given a complete and non-compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\le n\le 7$, we find conditions for the existence of compact exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ such that all boundaries $\partial U_i$ have the same sign of mean curvature. In particular, we show that in these dimensions, a manifold with one end satisfying a no tentacle condition always has a weakly mean convex, weakly mean concave, or minimal exhaustion, according to the behaviour of the area profile of separating hypersurfaces. This is a version of a result sketched by Gromov, under a condition which is weaker than his thickness at infinity. In more general situations, we study the existence of exhaustions which are weakly mean concave or weakly mean convex apart from an arbitrarily small $L^1$ error. That is, we find sufficient conditions for the existence of exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ which satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}H^+\to0$, $\int_{\partial U_i}H^-\to0$, or $\int_{\partial U_i}|H|\to0$, where $H^-$, $H^+$, and $|H|$ are the negative part, positive part, and the absolute value of the mean curvature respectively. As an application of our methods, we study the existence of almost $c$-convex exhaustions, that is, exhaustions whose boundaries satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}(H-c)^-\to0$ for some $c>0$.

Differential Geometry.title: All toric Hermitian ALE gravitational instantons
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the only smooth, Ricci flat, ALE gravitational instanton with a toric Hermitian non-Kähler structure is the Eguchi-Hanson instanton. The proof is analogous to the classification of toric Hermitian ALF instantons by Biquard and Gauduchon, although we avoid the use of toric Kähler geometry and instead perform a direct global analysis of the Tod form of the metric in Weyl-Papapetrou coordinates. This supports a conjecture by Gibbons and Bando-Kasue-Nakajima which states that any Ricci flat ALE instanton is self-dual.

Differential Geometry.title: Holography and Cheeger constant of asymptotically CMC submanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(M^{n+1},g_+)$ be an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold. We compute the Cheeger constant of conformally compact asymptotically constant mean curvature submanifolds $ ι: Y^{k+1} \to (M^{n+1},g_+)$ with arbitrary codimension. As an application, we provide two classes of examples of $(n+1)$-dimensional asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds with Cheeger constant equal to $n$, whose conformal infinity is of the following types: 1) positive Yamabe invariant, and 2) negative Yamabe invariant. Moreover, in the same spirit as Blitz--Gover--Waldron \cite{BlitzSamuel2021CFFa}, we show that an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold with umbilic boundary is conformally weakly Poincaré--Einstein if and only if the third conformal fundamental form of the boundary vanishes. Next, in the space of asymptotically minimal hypersurfaces $Y$ within a Poincaré--Einstein manifold, we identify an extrinsic conformal invariant of $\partial Y$ which obstructs the vanishing of the mean curvature of $Y$ to second order. This conformal invariant is a linear combination of two Riemannian hypersurface invariants of $\partial Y,$ one which depends on its extrinsic geometry within $\overline{Y}$ and the other on its extrinsic geometry within $\partial M;$ neither of which are conformal invariants individually. Finally, we show that for asymptotically minimal hypersurfaces with mean curvature vanishing to second order inside of a Poincaré--Einstein space, being weakly Poincaré--Einstein is equivalent to the boundary of $Y$ having vanishing second and third conformal fundamental forms when viewed as a hypersurface within the conformal infinity.
Differential Geometry.comment: 40 pages, 3 figures. Fixed typos, added more details to section 5

Differential Geometry.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
Differential Geometry.summary: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $Σ$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,Φ)$ with $(E,Φ)\cong(E,-Φ)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,Φ)$ corresponds to a representation $ρ$ of $π_1(Σ)$, then $(E,-Φ)$ corresponds to $(\overlineρ^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $η\mapsto-η$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

Differential Geometry.title: Panopticum of 3D snake models
Differential Geometry.summary: Motivated by the standard 2-dimensional 3-segment snake model, leading to the famous $(2,3,5)$ geometry, we discuss a series of 3-dimensional models of similar snakes. In particular, we seek for rules allowing to steer them exclusively by the two joints, which expects 4-dimensional control freedom. This leads to interesting $(4,9)$ and $(4,10)$ models. Finally, we discuss modifications of the previous snakes which lead to $(4,8)$ models. All of the models open further questions and should be a good baseline for further research.
Differential Geometry.comment: 19 pages, 10 figures. The supporting Maple computations are attached

Differential Geometry.title: Differential Invariants of Carrollian Spacetimes
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute invariants of Carrollian spacetimes, deriving them from the geometry of the screen bundle. For generic Carrollian structures we specify how to generate the entire algebra of differential invariants, with emphasis on dimension 3, which has special physical relevance. Then, in the framework of jet-spaces, we compute the numerology behind these invariants: the Hilbert and Poincaré functions that govern their numbers according to order. Finally, we compute the Spencer cohomology behind the Carrollian geometry that, in particular, contains the spaces of intrinsic torsion and intrinsic curvature, which are fundamental invariants, important in the equivalence problem and symmetry analysis. Thus, we also discuss symmetry sizes of Carrollian spacetimes.
Differential Geometry.comment: 24 pages. Minor improvements and typos corrected

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity of Three-Dimensional Self-Shrinkers with Constant Norm of the Second Fundamental Form
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $X:M^3\to\R^4$ be a complete, connected self-shrinker without boundary, and suppose that the squared norm $S$ of its second fundamental form is constant. We prove that $S=0$ or $S=1$. Accordingly, the image is a hyperplane through the origin or a generalized cylinder $\mathbb S^k(\sqrt{k})\times\R^{3-k}$, $1\le k\le3$, and the immersion is a Riemannian covering onto its image.

Geometric Topology.title: Arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds with bounded rank
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $n$-manifolds of bounded rank have bounded adjoint trace field degree, and consequently have lower bounded injectivity radius. From this, we obtain a number of corollaries. In particular, we obtain that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $3$-manifolds of bounded rank are contained in finitely many commensurability classes, and describe these commensurability classes. Additionally, it follows that for closed arithmetic hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, Heegaard genus is equal to rank for all but finitely many manifolds of each rank.

Geometric Topology.title: The Links--Gould polynomial of an alternating link is alternating
Geometric Topology.summary: Building on work of Kauffman--Saleur and earlier work of the second author, we derive a determinant formula for the Links--Gould polynomial of links. As an application, we prove a 20-year-old conjecture of Ishii: for any alternating link, the Links--Gould invariant is an alternating polynomial.

Geometric Topology.title: Stably exotic knotted surfaces up to equivalence
Geometric Topology.summary: In this short note we show the existence of stably exotic knotted surfaces in 4-manifolds in the sense that the embedded surfaces are topologically equivalent but are not smoothly equivalent even after any number of internal and external stabilisations.

Geometric Topology.title: Triple-cup product forms of 3-manifolds and Heegaard diagrams
Geometric Topology.summary: The triple-cup product form $μ$ is a classical invariant of $3$-manifolds, determining the cohomology ring up to torsion. Given a closed, connected, oriented $3$-manifold $M$, we describe an explicit formula for computing $μ$ from a Heegaard diagram of $M$. Then, we show that the triple-cup product form $μ$ can be recovered as a reduction of Turaev's homotopy intersection form $η$ of the Heegaard surface.

Geometric Topology.title: A proof of the framed LMOV conjecture for links
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove the Labastida--Mariño--Ooguri--Vafa conjecture for oriented links with arbitrary integer framings. Consequently, the framed reformulated invariants have finite integral LMOV expansions for every integer framing vector.

Geometric Topology.title: Braid Stability and a Floer theory of Braid Isotopies
Geometric Topology.summary:
We build a Floer theory on the space of braids of periodic orbits of a Hamiltonian flow on a closed symplectic surface. The differential and continuation maps are defined by counting Floer isotopies of braids: tuples of Floer cylinders with pairwise disjoint graphs.
  With this new perspective, we prove a quantitative braid stability result that shows the persistence of braids under possibly large Hamiltonian perturbations. As an application, we show that for every $α\geq 0$ there is a sequence of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms $φ_k$ on the two-torus $T^2$ such that $$d_H(\operatorname{Ent}_{\leq α}(T^2,ω),φ_k)\to \infty \quad (k \to \infty),$$ where $\text{Ent}_{\leq α}(T^2,ω)\subset \text{Ham}(T^2,ω)$ denotes the set of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with topological entropy at most $α$ and $d_H$ the Hofer metric. We prove this result by studying only contractible periodic orbits, whereas analogous higher-genus statements were previously obtained using non-contractible orbits.
Geometric Topology.comment: 67 pages, 15 figures, v2: corrected typos and added more citations and new remarks, comments are welcome

Geometric Topology.title: Maps between circle bundles: Fiber-preserving, Finiteness and Realization of mapping degree sets
Geometric Topology.summary:
Let $E_i$ be an oriented circle bundle over a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M_i$ with $i=1,2$ and assume that $M_2$ is aspherical. We prove the following geometric realization result, which extends the classical result for maps between circle bundles over surfaces to all dimensions $\geq 2$. Let $f\colon E_1\to E_2$ be a map. If the induced homomorphism $f_*$ on $π_1$ sends the fiber subgroup of $π_1(E_1)$ to the fiber subgroup of $π_1(E_2)$, then there is a fiber-preserving map in the homotopy class of $f$.
  Using the above result and a computation of the mapping degree set of fiber-preserving maps between $E_1$ and $E_2$, we obtain the following results on the finiteness and the realization problems of mapping degree sets.
  ($\mathcal F$) The mapping degree set $D(E_1, E_2)$ is finite if $M_2$ is hyperbolic and the Euler class of $E_2$ is not torsion.
  ($\mathcal R$) For any finite set $A$ of integers containing $0$ and any $n>2$, $A$ is the mapping degree set $D(M,N)$ for some closed oriented $n$-manifolds $M$ and $N$.
  Item ($\mathcal F$) extends the previously known $3$-dimensional case to all dimensions $\geq 3$. Item ($\mathcal R$) gives a complete answer to the realization problem on finite sets of integers (containing 0) in all dimensions, including in particular the previously unknown cases in dimensions $ 4$ and $5$.
Geometric Topology.comment: 22 pages; v2: final version, to appear in Mathematische Zeitschrift

Geometric Topology.title: A topological interpretation of numbers
Geometric Topology.summary: We survey recent advancements on the realisation problem for mapping degree sets. In particular, we explain that any finite set containing zero is the mapping degree set between some $n$-manifolds, for each $n\geq3$. Our building factors for the construction of the realising manifolds will be aspherical manifolds. Thus, along the way, we review a couple of open questions related to maps of non-zero degree for aspherical manifolds.
Geometric Topology.comment: 14 pages, survey chapter; v2: final version, to appear in the book "Nisyros 2025: Essays in Geometry, History and Philosophy", edited by A. Papadopoulos and S. Yamada

Geometric Topology.title: Barbell twists are natural
Geometric Topology.summary: For any oriented smooth $4$--manifold $X$ diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times D^2)^{\natural n}$ ($n\geq0$), the author establishes a natural isomorphism of abelian groups: $$\mathrm{Mod}(X,\partial X)\cong \mathrm{Mod}(D^4,\partial D^4)\times\wedge^2H_2(X;\mathbb{Z}),$$ concerning the (smooth) boundary-fixing mapping class group of $X$. For $n=2$, the Budney--Gabai barbell twist $\varphi\in\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{N},\partial\mathcal{N})$ is identified with a generator of the factor subgroup $\wedge^2H_2(\mathcal{N};\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}$. Up to boundary-fixing diffeotopy, the barbell spines of $\mathcal{N}$ are completely classified by the bases of $H_2(\mathcal{N};\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$, forming a homogeneous set modeled on the group $\mathrm{GL}(H_2(\mathcal{N};\mathbb{Z}))\cong\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$. Any barbell spine of $\mathcal{N}$ gives rise to an implanted barbell twist equal to $\varphi$ or $\varphi^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{N},\partial \mathcal{N})$, according to the sign of the homological basis orientation.
Geometric Topology.comment: 30 pages; a false assertion (Lemma 4.5 in Version 2) removed; Section 4 (Extendability for boundary diffeomorphisms of a 1-handlebody) added, replacing Section 4 (Embedding uniqueness for several 1-handles) and Section 5 (Embedding uniqueness for a 1-handlebody) in Version 2; Proof of Lemma 6.2 revised

Geometric Topology.title: A parity constraint on the topological numbers of self-complementary triply-periodic surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary: The stability zone of Novikov's problem of planar sections of triply periodic surfaces are labeled by indivisible triples of integers, which we call the soul of the zone. Which triples may occur is not known. We show that, if a Morse function $f$ on $\mathbb T^3$ admits a translation $τ(x)=x+v$ with $f\circτ=-f$, so that the sets $\{f<0\}$ and $\{f>0\}$ are congruent, then in the generic genus-$3$ situation every topological number $L$ satisfies $\langle L,2v\rangle\equiv1\pmod2$. The mechanism is that the electron/hole type of a null-homologous closed trajectory is invariant under the period lattice and is reversed by $τ$. For $f=\cos2πx+\cos2πy+\cos2πz$ and the $μ$-cube, this means that the sum of the components of each soul is odd.

Geometric Topology.title: Lagrangian cobordism functor in microlocal sheaf theory I
Geometric Topology.summary: Given a Lagrangian cobordism $L$ of Legendrian submanifolds from $Λ_-$ to $Λ_+$, we construct a functor $Φ_L^*: Sh^c_{Λ_+}(M) \rightarrow Sh^c_{Λ_-}(M) \otimes_{C_{-*}(Ω_*Λ_-)} C_{-*}(Ω_*L)$ between sheaf categories of compact objects with singular support on $Λ_\pm$ and its right adjoint on sheaf categories of proper objects, using Nadler-Shende's work. This gives a sheaf theory description analogous to the Lagrangian cobordism map on Legendrian contact homologies and the right adjoint on their unital augmentation categories. We also deduce some long exact sequences and new obstructions to Lagrangian cobordisms between high dimensional Legendrian submanifolds.
Geometric Topology.comment: 43 pages, 13 figures. v2: Minor revisions on Intro, Sec 2.2 and other places (theorem numbers changed in Sec 3). v3: Fixed the proof of Thm 2.10 and Prop 3.3 (Lem 3.4 in the previous version) based on referees' comments, revisions on Sec 2.4, 4.1 and other places (section and theorem numbers changed in Sec 3; title changed). To appear in J Topol. v4, v5: Minor modification: Thm 1.9 & Rem 2.13

Geometric Topology.title: Bi-contact plugs and dynamical hyperbolicity
Geometric Topology.summary:
We develop a theory of bi-contact plugs on oriented $3$-manifolds to construct Anosov flows or, more generally, structurally stable nonsingular flows. For a hyperbolic plug with filling Morse-Smale boundary laminations, we prove that every strongly transverse gluing map can be isotoped through strongly transverse maps to identify a strongly adapted unoriented contact form. The resulting flow is hyperbolic and is Anosov when the quotient is closed. This answers a question of Béguin-Bonatti-Yu. The result also extends to gluing nonsingular partially hyperbolic flows. Anosov completion by reflection embeds each such hyperbolic plug in an Anosov flow on its oriented double.
  Further applications include a classification of structurally generic projectively Anosov flows without saddle periodic orbits and Morse-Smale examples with prescribed saddle count. Generalizing the construction of Bonatti-Bowden-Potrie, finite capping embeds any bi-contact plug in a closed projectively Anosov flow with the same topological entropy, preserving partial hyperbolicity for attracting plugs. We also construct flows with controlled invariant torus dynamics on torus bundles and on doubles of plugs with coorientable boundary bi-foliations. Finally, every cooriented partially hyperbolic bi-contact plug admits a Liouville structure on its thickening, with Liouville trajectories projecting to positively reparametrized flow lines. Repelling plugs yield four-dimensional Liouville domains, often with chaotic skeletons.
Geometric Topology.comment: 67 pages. 7 figures. All comments are welcomed!

Geometric Topology.title: Cohomology ring of the strata of holomorphic differentials of genus 3
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that the rational Chow ring of every connected component of the multi-scale compactifications of the genus three strata $\mathcal{H}(4), \mathcal{H}(2,2)$ and $\mathcal{H}(3,1)$ is generated by boundary-stratum classes. Our proof shows Chow-Künneth generation property of boundary strata of the multi-scale compactification by reducing the boundary analysis to lower-genus generalized strata of meromorphic differentials, including residueless loci, described through plane-quartic and plane-cubic models. As a consequence, the rational cycle-class map is an isomorphism and the compactifications have no odd rational cohomology.

Geometric Topology.title: $3$-manifold groups are linear
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that the fundamental group of every compact graph $3$-manifold is linear over the complex numbers. As a corollary, all fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are linear over the complex numbers.

Geometric Topology.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s as unions of two thickened circles
Geometric Topology.summary: We give an infinite family of non-diffeomorphic exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s, each of which is the union of two copies of a standard open tubular neighborhood of the circle, which intersect in a standard open tubular neighborhood of the wedge of two circles. This gives the simplest known decomposition of an exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$ into two open sets, making progress on Question 4.43 (A) of Kirby's 1995 problem list. The decompositions are obtained by studying fibered slice disk complements in certain Casson-Gordon homotopy 4-balls, for which we provide similar decompositions. We distinguish the $\mathbb{R}^4$'s using end Floer homology.
Geometric Topology.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, No AI. Comments welcome!

Geometric Topology.title: Small Sets of Generators for Handlebody Groups
Geometric Topology.summary: Wajnryb gave a finite presentation of the handlebody group $\mathcal{M}(V_g)$ and showed that it is generated by five elements for $g\geq 2$. Using his relations, we show that $\mathcal{M}(V_g)$ is generated by three elements if $g\geq 2$.

Geometric Topology.title: 6-valent vertex in the $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ web category and its categorification
Geometric Topology.summary: We define a $2π/3$-rotationally invariant 6-valent vertex in the $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ web category. When $N = 4, 5$, we provide a categorification of the 6-valent vertex using $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ foams and decompose the hexagon web into a direct sum of indecomposables. A similar decomposition is conjectured for $N \geq 6$.

Geometric Topology.title: Enumeration of one-cycle signed chord diagrams and their duals for optimal Morse flows on closed surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary:
Optimal Morse vector fields on closed surfaces, i.e.\ fields with the minimal possible number of critical points (a single source and a single sink), are classified up to topological trajectory equivalence by one-cycle signed chord diagrams in Kybalko, Prishlyak and Shchurko (2018).
  We recall this construction and the associated duality, which corresponds to reversing the direction of the flow, in a unified encoding in which both endpoints of a chord carry the same label, and we make it algorithmic. We give an explicit traversal procedure that detects one-cycle diagrams, a canonical form of an equivalence class under cyclic shifts, reversal and relabeling of chords, and a construction of the dual diagram. On this basis we describe an algorithm that enumerates all one-cycle signed chord diagrams with a given number of chords, both for orientable and for non-orientable surfaces, groups them into equivalence classes, pairs each class with its dual, and identifies the self-dual ones. The algorithm is implemented in Python and archived in Zenodo; its output is validated against the Harer--Zagier numbers in the orientable case and against orbit-size counts in both cases. We also note that, when a one-cycle diagram is read as a cellular embedding of a one-vertex graph, its dual diagram describes the embedding of the dual graph.

Geometric Topology.title: Floer lasagna modules from link Floer homology
Geometric Topology.summary: In this paper, we introduce the notion of Floer lasagna modules, which is inspired by the construction of skein lasagna module in [MWW19] by Morrison, Walker and Wedrich. Here we use link Floer homology instead of Khovanov-Rozansky homology. We give a description of the Floer lasagna module for 4-manifolds obtained by adding 2-handles to the 4-ball and we compute some examples.
Geometric Topology.comment: 27 pages, 21 figure. v2: accepted version to AGT. Several errors in the previous statements and proofs corrected, with other improvements on exposition

Geometric Topology.title: Index for a mutation loop
Geometric Topology.summary: Motivated by the 3d-3d correspondence, we introduce an index $\mathcal{I}_g^φ$ for a mutation loop $φ$ of a quiver and an integer $g \geq 0$. We prove its integrality $\mathcal{I}_g^φ\in \mathbb{Z}$ under certain conditions, which extends the integrality conjecture of Gang--Kim--Yoon for $3$-manifolds to the broader framework of mutation loops in cluster algebras. Our index also has an interpretation as the genus-$g$ partition function of a $(1+1)$-dimensional TQFT. We provide explicit computations for mutation loops of period one. In particular, in the case of the generalized Kronecker quivers, we give an explicit formula expressing the generating function of the indices for all genera $g$ as a ratio of polynomials. Altogether, we provide a new insight to the interplay between the geometry of $3$-manifolds and cluster algebra.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimality conditions with cone-generalized convex vector functions
Optimization and Control.summary:
The object of investigation in this paper are generalized convex vector nonlinear programming problems with cone constraints. We prove that a quasiconvex vector function is pseudoconvex with respect to the same cone if and only if every vector critical point of the function is a weak global minimizer, a result, which is a natural extension of a known characterization of pseudoconvex scalar functions.
  We introduce a new notion of a Fréchet differentiable pseudoconvex problem. We derive that a problem with quasiconvex vector data is pseudoconvex if and only if every Fritz John vector critical point is a weakly efficient global solution. Thus, we generalize a lot of previous optimality conditions, concerning the scalar case and the multiobjective Paretian one.
  We also introduce the notion of a Fritz John cone-pseudoinvex vector problem. We prove that a problem with cone constraints is Fritz John pseudoinvex if and only if every vector critical point of Fritz John type is a weak global minimizer with respect to the considered cone..

Optimization and Control.title: Policy Iteration Is Not Strongly Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
Optimization and Control.summary: We establish exponential iteration lower bounds in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted and average-reward Markov decision processes (MDPs), with a constant number of actions per state. This rules out strong polynomiality of Howard's policy iteration in both settings. We further prove that a Dantzig counterpart of Howard's policy iteration runs in strongly polynomial time on deterministic average-reward MDPs. Together with the known strongly polynomial bound for Dantzig's rule on deterministic discounted MDPs, these results establish an exponential separation between the two algorithms in both settings. This separation between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest improvement across all states reveals a ``price'' of algorithmic anarchy.
Optimization and Control.comment: Added results on average-reward MDPs and extended the discounted lower bounds to constant-bit integer rewards

Optimization and Control.title: Compositional Sensitivity Analysis for Multiobjective System Co-Design
Optimization and Control.summary: Sensitivity analysis of coupled systems typically propagates derivatives of single-valued maps, whereas multiobjective optimization generally treats sensitivity at the system level rather than through interconnected subsystems. We develop a mathematical framework for compositional sensitivity analysis in multiobjective system design, building on monotone co-design. Subsystems are represented as design problems (DPs), interconnected through series, parallel, union, intersection, and feedback composition. We introduce tangential DPs (TDPs) to describe first-order variations around an operating point, show that they preserve the structure of DPs, and characterize their queries through graphical derivatives. To account for multiple internal realizations of a system-level operating point, tangential co-design problems compose families of local TDPs by taking a union over these realizations while retaining the original interconnection structure. We show that these compositions yield families of TDPs and establish conditions under which sensitivity analysis commutes with individual composition operations. Beyond infinitesimal sensitivity, we show that bounded tangential models of convex DPs provide tighter outer approximations of feasible finite changes, which can be propagated through co-design problems without union compositions. We conclude with several convex and nonconvex numerical examples that showcase the framework's accuracy and computational benefits.

Optimization and Control.title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for an associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, the convergence analysis of the stochastic gradient method reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE. The method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and provides a way to establish convergence rates for new optimization algorithms through calculus arguments applied to their associated SDEs.

Optimization and Control.title: Bayesian Optimization under Uncertainty for Training a Scale Parameter in Stochastic Models
Optimization and Control.summary: Hyperparameter tuning is a challenging problem especially when the system itself involves uncertainty. Due to noisy function evaluations, optimization under uncertainty can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we present a novel Bayesian optimization framework tailored for hyperparameter tuning under uncertainty, with a focus on optimizing a scale- or precision-type parameter in stochastic models. The proposed method employs a statistical surrogate for the underlying random variable, enabling analytical evaluation of the expectation operator. Moreover, we derive a closed-form expression for the optimizer of the random acquisition function, which significantly reduces computational cost per iteration. Numerical experiments demonstrate substantial gains in optimization efficiency: about 40-fold reduction in data usage relative to a Monte Carlo-based one-dimensional optimization scheme, and an order of magnitude improvement relative to a Gaussian process-based Bayesian optimization baseline.

Optimization and Control.title: The optimality of an (s, S) hiring policy on a workforce planning problem with fixed recruitment costs and binomial turnover
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a finite-horizon nonstationary workforce planning problem in which staff turnover in each period follows a binomial distribution whose parameters depend on the post-hiring workforce level. The model incorporates a fixed hiring cost that is incurred whenever recruitment occurs, regardless of the number of employees hired; this represents explicit (e.g. administration costs) or implicit (e.g. team disruption) factors that are commonplace in workforce planning. The objective is to minimise the expected total cost, including recruitment, salary, and shortage costs, where deviations below period-specific staffing requirements are penalised. To analyse this stochastic dynamic program with decision-dependent transition probabilities, we establish the discrete convexity of the variable single-period cost (the sum of expected salary and penalty costs) and the K-convexity of the expected total cost in presence of endogenous uncertainty. We then show that the optimal hiring policy exhibits an (s, S)-type structure: when the workforce level in a given period falls below a threshold s, staff are hired up to level S; otherwise, no hiring occurs. To compute approximate policy parameters, we develop a mixed-integer linear programming heuristic based on a piecewise approximation. In our computational study, we demonstrate that our approach achieves fast computation and small optimality gaps on the test instances.

Optimization and Control.title: Monotone Allocations without Single-Crossing: When to Bunch and When to Jump
Optimization and Control.summary: We study one-dimensional screening when the Spence-Mirrlees condition fails along a monotone dividing curve, on which all types value marginal output equally. A single ratio, marginal distortion over marginal rent, governs the problem. When the relaxed solution stays in the positive region, non-decreasing optima in the positive single-crossing region are continuous if the ratio increases in the decision. When it crosses a flat curve and marginal rents are separable, every continuous contract is improved by a jump. When it crosses a strictly monotone curve, a contract that pools and jumps continues along the mirror of the pool if the ratio does not increase along it. Optimality among all implementable allocations, deterministic or random, is proved by a measure on the binding constraints whose weights are the same ratio; with constant curvatures and no crossing, it is also necessary. As applications, we solve problems of procurement and nonlinear pricing.
Optimization and Control.comment: 48 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary Material (36 + 7 pages) as ancillary files. Replication package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23271020

Optimization and Control.title: Orientation Estimation of Cryo-EM Images for Molecules with Arbitrary Symmetry by Semidefinite Programming
Optimization and Control.summary:
This paper extends the non-unique games framework introduced in Bandeira et al. (2020) to address symmetric structures. Precisely, we consider the problem \[ \begin{aligned}
  \underset{g_1,\ldots,g_n\in \mathcal{G}}{\operatorname{min}}\,\, \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{i,j=1}^n \sum_{s\in S} f_{ij}(g_i s g_j^{-1}), \end{aligned} \] where $\mathcal{G}$ is a compact group, $S\subset \mathcal{G}$ is a finite subgroup of symmetry elements, and $f_{ij}:\mathcal{G}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a loss function. A notable example is common lines based orientation estimation of cryo-EM images for molecules with point group symmetry $S$, where $\mathcal{G}$ is the rotation group $\operatorname{SO}(3)$. With a semidefinite programming relaxation, we turn the problem into a convex program that is solved with the alternating direction method of multipliers. Unlike existing approaches which are tailored to specific symmetry groups, ours provides a unified computational framework for addressing all point group symmetries. We demonstrate the applicability of the proposed algorithm on the cryo-EM orientation estimation problem on both simulated and experimental datasets. In particular, our algorithm is effective in generating high-quality ab initio models from only a few class averages computed from experimental images.

Optimization and Control.title: High-Order Matrix Control Barrier Functions: Well-Posedness and Feasibility via Matrix Relative Degree
Optimization and Control.summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide an effective framework for enforcing safety in dynamical systems with scalar constraints. However, many safety constraints are more naturally expressed as matrix-valued conditions, such as positive definiteness or eigenvalue bounds - scalar formulations introduce potential nonsmoothness that complicates analysis. Matrix control barrier functions (MCBFs) address this limitation by directly enforcing matrix-valued safety constraints. Yet for constraints where the control input does not appear in the first derivative, high-order formulations are required. While such extensions are well understood in the scalar case, they remain largely unexplored in the matrix case. This paper develops high-order matrix control barrier functions (HOMCBFs) and establishes conditions ensuring well-posedness and feasibility of the associated constraints, enabling enforcement of matrix-valued safety constraints for systems with high-order dynamics. We further show that, using an optimal-decay HOMCBF formulation, forward invariance can be ensured while requiring control only over the minimum eigenspace. The framework is demonstrated on a double-integrator localization problem by enforcing positive definiteness of the information matrix.

Optimization and Control.title: Time-Invariant Linear Quadratic Regulators: A New Look
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper demonstrates that linear ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients serve as the main building block for time-invariant linear quadratic regulators (LQRs). By applying the Euler-Lagrange equations to a flat output, i.e., to a basis of the free finitely-generated module over the commutative principal ideal ring of time-invariant linear differential operators with respect to the time derivation, this result emerges directly. In module-theoretic terms. The freeness of this structure corresponds to the classical Kalman controllability condition (M. Fliess, Some basic structural properties of generalized linear systems, Syst. Contr. Lett., 15 (1990) 391-396). Within this framework, the two-point boundary value problem, including the control variables, becomes analytically tractable, enabling the derivation of optimal time horizons, optimal parameter design, and rest-to-rest trajectories. Furthermore, a novel turnpike-like phenomenon is established via nonstandard analysis. The feedback loop is closed thanks to the HEOL approach (C. Join, E. Delaleau, M. Fliess, Flatness-based control revisited: The HEOL setting, C.R. Math., 362 (2024) 1693-1706), an extension of model-free control (MFC) that leverages intelligent controllers. Our viewpoint, which significantly simplifies the presentation by avoiding the conventional Kalman state-space representation, relies on foundational algebraic concepts that, while elementary, are rarely used in today's control theory. To aid intuition, some rudimentary examples are presented, most of which include computer simulations.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Decay Matrix Control Barrier Functions: Soundness and Completeness for Matrix Safety Constraints
Optimization and Control.summary: Many safety requirements, such as keeping a manipulator away from kinematic singularities, a network connected, or a system observable, amount to keeping a state-dependent matrix positive definite. Matrix control barrier functions (MCBFs) enforce such requirements with a semidefinite program that minimally modifies a nominal control input. The MCBF constraint bounds how fast the safety margin, the smallest eigenvalue of the matrix, may decay. Yet a fixed decay rule is conservative, rejecting safe controls that drive the state quickly toward, but never across, the boundary of the safe set. Scalar optimal decay (SOD) addresses this issue by scaling the decay term by a scalar weight that is optimized together with the control. For scalar barrier functions, SOD then rejects a control at the boundary only if the control would decrease the margin. For MCBFs, however, SOD can reject controls that leave the margin unchanged, and near the safety boundary SOD accepts such controls only at a high cost. We introduce matrix optimal decay (MOD), which replaces the scalar weight with a matrix multiplier while keeping the semidefinite program convex. MOD is provably sound and complete, certifying at the boundary exactly the controls that do not decrease the margin. If some control can strictly increase the margin at every boundary point, the MOD-MCBF filtered controller is continuous and renders the safe set forward invariant. We also add an optional recovery condition that drives the system toward the safe set after a violation without affecting soundness or completeness. On a planar two-link arm avoiding singularities, MOD-MCBF certifies safe motions that both a fixed decay rule and SOD reject, and tracks an end-effector target more closely than SOD.

Optimization and Control.title: Dynamic Programming for A Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider an infinite-horizon discounted dynamic programming (DP) problem for a countable-innovation belief-state model. The model is a surrogate for a linear-Gaussian dual control problem involving an unknown parameter vector and Gaussian observation noise. The surrogate preserves the first two moments of the Gaussian innovation and the resulting posterior second-moment structure. We allow unbounded belief and control spaces and nonnegative stage costs with quadratic growth in the posterior mean and covariance. Using a posterior-moment weight, we show that the Bellman operator is a contraction in a weighted sup-norm space. We characterize the optimal cost as the unique solution of the Bellman equation in this space, establish the existence of optimal stationary policies. We further prove weighted sup-norm convergence of value iteration, policy iteration, and optimistic policy iteration under vanishing approximation errors. The convergence results under vanishing approximation errors rely on general weighted sup-norm contraction properties and are applicable beyond the particular dual control problem considered here.

Optimization and Control.title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation in an exterior domain
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the exact controllability of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the exterior $Ω=\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΘ$ of a non-trapping obstacle $Θ$, with internal controls supported outside a large ball, and the corresponding boundary control problem on $Ω_0=B_{R_0}\setminusΘ$ with Dirichlet controls acting only on the outer sphere $\partial B_{R_0}$. Using the local smoothing effect of Burq, Gérard and Tzvetkov [9], we prove observability inequalities for the linear Schrödinger equation in the whole scale of Sobolev spaces $H^σ_D(Ω)$, $σ\in[-2,2]$, associated with the Dirichlet Laplacian; they require only the non-trapping assumption (no star-shapedness of $Θ$), and their proofs use no normal boundary traces. Combined with Strichartz-type estimates and a perturbation argument, this yields local exact controllability in $H^1_0(Ω)$ and in $H^2(Ω)\cap H^1_0(Ω)$, in dimensions two and three, around the zero solution and, for internal controls and under a unique continuation assumption, around nontrivial trajectories. The same method applies to the quintic equation, which is energy-critical in dimension three. Several open problems are discussed.

Optimization and Control.title: Local-discrepancy ambiguity sets for distributionally robust optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we introduce a new class of data-driven ambiguity sets for distributionally robust optimization (DRO) that aim to enhance the local inference accuracy of an unknown distribution. Building on optimal transport-based discrepancy measures, we depart from the conventional paradigm of monolithic ambiguity balls, which rely on a single global transport budget to capture distributional uncertainty. Instead, we introduce local-discrepancy ambiguity sets, where the support of the distribution is partitioned into predefined regions and transport cost constraints are imposed locally to each region. This added flexibility allows for a more refined characterization of plausible distributions by preventing highly imbalanced transport across regions. As a result, the proposed approach can yield less conservative and more robust decisions, particularly in settings where decisions depend on the local properties of the sample space. We further derive tractable reformulations of the resulting DRO problems and demonstrate through simulations that our method can outperform traditional Wasserstein ambiguity sets in terms of decision quality.

Optimization and Control.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped SGD with Linear Decay
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we study the last-iterate convergence of clipped stochastic gradient descent under heavy-tailed noise. We assume that the stochastic gradients are unbiased and that the noise has a bounded central $p$-th moment, where $1<p\le2$. For smooth convex objectives, a linearly decreasing learning rate gives a high-probability error bound of order $O(LR^2\log(1/δ)/T+σR(\log(1/δ)/T)^{(p-1)/p})$. We further establish last-iterate guarantees for nonsmooth composite objectives and smooth composite objectives with proximal updates. In addition, when a causal adversary replaces at most $q$ gradients, the same clipped update achieves a bound with $\log(1/δ)$ replaced by $\log(1/δ)+q$. The corresponding lower bounds for the clean and corrupted oracle models are also provided.

Optimization and Control.title: Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Reinforcement Learning for Derivative-Free Model-Based Control
Optimization and Control.summary: Finite-horizon optimal control becomes difficult when a dynamical model can be simulated reliably, but its derivatives are unavailable, discontinuous, or unreliable. Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Optimization (HPDPO) is introduced as a derivative-free, model-based reinforcement learning framework for this setting. The control is represented as a time-indexed finite-horizon policy. Candidate actions are evaluated by deterministic suffix rollouts of the supplied transition model, while a regularized Hamiltonian dual formulation supplies structured future-cost information through block-coordinate multiplier updates. No differentiation of the state dynamics or learned critic is required. The method is validated on nonsmooth problems with exact solutions, an analytical and learned ReLU biomarker cascade, an amyloid Neural ODE trained from longitudinal ADNI data, and three multidimensional-control problems with up to five simultaneous controls. Across these examples, HPDPO closely reproduces exact or reference objective values, trajectories, and control structures. The results show that forward simulation and Hamiltonian dual structure can be combined to solve deterministic finite-horizon control problems involving nonsmooth, learned, or black-box dynamics.

Optimization and Control.title: Viscosity Solutions for Hamilton-Jacobi equations on Separable Banach Spaces
Optimization and Control.summary: This work provides a framework to treat optimal control problems on separable Banach spaces in the viscosity sense. First, it extends the notion of $B$-viscosity solutions to the Banach setting and relates the extension to the notions of viscosity solutions used in metric space settings. As the main results, the paper proves a strict comparison principle and characterizes the value function of an optimal control problem as the unique viscosity solution to an infinite-dimensional HJB equation.

Optimization and Control.title: Connection between MP and DPP for Mean-Field Stochastic Optimal Control Problems
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper deals with the optimal control problem for the general mean-field stochastic differential equations, in which the coefficients depend on both the state process as well as on its law. We focus on the connection between the general maximum principle and the dynamic programming principle for such a control problem. We establish the relationship between the value function of the mean-field optimal control problem and the adjoint equations in the maximum principle. We also give a general mean-field stochastic verification theorem. Some examples are solved explicitly to illustrate our results.

Optimization and Control.title: Adaptive Variance-Reduced Stochastic Sequential (Quadratic Constrained) Quadratic Programming
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we propose an adaptive variance-reduced stochastic sequential (quadratic constrained) quadratic programming (AVR-SS(QC)QP) method for nonlinear constrained optimization. The framework integrates SPIDER-based variance reduction, stochastic quasi-Newton curvature information, merit-function globalization, and adaptive switching between stochastic SQP and SQCQP models. The switching mechanism is governed by a relative constraint model curvature indicator that measures the second-order constraint information neglected by the linearized SQP model. A smoothed hysteresis rule ac?tivates the SQCQP model only when the relative constraint curvature is significant. An exact L1 merit function with Armijo backtracking globalizes the resulting directions, while a coupled stochastic Lyapunov analysis controls the interaction between gradient-estimation error and optimization progress. Under standard smoothness, sampling, regularity, and second-order conditions, we establish almost-sure consistency of the variance-reduced gradient estimator and global convergence of the KKT residual. We further show that, near regular KKT points, the curvature indicator vanishes and the method eventually selects the computationally cheaper SQP model. Numerical experiments on a sparse principal component analysis problem illustrate the practical be?havior of the proposed framework.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Transport for Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection
Optimization and Control.summary: The continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem is investigated in this paper through a rigorous integration of backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and Kantorovich duality theory. We propose a novel analytical framework for addressing feedback control in McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems. By solving three coupled systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), we derive an explicit, closed-loop optimal feedback investment strategy.

Optimization and Control.title: Quantitative Convergence of Markov Equilibria for Time-Inconsistent Controlled Diffusions
Optimization and Control.summary: Time-inconsistent stochastic control admits a natural game-theoretic interpretation in which successive decision dates are represented by different selves. In the Markovian framework of Björk-Khapko-Murgoci, the corresponding continuous-time equilibrium HJB system can be motivated by discrete subgame-perfect games, but the general discrete-to-continuous passage is not automatic. We establish a quantitative convergence theorem for a smooth uniformly elliptic class in which the control may enter both drift and diffusion. Using the exact sample-and-hold transition law on each time step, we construct, near a verified continuous equilibrium branch, a unique regular discrete Markov subgame-perfect equilibrium and prove first-order convergence of the continuation objects in an anisotropic $C^{2+β}$ topology and of the equilibrium policies in $C^0$. The key stability mechanism is structural: the discrete first-order condition forces the differential feedback correction in the frozen linearization to be nilpotent, which yields mesh-uniform block estimates through a two-norm dyadic Schauder argument despite the second-order coupling caused by controlled volatility. We also formulate a conditional transfer principle for structured polynomial-growth classes, with error-space stability stated as a separate hypothesis.

Optimization and Control.title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with Hölder Continuous Terms
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of Hölder continuous functions and satisfies the $σ$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $σ= 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (ε^{-1}) ε^{2 (\underlineα - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $ε$-approximate solution, where $\underlineα \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{ö}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.

Optimization and Control.title: A Practical Combinatorial Interior Point Method for Minimum-Cost Flow
Optimization and Control.summary: In a recent breakthrough, Chen, Kyng, Liu, Peng, Probst Gutenberg, and Sachdeva (arXiv:2203.00671) designed the first almost-linear-time algorithm for minimum-cost flow. Their approach uses an Interior Point Method (IPM) to achieve complexity $m^{1+o(1)}\log U \log C$. However, the $m^{1+o(1)}$ factor hides intricate recursive data structures, large constants and multiple log factors. In this paper, we give an implementation following the core ideas of their IPM with practical data structures and empirically obtained decision rules. We compare our solver with the cost scaling and network simplex solvers of LEMON on the instance families of the DIMACS Flow Challenge 2.0 core benchmark. Our implementation scales competitively on five of twelve families and better on two. On grid_wide we observe close to linear scaling: $m^{1.04}$ against $m^{1.48}$ for LEMON. We read these results as first evidence that the almost-linear-time framework can be relevant in practice, discuss our insights gained during the implementation process, and motivate where future work should focus to bridge the theory-practice gap.
Optimization and Control.comment: Submitted to the 13th DIMACS Implementation Challenge: Network Flows 2.0

Optimization and Control.title: Lyapunov characterization of boundedness of reachability sets for infinite-dimensional systems
Optimization and Control.summary:
We prove a converse Lyapunov theorem for boundedness of reachability sets for a general class of control systems whose flow is Lipschitz continuous on compact intervals with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. We show that this condition is satisfied by broad classes of semilinear evolution equations.
  For ordinary differential equations, as a consequence of our results, we obtain a converse Lyapunov theorem for forward completeness, without a priori restrictions on the magnitude of inputs. As an example, we rederive Wintner's classical result using our Lyapunov approach.

Optimization and Control.title: On Over-Conservatism Under Low-Probability Extreme Events: A KL-Regularized Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Planning Method
Optimization and Control.summary: The increasing penetration of renewable energy makes power systems more vulnerable to low-probability extreme events, elevating system planning to a critical role in ensuring reliability. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) based on the Wasserstein distance is widely used to address this challenge. However, we find that the conventional Wasserstein ambiguity set tends to excessively amplify the probabilities of low-probability extreme events, leading to over-conservative investment decisions. To mitigate this over-conservatism, this paper proposes a novel ambiguity set that modifies the Wasserstein distance with a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence regularization term. By leveraging the KL divergence's sensitivity to relative probability changes, the proposed set effectively curbs the unrealistic magnification of low-probability events. A two-stage distributionally robust planning model built upon this new ambiguity set is developed to optimize the installed capacity of photovoltaic, wind, and energy storage. The complex model is then reformulated as an equivalent exponential cone program with strict theoretical proofs, making it computationally tractable. Numerical results on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems reveal the over-conservatism of standard Wasserstein DRO under low-probability extreme events and validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed planning model and solution algorithm.

Optimization and Control.title: Improved Analysis of Adaptive Task Allocation and Non-Stationary Processing Times
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the task allocation problem, where our goal is to develop an online algorithm that efficiently distributes tasks among workers based on their computational performance. This task is challenging since computation times are random and non-stationary in practice. Recent works have introduced different online algorithms to address this problem. One of them is Adaptive Task Allocation (ATA), a bandit-style algorithm. However, previous theoretical guarantees leave substantial room for improvement, and existing methods are designed only for stationary computation times. Using new proof techniques, our work establishes an improved analysis of ATA with better gap-dependent and gap-independent regret guarantees, improving upon all previous approaches. We also introduce a new method, Sliding Window Adaptive Task Allocation (SW-ATA), designed for more practical non-stationary environments. Finally, we prove new lower bounds in both the stationary and non-stationary settings.

Optimization and Control.title: Composite and Stochastic Smoothed Decentralized Bregman Proximal-Gradient Methods
Optimization and Control.summary: Smoothed decentralized Bregman proximal-gradient (SDBPG) methods combine relative-smoothness geometry with edge-dual consensus. We extend SDBPG to node-specific convex nonsmooth regularizers and unbiased stochastic local gradients while retaining its Bregman primal-dual smoothing mechanism. The analysis isolates temporal subgradient motion and aggregation mismatch as two defect sequences. For trajectories in a forward-invariant compact subset of the kernel domain and admissible parameters, finite accumulated defects yield an $O(T^{-1})$ bound on the squared best-iterate proximal residual over $T$ iterations. The stochastic bound separates accumulated oracle variance from expected defects and attains the same order when the variance bounds and expected defects are summable. Common active-structure identification, together with local subgradient conditions, gives sufficient finite-defect conditions for $\ell_1$ and group $\ell_{2,1}$ regularization. Experiments with common regularizers and heterogeneous sensing operators relate defect decay to observed support stabilization and compare reconstruction and communication with decentralized proximal and gradient-tracking methods. A separate phase-retrieval study evaluates the effect of a quartic Bregman kernel. Code and experiment scripts are available at https://github.com/shengze-xu/composite-stochastic-sdbpg .

Optimization and Control.title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
Optimization and Control.summary: We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. A six-node network with nine unknown coefficients has exactly two compatible parameter vectors generically. Adding six excited and measured nodes preserves this ambiguity while making the added coefficients directly recoverable. The resulting twelve-node structure has forty-two independent unknown coefficients and zero diagonal. For every positive bound on the largest eigenvalue magnitude, a nonempty open set of parameters has two distinct compatible networks satisfying that bound. This holds for both real and complex coefficients. Other open regions have exactly one admissible solution. The proof uses a rational transformation exchanging the two solutions and a common limiting matrix whose fourth power vanishes. Exact rational-number certificates verify an explicit pair. The construction also extends algebraically when the unknown coordinates are whole rational transfer functions. Genericity in prescribed numerator and denominator coefficient families, and the requirement that every transfer function vanish at infinite frequency, remain separate questions.

Optimization and Control.title: Hyperelastic Modeling of Cardiac Tissue Deformation for Data Registration
Optimization and Control.summary: This work proposes a biomechanical registration framework designed to combine functional optical-mapping data with structural high-resolution MRI of cardiac tissue. The two acquisitions are performed in different mechanical configurations: optical mapping is obtained after stretching the sample, whereas MRI is acquired in a fixed resting state. To estimate the deformation between these configurations, the tissue is modeled as a nearly incompressible transversely isotropic hyperelastic material, and the traction amplitude is identified from optical-map marker positions through an inverse problem. Two-and threedimensional simulations show physically admissible deformations and provide a first proof of concept for the proposed strategy.

Optimization and Control.title: Amplitude-Dependent Bode Diagrams via Scaled Relative Graphs
Optimization and Control.summary: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide an intuitive graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of Nonlinear (NL) systems, generalizing the Nyquist diagram. In this paper, we develop a method for computing $L_2$-gain bounds for Lur'e systems over bounded frequency and amplitude ranges. We do this by restricting the input space of the SRG both in frequency and energy content, and using methods from Sobolev theory. The resulting gain bounds over restricted sets of inputs are less conservative than bounds computed over the entire $L_2$, and yield three-dimensional NL generalization of the Bode diagram, plotting $L_2$-gain as function of both input frequency and energy content. In the zero-energy limit, the Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Bode diagram is recovered, and at the infinite-energy zero-frequency limit, we recover the $L_2$-gain. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated on an example that resembles Phase-Locked Loop dynamics.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS). This is the author's version, see the copyright notice in the PDF/source file

Optimization and Control.title: UQ-ACE: Stability-Aware Counterfactual Controller Tuning via Bayesian SINDy
Optimization and Control.summary: Retuning feedback controllers in critical processes is challenging when experiments are costly, open-loop excitation is infeasible, and candidate controllers must be screened before deployment. The existing Adaptive Sampling for Counterfactual Explanations (ACE) method provides a sample-efficient approach for finding minimal controller-parameter changes that recover prescribed closed-loop performance, but it does not explicitly account for stability of candidate controllers proposed during the search, which may be destabilizing under plant uncertainty. This paper introduces UQ-ACE, a stability-aware retuning method based on Bayesian SINDy. In UQ-ACE, closed-loop trajectories are used to infer a posterior distribution over local dynamical models, from which candidate controllers are screened for stability before implementation. Extensive simulations show that UQ-ACE achieves valid retunings with few closed-loop experiments while preventing deployment of unstable candidates.

Optimization and Control.title: Sample-Efficient Counterfactual Tuning for Compressor Pressure Control
Optimization and Control.summary: In controlled industrial environments, ensuring safety and performance during controller tuning is a challenging and critical task. In particular, control loops in compressor-plenum-throttle systems cannot tolerate costly interruptions, and aggressive excitation may lead to unsafe operating regimes. Given the wide availability of historical data, this paper introduces a counterfactual explainability approach for sample-efficient retuning of compressor control loops. The proposed data-driven algorithm determines, without an explicit plant model or previous control law, the smallest controller adjustment required to achieve predefined performance specifications while guaranteeing stability. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through an extensive Monte Carlo simulation study.

Optimization and Control.title: Identifiability of a dissipative knowledge-dynamics model: exact recovery under designed excitation, degeneration on observational data
Optimization and Control.summary: Human learning is a dissipative dynamical process: mastery accumulates through practice, decays through forgetting, and propagates across interdependent concepts. We model it as a nonlinear dissipative system of ordinary differential equations whose parameters are mechanistically meaningful (a transfer-of-practice matrix, per-concept forgetting rates, and a saturating practice-response gain), and we study when those parameters can actually be recovered from data. For two concepts, we prove a constructive structural identifiability theorem for the associated inverse problem under explicit excitation conditions, together with monotonicity, robustness and L-stability results. We derive an implicit L-stable scheme and a batched solver numerically equivalent to the per-trajectory formulation (bit-exact predictions, gradients to $10^{-10}$) yet two orders of magnitude faster, making estimation feasible on cohorts of $2.5\times10^4$ learners. The empirical study is two-sided. Under the theorem's excitation conditions, synthetic recovery is exact: parameters to machine precision, coupling structure at $F_1 = 1.0$. On large observational benchmarks it is not. An apparently strong recovery, with forgetting rates correlating with topic error rates at Spearman $ρ= 0.83$, is refuted by four controls: it survives destroying the temporal order of the data, is matched by a classical Bayesian baseline, and is unaffected by removing real timestamps. We trace this to the stationary structure of the model and show that it is consistent with the degeneration anticipated by the theory in the absence of designed excitation. The result delineates a boundary between identifiable and unidentifiable regimes and motivates controls for interpretability claims.
Optimization and Control.comment: corrected the implicit integration scheme and the box-preservation statement of Proposition 4; revised the proof of Lemma 1; specified the construction of the practice input, the difficulty reference and the rank; moderated claims linking the theorem to the observational failure; added relation to companion work and an AI-use declaration. Code: https://github.com/armankostanian/cognitive-pinn

Optimization and Control.title: A Smoothed Augmented Lagrangian Method for Mathematical Programs with Vertical Complementarity Constraints
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a smoothed augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) for solving mathematical programs with vertical complementarity constraints (VCCs). The augmented Lagrangian function involving the VCCs is smoothed by the Lasry--Lions double envelope, which is an extension of the Moreau envelope that enjoys enhanced smoothness properties. This construction yields a smooth unconstrained subproblem within the ALM framework that can be efficiently solved by many fast optimization algorithms. In the limiting setting, we establish global convergence to Mordukhovich- and Clarke-stationary points.
