Probability.title: A unified spectral analysis of high-dimensional linear regression: debiasing and thresholding
Probability.summary: We use spectral analysis to establish a unified theory of debiasing, thresholding, and simultaneous inference for high-dimensional linear regression with ill-conditioned designs. The methods include Ridge regression, spectral cut-off, and iterative and dynamical regression procedures. A common debiasing procedure uses two applications of the original linear algorithm with fixed parameters. Spectral analysis shows that debiasing squares the residual, while implementations based on matrix-vector products require no explicit spectral decomposition. Under explicit design, signal, and moment conditions, we establish maximum-norm consistency, recovery of the population threshold set, and error bounds for coefficient and noise-variance estimation. We derive Gaussian approximations for maximum coordinate errors and, under full column rank and deterministic sequences of regression parameters and thresholds, prove bootstrap validity for simultaneous confidence regions. Under additional regularity and gain conditions, we relate noise-free bias rates to best-worst-case error rates. Sparse and non-sparse regression experiments examine the effects of debiasing and thresholding under specified tuning rules. An elliptic inverse source problem extends the numerical assessment to reconstruction and empirical simultaneous coverage.

Probability.title: Closed-form evaluation of the cumulative distribution function and absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution
Probability.summary: Closed-form formulas are derived for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution. As a special case, closed-form expressions are deduced for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute central moments of the product of two correlated zero-mean normal random variables.

Probability.title: Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes
Probability.summary: This is preliminary, AI-generated note on the Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes postulated by M. Talagrand based on the unpublished notes of the authors and the recent note \cite{invariant} which in turn is an alternative proof of the result by Hu, Wang, Wu.

Probability.title: Poincaré inequalities, logarithmic growth and doubling
Probability.summary:
We investigate when a Poincaré inequality forces the underlying measure to be doubling, with particular attention to the space \(X\) controlling the oscillation. We identify \(L\log L\) as the sharp threshold: under a natural local growth condition on the measure, doubling is forced precisely when \(L\log L(0,1)\not\hookrightarrow X\). We also obtain a doubling criterion under a weaker geometric assumption when the oscillation norm is sufficiently stronger than \(L\log L\).
  We show that this threshold is sharp in every fixed Euclidean dimension, using a dimension-free local \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality for log-concave measures and non-doubling Gaussian examples. We then turn to infinite-dimensional spaces, where doubling is impossible for the measures under consideration. Nevertheless, the \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality continues to hold, and we establish sharp characterizations for infinite product models, Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces under power-type small-ball estimates, and Wiener measure with the uniform norm.

Probability.title: Denseness in total variation and the class of rational-infinitely divisible distributions
Probability.summary: We study a new class of so-called rational-infinitely (or quasi-infinitely) divisible probability laws on the real line. The characteristic functions of these distributions are ratios of the characteristic functions of classical infinitely divisible laws and they admit Lévy--Khinchine type representations with ``signed spectral measures''. This class is rather wide and it has a lot of nice properties. For instance, this class is dense in the family of all (univariate) probability laws with respect to weak convergence. In this paper, we consider the questions concerning a denseness of this class with respect to convergence in total variation. The problem is considered separately for different types of probability laws taking into account the supports of the distributions. A series of ``positive'' and ``negative'' results are obtained.

Probability.title: Resolvent intertwining and spectral duality in Markov chains with geometric resetting
Probability.summary: We uncover the resolvent origin of the spectral duality governing reset-neutral distributions in Markov chains with geometric resetting. Starting from the abstract conditions of Paper~III, we show that the spectral duality $B_ν(z)=κ(z)\,A_ν(σ(z))$ is equivalent to a single symmetry of the resolvent $R(γ)=(I-(1-γ)P)^{-1}$: the intertwining relation $[Δ^2\mathcal{R},R(γ)]=0$, where $\mathcal{R}$ is the reflection operator of an involution $σ$ and $Δ=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{κ(z)})$; equivalently, $\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}=K^{-1/2}Δ^2\mathcal{R}$ is an involution. This symmetry determines the universal critical value $C^*=1/(1+\sqrt{K})$, with $K=κ(z)κ(σ(z))$, which depends only on the scalar $K$ --- not on the resetting rate $γ$, the reset distribution, or the particular chain. We characterize the class of $(σ,κ)$-reversible chains, encompassing both the biased random walk and genuinely non-homogeneous dynamics sharing the same $C^*$; a Doob $h$-transform realizes the duality $K\mapsto1/K$, hence $C^*\mapsto1-C^*$, with fixed point $C^*=1/2$. The orientation field admits the explicit resolvent representation $ψ(γ)=R(γ)(b^{(0)}-C^*b)$: its gauge-normalized form $Δ^{-1}ψ(γ)$ is antisymmetric under $σ$, it has an exact node at the fixed point of $σ$, and it governs the exact sign law $\operatorname{sgn}(C(π,γ)-C^*) =\operatorname{sgn}\langleπ,ψ(γ)\rangle$. Numerical experiments confirm the theory to machine precision. These results establish the operator-theoretic foundation of the spectral duality of Paper~III and provide the bridge to the information-geometric framework of Paper~V.

Probability.title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
Probability.summary: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes. The key tool is a structure theorem valid for an arbitrary permutation and an arbitrary positive weight: every insensitive distribution is supported on a union of cycles balanced at a common level, and the level of a cycle is fixed by the geometric mean of the weight on it. From it, positivity selects the admissible root, the constant orbit product is equivalent to the existence of an insensitive distribution of full support, and the involution is equivalent to the response rank being equal to the number of free weight parameters. Without the duality relation, insensitivity of a single distribution is cheap and generically isolated; duality turns it into structural neutrality of the separatrix. The full-rank condition splits into two layers: a weaker condition is equivalent to maximal response rank, while full rank also excludes insensitivity at any other level. We then show that a single SDS is internally rigid: compatible semigroup structures force a constant weight, compatible abelian group structures obey a precise arithmetic condition, congruences form a simple lattice, and the automorphism group is computed explicitly. Finally, the axioms do not determine the orientation of the response; in the two-site case we give the exact condition under which the geometric and analytic sign criteria agree.

Probability.title: The rank evolution of block bidiagonal matrices over finite fields
Probability.summary:
We investigate uniform random block lower bidiagonal matrices over the finite field~$\mathbb{F}_q$, and prove that their corank undergoes a phase transition.
  First, we consider block lower bidiagonal matrices with $(k_n+1)\times k_n$ blocks where each block is of size $n\times n$. We prove that if $k_n\ll q^{n/2}$, then the corank of these matrices is $0$ with high probability, and if $k_n\gg q^{n/2}$, then the corank has Gaussian fluctuations.
  Second, we consider block lower bidiagonal matrices with $k_n\times k_n$ blocks where each block is of size $n\times n$. We prove that if $k_n\ll q^{n/2}$, then the corank exhibits the same constant order fluctuations as the corank of the matrix products considered by Nguyen and Van Peski, and if $k_n\gg q^{n/2}$, then the corank has Gaussian fluctuations.
  Finally, we also consider a truncated version of the first model, where we prove that at $k_n\approx q^{n/2}$, we have a phase transition between a Cohen-Lenstra and a Gaussian limiting behavior of the corank. We also show that there is a localization/delocalization phase transition for the vectors in the kernels of these matrices at the same critical point.
  In all three cases, we also provide a precise description of the behavior of the corank at criticality.

Probability.title: $\mathcal{D}$-Pullback Measure Attractors of McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Lattice Wave Equations
Probability.summary: This paper deals with the pullback measure attractor for a non-autonomous distribution-dependent stochastic lattice wave equation with nonlinear noise on $\mathbb{Z}$. We establish well-posedness in the energy space $\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2}$ and show that the solution generates a continuous non-autonomous dynamical system on $\mathcal{P}_{4}(\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2})$, which possesses a unique pullback measure attractor $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, we prove the convergence of the attractor $\mathcal{A}^{\varepsilon}$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^{+}$ to the attractor of the corresponding distribution-independent limit system.

Probability.title: Limit theorems for the number of sign and level-set clusters of the Gaussian free field
Probability.summary:
We study the limiting fluctuations of the number of sign and level-set clusters of the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 3$, that are contained in a large domain. In dimension $d \ge 4$ we prove that the fluctuations are Gaussian at all non-critical levels, while in dimension $d=3$ we show that fluctuations may be Gaussian or non-Gaussian depending on the level. We also show that the sign clusters experience a form of Berry cancellation in all dimensions, that is, the fluctuations of the sign cluster count are suppressed compared to generic levels.
  Our proof is based on controlling the Wiener-Itô chaos expansion of the cluster count using percolation theoretic inputs; to our knowledge this is the first time that chaos expansion techniques have been applied to analyse a non-local functional of a strongly correlated Gaussian field.

Probability.title: Large deviation principles for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations on unbounded channel-like domains
Probability.summary: This paper investigates the large deviation principle for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations driven by multiplicative noise and defined on an unbounded channel-like domain. We first prove the existence and uniqueness of probabilistically strong solutions for the stochastic equation under small noise perturbations by means of the local monotonicity method. Subsequently, we show the well-posedness of solutions to the corresponding control equation and the convergence in distribution of the solutions for the stochastic equation as the noise intensity tends to zero. Finally, we establish the Freidlin-Wentzell type large deviation principle for the solutions of the stochastic equation by using the weak convergence method. To overcome the lack of compactness of Sobolev embedding on unbounded domains, we employ a scalar stream function together with a truncation technique to derive uniform tail estimates for the solutions of the control equation.

Probability.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
Probability.summary: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished.

Probability.title: Optimal information loss for Liouville spectral responses
Probability.summary: We study Fisher information about the amplitude of a known smooth mean shift from the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and spatial responses of a Liouville random medium. The complete response record determines the speed measure and the Gaussian free field, whereas every finite record strictly loses information; an optimal design exists in each finite-dimensional probe space. We quantify this gap as the known Liouville parameter $γ$ tends to zero. If the probe space contains an explicit matching probe, the minimum loss equals $γ^2$ times a positive compression error for a deterministic second-chaos operator, up to $o(γ^2)$, with designs allowed to depend on $γ$. After enlarging the probe dictionary, the optimal $m$-response coefficient is asymptotic to $\|Lg\|_{L^1(D)}^2/(8m)$, where $L=-(2π)^{-1}Δ_D$ on the unit disk $D$. A quadratic correction of the readouts attains the same fixed-design loss to second order.

Probability.title: Classical and Quantum Information Measures Characterizing Convertibility: An Axiomatic Approach
Probability.summary: In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate Rényi divergences. Unlike previous studies, we do not require the distributions to have the same support, yielding interesting new divergences. In the quantum setting, we consider pairs of classical-quantum states with pure component states, and find that majorization is characterized by all $α$-$z$ relative entropies for $α<1$. This demonstrates the first operational interpretation of these relative entropies.
Probability.comment: PhD thesis at the Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore; contains corrections of some minor errors appearing in the published papers that this thesis is based on

Probability.title: Commutative diagram of the Gross-Pitaevskii approximation
Probability.summary: It is well-known that the Gross-Pitaevskii variational formula describes the ground-state energy per particle of $N$-indistinguishable trapped particles (Bosons) in a dilute state in the large system size $N\to\infty$. The goal of the present article is to prove that the Gross--Pitaevskii formula also appears in the iterated limit of zero temperature and large system size of the product ground-state energy per particle of the $N$-particle Hamiltonian operator. For fixed particle number $N$, we moreover identify the low-temperature limit of the Brownian model with mutual intersection-local-time interaction as the ground-product-state energy per particle of the corresponding $N$-body system with repulsive Dirac interaction. This proves the conjectures of Adams, König and Bru from arXiv:math/0411660 and arXiv:math/0512305.
Probability.comment: Same results, reworked proofs, comments welcome

Probability.title: Limiting distributions of the rightmost eigenvalue of the truncated circular Unitary ensemble across all truncation regimes
Probability.summary: We study the limiting distribution of the largest real part of the eigenvalues of truncated unitary matrices. Let \(U_m\) be an \(m\times m\) Haar-distributed unitary matrix, and let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be the eigenvalues of its upper-left \(n\times n\) principal submatrix. We determine the limiting distribution of \(\max_{1\le i\le n}\Re Z_i\) under a unified normalization: the limiting law is Gumbel when $q:=m-n\to\infty$ and is of Weibull type when $q$ is fixed. The fixed-\(q\) limiting laws converge to the Gumbel law as \(q\to\infty\). We also give a unified formulation of the normalizing constants for the spectral radius that recovers the previously known limiting laws.

Probability.title: How fast does spectral radius of truncated circular unitary ensemble converge?
Probability.summary:
Let $z_1, \cdots, z_p$ be the eigenvalues of $A,$ which is the left-top $p\times p$ submatrix of an $n\times n$ Haar-invariant unitary matrix. Suppose there exist two constants $0<h_1<h_2<1$ such that $h_1<\frac pn<h_2.$ Then,
  $$\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}}|\mathbb{P}(X_n\le x)-e^{-e^{-x}}|=\frac{(\log \log n)^{2}}{2e\log n}(1+o(1))$$ and further
  $$ W_{1}\left(\mathcal{L}(X_n),Λ\right)=\frac{(\log\log n)^2}{2\log n}(1+o(1))$$
  for $n$ large enough. Here, $Λ$ is the Gumbel distribution and $\mathcal{L}(X_n)$ is the distribution of $X_n$ with $X_n$ being some rescaled version of $\max_{1\le i\le p}|z_i|,$ the spectral radius of $A.$
Probability.comment: We plan to abandon this result

Probability.title: A Proof of the Erdős Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
Probability.summary:
We resolve a conjecture of Łuczak, Mieczkowska and Šileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove
  \[
  \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1)
  =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\},
  \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions.
  Using this result, we prove the Erdős Matching Conjecture for every fixed $k\ge3$, all sufficiently large $s$, and every $n\ge k(s+1)$. More specifically, we show that in this range, the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges is
  \[
  \max\left\{
  \binom{k(s+1)-1}{k},
  \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k}
  \right\}.
  \] Moreover, every extremal family consists either of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set or of all $k$-sets contained in a fixed $(k(s+1)-1)$-set.

Probability.title: Local properties for $1$-dimensional critical branching Lévy process
Probability.summary:
Consider a one dimensional critical branching Lévy process $((Z_t)_{t\geq 0}, \mathbb {P}_x)$. Assume that the offspring distribution either has finite second moment or belongs to the domain of attraction to some $α$-stable distribution with $α\in (1, 2)$, and that the underlying Lévy process $(ξ_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is non-lattice and has finite $2+δ^*$ moment for some $δ^*>0$. We first prove that $$t^{\frac{1}{α-1}}\left(1- \mathbb{E}_{\sqrt{t}y}\left(\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{t^{\frac{1}{α-1}-\frac{1}{2}}}\int h(x) Z_t(\mathrm{d}x) -\frac{1}{t^{\frac{1}{α-1}}} \int g\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{t}}\right)Z_t(\mathrm{d}x)\right\}\right)\right)$$
  converges as $t\to\infty$ for any non-negative bounded Lipschtitz function $g$ and any non-negative directly Riemann integrable function $h$ of compact support.
  Then for any $y\in \mathbb{R}$ and bounded Borel set of positive Lebesgue measure with its boundary having zero Lebesgue measure, under a higher moment condition on $ξ$, we find the decay rate of the probability $\mathbb {P}_{\sqrt{t}y}(Z_t(A)>0)$. As an application, we prove some convergence results for $Z_t$ under the conditional law $\mathbb {P}_{\sqrt{t}y}(\cdot| Z_t(A)>0).$
Probability.comment: 37 pages. Updated some information of the references

Probability.title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
Probability.summary: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{é}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$.

Probability.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
Probability.summary: Let $μ_q$ be the distribution of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and let $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be the Sato--Tate law. We prove $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s\le2$, $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6-1/(3s)}$ for $2\le s<\infty$, and $W_\infty(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6}$, answering a question of Kowalski and Untrau. More generally, we bound $W_s(μ,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})$ for all $s$ whenever the Chebyshev moments of $μ$ satisfy bounds of Katz type. For $s=2$ the bound also follows from a smoothing inequality of Borda and Cuenin; for $s>2$ and $s=\infty$ our bounds are stronger. The proof uses the quantile coupling, which arises from Stieltjes sums over two different intervals whose cells are paired so as to balance two measures, and which is optimal for all $s$ simultaneously; an explicit $W_2$ smoothing inequality relative to $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$; and a sharp comparison between $W_s$ and the Kolmogorov distance for laws with square-root edges. The last result shows that $q^{-1/6}$ is the best rate for $W_\infty$ obtainable from Niederreiter's discrepancy bound. Numerically, for primes $10^3<p<10^6$, all these distances appear to decay like $p^{-1/2}$.

Probability.title: Translators asymptotic to vertical hyperplane
Probability.summary: We prove that a vertical hyperplane is the only complete translator, properly immersed in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ ($n \ge 3$) and having finite topology, whose ends are $C^1$-asymptotic to vertical hyperplanes.

Probability.title: On the $L^p$ Norms of Random Exponential Sums and the Metric Domination Principle over the Simple Random Walk
Probability.summary: Let $R(n)$ denote the Simple Random Walk on $\mathbb{Z}$. We investigate the $L^p$-norms of random exponential sums of the form $S_A(a, y) = \sum_{j \in A} a_j e^{2πi y R(j)}$ evaluated on the torus $\mathbb{T}$, where $A$ is an arbitrary finite subset of $\mathbb{N}$. By establishing a strict inductive bound on the central binomial coefficient, we precisely estimate the collision probability kernel of the random walk. To address the non-monotonicity of the walk, we introduce a Metric Domination Principle, proving that the $L^2$-energy of the random sum over any sparse set $A$ is majorized by that of a contiguous initial segment of integers of the same cardinality. Interpolating between $L^\infty$ and $L^2$, we show that for any $p \ge 2$, the expectation of the supremal $L^p$-norm over all bounded coefficients is universally bounded by $C_p |A|^{p-1/2}$.

Probability.title: Generalized Mean-Reflected McKean--Vlasov BSDEs: Well-Posedness and a Markovian PDE Representation
Probability.summary: This paper investigates a class of generalized mean-reflected McKean--Vlasov type backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs). Our new framework combines a mean reflection constraint on the solution's expectation with a generalized integral with respect to a continuous non-decreasing process. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution. The uniqueness is derived via stability estimates, while the existence is proved by employing a penalization method combined with a smooth approximation of the obstacle. We further study a Markovian case, where the equation reduces to a nonlocal parabolic PDE with a mean constraint. We establish the well-posedness and the probabilistic representation of this problem, and we describe the regularity of the multiplier in terms of the regularity of the obstacle.

Probability.title: Fourier entropy of threshold functions and their compositions
Probability.summary: We prove the Fourier entropy--influence inequality for every linear threshold function, with a constant below $8.937$ and no restrictions on its weights or threshold. The argument applies to regular Boolean functions and gives logarithmic bounds for their Boolean combinations and for unions with bounded variable overlap. Character multiplication preserves the estimates and yields bounds by influence minus variance. Under arbitrary product measures, symmetric thresholds satisfy the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition, uniformly in depth and fan-in. A joint description of each Fourier set refines the overlap estimate and recovers constant bounds for addressing. Exact selector identities extend the bound to orthogonal multiplexers with shared data. Rare activation preserves the optimal constant of unrestricted FEI. The proofs combine pivotal antichains, spectral reference measures, and product-measure composition.

Probability.title: A Generalized Elephant Random Walk with Time-Dependent Memory
Probability.summary: The elephant random walk (ERW) is a discrete-time random walk with complete memory. At every step the walker chooses one of the previous increments at random and then either repeats with a constant probability $p\in [0,1]$ or reverses it. Since its introduction by Schütz and Trimper, the model has become a useful probabilistic framework for studying long-range dependence, anomalous diffusion, reinforcement, and phase transitions. This paper proposes a generalized ERW model with time-dependent memory. In this generalized model, the usual constant memory parameter $p$ in the standard ERW is allowed to change with time. The cental limit theorems, and the law of the iterated logarithm and some other strong laws are obtained.

Probability.title: On the Regularity of Reaction Systems
Probability.summary: Reaction networks have been widely used as generic models in diverse areas of applied sciences, such as biology, chemistry, ecology, epidemiology, and computer science. A reaction network incorporating noisy effects is modeled as a continuous time Markov chain (CTMC) and is called a stochastic reaction system. In contrast, the mean field limit of a sequence of volume-scaled stochastic reaction systems as the volume tends to infinity is modeled as an ordinary differential equation (ODE) and is called a deterministic reaction system. Non-explosivity of CTMCs and global existence of solutions of ODEs capture the regularity of respective dynamical processes. In this paper, we study the regularity of reaction systems, in both stochastic and deterministic senses. By constructing a simple linear Lyapunov function, we obtain the regularity in both senses for a class of reaction systems in terms of a simple checkable condition. In particular, we prove that (a) every binary mass-action system is regular, and (b) every second-order endotactic mass-action system is regular. We apply our results to diverse models in biochemistry, epidemiology, ecology, synthetic biology, and natural computing in the literature.

Probability.title: Delta functions, a local coarea formula and marginal distributions
Probability.summary: We define multidimensional delta functions as generalized functions by pulling back the Dirac delta function, as well as products of such. We prove various formulas including a local version of the coarea formula and we use delta functions to compute marginal probability distributions on spheres.

Differential Geometry.title: A nonlinear Li-Yau inequality and its consequences
Differential Geometry.summary:
We prove a sharp nonlinear analogue of the Li-Yau inequality for positive solutions of the normalized parabolic $p$-Laplacian equation \[ u_t = Δu + (p-2)|
abla u|^{-2}
abla^2u(
abla u,
abla u),\ \ \ 1<p<\infty, \] on a closed Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the equation being interpreted in the viscosity sense on the critical set of the solution. We also derive a sharp global Harnack inequality from the gradient estimate.
  The constant is best possible. Equality holds identically for an explicit self-similar solution in $\Rn$, and sharpness on closed manifolds follows by taking the limit along the flat tori $\mathbb R^n/(L\mathbb Z)^n$ as $L 	o \infty$. The proof rests on an exact Bochner-type identity for a family of uniformly parabolic approximating flows. We choose the first-order term separately from the second-order regularization so that the maximum principle yields the sharp constant, uniformly in the regularization parameter and without any assumption on the critical set of the solution.
  Using this Bochner identity with a modified Li-Yau functional, we extend the estimate to closed manifolds with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -κ$.
Differential Geometry.comment: Reorganized version of the original Aug 28, 2026, submission. All results are unchanged

Differential Geometry.title: Compactness of Cone Yang-Mills Connections
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider the cone Yang-Mills functional recently introduced by Tseng and Zhou. This functional generalizes the Yang-Mills functional by coupling it to a closed 2-form which can represent a geometric structure of interest, e.g. a symplectic form or Ricci form. While the perspective of dimensional reduction is not always possible, we show that a cone Yang-Mills field is always locally the dimensional reduction of a pure Yang-Mills field. We then prove a monotonicity formula and use the dimensional reduction framework to prove an $ε$-regularity theorem in two ways. Finally, we prove a compactness theorem for sequences of cone Yang-Mills connections with bounded action and $L^p$-bounded Higgs fields. Away from a singular set of codimension at least 4 and after suitable bundle identifications, the sequence subconverges in the $C^\infty_{\operatorname{loc}}$-topology.

Differential Geometry.title: On the Morse index of nonorientable minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute the Morse index of several complete nonorientable minimal surfaces immersed in Euclidean three-space. In particular, we prove that the Meeks minimal Möbius band has Morse index two, which is the least possible Morse index for such nonorientable minimal surfaces, by previous works of Ros and Chodosh-Maximo. This is the first known minimal surface with index two. We show that the López minimal Klein bottle has Morse index three. As a consequence of this computation, we extend results in the literature and observe that any complete minimal surface immersed in Euclidean three-space with total curvature $8 π$ has Morse index three. We also compute the Morse index of the Oliveira family of minimal Möbius bands in terms of their total curvature and show that every non-negative integer is the Morse index of a complete minimal surface immersed in Euclidean three-space. We show that five is a sharp lower bound for the Morse index of any minimal oriented double cover in Euclidean three-space, and equality is attained by the double cover of the Meeks minimal Möbius band. Finally, we prove results towards the classification of complete minimal surfaces with Morse index two immersed in Euclidean three-space, obtaining topological and geometric restrictions on such surfaces.
Differential Geometry.comment: 56 pages, 1 figure. Minor revision. A Mathematica notebook has been attached to the submission

Differential Geometry.title: Classification of the geodesic curves of the sub-Riemannian LR system on the Heisenberg group in dimension 5
Differential Geometry.summary: We study sub-Riemannian structures obtained by the restriction of the standard left-invariant Riemannian metric to a right-invariant completely nonholonomic distribution on the second Heisenberg group. The corresponding Hamiltonian system is completely integrable and in this paper we study its solutions. We obtain a complete classification of the geodesic curves by studying the reduced Hamiltonian system. Moreover, we compute $r(t)$ as the first step of the quadrature in the reduced system in the hyper-spherical coordinates and present numerical examples that illustrate the theoretical results.

Differential Geometry.title: Vanishing of $\ell^p$-cohomology and transportation cost
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, it is shown that the reduced $\ell^p$-cohomology is trivial for a class of finitely generated amenable groups called transport amenable. These groups are those for which there exist a sequence of measures $ξ_n$ converging to a left-invariant mean and such that the transport cost between $ξ_n$ displaced by multiplication on the right by a fixed element and $ξ_n$ is bounded in $n$. This class contains groups with controlled Følner sequence (such as polycylic groups) as well as some wreath products. Note: Examples 5.1 and 5.2 are incorrect (in particular $\mathbb{Z} \wr \mathbb{Z}$ and $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})\wr \mathbb{Z}^2$ are not transport amenable); an erratum and addendum is appended to this version.
Differential Geometry.comment: 12 pages (original paper); followed by an erratum and addendum 12 pages. Examples 5.1 and 5.2 are incorrect

Differential Geometry.title: On the collapsing of spaces with local rewinding Reifenberg control
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(M^n,g_0)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with $\Ric_{g_0}\ge-(n-1)g_0$ whose local universal covers are uniformly $δ$-Reifenberg-close to $\R^n$ below a fixed radius $ρ$. We show that for every $α\in(0,1)$ there are $δ(n,α)>0$ and $T(n,ρ,α)>0$ such that, if $δ\leδ(n,α)$, a complete Ricci flow $g(t)$ with $g(0)=g_0$ and $|\Rm_{g(t)}|\leα/t$ exists on $(0,T]$. On closed manifolds this is a uniform lower bound for the lifetime of the Ricci flow; on noncompact manifolds, where the initial curvature may be unbounded, it is an existence theorem, and the flow is unique among complete Ricci flows from $g_0$ with a curvature bound of the form $A/t$. The key step is a finite-buffer comparison of two Ricci flows through the Ricci--harmonic map heat flow, following Lee, which transfers a Type-I curvature bound from a complete selected flow to the incomplete flow lifted to a local cover. Consequently, below a dimensional Reifenberg threshold, collapsing closed manifolds admit singular nilpotent fibrations over their Gromov--Hausdorff limits. The Reifenberg hypothesis cannot be weakened to noncollapsing of the local covers: products of shrinking circles with Nifa's four-manifolds have $\Ric\ge0$ and uniformly noncollapsed local covers, but admit no continuous Gromov--Hausdorff approximations onto their limit.

Differential Geometry.title: Symplectic symmetries of a hypothetical exotic $CP^2$: a potential construction or a nonexistence proof
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper is primarily concerned with the existence of a symplectic $4$-manifold, homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $CP^2$, which admits a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism. We reduced the existence of such an exotic $CP^2$ to a question in contact geometry. More concretely, we showed that there are precisely $12$ plumbed manifolds, each equipped with a canonical contact structure associated to the plumbing, such that an exotic $CP^2$ with a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism exists if and only if one of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds admits a certain specific symplectic filling. As the main technical result, we completely determined the order and local representations of a pseudofree symplectic $Z_p$-action for an odd prime $p$ on a rational homology $CP^2$ with positive canonical class. Our result suggests that potentially, there are symplectic $Z_p$-actions which are not a finite automorphism of a fake projective plane. Moreover, we introduced a construction, which, under the minimal assumptions on the symplectic fillings of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds, produces a symplectic $4$-manifold on the Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau line via a reverse-engineering process.
Differential Geometry.comment: Minor corrections and improvements, added key words and phrases and MSC, 65 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables

Differential Geometry.title: Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $λ$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $λ$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.
Differential Geometry.comment: 45 pages, 1 figure. v3: new title, shorter abstract and introduction. Minor corrections throughout

Differential Geometry.title: Laplacian Algebras and Subcalibrations for Minimal Hypercones
Differential Geometry.summary: We develop an algebraic mechanism based on Laplacian algebras for constructing minimal hypercones and determining their variational properties. Generator counts and degrees organize the constructions; homogeneous multipliers depending on the generators yield subcalibration fields, stability bounds and quantitative area-minimizing inequalities. Two-generator isoparametric algebras give polynomial subcalibrations for their minimizing hypercones. In ambient dimension at least three, strict gradient-square closure forces nonlinear odd degree to be cubic. We then study algebras of degrees $(2,2,g)$ and quadratic compositions, placing OT--FKM splitting quartics and Riedler's pullbacks in a common quadratic-composition framework. It yields two further infinite quartic families with a sharp minimizing threshold, as well as harmonic sextics from complex Gram coordinates. For an irreducible harmonic minimal cubic on its essential space, we prove a sharp bound of five generators for its smallest Laplacian algebra. We determine the minimizing range of Clifford cubics and construct irreducible nonradial harmonic examples in ambient dimensions $8,14,26$; the last is strictly area minimizing. Finally, spectral families whose smallest algebras have arbitrarily many generators provide examples in every degree at least two: real parts of octonionic products, complex Pfaffians and complex determinants. Explicit potentials establish strict area minimality and stability bounds, including across nonisolated singularities. The algebraic identities and certificates are supported by reproducible exact symbolic computations.
Differential Geometry.comment: 166 pages. Substantially revised and expanded, with new results on Laplacian algebras and constructions of minimal hypercones. Mathematica verification code and execution records are available on GitHub

Differential Geometry.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.

Differential Geometry.title: The index of conformal Hopf maps
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute the index and nullity of any harmonic morphism from $S^3$ to $S^2$.

Differential Geometry.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
Differential Geometry.summary:
Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Frączyk, Mellick, and Wilkens (arXiv:2307.01194) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and Ünel (arXiv:2303.16831). In this paper we introduce and study ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on higher rank symmetric spaces. We show that ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with respect to polyhedral Finsler metrics can exhibit either behavior seen in these previous works: generically they resemble the hyperbolic case, where almost surely all cells have bounded sides.
  We further introduce the ideal Selberg--Poisson--Voronoi tessellation of the space of positive definite symmetric matrices, which has particularly nice properties.
Differential Geometry.comment: 72 pages, 20 figures. Comments and suggestions are welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Identifiability and Consistent Recovery for the Unnormalized Graph Laplace Operators
Differential Geometry.summary: We study whether an unnormalized graph Laplace operator can determine both the geometry of a manifold and its sampling density. On a fixed compact smooth manifold without boundary, we use a known positive, continuous, strictly decreasing radial kernel at a fixed positive bandwidth. For positive sampling densities, the operator built from geodesic distances determines the Riemannian metric and identifies the density up to equality almost everywhere. When the metric is induced by a Euclidean embedding, the operator built from ambient distances also determines the embedding up to rotations, reflections and translations, and the density. On compact parameter classes with positive continuous densities, minimizing the distance between empirical and popula- tion operators gives estimates that converge to the true parameters under independent, identically distributed sampling. This recovery result assumes that the empirical operator can be evaluated at arbitrary points of the manifold.

Differential Geometry.title: Intrinsic Rigidity of Bar-and-Joint Frameworks on Riemannian Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We develop an intrinsic rigidity theory for bar-and-joint frameworks whose vertices are constrained to a Riemannian manifold and whose edges are given by minimizing geodesic arcs. Such frameworks are called rigid if they cannot be deformed beyond the ambient isometries, while preserving the geodesic edge lengths. For admissible placements, for which adjacent vertices are joined by unique minimizing geodesics, we define a coordinate-free rigidity operator as the differential of the squared geodesic distance of the edges. By the first-variation formula, its edge rows are expressed in terms of the Riemannian logarithm, providing an intrinsic analogue of the classical Euclidean rigidity matrix. Trivial motions are characterized by orbits of the diagonal action of the isometry group, leading to notions of infinitesimal and local rigidity. We further develop a covariant second-order rigidity theory using the Riemannian Hessians of the edge constraints and characterize second-order rigidity through self-stresses and associated quadratic forms. Finally, we show that infinitesimal and second-order rigidity can be used as sufficient conditions for the local rigidity of an intrinsic framework. Our overarching goal is to provide a unified differential-geometric formulation of intrinsic framework rigidity on smooth manifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: Intrinsic Geometry Matching: learning observation-equivariant process geometry
Differential Geometry.summary: Real data are often arbitrary, indirect observations of an unknown underlying process, and those observations can distort its geometry. Existing geometric methods equip data with the induced geometry of the ambient space, but this entangles the true geometry of the process with the distortion of the observation. To address this, we introduce Intrinsic Geometry Matching (IGM): a scalable approach to learn the intrinsic geometry of the underlying process. Specifically, we learn the carré du champ operator of the process, allowing us to recover its diffusion geometry. Our method uses the fact that data often come with natural perturbations, like steps in a time series, to recover the intrinsic carré du champ while transforming naturally with changes in observation: it is observation-equivariant. Furthermore, since this equivariance relates the geometry of different spaces, we can train a model using additional sources of data, even when that data lies in another space. We evaluate IGM on molecular dynamics, image, and video data and find better performance and scaling than existing neural and graph-based geometric tools.

Differential Geometry.title: Spectral and Nodal Properties of Static Manifolds with Boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We study compact static manifolds with boundary from a spectral point of view, with particular emphasis on the relation between Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin spectra and the nodal structure of static potentials. We establish comparison inequalities linking Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues with the scalar curvature and derive sufficient spectral conditions ensuring that a static potential changes sign. We also obtain bounds on the number of connected components of the zero set, sufficient conditions for its connectedness, and sufficient conditions ensuring that its components intersect the boundary. Finally, we study variational properties of Robin static triples and characterize compact Robin static triples whose metrics are critical for the first mixed Robin--Dirichlet eigenvalue under admissible volume-preserving deformations.

Differential Geometry.title: Prüfer $2$-group and Milnor's Conjecture on Fundamental Groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct complete, one-ended Riemannian manifolds in dimensions four and five having strictly positive Ricci curvature, with fundamental group isomorphic to the Prüfer $2$-group $C_{2^\infty}$ and any subgroup $Γ\leq \mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, respectively. This gives counterexamples to Milnor's conjecture in the two remaining dimensions.
Differential Geometry.comment: 69 pages; improved exposition, add full construction for all subgroups of $\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ in 5 dimension, and the complete description of volume growth

Differential Geometry.title: The Adiabatic b-Calculus and the Global Anomaly Formula on Manifolds with Boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the determinant line bundle for a family of elliptic operators on compact manifolds with boundary with the associated Quillen metric and Bismut-Freed connection, and we prove the global anomaly formula in this context. This extends Witten's holonomy theorem to manifolds with boundary. Witten studied the limiting behavior of the eta invariant of a Dirac operator on the total space of a fibration over $\mathbb{S}^1$ when the metric in the base $\mathbb{S}^1$ is blown up in a certain manner, a process known as taking the adiabatic limit. In this paper, we construct the calculus of adiabatic $b$-pseudodifferential operators, which naturally synthesizes the $b$-calculus and the adiabatic calculus of pseudodifferential operators. Using this calculus, and assuming the fiber operators to be invertible, we compute the adiabatic limit of the natural eta invariant in this setting and relate it to the integral of the Bismut-Freed connection and new correction terms coming from the boundary of the fibers.

Differential Geometry.title: Non-algebraicity of the Lawson surfaces $ξ_{k,l}$
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every Lawson surface $ξ_{k,l}\subset\mathbb S^3$ of genus $kl>1$ is non-algebraic: any real polynomial vanishing on $ξ_{k,l}$ vanishes identically on $\mathbb S^3$. This answers a question posed by Hsiang in 1967 and proves Lawson's 1970 conjecture for $ξ_{2,2}$. The proof uses a reflection principle for the monodromy of the associated family of flat connections.

Differential Geometry.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
Differential Geometry.summary:
The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $σ: \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $Λ$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in Λ} \|σ_i -σ_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $σ_{|\partial Λ}$.
  One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main Hölder regularity statement in a large domain $Λ\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $σ$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the Hölder regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $σ\in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial Λ}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces).
  The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$.
  We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.

Differential Geometry.title: Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in complex space forms
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $M$ be a connected Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surface of constant Gaussian curvature $K$ in a two-dimensional complex space form $\Mtilde^2(4ε)$ of constant holomorphic sectional curvature $4ε$, and let $H$ denote its mean curvature vector field. We prove that either $K=ε$ or $K=0\neε$ and $|H|$ is constant. In particular, if $|H|$ is non-constant, then $K=ε$.

Differential Geometry.title: Positive sectional curvature on homotopy nine-spheres
Differential Geometry.summary: We determine which homotopy nine-spheres admit positive sectional curvature: they are precisely the four smooth types with vanishing real Dirac index. The other four admit no metric of nonnegative sectional curvature. In particular, we construct a strictly positively curved metric on the exotic Kervaire nine-sphere, answering the longstanding nonnegative-curvature existence question in this dimension. The proof keeps explicit attaching maps throughout. A quaternionic commutator realizes the Kervaire sphere, a mixed representation realizes the Hopf image of the exotic eight-sphere, and a four-periodic normal-framing formula identifies the remaining index-zero class. Following the compatible-disk method, we give the curvature and boundary estimates for the first two models, including an explicit lower bound for the Kervaire metric in terms of the curvature and first covariant-derivative norms of a fixed connection, with the base scale and fiber normalization fixed. For the third model, we construct a positive metric on a cylinder joining a quotient metric to its pullback by a marked right Hopf twist. A four-form modification controls the connection terms involving both left and right quaternionic multiplication. Two positive disk fillings close the cylinder with the prescribed attaching map. A local convolution lemma supplies the smooth gluing while preserving a strict sectional-curvature lower bound.

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp parameter gaps for quantized Mabuchi energies and cscK metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: For polarized manifolds, we show that semistability for the quantized Mabuchi energy at one fixed finite parameter is equivalent to uniform K-stability and to unique existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler (cscK) metrics. We obtain sharp comparisons between quantized Mabuchi slopes at different parameters and with the ordinary Mabuchi slope. In the presence of automorphisms, we give an equivariant criterion using torus twists under the vanishing of the Futaki character. The estimates also hold for finite-energy geodesic rays in compact Kähler classes. On a fixed ruled surface with discrete automorphism group, we construct cscK polarizations with unbounded critical parameters. Their ratios to the $α$-invariant are also unbounded.

Differential Geometry.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_θ$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

Differential Geometry.title: Minimal time for heat observability on almost-Riemannian surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-Riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple Baouendi-Grushin circles. The structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. The formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. Regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. For singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. We also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. Their superpositions give a lower bound for the Schrödinger observation time.

Differential Geometry.title: Ricci pinching on complete Kahler manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We study Ricci pinching problem on complete Kähler manifolds. For complete noncompact manifolds with Euclidean volume growth, we prove flatness under nonnegative bisectional curvature and Ricci pinching, and Ricci flatness under nonnegative Ricci curvature, quadratic curvature decay, and the same pinching condition. In both cases, the pinching constant may tend to zero at a logarithmic rate. Examples show that the logarithmic exponent is sharp in complex dimension two. Second part of the paper proves that a complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension at least two with positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is compact if its sectional curvature is nonnegative and its Ricci curvature is uniformly pinched outside a compact set. No volume-growth assumption or curvature upper bound is needed. Heat smoothing of the Busemann function supplies a strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion with bounded gradient, so the general top Ricci-mass theorem of Datar--Pingali--Seshadri applies. The new ingridents are integral estimates for the Ricci form. The analytic arguments use scalar curvature gap theorems and a critical-$L^n$ vanishing theorem for closed real $(1,1)$-forms under nonnegative Ricci curvature and nonnegative quadratic orthogonal bisectional curvature. The Hodge-Laplace heat eqution deformation conserves the signed top-degree integral, including its initial value, while norm domination and scalar heat-semigroup decay force this integral to vanish. For semipositive initial forms this gives pointwise vanishing of the top wedge power.

Differential Geometry.title: Graphon as a Bridge between Graphs and Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that there exist graphons that interpolate between Riemannian manifolds and weighted geometric graphs. Specifically, the graph-to-manifold approximation used in manifold learning can be regarded as the composition of a graph-to-graphon convergence and a graphon-to-manifold convergence in a certain sense. Furthermore, we establish a monotonicity inequality which reveals an implicit relationship between numerous combinatorial parameters and geometric quantities on graphons. Using this inequality, we find relations among conductance, maxcut problem, capacity, and packing radius, as well as their limiting behaviors under graph-to-graphon and graphon-to-manifold convergences; some of these relations are novel even for simple graphs and closed manifolds. We also find that in the graphon-to-manifold limiting process, the purely combinatorial parameters diverge, leading to a ``blowup'' phenomenon; and continuous versions of some graph parameters cannot be realized via Riemannian manifolds, but can be realized via graphons.

Differential Geometry.title: Stability of Minkowski-type inequalities in certain warped product spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper explores the stability of Minkowski-type inequalities for hypersurfaces in warped product spaces. We establish a stability estimate that bounds the norm of the traceless second fundamental form of the hypersurface in terms of the deficit in the Minkowski inequalities satisfied by the hypersurface. Additionally, we prove the stability of Minkowski inequalities in specific cases of the Reissner-Nordström Anti-de Sitter (RN-AdS) and Anti-de Sitter Schwarzschild (AdS-Schwarzschild) manifolds, which serve as examples of warped products. We also establish a new rigidity result for locally conformally flat manifolds to understand the stability of these inequalities.

Differential Geometry.title: The triangular metric on projective surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: In \cite{ThurstonStretch} Thurston introduced stretch paths and stretch maps between hyperbolic surfaces. In this paper we extend similar constructions to the space of convex real projective structures on surfaces. Using Fock-Goncharov-like parameters, we introduce stretch paths and construct explicit stretch maps between the projective surface. We show that stretch maps are $e^t$--Lipschitz with respect to a triangular metric we introduce on the projective surface. This allows us to gain control on several length functions on an open set of the space of convex real projective structures (those where there is no ``local back--tracking"). As an application we obtain pointwise upper bounds for the Hilbert entropy of some convex real projective structures in terms of Fock-Goncharov-like parameters.

Differential Geometry.title: On the Weyl tube formula for nonlocal perimeters
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the nonlocal perimeter of tubular neighbourhoods. For a closed $C^{1,1}$ submanifold of Euclidean space, we show that a suitable rescaling of the nonlocal perimeter of its tube converges to an explicit constant times the Hausdorff measure of the submanifold. The constant is the fractional perimeter of the unit ball in the codimension of the submanifold. For finite point sets, we obtain an exact tube formula in terms of a generalised hypergeometric function. In contrast with the classical Weyl formula, this expansion has infinitely many terms, contains both noninteger and integer powers of the tubular radius, and has coefficients that depend on the relative positions of the points rather than only on their intrinsic geometry. We also establish a point-set expansion for general analytic kernels.

Differential Geometry.title: Biconservative hypersurfaces in Euclidean Spaces
Differential Geometry.summary:
An isometric immersion $X: Σ^n \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is biharmonic (BHH) if
  $Δ^2 X = 0$, i.e., if $ΔH =0$, where $Δ$ and $H$ are
  the metric Laplacian and the mean curvature vector field of $Σ^n$ respectively. 
  More generally, biconservative hypersurfaces (BCHs) are isometric immersions for which only the tangential part of the biharmonic equation vanishes.
  BCHs are first described and then constructed.

Differential Geometry.title: Prescribing the mean curvature of an achronal hypersurface as a measure: the case of 3D spacetimes
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the existence problem for achronal hypersurfaces $M \hookrightarrow \overline{M}$ in a globally hyperbolic spacetime, whose mean curvature is a prescribed -- possibly singular -- source, and whose boundary is a given smooth spacelike submanifold. Since $M$ is allowed to go null somewhere, the mean curvature prescription is to be understood in the distributional sense. We prove a general existence and regularity theorem for surfaces in ambient dimension $3$. Although most of our estimates hold in any dimension, recent counterexamples show that some of our conclusions fail in ambient dimension at least $5$. The case of $4$D-spacetimes is an open problem. Our theorems have application to Born-Infeld electrostatics in general static spacetimes.

Differential Geometry.title: Four-dimensional almost-Einstein manifolds with circulant structures
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper considers a four-dimensional Riemannian manifold with an additional circulant tensor structure $Q$. We prove that such a manifold is almost-Einstein if the curvature tensor preserves the action of the structure on the last two arguments. Additionally, we examine an associated Riemannian product manifold $(M, g, Q)$ where $P=Q^{2}$, deriving explicit expressions for the curvature tensor in terms of the metric and the product structure. The sectional and Ricci curvatures of these manifolds are determined using special bases generated by the images of a given vector under the structure $Q$. Finally, we construct a non-trivial example of a four-dimensional locally product manifold by embedding a four-dimensional hypersurface into a ten-dimensional Euclidean space.

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity and volume pinching for the sharp gradient estimate in positive Ricci curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: Colding established a sharp gradient estimate for the Green function on manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature, which was extended to positive Ricci curvature by Manea recently. We prove almost rigidity of such gradient estimates for positive Ricci curvature. We show that the average of the gradient deficit, namely $\fint (1-|\nabla b|^2)\,dV$, controls the volume deficit in an optimal quantitative manner; here $b$ is the distance-like function defined using the Green function. This implies a quantitative almost rigidity theorem for manifolds with $\ric\ge(n-1)g$ and a gap theorem for Einstein manifolds. We also prove a rigidity theorem for closed 4-dimensional Einstein manifolds by finding a new monotonicity formula.
Differential Geometry.comment: exponent in Theorem 1.1 improved to be optimal; overall exposition improved

Differential Geometry.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the relation between canonical positivity, rigidity of a prescribed Hermitian metric, and the curvature not detected by Chern holomorphic sectional curvature. A compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold admitting an independent smooth plurinegative Hermitian metric is projective with ample canonical bundle. In Fujiki's class, nonpositive constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature forces the original metric to be Kähler. On compact complex threefolds, without an auxiliary metric or a Fujiki-class assumption, a nonzero constant forces Kählerness. We also give an alternative proof of Chen--Zheng's Chern-flatness theorem for zero-HSC threefolds, by proving local rank-two differential compatibility and localizing their curvature bound under $\partialη=0$. In contrast, for every complex dimension at least seven we give compact balanced zero-HSC metrics with nonzero Chern curvature. Their octonionic curvature formula also implies the vanishing of all four Chern--Ricci contractions, and an explicit invariant volume form is Chern parallel. Finally, an auxiliary semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form, positive definite at some point, restores flat Kählerness under zero HSC and vanishing first Chern--Ricci tensor. A mixed Ricci integral criterion explains the role of this last curvature hypothesis.

Differential Geometry.title: Optimal Synthesis on the Special Linear Group
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the exponential map on the group of real two-by-two matrices with determinant one, endowed with a left-invariant Riemannian metric. Using the Euler-Poincaré equation and its linearization, we determine the conjugate and Maxwell times and identify a domain on which the exponential map is a global diffeomorphism onto the complement of the Maxwell stratum. This provides an alternative proof that the first Maxwell time coincides with the cut time. We obtain an explicit matrix description of the cut locus and characterize the globally minimizing geodesics. Furthermore, we analyze the first Maxwell-time function, determine its unique global minimum, and show that the injectivity radius is $\frac{π\sqrt{14}}{4}$. Finally, we characterize the intersection of the cut and conjugate loci and prove that every geodesic is equi-optimal.

Differential Geometry.title: Higher order isoperimetric inequalities and rigidity for surfaces in $\R^n$
Differential Geometry.summary:
We establish a family of sharp higher order isoperimetric type inequalities for smooth compact surfaces in Euclidean spaces of arbitrary codimension. These inequalities involve arbitrarily high derivatives of the boundary curve, together with the mean curvature vector of the surface. For example, the first and second order inequalities yield the sharp two-sided estimate for the isoperimetric deficit: \begin{align*} & \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA \le L^2-4πA\\ \le& \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA +\fracπ{3R}\int_{\partial M}|x+R^2κ|^2\, ds, \end{align*} where $R=\frac{L}{2π}$ and the origin is chosen to be the centroid of the boundary. For minimal surfaces, equality in the lower bound holds precisely for flat disks, whereas the second inequality admits non-round equality cases. Our results extend that of Carleman, Sachs, Chakerian, and Li-Schoen-Yau.
  A distinctive feature of our work is the unexpected rigidity structure arising at higher orders. At the first and second orders, equality curves admit decompositions into circular Fourier modes supported in mutually orthogonal planes. Remarkably, this phenomenon fails at higher orders. We establish a multiplicative factorization of the unit tangent map into elementary planar rotations acting on a fixed unit vector, providing a characterization of equality cases at arbitrary order. As a result, we construct a third order equality curve in $\mathbb R^3$ whose Fourier modes cannot be decomposed into mutually orthogonal circular modes.

Differential Geometry.title: A Dimension Estimate for Polynomial Growth Holomorphic Functions
Differential Geometry.summary: On a complete noncompact Kähler manifold $M^n$ of complex dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature, we prove that polynomial growth holomorphic functions of degree $d$ ($d\geq 0$) have an dimension upper bound $C(n)(1+d)^n$. In particular, $\dim_{\C}\OO_d(M)\leq C'(n)d^n,$ for $d\geq1$, and the estimate is sharp.

Differential Geometry.title: Steady gradient Ricci Yang-Mills solitons on 2-orbifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Following the recent work of M. Womack \cite{Wo26} we consider the steady Ricci Yang-Mills solitons on 2d surfaces containing orbifold point $\mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}_p$. We show that there are a family of solitons depending parameter $λ$ which approaches to $\mathbb{Z}_p$-quotient of Hamilton cigar soliton as $λ\to (-2/p)^+$ and approaches to (after rescaling) $\mathbb{Z}_p$-quotient of round sphere as $λ\to \infty$. For any integer $q >p$ there is a $λ$ whose corresponding soliton metric is defined on football orbifold $S_{p,q}^2$.

Differential Geometry.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $λ$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(λ^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\logλ)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.

Differential Geometry.title: Conformal Renormalisation of 8D Einstein Gravity
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that Holographic Renormalisation (HR) in eight dimensions is encoded in the unique conformal gravity theory that admits an Einstein sector with constant negative curvature. We explicitly relate HR to Topological Regularisation (TR), where the latter prescribes to add the Euler term to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian density, with a precise coefficient so as to ensure that the resulting density is polynomial in the anti de Sitter (AdS) curvature. The polynomial is still asymptotically divergent. We find that the aforementioned, unique conformal gravity action in 8D, reproduces the polynomial, together with extra boundary terms that cancel the divergent terms in the action. We conjecture that, in arbitrary even dimension, HR is equivalent to conformally completing the Einstein-Hilbert action with negative cosmological constant, plus the Euler term with fixed coupling prescribed by TR.
Differential Geometry.comment: 20+1 pages, no figure; V2: typos and minor corrections fixed

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp degree bound for rational proper maps from $\mathbb B^2$ to $\mathbb B^4$
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every rational proper holomorphic map from $\mathbb{B}^2$ to $\mathbb{B}^4$ has degree at most $5$, confirming D'Angelo's conjecture in this case. This sharp bound follows from Meylan's degree estimates and an intersection-theoretic argument ruling out degree $6$.

Geometric Topology.title: Asymptotics of rational representations for algebraic groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the cohomology of subgroups $Γ$ of an algebraic group $G$ with coefficients in the various irreducible rational representations of $G$ and raise a conjecture about it. Namely, we expect that the dimensions of these cohomology groups approximate the L2-analogues of Betti numbers of $Γ$ with a controlled error term. We provide positive answers when $G$ is a product of copies of $SL_2$.

Geometric Topology.title: Purely non-free actions on Riemann surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary:
A group of conformal automorphisms of a Riemann surface is said to act purely non-free, or to produce a gpnf-action, if each of its finite-order elements has fixed points.
  It is known that every finite group admits a gpnf-action on a suitable closed Riemann surface of genus at least two. If $G$ is an infinite countable group, and $X$ is an infinite-type orientable surface, without planar ends and whose space of ends is self-similar, then we observe that there is a Riemann surface structure on $X$ admitting a gpnf-action by $G$.
  We obtain upper bounds for those finite groups producing a gpnf-action on a closed Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$.
  If $G$ is a finite group, then its purely non-free genus $σ^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$ is the minimum genus of at least two of a closed Riemann surface admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. This parameter is already known for cyclic, abelian non-cyclic groups, ${\mathcal A}_{4}$, ${\mathcal A}_{5}$ and ${\mathfrak S}_{4}$. For general $G$, we provide the value of $σ^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$, correcting a previous statement on this value. In particular, we observe that every genus is the purely non-free genus of some group.
  As an application, we describe the minimal purely non-free actions for the family of metacyclic groups $G^{0}_{s}(n)=\langle x,y: x^{n}=y^{2}=1, yxy=x^{s}\rangle,$ where $n \geq 3$ and $2 \leq s \leq n-1$ is such that $s^{2} \equiv 1 \mod(n)$.

Geometric Topology.title: Point Processes and Gap Statistics for Translation Surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the behavior of saddle connection directions on translation surfaces from the point process viewpoint. We define a direction point process for saddle connections of length at most $R>0$ on every translation surface. Given a general ergodic $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$-invariant measure $μ$ on a stratum of translation surfaces, we also define a slope point process associated with $μ$. By utilizing the dynamics and geometry of strata, we show that for almost every translation surface, the direction point processes, rescaled by $R^2$, converge in distribution to the slope point process as $R\to\infty$. Using Palm distribution theory, we prove the existence of limiting joint gap distributions and obtain new regularity results for gap distributions associated with the general $μ$. Finally, we study how these point processes and joint gap distributions behave as the genus $g$ tends to infinity. In the principal stratum, we show that the slope point processes, rescaled by $g^2$, converge in distribution to a Poisson point process. By passing to the corresponding Palm distributions, we show that the rescaled slope gaps converge jointly to independent exponential random variables, which is in stark contrast to the known non-exponential gap distributions in a fixed genus.

Geometric Topology.title: Turaev cobracket, synthetic geometry and applications
Geometric Topology.summary: A teardrop geodesic on a hyperbolic surface is a closed curve that is geodesic except at exactly one point, called its vertex. One imagines a closed curve with one point held down as it deforms to a geodesic. For each teardrop geodesic, we give an explicit geometric construction of the closed geodesic in its free homotopy class. This construction also yields a relation between the length of the teardrop geodesic, the angle at its vertex, and the length of its geodesic representative. We then apply the construction to a self-intersecting closed geodesic at a chosen self-intersection point. Since, at that point, the geodesic splits into two directed teardrop geodesics, our construction gives a geometric description of Turaev's cobracket in terms of geodesic representatives. Using this description we prove that if two self-intersection points yield a pair of canceling terms in the cobracket, then the angle at these points and the lengths of the small loops determined are the same.

Geometric Topology.title: Symplectic symmetries of a hypothetical exotic $CP^2$: a potential construction or a nonexistence proof
Geometric Topology.summary: This paper is primarily concerned with the existence of a symplectic $4$-manifold, homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $CP^2$, which admits a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism. We reduced the existence of such an exotic $CP^2$ to a question in contact geometry. More concretely, we showed that there are precisely $12$ plumbed manifolds, each equipped with a canonical contact structure associated to the plumbing, such that an exotic $CP^2$ with a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism exists if and only if one of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds admits a certain specific symplectic filling. As the main technical result, we completely determined the order and local representations of a pseudofree symplectic $Z_p$-action for an odd prime $p$ on a rational homology $CP^2$ with positive canonical class. Our result suggests that potentially, there are symplectic $Z_p$-actions which are not a finite automorphism of a fake projective plane. Moreover, we introduced a construction, which, under the minimal assumptions on the symplectic fillings of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds, produces a symplectic $4$-manifold on the Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau line via a reverse-engineering process.
Geometric Topology.comment: Minor corrections and improvements, added key words and phrases and MSC, 65 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables

Geometric Topology.title: Mock Modularity, Resurgence, and Dual False Theta Functions
Geometric Topology.summary: The $\hat{Z}$ invariant of a three-manifold $M_{3}$, a half-index of the $3d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_{3}]$, is well understood for negative-definite plumbed three-manifolds. For orientation-reversed manifolds, however, the known formulas fail to produce $q$-series, and making sense of the operation $q \rightarrow q^{-1}$ remains a central open problem. Seifert manifolds, whose $\hat{Z}$ invariants are built from false theta functions, offer a natural testing ground. We study ``dual false theta functions'', the objects that should replace false theta functions under orientation reversal.
