For vanishing thresholds, we establish convergence of the corresponding posterior distributions in total variation. In the large-sample regime, we identify conditions under which the posterior converges to the prior conditioned on an asymptotic compatibility region, showing that concentration need not occur at a fixed positive tolerance. We also derive persistence bounds under weaker assumptions and prove stability of the associated entropy-regularized variational problems. For Wasserstein discrepancies, we obtain a geometric representation through distances from compatibility balls and an exact variational reduction to probability distributions over model laws.

Differential Geometry.title: Strongly isotropy irreducible spaces whose Laplacians have all their eigenspaces irreducible
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $H$ be a closed subgroup of a compact connected Lie group $G$ such that $G/H$ is simply connected, the action of $G$ on $G/H$ is almost effective, and $G/H$ is a strongly isotropy irreducible space. The smallest positive eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator $Δ$ associated to the standard metric on $G/H$ was recently computed. In this article we obtain a second non-zero eigenvalue of $Δ$.
  As a consequence, we prove that all eigenspaces of the Laplacian are irreducible as $G$-modules if and only if $(G,H)$ is a compact symmetric pair of real rank one, or $(G,H)$ is equal to $(\operatorname{G}_2,\operatorname{SU}(3))$ or $(\operatorname{Spin}(7),\operatorname{G}_2)$.

Differential Geometry.title: A Bernstein Theorem for the Self-Shrinking $J$-Equation and Some Generalizations
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every entire smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution of the self-shrinking $J$-equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a quadratic polynomial. This removes the asymptotic lower bound assumption on the complex Hessian in \cite[Theorem 4]{HJ}. The result also recovers the corresponding real rigidity theorem in \cite[Theorem 1.1]{HOW} as a special case. More generally, our method applies to self-shrinking equations associated with a broad class of fully nonlinear elliptic operators satisfying suitable structural conditions, including the adjacent inverse complex Hessian quotient operators $-σ_{k-1}/σ_{k}$, $1\leq k\leq n$. For the remaining quotients $-σ_l/σ_k$ with $l<k-1$, we prove the same rigidity conclusion under the additional assumption that the solution is proper.
Differential Geometry.comment: Updated to the version submitted to a journal on August 5, 2026, with minor clarifications. Includes a rigidity theorem for proper solutions of general inverse complex Hessian quotient self-shrinker equations

Differential Geometry.title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.

Differential Geometry.title: Anomaly Flow II: Estimates and Long-time Existence for the Coupled Flow
Differential Geometry.summary: In this follow-up to \cite{Sua25}, we extend the results to the coupled anomaly flow which incorporates the evolution of a Hermitian metric on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact complex $3$-fold with general slope parameter $α'$. This yields a similar sufficient smallness condition on the slope parameter $α'$ in order to extend the flow on $[0, τ)$ to $[0, τ+ ε)$. We also augment the argument of \cite{Sua25} slightly to fix the peculiarity of the units in the condition for $α'$ for the $k = 1$ case.

Differential Geometry.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.

Differential Geometry.title: Morse Index of a $G_2$-Instanton over $S^7$
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we determine the nonpositive spectrum of the Yang-Mills Jacobi operator in Coulomb gauge at the standard $G_2$-instanton on $S^7$. We prove that the only negative eigenvalue is $-3$, with multiplicity $8$, and the kernel has dimension $20$. Thus the connection attains the sharp lower bound for the Morse index of nonflat Yang-Mills connections on $S^7$. We also give an explicit description of the kernal of the Jacobi operator, which contains Waldron's $15$-dimensional deformation space for the fixed nearly parallel $G_2$-structure. The 5 additional zero modes are isometry-induced variations that do not satisfy the corresponding linearized instanton equation.

Differential Geometry.title: Timelike surfaces of constant mean and constant Gaussian curvature in anti-de Sitter 3-space via loop groups
Differential Geometry.summary: The loop group description of surfaces whose Gauss map is Lorentz harmonic is known for timelike surfaces of constant mean curvature in the flat Lorentzian 3-space, and for surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in the 3-sphere. We carry out the corresponding construction for timelike surfaces in anti-de Sitter 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3_1\cong SL(2,\mathbb{R})$: those of constant mean curvature, whose Gauss map is harmonic for the conformal structure of the first fundamental form, and those of constant Gaussian curvature $K>-1$, $K\neq0$, whose Gauss map is then an immersion and is harmonic for the second fundamental form. For both classes we prove the harmonicity characterization, recover the surfaces from extended frames by Sym-Bobenko-type formulas, and solve the geometric Cauchy problem by the generalized DPW method, with potentials written explicitly in terms of the data and no normalization of the Gauss map. We then show that the two constructions differ only by a normalization: after the substitution $λ=ζ^2$ and a constant gauge, a constant mean curvature extended frame $\hat F$ is an extended frame of its Gauss map, and the maps $\hat F|_{λ=e^{4θ}}\exp(θe_3)\hat F|_{λ=1}^{-1}$ and $e_3\hat F|_{λ=e^{4θ}}e_3\exp(θe_3)\hat F|_{λ=1}^{-1}$, with $e_3=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$, are timelike surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature $1/\sinh^2θ$ and $-1/\cosh^2θ$ wherever the constant mean curvature surface is not flat. The first is the classical parallel surface, the second its polar surface. Explicit families, with extended frames and surfaces in closed form, illustrate the constructions.

Differential Geometry.title: Global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for complex Monge--Ampère equations on compact Kähler manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Ampère equation with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side on a compact Kähler manifold.

Differential Geometry.title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{λ,μ}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities ($λ\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $μ\in\mathbb{R}$).

Differential Geometry.title: A concise proof of homogeneity of an isoparametric hypersurface with $(g, m)=(6, 2)$
Differential Geometry.summary: A well-known hypersurface classification theorem states that any isoparametric hypersurface in $S^{13}$ with six principal curvatures is homogeneous. This landmark result was first proved in her Annals paper in 2013 by R. Miyaoka with 58 pages, and with errata in Annals in 2016 with 15 pages. The main purpose of this paper is to provide a concise proof of this theorem through an interplay between topological and geometric insights into the Euler class of an oriented vector bundle.
Differential Geometry.comment: The title has been revised, and an acknowledgment and a remark have been added

Differential Geometry.title: Geometric and topological rigidity of pinched submanifolds in Riemannian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the rigidity of compact submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Riemannian manifolds satisfying a pinching condition involving the norm of the second fundamental form and the mean curvature. In contrast to the corresponding earlier results, the pinching condition is not required to hold strictly. Allowing equality gives rise to richer and subtler geometric and topological phenomena. By analyzing the nonstrict boundary case in arbitrary ambient manifolds, we obtain a classification of the possible intrinsic geometries and topologies of the submanifold, together with restrictions on its extrinsic geometry. We also provide several families of examples satisfying the pinching condition, showing that the conclusions cannot, in general, be strengthened to extrinsic rigidity statements. The resulting theorems extend several known results in the literature, particularly sphere theorems, to the nonstrict setting while removing several additional geometric or topological assumptions appearing in earlier results.

Differential Geometry.title: Orbit stratifications and smooth topology of positively curved six-manifolds with rank-one nonabelian symmetry
Differential Geometry.summary: We study closed simply connected six-manifolds with positive sectional curvature and an effective isometric action of $SO(3)$ or $SU(2)$. Starting from Liu's corrected orbit-space analysis, we refine the stratification and recover smooth topology in several previously unresolved cases. For a boundaryless $SO(3)$ quotient, singular isotropy is connected, the weighted nonprincipal graph belongs to nine necessary families, and every action with only cyclic exceptional isotropy is classified equivariantly. The remaining branching families admit explicit rational intersection and Pontryagin formulas. For a three-ball $SO(3)$ quotient, the uniform-boundary configurations give sphere bundles over $S^4$ and a completely distinguished odd-integer family of non-spin six-manifolds. A doubled-quotient argument excludes the configuration with two boundary fixed points and an interior singular orbit, while the configuration with one fixed point and an exceptional interval has underlying manifold $\mathbb{CP}^3$. For a boundaryless $SU(2)$ quotient, an adjoint-weight matching argument reduces the exceptional three-orbit case to a unique action on the Eschenburg flag and identifies every two-orbit candidate with a weighted action on $S^2\times S^4$. These classifications imply rational ellipticity throughout the stated symmetry class. We also establish restricted curvature obstructions for the two diagonal product actions, without asserting nonexistence for arbitrary invariant metrics. Abstract graph restrictions, smooth realizability, and positive-curvature realizability are kept distinct. Some of the results in this paper are discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors.
Differential Geometry.comment: 33 pages, 1 figure. Some of the results in this paper are discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors. Comments are welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity of Immersed Gauss Curvature Shrinkers in Euclidean Space
Differential Geometry.summary:
For every $m\geq2$, we prove that any connected closed oriented smooth immersion $X:M^m\to\mathbb{R}^{m+1}$ satisfying \[
  K=\left\langle X,ν\right\rangle \] is an embedding onto the unit sphere. No convexity is assumed. At a point maximizing $|X|$, we find a strictly convex component of $\{K>0\}$. If this component does not coincide with $M$, its polar immersion bounds an unbounded convex set. A finite area lemma then extends the local surface area formula for the polar body to a global measure identity. Using the vanishing first moment of surface area measure, we show that the origin lies in the interior of the polar body, contradicting the existence of recession directions. Thus the hypersurface is strictly convex, and the classification of strictly convex shrinkers completes the proof.

Differential Geometry.title: Localization of Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
Differential Geometry.summary:
For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith.
  The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.

Differential Geometry.title: Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework
Differential Geometry.summary:
This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincaré-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems.
  Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.

Differential Geometry.title: Properness and finiteness of totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core
Differential Geometry.summary: We study totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core of geometrically finite rank-one locally symmetric manifolds. Although the infinite-volume setting can exhibit highly complicated behavior, including geodesic planes with fractal closures, we show that a strong rigidity persists inside the convex core. This rigidity has striking consequences in the infinite volume setting: every maximal totally geodesic submanifold of dimension at least two contained in the convex core is properly immersed and has finite volume, and only finitely many such submanifolds can occur. These results stand in sharp contrast to the behavior in the finite-volume setting. Moreover, combining this finiteness result with the work of Bader-Fisher-Miller-Stover and of Gromov-Schoen, we deduce that any geometrically finite rank-one manifold with infinitely many maximal totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two and of finite volume must be arithmetic.
Differential Geometry.comment: 32 pages, 1 figure, Final version, To appear in Geometry & Topology

Geometric Topology.title: Boundary of Anosov coaffine representations
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $Γ\le \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group dividing a properly and strictly convex domain $Ω\subset \mathbb R\mathrm P^d$, and let $ρ: Γ\to \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be the inclusion. We study representations of $Γ$ into the coaffine group that are deformations of $ρ\oplus 1 \in \mathrm{Hom}(Γ, \mathrm{GL}(d+2,\mathbb R))$ and that lie on the boundary of the locus of projective Anosov representations. In this setting, we identify a canonical limit set $Λ$ for the action and study its fine geometric features which are, in a suitable sense, stable. We prove the existence of an ending lamination that encodes the failure of the Anosov condition and the non-existence of a Cannon--Thurston map. Under certain conditions, we compute the Hausdorff dimension and show that the corresponding measure is positive.

Geometric Topology.title: Some non-trivial cycles of the space of long embeddings detected by configuration space integral invariants using g-loop (g =2, 3) graphs
Geometric Topology.summary: In this paper, we give some non-trivial geometric cycles of the space of long embeddings R^j --> R^n (n-j >= 2) modulo immersions. We construct a class of cycles from specific chord diagrams associated with 2-loop or 3-loop hairy graphs. To detect these cycles, we use cocycles obtained by the 2-loop or 3-loop part of modified configuration space integrals using a modified Bott-Cattaneo-Rossi graph complex. We show the non-triviality of the cycles by pairing argument, which is reduced to pairing of graphs with the chord diagrams. As a corollary of the 2-loop part, we provide an alternative proof of the non-finite generation of the (j-1)-th rational homotopy group of the space of long embeddings of codimension two, which Budney--Gabai and Watanabe first established. We also show the non-finite generation of the 2(j-1)-th homotopy group by using the 3-loop part.
Geometric Topology.comment: 31 pages. Accepted for publication in the Journal of Topology

Geometric Topology.title: On hidden face contributions of configuration space integrals for long embeddings
Geometric Topology.summary: Configuration space integrals are powerful tools for studying the homotopy type of the space of long embeddings in terms of a combinatorial object called a graph complex. It is unknown whether these integrals give a cochain map due to potential obstructions called hidden faces. The purpose of this paper is to address these hidden faces by modifying configuration space integrals: we incorporate the acyclic bar complex of some dg algebra into the original graph complex, without changing its cohomology. Then, we give a cochain map from the new graph complex to the de Rham complex of the space of long embeddings modulo immersions, by combining the original configuration space integrals with Chen's iterated integrals. As the original complex, we choose a modified graph complex so that it is quasi-isomorphic to both the hairy graph complex and a graph complex introduced in the context of embedding calculus.
Geometric Topology.comment: 57 pages. Accepted for publication in the Journal of Topology

Geometric Topology.title: Shake concordance in the topological concordance class of the Hopf link
Geometric Topology.summary: Within the topological concordance class of the Hopf link, we construct infinitely many classes under the equivalence relation generated by smooth $0$-shake concordance. Each contains infinitely many smooth concordance classes represented by links that are pairwise strongly $0$-shake concordant and whose second components have unbounded smooth slice genus.

Geometric Topology.title: On the Kashaev--Luo--Vartanov Partition Function for Cusped 3-Manifolds: Asymptotics and a squared norm property
Geometric Topology.summary:
We study the asymptotic and TQFT-type properties of the Kashaev--Luo--Vartanov (KLV) partition function. We show that the partition function depends on the prescribed angle structure only through its peripheral angular holonomies. For any geometric triangulation of a cusped 3-manifold realizing a possibly incomplete hyperbolic structure, we express the exponential decay rate and the 1-loop term of the partition function in terms of, respectively, the volume and the adjoint twisted Reidemeister torsion of the corresponding incomplete hyperbolic structure. Consequently, these asymptotic formulas hold for any angle structure having the same peripheral angular holonomies as the geometric one.
  We further introduce a Reshetikhin--Turaev-type function associated with certain admissible Neumann--Zagier data, extending the Jones function in Teichmüller TQFT previously studied by Ben Aribi and the author. We show that, after a combinatorial normalization, for any triangulation, the KLV partition function can be expressed as a weighted integral of the squared norm of the Reshetikhin--Turaev-type function, where the weight is determined by the angular holonomies of peripheral curves. In particular, for FAMED triangulations, the Reshetikhin--Turaev-type function agrees with the Jones function, so that the normalized KLV partition function is obtained by integrating the squared norm of the integrand defining the Teichmüller TQFT partition function. This provides a noncompact analogue of the relationship between Turaev--Viro and Reshetikhin--Turaev invariants.

Geometric Topology.title: Localization of Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
Geometric Topology.summary:
For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith.
  The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.

Geometric Topology.title: Properness and finiteness of totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core
Geometric Topology.summary: We study totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core of geometrically finite rank-one locally symmetric manifolds. Although the infinite-volume setting can exhibit highly complicated behavior, including geodesic planes with fractal closures, we show that a strong rigidity persists inside the convex core. This rigidity has striking consequences in the infinite volume setting: every maximal totally geodesic submanifold of dimension at least two contained in the convex core is properly immersed and has finite volume, and only finitely many such submanifolds can occur. These results stand in sharp contrast to the behavior in the finite-volume setting. Moreover, combining this finiteness result with the work of Bader-Fisher-Miller-Stover and of Gromov-Schoen, we deduce that any geometrically finite rank-one manifold with infinitely many maximal totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two and of finite volume must be arithmetic.
Geometric Topology.comment: 32 pages, 1 figure, Final version, To appear in Geometry & Topology

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Deterministic Metric Distortion of Top-2 Voting
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We give tight bounds on the metric distortion of top-2 deterministic voting mechanisms. We first exploit the restrictive structure of top-2 voting to reduce the space of worst-case metrics from the continuum of biased metrics to $2^n$ subset metrics, where every candidate has distance $0$ or $1$ to the optimal candidate and $n$ is the number of candidates. We then reduce these further to just $2n$ polar metrics: $n$ of these have a single optimal candidate, and the other $n$ have a single sub-optimal candidate. This reduction yields an efficient algorithm that computes the exact distortion of every candidate on a given profile and runs in $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ time. As a corollary, we can derive the exact worst-case distortion for top-2 voting for all values of $n$, for which previous work had non-matching lower and upper bounds.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 9 pages

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Multi-Agent Learning of Reactive Strategies in Iterated Games
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Learning agents, whether humans or algorithms, adapt to one another rather than to a fixed environment. Selfish learning need not produce a good outcome for the group, especially when learners face a social dilemma. The iterated prisoner's dilemma (IPD) is the classical example, but it is usually studied in populations of agents who imitate successful strategies. Here, we instead study selfish gradient ascent learners on the two-dimensional space of reactive strategies. A reactive strategy is described by two continuous traits: reciprocity, the chance of cooperating after the co-player cooperates, and forgiveness, the chance of cooperating after the co-player defects. Each learner updates its strategy in the direction that most rapidly improves its payoff against all other learners, by an amount governed by its learning rate. We show that heterogeneity in learning rates can qualitatively change the long-term outcome: a population with uniform learning rates converges to always-defect (ALLD), whereas a population with variable learning rates approaches generous-tit-for-tat (GTFT), which produces nearly optimal collective payoffs. In simulations, every population passes through a transient state of minimal forgiveness, in which the distribution of reciprocity determines the outcome. Variable learning rates promote cooperation because slow learners preserve high reciprocity until the population reaches this state. We prove sufficient conditions on the distribution of reciprocity for convergence to ALLD or to tit-for-tat (TFT). Variable learning rates also allow cooperation to recover from perturbation, which is provably impossible under uniform learning. These results suggest that purely selfish and myopic learning can produce persistent cooperation provided the population has intrinsic variability in learning rates.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 27 pages, 14 figures (12 pages + 3 figures main text; 15 pages + 11 figures Supplemental Material). Code: https://github.com/james-wolfe/reactive-learning

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Can You Trust Your Preference Models? Stackelberg Games for Alignment
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Language models are frequently aligned to human preferences via imperfect evaluators whose errors can be exploited during optimization. We train policies to search for comparisons on which an evaluator may reverse the underlying preference, providing candidates for additional supervision. Since human preferences are unavailable during policy training, we use disagreement among an ensemble of preference models as a proxy for prediction error. We formulate this search as a zero-sum Stackelberg game between two opposing policies, a Leader which tries to minimize disagreement, and a Follower which maximizes it. For a general class of finite contextual Stackelberg games, we establish equilibrium existence and, under regularization, uniqueness and a closed-form characterization. We introduce Stackelberg Mirror Descent-Ascent (SMIDA), a two-timescale algorithm with linear last-iterate convergence in the tabular setting, and develop a neural policy-gradient analogue. Experiments with a synthetic oracle support disagreement as an informative proxy for prediction error. On held out data the trained policies outperform reference policies and increase the fraction of comparisons that exceed a disagreement threshold and reverse the oracle's preference.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Best-of-Both-Worlds Fair Division via Subsidies
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We study the relationship between fair division with $\textit{subsidies}$ and $\textit{best-of-both-worlds}$ (BoBW) fairness for indivisible items. We prove a general reduction of BoBW existence to envy-freeability. Specifically, for any scale-free ex-post property $P$ (e.g., EF1, EFX, PO) and any scale-free valuation class $\mathcal{V}$ (e.g, additive, submodular, subadditive, monotone), if every instance in $\mathcal{V}$ admits a $P$-allocation that can be made envy-free using subsidies, then every such instance admits an ex-ante envy-free lottery supported on $P$-allocations. The proof uses linear programming duality. As applications, the reduction gives alternative proofs of BoBW existence results for additive goods, chores, and mixtures of goods and chores. The converse of our general reduction holds for two agents but fails for three: We provide a four-good counterexample with monotone submodular valuations where an ex-ante envy-free and ex-post EF1 lottery exists, but no allocation is simultaneously EF1 and envy-freeable. For lexicographic valuations, we prove simultaneous EFX, Pareto optimality, and envy-freeability (and hence BoBW guarantees for EFX+PO) for three agents, and show that even EFX and envy-freeability can be incompatible for four agents.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 16 pages in main body, 1 page appendix

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: MILP the Gap: An Automated Reasoning Approach to Condorcet's Paradox
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Computational social choice studies how conflicting individual preferences are aggregated into a collective decision, with applications to elections, AI evaluation/alignment, and recommendation systems. We focus on settings where $n$ voters (e.g., human evaluators or algorithmic benchmarks) each rank $m$ alternatives (e.g., human candidates or AI models/outputs), and the goal is to select a committee of $k$ alternatives. One measure of the (in)stability of the outcome is the number of voters who prefer an unchosen alternative to all alternatives in the committee. If this number is less than half the electorate, the committee is a Condorcet winning set, which may not exist if $k \leq 2$. More generally, there exist instances where any committee of size $k$ has at least a $\frac{2}{(k+1)}-ε$ fraction of the electorate preferring another alternative, for arbitrarily small $ε$. While recent work has made remarkable progress narrowing the gap, it is currently unknown whether this lower bound is tight. We develop a mixed-integer linear programming framework that computes exact bounds for fixed parameter values. Our approach depends only on $m$ and $k$; by modeling electorates as distributions over rankings, we eliminate any dependence on $n$. Our programs allow us to rule out counterexamples over arbitrary electorate sizes and obtain tight bounds for fixed $m$ and $k$. Further, our framework provides a pathway for proving general upper bounds. In particular, we show a linear regime, $k \ge \frac{8m}{9}$, in which the conjectured $\frac{2}{(k+1)}$ upper bound indeed holds, providing the first results that match known lower bounds. Beyond stability, our framework can characterize the relationships among other social choice axioms, which we demonstrate by producing minimal incomparability results.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: An earlier version titled "Is Four Enough? Automated Reasoning Approaches and Dual Bounds for Condorcet Dimensions of Elections" appears at the 8th Games, Agents, and Incentives Workshop (GAIW-26), held as part of the Workshops at the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Beyond Independent Values: Optimal Auctions with Correlated Valuations for LLM-Native Advertising
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Conversational assistants are becoming the place where people ask what to buy, and sponsored content is moving into their answers. Several advertisers then compete for one sponsored slot, and all of them read the same conversation, so their willingness to pay usually moves together. Existing auctions for LLM advertising treat these values as independent. We therefore present AffMyerson, an auction that captures this correlation and turns it into revenue. We model the advertisers' values given the conversation as a multivariate normal and turn the economic premise of positive dependence (affiliation) into a sign condition on the precision matrix. We design a neural parameterization whose every output satisfies it. We prove that every prior in this family yields a truthful, ex-post individually rational auction, so estimation error can cost revenue but never truthfulness. We derive the conditional virtual values in closed form. By the design of the prior, pricing an auction needs no matrix inversion and takes O(n^2) time, fast enough to run at query time. We also work out the log-normal family used in empirical ad-auction work. There we prove that the auction is truthful for every prior and revenue-optimal when the prior is correct, and that the virtual value is regular everywhere whenever the conditional spread is below a loose threshold, which our fitted priors stay well under. With LLM-agent bidders, AffMyerson earns 6.2% more than a second-price auction with a tuned reserve, 6.1% more than Ronen's lookahead auction with the same prior, and 9.2% more than Myerson's auction run as if values were independent. This gain is still 4.5% on real keyword search queries where willingness to pay is hard to read. The correlation comes from common demand. Agents that judge the conversation bid together and agents told to calculate do not. The gain from conditioning moves with the correlation.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 23 pages, 4 figures

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Diffusion-Based Auctions for Multi-Winner Banner Ads
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We propose a new framework for banner ad auctions, leveraging diffusion models to allow for multiple bidders to co-win a single banner ad opportunity, and in particular influence the ad shown on the banner depending on the strength of their bids, enabling a far richer outcome space compared to standard banner ad auctions, where there is a single winner who shows their ad. In our framework, the outcomes are images (what ad to show) and each bidder expresses their preferences over outcomes by declaring their value per unit of alignment between the image chosen by the mechanism and a textual description of their desired image. Our proposed mechanism combines the advertisers' bids and textual descriptions into a score that drives the reverse process of a diffusion model. This is used to sample a set of candidate images from which the welfare maximizing one is eventually chosen. Extensive experimentation evaluates our proposed mechanism around the following axes: (1) efficiency improvements of our allocation rule relative to the single-winner allocation rule; (2) monotonicity of our allocation rule; and (3) approximate incentive compatibility when combining our allocation rule with Myerson lemma-based or Clarke rule-based payments. Improvements along all these axes are shown with the number of Monte Carlo samples. Meanwhile, these benefits are attained while preserving the image quality.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: Appeared in EC 2026

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Beyond a Single Optimal Design: A Dynamical Systems Characterization of Online Allocation with Convex Costs
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary:
We study online allocation with convex costs (\OACC), a generalization of limited-supply models in which additional resources can be produced dynamically at convex cost. Prior work largely focuses on constructing a single algorithm that achieves strong competitive guarantees. In contrast, our main contribution is a structural characterization of the optimal design space of reserve functions (i.e., normalized pricing rules) for \OACC, yielding a family of optimal online algorithms.
  Using a principled dynamical-systems approach, we show that optimal online algorithms arise as solutions of a nonlinear eigenvalue problem: the optimal competitive ratio corresponds to the dominant eigenvalue, and the associated eigenfunction determines the optimal reserve function. This perspective establishes the existence of infinitely many optimal designs attaining the best possible competitive ratio, thereby unifying and generalizing a broad class of prior algorithms. Beyond unification, our characterization uncovers new structural phenomena, including the ability to flexibly mix dynamic and static pricing without loss of optimality and the construction of universally competitive algorithms under unknown or stochastic costs. We further extend the analysis to more structured settings such as supply-oblivious arrivals and hard supply constraints, obtaining sharper guarantees that improve upon previous bounds.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: Accepted at WINE 2026

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Randomly Wrong Signals: Bayesian Auction Design with ML Predictions
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Machine learning can help sellers predict buyers' willingness to pay, but its predictions may be plausible and yet entirely unrelated to a buyer's value. We introduce a Bayesian auction model that distinguishes such hallucinations from ordinary measurement noise. We characterize revenue-maximizing auctions with publicly disclosed predictions in the benchmark where informative predictions are exact. For a single buyer, this characterization explains when the seller should follow a prediction and when to hedge against its failure by ignoring it or capping the price. These insights guide the design of simple auctions that account for both hallucinations and measurement noise. Numerical experiments show that the resulting auctions achieve near-optimal revenue.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Revenue Maximization in Choice-Based Matching Markets
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: The primary contribution of this paper resides in devising constant-factor approximation guarantees for revenue maximization in two-sided matching markets with general pairwise rewards. A major distinction between our work and state-of-the-art results in this context (Ashlagi et al., 2022; Torrico et al., 2023) is that, for the first time, we are able to address reward maximization, reflected by assigning each customer-supplier pair an arbitrarily-valued reward. Our performance guarantees apply to two different settings: the customized model and the inclusive model. The fundamental difference between these settings lies in whether the platform should display to each supplier all selecting customers, as in the inclusive model, or whether the platform can further personalize this set, as in the customized model. Technically speaking, our algorithmic approaches and their analysis revolve around presenting a closely related combinatorial problem, a novel linear relaxation, and developing tailor-made analytical ideas. In both models considered, these ingredients allow us to overcome the lack of submodularity and subadditivity that stems from pairwise rewards, plaguing the applicability of existing methods. We complement our theoretical results with an extensive computational study under different classes of instances where we analyze the empirical reward and running time performance of our proposed methods.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Using Evidence-Centered Design to Guide Prompt Engineering in Measurement: An Illustration with Automated Essay Scoring
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) models, particularly large language models (LLMs), are increasingly used in educational settings for tasks such as item generation, automated scoring, and feedback delivery. The quality of these outputs depends not only on the AI model but also on how users construct the prompts that guide model behaviors. Current prompt engineering practices are largely ad hoc, relying on trial and error rather than principled design. This lack of structure introduces validity threats including construct misrepresentation, construct-irrelevant variance, and limited reproducibility. We propose that Evidence-Centered Design (ECD), a framework in educational measurement for structuring valid inferences from observed performance, can serve as a principled foundation for prompt engineering in educational applications. We map the three core ECD models, the student model, the evidence model, and the task model, onto the components of educational prompt design, and describe a workflow for ECD-based prompt engineering. We derive five design principles from this mapping and present an empirical study contrasting ECD-designed prompts with state-of-the-art (SOTA) prompting baselines on an automated scoring task. Our empirical study demonstrates the usefulness of this framework on automated scoring. Results suggest that treating prompting as assessment design rather than informal instructions strengthens the validity, reliability, and fairness of AI-generated educational outputs.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Trust Hinders Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Trust calibration remains the dominant framing of AI-assisted decision making: the goal is to close the gap between perceived and actual trustworthiness of AI systems so that users exhibit appropriate reliance on them. We argue that this approach, while useful for decision problems that are well-defined and clearly scoped, overly restricts what it means to make a decision with AI support. To overcome this limitation, we develop three dimensions of AI-assisted decision making. First, trusting AI is only one of several possible strategies for managing uncertainty. Second, trust calibration is often misapplied when AI models "large-world" decision problems, i.e., ill-defined situations where goals and states are only partially known or unknowable. Third, in such settings human-AI alignment requires addressing higher-order decision processes. We conclude by reflecting on the implications of our observations on the design of process-oriented human-AI coupled systems that jointly identify and negotiate uncertainty throughout the decision-making task.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: Dynamic Alignment in Human-AI Coupled System (BiAlign Workshop)

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Moral Missions: Sustaining Responsible Practice by Surfacing Practitioner Moral Decision-Making Procedures
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: A growing ecosystem of techniques, toolkits, and guidelines has been developed to help data scientists consider the social implications of data-driven technologies. However, prior literature highlights that even when this ecosystem of techniques is provided to professional data scientists, they still struggle to consistently adopt a responsible data science practice. We posit that the key to sustained responsible data science practice is to approach it as a moral mission: a conviction-driven technical practice that seeks to transform social conditions by any degree possible. In this paper, we present a semi-structured interview study with 15 responsible data scientists and AI practitioners to understand the moral decision-making procedures they use to articulate and actualize their moral missions. Through a phenomenological analysis of our participants' accounts, we find participants engage in embodied introspection, circumvent institutional expectations, and center relationality throughout their moral missions. We also present how our participants engage in similar processes to contend with generative AI (GenAI) in their responsible practice. We conclude by calling for subversive data science communities and identifying sociotechnical design implications to better support sustainable responsible data science practice.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: To be published in AIES 2026 without appendix

Human-Computer Interaction.title: MotionAnimator: Semantic-to-Motion Reasoning for Animating Part-Structured 3D Assets in XR
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: 3D digital assets are increasingly used in education, simulation, design, and immersive content creation, yet most remain behaviorally inert: they provide geometry and component structure but lack the semantic annotations, motion constraints, and executable behaviors needed to function as dynamic objects in Extended Reality (XR). Animating such assets therefore still requires manual rigging, object-specific templates, or substantial programming expertise. We introduce MotionAnimator, an intent-driven, part-aware XR animation authoring system that transforms semantically unlabeled, part-structured 3D assets into executable animations from natural-language instructions. Rather than generating code directly from text, MotionAnimator externalizes object understanding and motion reasoning into explicit semantic and motion representations. It grounds object identity, semantic parts, and functional directions, constructs a structured plan that coordinates object- and part-level motion, and translates the plan into executable Unity behavior. On a benchmark of 90 prompts across 30 objects, MotionAnimator demonstrated reliable semantic grounding and coordinated animation generation across diverse objects and animation intents. An exploratory user study further provided insights into users' experiences with MotionAnimator and highlighted its potential for part-aware XR animation authoring. These findings demonstrate how explicit semantic and motion representations can bridge high-level user intent and executable behavior, enabling existing part-structured assets to support coordinated XR animations beyond object-level transformations and predefined behaviors.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: EnRoute: Iterative Design and Evaluation of a Mobile App for Lower-Carbon Fashion and Transportation Choices
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: EnRoute is an iOS application designed to support more sustainable everyday choices in transportation and fast fashion consumption. We describe three design iterations and the user research and field evaluations that shaped each one. Interviews with 15 people from 12 countries informed Version I, which combined errand route planning with basic fashion guidance. A survey of 1,200 people in five countries found much stronger interest in sustainable shopping (78%) than in switching to lower-carbon transport (46%); respondents most often named limited public transport as the main barrier to lower-carbon travel. We therefore narrowed the focus to fashion. Version II added item-level garment scanning with a manual-entry fallback, a Sustainability Coefficient that rates items, and recommendations of more sustainable alternatives; in a two-week evaluation with 3,021 participants in eight countries, participants randomly assigned to receive a short tutorial and educational prompts viewed more recommended alternatives and reported larger gains in purchase intent than those without it. Version III shifted from "buy better" to "buy less," adding a wardrobe inventory, outfit matching, and a "Real Price" that combines cost per wear with estimated environmental and social costs. In a four-week pre/post pilot with 500 participants, self-reported monthly garment purchases fell from 2.9 to 1.9. We report descriptive results, discuss the substantial limitations of these uncontrolled and self-reported measures, and outline what the iterations suggest about designing for sustainable consumption.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Design and Evaluation of a Collaborative Teleoperation Interface for Multi-Operator Multi-Robot Systems in Challenging Environments
Human-Computer Interaction.summary:
Multi-robot systems that combine the complementary capabilities of specialised platforms are critical for complex missions in challenging, inaccessible environments. Current deployments assign an operator or operator team to each robot, with collaboration relying on operator-to-operator communication to manually coordinate heterogeneous platforms with incompatible interfaces. This operator-dependent approach increases cognitive load and limits scalability across robots from different manufacturers. This study designs and evaluates a shared-visualisation collaborative teleoperation interface to improve operator coordination, situational awareness, and the task performance in multi-operator, multi-robot systems.
  A comparative user study with 16 participants compared three teleoperation conditions: co-located operators with a shared interface, remote operators with a shared interface, and co-located operators with individual interfaces. Participants controlled two simulated robots in a nuclear power plant digital twin to complete disaster response tasks. Performance metrics, physiological data, and behavioural measures were recorded to assess task performance, cognitive load, and operator awareness across conditions. The co-located shared-interface condition achieved the fastest mission completion (292.8 s), outperforming remote operation (351.6 s) and individual interfaces (385.1 s), with the fewest collisions (0.9 per trial) and highest situational awareness accuracy (91.1 %). Physical co-presence was associated with reduced cognitive load, with NASA-TLX scores increasing from 38.2 in co-located to 57.7 in remote operation, supported by consistent physiological indicators. These results demonstrate that co-presence and shared interfaces provide complementary benefits, supporting workload regulation and mutual awareness respectively in multi-operator, multi-robot teleoperation.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 9 pages, 8 figures, accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE Conference on Telepresence in Bristol, United Kingdom, November 9-13, 2026

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Answer with Evidence: Consistency-Aware Grounded Visual Question Answering for Roadside Traffic Scenes
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Roadside traffic reasoning requires every free-form textual claim to be backed by visual evidence. Existing grounded multimodal large language models (MLLMs) frequently exhibit say-point mismatch, in which the textual answer contradicts the bounding boxes the model localizes. Evaluation metrics that score answers and boxes separately leave this failure unpenalized. We trace the mismatch to the conventional answer-then-ground factorization, which commits to a numerical claim before any object is enumerated. To measure it, we build RoadSceneVQA-G, a benchmark of 34.7K question-answer pairs in which every free-form answer is linked to the set of boxes that witnesses it, and we propose the Answer-Grounding Consistency (AGC) evaluation suite. To address it, we introduce Enumerate-then-Answer (EtA), which reverses the generation order so that answer-evidence agreement becomes a property of the output structure, and Enumeration-Consistent Policy Optimization (ECPO), a reinforcement learning stage that uses the union of multiple rollouts as a recall teacher without ground-truth boxes. EtA raises say-point consistency from 26.6\% to 93.7\% and grounding F1 from 52.2\% to 73.0\%, and ECPO further increases F1 to 75.6\% without per-box supervision. On gRefCOCO, the same framework outperforms the strongest compared method, indicating that it transfers beyond traffic scenes. The project is available at https://github.com/GuanRunwei/RoadSceneVQA-G.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 14 pages, 7 figures

Human-Computer Interaction.title: How Should a Camera-First AI Agent Work?
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Camera-first agents must act on the visual world as it unfolds. We argue that the central obstacle for future camera-first agents is not recognition ability - multimodal models (vision-language and live/streaming alike) generalize well through language and remain the right tool for semantic reasoning - but time. Many visual targets are ephemeral: they appear, are query-relevant, and leave within a short window. Binding memory to the same end-to-end path as reasoning means that by the time a monolithic pipeline completes, the evidence is gone. We formalize this as Ephemeral-Target Interaction (ETI) and a Perceptual Deadline Contract separating a hard memory deadline from a soft reasoning deadline, grounded in the bounded, passive nature of sensory and working memory. We propose a two-deadline architecture: an always-on, bounded, non-semantic fast path; an active remembering mechanism that commits a moment to durable memory before it is overwritten (event-driven in v1); and a deferred deliberation layer (multimodal model + tools). We instantiate the contract on real MOT17 track windows, a consistency check, and calibrate the single-path baseline from measured frontier-model latency: even a short answer takes 1.2-9.3 s, and an agentic identify-and-search longer. Answers can be late; evidence cannot be missed.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Position/contract paper on time-critical camera-first agents (systems/timing).Primary cs.AI;

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Rethinking Opinion Measurement Interfaces for Human-in-the-Loop Optimization
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Human-in-the-loop optimization refers to systems that present choices to a human decision-maker and query their judgment to optimize system parameters iteratively. The user interface typically provides either an absolute rating scale or asks for a preferred option. However, these approaches can potentially suffer from calibration problems, inconsistencies, and completeness violations of user preferences in such a sequential evaluation. This paper revisits the design space of opinion measurement interfaces for human-in-the-loop optimization. We conducted a study (N=360) using text summarization and image color enhancement tasks to evaluate human sequential feedback in six representative opinion measurement interfaces. Based on our analysis, we recommend using a listwise approach to support sequential opinion measurement, which counterweighs individual rating and preferential choice limitations and conveys more information for subsequent use. We further discuss the trade-offs in different user interface designs and provide guidelines to inform future research.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 29 pages. Written in 2022, published as last revised. Dataset, analysis scripts, and system source code: https://github.com/changkun/rankui

Human-Computer Interaction.title: sGLP: Specifying Stochastic Agents that Simulate People
Human-Computer Interaction.summary:
Grassroots platforms are designed to be owned, operated and governed by their participants, and thus are constituted from person-to-person smartphone apps that run on participants' smartphones. A grassroots app is specified using a grassroots social contract, which is compiled through an abstraction cascade into a volition-guarded Grassroots Logic Program (vGLP), a multiagent concurrent logic programming language. A vGLP program in turn specifies a smartphone UI via which people express their volitions and thus control the app. Prudence dictates large-scale evaluation and testing of grassroots platforms prior to deployment, but using the many people needed to do that is a contradiction in terms. Hence another solution is needed.
  Here, we present stochastic GLP (sGLP), designed to allow grassroots platforms to be simulated at scale from the vGLP programs that deploy them, with stochastic agents in place of people. sGLP is GLP with a rate extension for specifying stochastic behaviour. A stochastic agent is an sGLP program replacing both the vGLP UI and the person behind it. It is typed by the dual of the interactive type of the UI and specifies a stochastic profile of a person's behaviour.
  We demonstrate sGLP on the grassroots social graph, with a population of men and women drawn from four stochastic profiles --- homophile or indifferent, wary or sociable --- and on grassroots currencies, with four profiles --- spenders or savers, cautious or generous --- and report what the mix of profiles does to the social graph that forms and to the currencies that circulate.
  We prove that every run of a vGLP program in which sGLP agents replace the UI and the people behind it is a vGLP run. We implemented sGLP in GLP by Gillespie's method, and ran reproducible simulations with it.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: To Embody or Not: The Effect Of Embodiment On User Perception Of LLM-based Conversational Agents
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Embodiment in conversational agents (CAs) refers to the physical or visual representation of these agents, which can significantly influence user perception and interaction. Limited work has been done examining the effect of embodiment on the perception of CAs utilizing modern large language models (LLMs) in non-hierarchical cooperative tasks, a common use case of CAs as more powerful models become widely available for general use. To bridge this research gap, we conducted a mixed-methods within-subjects study on how users perceive LLM-based CAs in cooperative tasks when embodied and non-embodied. The results show that the non-embodied agent received significantly better quantitative appraisals for competence than the embodied agent, and in qualitative feedback, many participants believed that the embodied CA was more sycophantic than the non-embodied CA. We believe that a possible reason for this is how users' perceptions are affected by LLM sycophancy and anthropomorphic features: the typically positive impact of embodiment on perception of CA credibility can become detrimental in the presence of sycophancy. The implication of such a phenomenon is that, contrary to intuition and existing literature, embodiment is not a straightforward way to improve a CA's perceived credibility if there exists a tendency to sycophancy.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Accepted to IEEE TENCON 2026

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Impact of Expertise and Trust on AI-assisted Work
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents promise to extend what users can accomplish beyond their existing expertise, but they also raise the risk of producing plausible-looking work that users may struggle to evaluate. We ask how task-relevant expertise and trust in AI shape agent-assisted work. To isolate these factors, we conduct a think-aloud study in which 20 professionals with varying data-science expertise use the same agentic tool to complete the same data-science hiring assessment, used at a major U.S. company. We find that surface productivity can come at the expense of understanding: participants who delegated more completed more of the task, but were also more likely to produce invalid solutions. Experts more often resisted this tradeoff, sacrificing completion to decompose the task and scrutinize agent outputs. Our findings call for evaluating agentic assistance not only by how much it accomplishes, but by whether users remain able to evaluate the work they produce.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: FlexGuard: A Design Space for On-Body Feedback for Safety Scaffolding in Strength Training
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Strength training carries inherent safety risks when exercises are performed without supervision. While haptics research has advanced, there remains a gap in how to integrate on-body feedback into intelligent wearables. Developing such a design space requires experiencing feedback in context, yet obtaining functional systems is costly. By addressing these challenges, we introduce FlexGuard, a design space for on-body feedback that scaffolds safety during strength training. The design space was derived from nine co-design workshops, where novice trainees and expert trainers DIY'd low-fidelity on-body feedback systems, tried them immediately, and surfaced needs and challenges encountered in real exercising contexts. We then evaluated and refined the design space through a multi-stakeholder speed dating study, using storyboards to cover the design dimensions. The study involved novice trainees and experienced trainers, allowing us to validate the design space from both usability and safety perspectives while synthesizing design implications for future wearable systems. Our findings extend the design space for sports and fitness wearables in the context of strength training.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Accepted to IMWUT

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Logarithmic Scores, Power-Law Discoveries: Disentangling Measurement from Coverage in Agent-Based Evaluation
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: LLM-based agent judges are an emerging approach to evaluating conversational AI, yet a fundamental uncertainty remains: can we trust their assessments, and if so, how many are needed? Through 960 sessions with two model pairs across 15 tasks, we show that persona-based agent judges produce evaluations indistinguishable from human raters in a Turing-style validation. We then identify a score-coverage dissociation: quality scores improve logarithmically with panel size, while unique issue discoveries follow a sublinear power law-both exhibit diminishing returns, but scores saturate roughly twice as fast as discoveries. We hypothesize this reflects a power law distribution of the finding space: critical issues are discovered first by small panels, while corner cases require progressively larger panels, analogous to species accumulation curves in ecology. The mechanism traces to ensemble diversity-Big Five personality conditioning makes agents probe different quality dimensions, with expert judges acting as adversarial probes that push discovery into the tail of the finding distribution. A controlled ablation confirms that structured persona conditioning, not simple prompting, is required to produce these scaling properties.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Accepted to COLM 2026

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws for Spiking Language Models
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Spiking neural networks target energy-efficient language modeling through sparse, binary activations, but the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff of spiking language models is uncharacterized at scale. We present the first Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP scaling study of a spiking language model, sweeping SpikeGPT-family models (RWKV backbone) from width 384 to 1536 across compute budgets from $3\times10^{17}$ to $10^{19}$ FLOPs on FineWeb-EDU. We report two findings. First, the compute-optimal frontier is $N_{opt} \propto C^{0.56}$, close to the 0.50 that Hoffmann et al. report for dense Transformers, so spiking does not change how parameters and data should be traded off under a compute budget. Second, against non-spiking RWKV and Transformer baselines trained the same way, the loss gap splits into a backbone cost of about 0.16 nats that does not change with compute and a spiking cost that falls from 0.34 to about 0.23 nats and then levels off. These results give the first compute-optimal recipe for spiking language models and quantify the accuracy cost of their sparsity.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: Accepted to AXIOM: Foundations of Efficient Deep Learning (NeurIPS 2026 workshop). 4 pages + appendix, 4 figures, 5 tables

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: RELAGRAM: Recursive Latent Graph Model for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Latent recursion repeatedly processes internal representations through the same neural network. Recent work has shown this approach to be effective on structured reasoning tasks such as Sudoku and maze solving. However, whether latent recursion can support neural routing remains unclear. We introduce RELAGRAM (Recursive Latent Graph Model), a novel approach that brings latent recursion to graph combinatorial optimization. RELAGRAM encodes a capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) instance as edge tokens; a compact transformer recurrently updates the latent representations of these tokens. An output head maps the answer state to an edge heatmap, from which an autoregressive decoder constructs a feasible solution. On CVRP-100 instances, the 0.53M-parameter RELAGRAM achieves gaps to a PyVRP reference of 13.4%, 9.8%, and 8.3% under greedy decoding, eightfold symmetry augmentation, and 256-candidate search, respectively. Trained only on CVRP-100, RELAGRAM generalizes zero-shot to CVRP-500 and CVRP-1000, achieving gaps of 15.6% and 21.7% under 256-candidate search. Together, these results demonstrate that latent recursion is a promising approach to neural routing.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 MLxOR workshop. Paper contains 6 pages (4 main text, 1 references, 1 appendix); 1 figure and 3 tables

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: When LLMs Develop Languages: Symbolic Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves large language models (LLMs) on difficult reasoning tasks, but it often incurs long natural-language rationales that are poorly aligned with efficient machine reasoning. We propose Communicative Language Symbolism Routing (CLSR), a test-time framework in which multiple LLM agents autonomously invent, evolve, and share compact Language Symbolism Frameworks (LSFs), while a latent-free router adaptively selects and composes these languages per query to optimize the accuracy-token trade-off. Unlike prompt optimization that refines surface instructions, CLSR treats each LSF as a reusable symbolic protocol with compact symbols, usage rules, and a message-passing contract, and improves it through an evolutionary loop driven by correctness and token cost. At inference time, the router may invoke a single low-cost LSF call, ensemble multiple LSFs, or execute a multi-round LSF composition protocol on harder queries. Across challenging benchmarks, CLSR reduces latency-oriented generated token completion by $3\sim 6\times$ compared to standard CoT while maintaining accuracy. We further derive an information-theoretic lower bound on token cost under arbitrary symbolism and show that, under an interpreter-realizability premise, multi-round LSF protocols conditionally subsume program-execution pipelines. Code is publicly available (https://github.com/pzqpzq/LSF_MDia).
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: ICML2026 Regular paper

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: Large Language Model-Guided Evolutionary Discovery of Native Neural Architectures for Spiking Sequence Modeling
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer low-energy sequence modeling through sparse, event-driven computation. However, interactions among spike encoding, neuronal dynamics, and information propagation complicate architecture design. Existing SNN sequence models often adapt artificial neural network (ANN) architectures designed for real-valued activations, potentially underusing spike-based communication and temporal state updates, motivating automated discovery of native SNN architectures. Most evolutionary neural architecture search (ENAS) methods operate within predefined configuration spaces, limiting discovery to mechanisms expressible within those spaces. We introduce OpenArchEvo, which uses large language models (LLMs) to evolve executable architecture code in an open program space under spiking-projection constraints. In this space, code differences need not reflect architectural novelty, while direct performance evaluation requires costly training. We construct a three-view representation spanning code, design rationale, and a behavioral fingerprint to support novelty estimation and performance prediction. The search treats predicted performance and estimated novelty as two objectives, using surrogate predictions to select candidates for expensive training evaluations. With an estimated candidate-training cost of 132 V100 GPU-days, the search uncovers multiple native SNN architectures, exemplified by three designs featuring mechanisms such as spike-activity-dependent control of state updates and residual pathways. The discovered NeuroGate surpasses the ANN DeltaNet on WikiText-103, and the discovered architectures reduce estimated architecture-level arithmetic energy by up to 50.6x (LoopMem) relative to a common dense Transformer (ANN) baseline. Code and all discovered architectures: https://github.com/Optima-CityU/OpenArchEvo
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: 38 pages (15 pages main text + appendix), 12 figures, 10 tables. Code: https://github.com/Optima-CityU/OpenArchEvo

Neural and Evolutionary Computing.title: PotentialEP: Backprop-Free Training of CIFAR-Scale Generative Models via Equilibrium Propagation
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.summary: Generating an image with a diffusion or flow-matching model typically involves integrating a velocity field for hundreds of sequential steps. That computation suits a GPU poorly and an analog neuromorphic substrate well, where one fast, low-power physical relaxation could replace the whole sequence. Two things are needed: a generative algorithm whose computation is a relaxation, and a way to train it without backpropagation, whose global gradient transport is hard to realise in analog. Energy Matching supplies the first, sampling by gradient-descent relaxation on a time-independent potential - but obtaining the gradient that descent follows is itself a backward pass, once per integration step. We prove that a predictive coding network with a single linear injection term added to its energy relaxes to a state whose visible layer carries that gradient inherently, with an error that vanishes for small injection strengths. An Energy Matching model trained by backpropagation can therefore be loaded into this network unchanged and sampled by relaxation alone, matching the original model's FID to within 0.04 at CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32 scale. The network can also be trained without backpropagation: Equilibrium Propagation reproduces backpropagation's parameter updates to a cosine similarity of 0.9998, and training end to end with those updates reaches an FID of 3.64 on unconditional CIFAR-10 against 3.54 for backpropagation. To our knowledge this is the first CIFAR-10 generative model trained with Equilibrium Propagation, and the first at competitive quality by any backpropagation-free rule. This quality does not require group normalisation or attention: an architecture of only convolutions and pointwise nonlinearities, both native to an analog crossbar, reaches an FID of 3.51 when trained by backpropagation.
Neural and Evolutionary Computing.comment: Under review at ICLR 2027. Code: github.com/alexgower/EnergyMatchingEqProp

Methodology.title: Estimation and Inference for Win Measures with Multiple Ordinal Endpoints Subject to Missingness
Methodology.summary: Win measures, including the win ratio, win odds, net benefit, and desirability of outcome ranking, are increasingly used in randomized clinical trials with multiple hierarchical ordinal endpoints. In practice, however, one or more component endpoints may have missing data. The standard pairwise-comparison approach, which treats pairs with missing outcomes as ties, can produce biased estimates, even if the data are missing completely at random. Although inverse probability of censoring weighting methods have been developed for censored survival endpoints, corresponding methods for addressing missing hierarchical ordinal endpoints are not yet available. To address this gap, we develop inverse probability weighted (IPW) and augmented IPW (AIPW) estimators for win measures with hierarchical ordinal endpoints subject to missing data, allowing missingness to depend on treatment assignment and baseline covariates. The IPW estimator corrects bias by reweighting complete observed outcomes using joint non-missingness probabilities involved in estimating the joint cell probabilities that define the win measures. The AIPW estimator additionally incorporates outcome modeling, potentially improving estimation precision and achieving double robustness. For inference, we derive closed-form variance estimators for both methods based on influence functions. Simulation studies show that the standard approach can be substantially biased, whereas the proposed IPW and AIPW estimators exhibit small bias and near-nominal coverage under their respective identifying and model conditions. Applications to the SCOUT-CAP and ACTT-1 trials illustrate the practical utility of the proposed methods. An R package WinMO is provided for implementation.

Methodology.title: Mixtures of spatial factor analyzers for tensor-variate data
Methodology.summary: A mixture of spatial factor analyzers (MSFA) is introduced to address the challenges of clustering high-dimensional spatial data. The proposed framework utilizes the given coordinate system to implement a flexible, spline-based spatial decay covariance structure. In this approach, the number of covariance parameters increases linearly with the number of spatial locations, rather than increasing quadratically. To model non-spatial dependence, matrix variate factor analyzers are employed for further dimensionality reduction. Parameter estimation is conducted via a variant of the expectation-maximization algorithm combined with a generalized least squares estimator. The proposed models are explored in the context of tensor-variate data analysis, where simulation studies and three applications---Raman spectroscopy, SpecTex hyperspectral textures, and the Salinas hyperspectral scene---illustrate their ability to recover and distinguish spatial dependence patterns. The R implementation is available on CRAN: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=SpatMix.

Methodology.title: Stable Causal Estimation with Optimal Transport
Methodology.summary: In observational studies, the overlap assumption, also called positivity, is frequently strained in practice. Limited overlap destabilizes widely used estimators such as inverse propensity weighting (IPW), whose variance depends on density ratios that explode as propensity scores approach zero or one. To address this challenge, we propose the Stable Transport Estimator (STE), an optimal transport-based approach for estimating average causal effects when overlap holds but strict overlap fails. Unlike IPW, the variance of STE contains no density-ratio factor; it is governed by the transport map itself and stays finite under bounded moments, even when density ratios diverge. By replacing reweighting with a geometry-aware transport map, STE constructs stable counterfactual comparisons without requiring density estimation or propensity score modeling. STE further extends to settings where the overlap condition is violated: when covariate supports overlap only partially, a linear interpolation transport map enables principled extrapolation with explicit bias-variance trade-offs. We establish consistency, asymptotic normality, and a variance characterization that makes explicit the contribution of the estimated transport map to the asymptotic variance. Across synthetic and real datasets, STE demonstrates improved robustness, reduced bias, and markedly more stable variance compared to existing estimators.

Methodology.title: Targeted Data Fusion for Region-Specific Survival Effects in the AMP HIV Prevention Trials
Methodology.summary: The Antibody Mediated Prevention (AMP) trials opened a new scientific frontier by showing that passively administered monoclonal broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) could prevent HIV-1 acquisition. The trials enrolled 4,611 participants across four epidemiologically distinct regions, with 174 HIV-1 diagnoses observed during follow-up. Regional heterogeneity in treatment efficacy, together with privacy and regulatory limits on central data pooling, calls for methods that borrow strength across regions without sharing individual-level data. To estimate region- and treatment-specific survival curves under distributional heterogeneity, we develop a federated learning approach that combines site-specific estimators via an L1-regularized criterion that downweights data sources not aligned with the target. We further extend the framework to a general class of causal contrasts, including the survival difference, survival ratio, and restricted mean survival time difference. In the AMP analysis, for example, the standard error of the day-148 survival difference decreased from 0.007 using the target-only estimator to 0.004 using the federated estimator. For women in South Africa, the region-specific analyses provided no strong evidence of an overall VRC01 benefit, consistent with the primary AMP findings. Overall, the proposed approach provides region-adaptive inference with improved precision without sharing individual-level data, while preserving estimation of region-specific treatment effects under cross-region heterogeneity.

Methodology.title: Precision follows the decision: how well an acceptance probability is known for mean-spread release rules
Methodology.summary: Many release rules accept a lot when a statistic built from the sample mean and standard deviation stays within a limit, and the probability that a process passes such a rule can be computed exactly for a broad class of parent distributions. This paper asks how well that probability is itself known once the parent has been estimated. Under a stated reference posterior the answer is an interval, narrow where a lot clearly passes or fails and wide where it is contested. In ninety-eight published content-uniformity lots that position, not the sample size, sets the width: among the forty-eight lots assayed at the same ten units, and so equally informed about the spread, the $95\%$ interval runs from essentially zero width to $0.96$.
