Unlike the peak-constrained formulation, an exact finite signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) analysis under average power leads in general to a nonconvex, high-dimensional optimization problem with no closed-form solution. We show that the problem admits a tractable characterization in the high-SNR regime. Using a genie-aided argument, we derive closed-form single-user high-SNR capacity bounds for the RP interference channel and identify constant-amplitude interferer signaling as extremal. Furthermore, under an empirically validated non-negativity condition on the dominant RP kernels and within a truncated first-order RP model, we establish a finite-SNR extremality result, yielding a single-user capacity characterization within the RP model under average power constraints. Building on these single-user corner points, we construct an all-helpsone achievable region via time sharing, which strictly improves upon treating nonlinear interference as noise. Numerical results and split-step Fourier simulations of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation channel confirm that the qualitative conclusions persist over practical launch powers. The results provide new insight into extremal signaling and multiuser trade-offs for nonlinear WDM systems within the RP approximation.

Information Theory.title: Efficient construction of subspace design codes over constant alphabet
Information Theory.summary: Subspace-design codes form a central unifying framework in coding theory, connecting probabilistic existence results and explicit algebraically structured constructions. The two core families are folded Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes, both possessing the subspace-design property. These codes reach list-decoding capacity with polynomial-size lists, but their alphabet size grows with code length and hurts practical efficiency. Goyal, Guruswami, and Hsieh achieved a major breakthrough: they constructed the first explicit subspace-design codes over constant-size alphabets via the Alon-Edmonds-Luby expander framework, settling an open problem and showing subspace-design properties can hold without large alphabets. Despite recent progress, constructing subspace-design codes with low-complexity efficient encoding remains a critical open challenge. This work gives an explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r. By comparison, Goyal et al. (FOCS 2026) built r-dimensional subspace-design codes with alphabet size doubly exponential in r squared. Our construction is computationally efficient: encoding scales quadratically with block length and linearly with dimension r in field operations. We use modified algebraic geometry codes, replacing rational evaluation points with higher-degree places to obtain a valid additive code. To confirm parameter bounds, we use Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries. We also generalize univariate multiplicity codes, originally built from Reed-Solomon codes, to algebraic geometry codes, and prove these AG-multiplicity codes achieve optimal parameters.

Information Theory.title: Hermitian Hulls of Cyclic Codes and Exact Dual Distances of Extended Linear Codes
Information Theory.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an $[n,k,d]$ linear code over $\F_{q^2}$ with parity-check matrix $H$. The rank $r=\Rank(HH^{\dagger})$ measures how far the Hermitian dual $\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}$ is from being Hermitian self-orthogonal, and it is the least number of coordinates that must be adjoined to $\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}$ to make it Hermitian self-orthogonal; equivalently, the Hermitian hull $\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{C}^{\perp_h}$ has dimension $(n-k)-r$. In this paper, we develop a structure theory of the Hermitian hull of a cyclic code and apply it to the construction of quantum stabilizer codes. For a cyclic code with defining set $T\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n$, we show that $r$ is additive over the orbits of the involution $τ(ν)=-qν$ on the $q^2$-cyclotomic cosets and satisfies a parity constraint. A parameter dictionary exhibits $r$ as a gauge trading one-for-one against the code length, and a complementation duality shows that the complement of $T$ realises the logical-qubit count of the quantum code. The extreme values of $r$ are settled by closed subset-sum criteria, and the $τ$-invariant defining sets are shown to be the unique locus on which the Hermitian dual is again cyclic. On the distance side, we determine the Hermitian dual distance of an $r$-fold extension of an arbitrary linear code exactly, and we prove that the admissible extension vectors lie in the image of $HH^{\dagger}$, which reduces the search space from $q^{2(n-k)}$ to $q^{2r}$. Applied to cyclic, quasi-cyclic and BCH codes, the construction improves $23$ best-known parameters in Grassl's code tables, one of them provably optimal.
Information Theory.comment: v3: corrected the distance-preservation criterion and Exact Dual Distances

Information Theory.title: High-Probability Regret Bounds for Feel-Good Thompson Sampling
Information Theory.summary: Feel-good Thompson sampling (FGTS) augments the posterior of vanilla Thompson sampling with an exploration term that favors reward functions with high predicted optimal values. This modification achieves minimax-optimal regret up to logarithmic factors in linear contextual bandits, but existing analyses of its two standard variants establish regret guarantees in expectation. In this paper, we derive the first high-probability regret bounds for both cumulative and current-step FGTS in contextual bandits with general realizable function approximation. Our bounds depend on the corresponding decoupling coefficients and the prior mass near the true reward function. In the $d$-dimensional linear setting, both variants satisfy $\mathrm{Regret}(T)=O\big(d\sqrt T\log(2T)+\sqrt T\log(1/δ)\big)$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $T$ is the time horizon. This bound matches the dimension and horizon dependence of algorithms based on the upper confidence bounds, up to logarithmic factors. Relative to the expected-regret guarantees, the cost of controlling the regret with high probability is confined to additive terms with at most linear dependence on $\log(1/δ)$. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

Information Theory.title: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation for In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Based on Transformer Neural Operators
Information Theory.summary: Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is essential in in-band full-duplex radios after passive suppression and analog cancellation. It is particularly challenging when the desired signal is strong relative to the residual self-interference. In this regime, conventional iterative digital cancellers update their coefficients from desired-signal-contaminated received samples and may suffer substantial performance degradation. This paper reformulates digital-domain self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem. The proposed framework learns the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations and uses the learned operator together with the known local transmit signal to reconstruct the current residual self-interference. A Transformer neural operator is used to realize this framework. The resulting method is trained in a desired-signal-free setting and then applied in the presence of a desired signal. A continuity-based analysis characterizes the sensitivity of the learned operator to the resulting input perturbation. Numerical experiments in static and time-varying channels, including time-varying SIR conditions, demonstrate stable cancellation performance over a wide range of interference levels. At 30 dB SIR, the proposed method improves the cancellation performance by 5--15 dB over the considered conventional methods.

Information Theory.title: Low-Complexity Channel Estimation Framework for Non-Square UPA-Assisted XL-MIMO Systems
Information Theory.summary: Low-complexity channel state information acquisition is crucial for extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems. However, practical deployments of non-square uniform planar arrays (UPAs) in hybrid-field environments face prohibitive computational complexity and degraded estimation accuracy due to limited elevation angle-of-arrival (AoA) resolution and deteriorated channel sparsity. To tackle these challenges, we propose a low-complexity channel estimation framework. First, an antenna-domain extrapolation scheme synthesizes a virtually enlarged vertical aperture via the spatial correlation among adjacent elements, breaking the elevation resolution limit. The framework then disentangles the parameter coupling by transforming the two-dimensional joint search into two sequential one-dimensional searches. Specifically, elevation AoAs are extracted via an extrapolation-enhanced discrete Fourier transform-Newtonized orthogonal matching pursuit (NOMP) algorithm along the virtually enlarged vertical uniform linear array (ULA), while azimuth AoAs, ranges, and gains are acquired utilizing a discrete fractional Fourier transform-NOMP algorithm along a horizontal ULA. A subspace fitting-driven path matching algorithm pairs these decoupled parameters. To overcome the accuracy bottleneck of the antenna-domain scheme, a correlation-domain extrapolation scheme is further developed by exploiting the structural properties of the spatial correlation matrix to decouple the near-field quadratic and azimuth phase components, yielding a noise-suppressed virtual array. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
Information Theory.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Information Theory.title: Weak Private Information Retrieval for Graph-based Storage under $ε$-privacy
Information Theory.summary: The problem of Private Information Retrieval (PIR) across graph-based replicated systems has seen a surge of interest in recent literature. In such systems, servers are modeled as the vertices of a graph, and each file is represented by an edge connecting the pair of servers that store it. While previous research on Graph-PIR (G-PIR) has focused mostly on perfect information-theoretic privacy, relaxing this constraint has the potential for significantly higher retrieval rates. In this work, we consider the setting of Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR), under an $ε$-privacy metric. We adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to analyze its performance under the $ε$-privacy metric. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the expected download cost for arbitrary graphs under the $ε$-privacy metric and derive from it an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs. Finally, we show the achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for two specific graph classes---complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs.

Information Theory.title: High-Girth QLDPC Codes from Circulant and Affine Permutation Matrices
Information Theory.summary: We study two explicit constructions of binary Calderbank--Shor--Steane quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes with check weight six. The first uses a fixed circulant shift pattern and yields parameters $\code{6N}{2N+2}{6}$ with Tanner graph girth twelve for $N=31$ and every $N\ge37$. A graph incidence interpretation gives the ranks and girths, and a uniform weight six logical operator establishes the exact distance. The second construction uses fixed matrix polynomials with circulant and affine permutation coefficients. Here, a polynomial commutation identity guarantees orthogonality for every cyclic lift. Four realizations give $[[192,16,8]]$, $[[288,16,12]]$, $[[384,16,14]]$, and $[[576,32,20]]$, with Tanner girth eight and computationally certified distances. We give reproducible construction data, distinguish classical cycle distance from quantum distance, and identify the limitations of both families.

Information Theory.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
Information Theory.summary: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

Information Theory.title: AirPASS: Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Pinching Antenna Systems
Information Theory.summary: This paper investigates over-the-air federated learning (AirFL) in wireless systems where the access point is equipped with a multi-waveguide pinching antenna system (PASS). We adopt the widely studied learning-oriented AirFL formulation, which seeks to maximize the number of selected devices while keeping the aggregation distortion below a prescribed threshold. The resulting joint optimization of device selection, receive beamforming, and pinching-antenna placement is highly nonconvex due to the intricate coupling among these system variables. To address this challenge, we develop AirPASS, an alternating optimization framework with two main components: a homotopy-Riemannian margin-consolidation method for device selection and receive beamforming under a fixed PASS configuration, and a homotopy-assisted geometry optimization method for updating the pinching-antenna positions under fixed selected devices and beamformer.

Information Theory.title: BOLT: Universal Classifier Training via a Bayes-Error Upper Bound
Information Theory.summary: This work introduces a novel approach to compute a universal upper bound on the Bayes error rate (BER) from classifier-output samples, which serves as a Bayes-error-related performance criterion for the underlying classification task. We show that the bound is tight in the binary case and characterize the max-sum gap that appears in the aggregate multiclass formulation. Based on this bound, we define a new loss function, called Bayes optimal learning threshold (BOLT), for training parameterized classifiers. For each data sample, the BOLT loss computes a term whose expectation upper-bounds the Bayes error, so that during training the model parameters can be updated toward minimizing this bound. Numerical experiments with both synthetic and real-world datasets show that, in the reported settings, BOLT training often attains lower held-out classification error than cross-entropy training.

Information Theory.title: Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling
Information Theory.summary: We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with $k$ bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly $O(2^{k})$ size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.

Information Theory.title: New scattered linearized quadrinomials
Information Theory.summary: Let $1<t<n$ be integers, where $t$ is a divisor of $n$. An R-$q^t$-partially scattered polynomial is a $\mathbb F_q$-linearized polynomial $f$ in $\mathbb F_{q^n}[X]$ that satisfies the condition that for all $x,y\in\mathbb F_{q^n}^*$ such that $x/y\in\mathbb F_{q^t}$, if $f(x)/x=f(y)/y$, then $x/y\in\mathbb F_q$; $f$ is called scattered if this implication holds for all $x,y\in\mathbb F_{q^n}^*$. Two polynomials in $\mathbb F_{q^n}[X]$ are said to be equivalent if their graphs are in the same orbit under the action of the group $ΓL(2,q^n)$. For $n>8$ only three families of scattered polynomials in $\mathbb F_{q^n}[X]$ are known: $(i)$~monomials of pseudoregulus type, $(ii)$~binomials of Lunardon-Polverino type, and $(iii)$~a family of quadrinomials defined in [1,10] and extended in [8,13]. In this paper we prove that the polynomial $\varphi_{m,q^J}=X^{q^{J(t-1)}}+X^{q^{J(2t-1)}}+m(X^{q^J}-X^{q^{J(t+1)}})\in\mathbb F_{q^{2t}}[X]$, $q$ odd, $t\ge3$ is R-$q^t$-partially scattered for every value of $m\in\mathbb F_{q^t}^*$ and $J$ coprime with $2t$. Moreover, for every $t>4$ and $q>5$ there exist values of $m$ for which $\varphi_{m,q}$ is scattered and new with respect to the polynomials mentioned in $(i)$, $(ii)$ and $(iii)$ above. The related linear sets are of $ΓL$-class at least two.

Information Theory.title: Defining and Generating Compositional Structure
Information Theory.summary: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Yet despite its importance, and despite our apparent ease in recognizing it, mathematical accounts capturing what we intuitively mean by compositional structure remain limited. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. We express this idea using algorithmic information theory, the mathematics of information and compression, which provides a natural way to identify structure in arbitrary data without specifying in advance what that structure must look like. Applied across scales, our definition informs where and how compositional structure emerges within an object. Using tractable approximations, we then invert the framework to generate compositional objects: we specify the desired form of their compositional structure without prescribing their particular content, and optimize directly over strings and images. The resulting objects exhibit readily recognizable hierarchical reuse and part-whole organization, suggesting that the definition captures compositional structure rather than merely complexity, regularity, or shared information. Finally, we discuss implications for machine learning, including a new perspective on depth in neural architectures and principles for constructing compositional data curricula capable of supporting open-ended learning.

Information Theory.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
Information Theory.summary: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.
Information Theory.comment: We take a step toward wireless networks that can compute as well as communicate, using analog RF computing to deliver AI inference to resource-constrained edge devices while simultaneously serving conventional data transmission. This is a follow-up to our analog RF computing framework: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14331. To be presented at IEEE Globecom 2026

Information Theory.title: Multimodal Remote Inference
Information Theory.summary: We consider a remote inference system with multiple modalities, where a multimodal machine learning (ML) model performs real-time inference using features collected from remote sensors. When sensor observations evolve dynamically over time, fresh features are critical for inference tasks. However, timely delivery of features from all modalities is often infeasible under limited network resources. To address this challenge, we formulate a multimodal scheduling problem to minimize the ML model's inference error. We model this error as a general function of the Age of Information (AoI) vector, where AoI quantifies data freshness. We cast the problem as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) and derive an equivalent reformulation with a reduced state set. We then show that the problem has fundamentally different chain structures in the two-modality and multi-modality cases. For the two-modality case, we prove that the optimal policy has an index-based threshold structure. For the general multi-modality case (two or more modalities), we develop an optimal switching-type policy (OPT-ST), which is computed using a multichain policy iteration algorithm (MPI). To further reduce complexity, we also develop two low-complexity policies: the round-robin-like switching-type policy (RR-ST) and the round-robin-like threshold policy (RR-Thres). Numerical results show that OPT-ST achieves the lowest inference error among all baselines, with reductions of up to 80.3%. In a five-modality case, RR-ST and RR-Thres achieve $5.2\times$ and $89.8\times$ speedups in offline computation over OPT-ST, respectively, at the cost of increasing the inference error by 23.3% and 38.6%, respectively.
Information Theory.comment: Submitted to IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking; a preliminary version appeared in the Proceedings of the 22nd IEEE International Conference on Mobile Ad-Hoc and Smart Systems (MASS 2025)

Information Theory.title: ChaosBench-Logic: A Benchmark for Logical and Symbolic Reasoning on Chaotic Dynamical Systems
Information Theory.summary: Large language models (LLMs) excel at natural language tasks but remain brittle in domains requiring precise logical and symbolic reasoning. Chaotic dynamical systems provide an especially demanding test because chaos is deterministic yet often misinterpreted as randomness or complexity. We introduce ChaosBench-Logic, a benchmark that evaluates LLM reasoning across 30 diverse dynamical systems using a unified first-order logic (FOL) ontology. Each system is annotated with truth assignments for 11 semantic predicates, and 621 questions are generated across seven reasoning categories, including multi-hop implications, cross-system analogies, counterfactual reasoning, bias probes, and multi-turn dialogues. We define metrics for logical accuracy, implication consistency, dialogue coherence, and contradiction, and we release an open-source evaluation pipeline. Initial experiments show that frontier LLMs such as GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and the open-source LLaMA-3 70B achieve 91-94% per-item accuracy, yet still score 0% on compositional items and exhibit fragile global coherence. Dialogue-level accuracy ranges from 53.1% (GPT-4 CoT) to 75.5% (LLaMA-3 zero-shot). ChaosBench-Logic provides a rigorous testbed for diagnosing such failures and a foundation for developing neuro-symbolic approaches that improve scientific reasoning in LLMs.
Information Theory.comment: 7 pages, 0 figures, Accepted to AAAI-26 Bridge Program: Logical and Symbolic Reasoning in Language Models (camera-ready). v2: corrected bibliographic errors in the references

Information Theory.title: Mixing and Merging Metric Spaces using Directed Graphs
Information Theory.summary: Let $(X_1,d_1),\dots,(X_N,d_N)$ be metric spaces with $d_i:X_i\times X_i\to[0,1]$ and let $X=\prod_{i=1}^N X_i$. Let $G$ be a directed graph with vertex set $[N]=\{1,\dots,N\}$ and edge set $E(G)$. Given edge weights $P=\{p_{ij}\in(0,1]:(i,j)\in E(G)\}$, define the closed in-neighborhood $B_j(G):=\{j\}\cup\{i:(i,j)\in E(G)\}$ and put $p_{jj}=1$. Define, for $g,h\in X$, \[ d_{X,G,P}(g,h)\;:=\;1-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^N\ \prod_{i\in B_j(G)}\bigl(1-d_i(g_i,h_i)\bigr)^{1/p_{ij}}. \] We prove that $d_{X,G,P}$ is a metric and analyze its behavior under graph operations (disjoint unions, Cartesian products). Two quantitative principles govern this family: (i) \emph{edge densification} (adding edges) increases the distance pointwise and in expectation, with an exact single-edge increment formula and a uniform $1/N$ sensitivity bound; and (ii) \emph{weight monotonicity}: increasing an edge weight $p_{ij}$ decreases the metric. When the coordinate pairs are independent across coordinates, we obtain a closed-form factorization of the mean distance.} In the discrete specialization $X=\mathbb{F}_q^N$ with $d_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $G$ acyclic, after replacing $G$ by the oriented reflexive transitive closure $G^{\preceq}$ of Corollary~1.4, the unnormalized distance $D_{X,G^{\preceq},P}:=N d_{X,G^{\preceq},P}$ coincides with the size of the hereditary closure of the support, yielding a poset/digraph \emph{sphere-packing bound} via the counting of lower ideals. Finally, we give a continuous analog of the construction, yielding a metric on $C([0,1],\mathbb C)$ through an explicit integral formula. These results unify and generalize several graph-based metrics used in coding theory while providing new design levers for mean-distance control.

Probability.title: Supercritical sharpness for Ising double random currents
Probability.summary: We show that the percolation model induced by the double random current representation of the Ising model on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d\geq 3$, satisfies local uniqueness of the macroscopic cluster with high probability for every $β>β_c$, uniformly in boundary conditions (i.e. sources). Such a result is sometimes called supercritical sharpness in percolation theory and yields a detailed description of the model via standard renormalisation techniques. As applications, we show the exponential decay of truncated correlations for the Ising model and exponential mixing for the FK-Ising measure, results previously obtained by Duminil-Copin, Goswami and Raoufi. However, our proof is considerably simpler, as it replaces the use of a highly technical multi-valued map principle with a simple sprinkling argument.

Probability.title: Variation and Hausdorff dimension of fractional Wiener-Weierstrass bridges
Probability.summary: Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass bridges are a class of Gaussian processes obtained by replacing trigonometric functions in the construction of classical Weierstrass functions by fractional Brownian bridges. A number of their sample path properties were derived in Schied--Zhang (2024,2026). The analysis in these papers left several open questions, most of which are addressed here. Specifically, we prove that, in the regime in which the Weierstrass mechanism dominates the underlying fractional Brownian bridge, the limiting $b$-adic variation coefficient has an absolutely continuous distribution and is therefore genuinely random. At the critical point between the two roughness regimes, we establish the power-variation formula and the critical $Φ$-variation limit conjectured in Schied--Zhang (2024). Finally, we derive the Hausdorff dimension for the graphs of the sample paths by proving a conjecture from Schied--Zhang (2026) for the missing high-Hurst case.

Probability.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
Probability.summary: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-N,N]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain. Athreya and Járai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $N\to\infty$. They asked whether, when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the resulting avalanche of topplings is finite. Járai and Redig (2008) proved that the answer is yes for $d\geq 3$, using the transience of random walk. We prove, using a different method, that avalanches are also finite for $d=2$.

Probability.title: Loglinear Hawkes processes: existence, nonexplosion, stability and moment bounds
Probability.summary: This paper discusses a special class of nonlinear Hawkes processes, where the rate function is the exponential function. We call these processes loglinear Hawkes processes. Such processes are used with success in computational neuroscience and we provide a mathematical background for them. After obtaining existence from a standard Poisson embedding, we give sufficient conditions for explosion and nonexplosion that cover a large class of memory functions. In order to give sufficient stability conditions, we construct an autoregressive integer-valued time series that gives pathwise upper bounds for the bin counts of a loglinear Hawkes process. From here, a Markov chain argument shows that the regeneration time for a loglinear Hawkes process has finite expectation if the memory function is negative enough in a neighborhood of zero. Stability in total variation follows. Finally, we show that both the loglinear Hawkes process under a large class of initial conditions and its stationary version have finite exponential moments.

Probability.title: Intermittency for the parabolic Anderson model on spaces with sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates
Probability.summary: We study the parabolic Anderson model $\partial_t u=Δu+βu\,\dot W_α$ on an unbounded Ahlfors $d_h$-regular Dirichlet metric measure space whose heat kernel satisfies two-sided sub-Gaussian estimates with walk dimension $d_w$. The noise is white in time and, in space, either white ($α=0$) or colored through the Riesz kernel of $(-Δ)^{-2α}$, where $0\le 2α<d_h/d_w<1+2α$. No recurrence is assumed. We prove existence, uniqueness and Hölder regularity of the mild Skorohod solution for bounded initial conditions. For nonzero nonnegative bounded initial conditions, the solution is positive and its moment Lyapunov exponents exist for every real $p\ge1$, independently of the spatial point and the initial condition. For $p\ge2$, these exponents have order $p\,(β^2(p-1))^{d_w/((1+2α)d_w-d_h)}$, with upper and lower bounds matching up to constants.

Probability.title: Asymptotic behaviour for escaping an interval by Lévy flights under stochastic resetting
Probability.summary: The resetting of stochastic processes has become a key mechanism appearing in many research fields, such as searching for a target, the transmission control protocol, biology, chemistry, finance, insurance, etc., with the main interest concerning the first passage time (FPT) by the process under resetting. In this paper, we focus on the exit time $\mathcal{T}_L$ from the interval $(-L, L)$ of Lévy flights (LF) under resetting, but we also consider spectrally negative Lévy processes (SNLP). As the main result, we find the asymptotics of the mean first passage time (MFPT) as $L$ tends to $+ \infty$. For LF with $α\in (0, 2)$, the scaling behaves as $L^α$ regardless of the reset rate and the asymmetry of the initial condition, a behaviour completely different from that for the known case of Brownian Motion ($α=2$). For the symmetric $α$-stable case with $α\in (0, 2)$, we also found that taking $r \to \infty$ with fixed $L$ yields a finite MFPT, which therefore may be used as a valid approximation. For completely asymmetric stable processes, we show that the scaling is very different from that for LF, and point out a method to obtain the exact distribution of FPT under resetting. The analytical calculations are verified by numerical simulations of the processes under resetting.

Probability.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
Probability.summary:
Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $μ$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional \emph{Gaussian discrepancy}, defined as $$\mathcal D(μ):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}μ}|G_R^μ(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^μ(x):=(4πR^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,dμ(z)$. Provided that $μ$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\leδ<\infty$, called the \emph{width} of $μ$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}μ\subseteq \bar B_δ(V+x_0),\quad δ^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(μ),$$ where $\bar B_δ(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $δ$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance.
  In particular, when $\mathcal D(μ)=0$, the support of $μ$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $μ$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order.
  The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $μ$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.

Probability.title: Stochastic partial differential equation model for environmental DNA dynamics in river environments
Probability.summary: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a novel tool for quantifying the seasonal abundance of aquatic species in water bodies; however, its mathematical modeling is still at a germinating stage because of its mechanistic uncertainties. We propose a first-step mathematical and computational framework for the eDNA dynamics of migratory fish based on a novel stochastic partial differential equation model with a delayed source input. The model governs spatiotemporal eDNA concentration in rivers where the source comes from a stochastic differential equation for the migration dynamics of the fish. The affine nature of the model facilitates its theoretical analysis, including the guarantee of well-posedness and the closed-form derivation of the Laplace functional despite the proportionality coefficient of the multiplicative noise term being non-Lipschitz. We also propose a discretization scheme for the model that theoretically generates nonnegative numerical solutions. We finally apply the proposed model to eDNA concentration data sampled from midstream reaches of a river system and perform sensitivity analysis.

Probability.title: Critical oriented percolation enhanced along random supercritical horizontal lines
Probability.summary: We consider the oriented site percolation model in a random environment introduced by Kesten, Sidoravicius and Vares (2022), in which the horizontal lines of the lattice are independently declared bad or good, sites being open with a probability that depends only on the type of their line. We study the boundary case where the bad lines are critical and the good ones supercritical, so that the model is critical oriented site percolation enhanced along a random set of good lines. We prove that percolation occurs for any positive density of the good lines. An arbitrarily sparse set of arbitrarily weakly enhanced lines suffices, the density of good lines and the strength of the enhancement being decoupled. The proof adapts the renormalization scheme of Archer, Hartarsky, Kolesnik, Olesker-Taylor, Schapira and Valesin (2026). We show that the edge of the process travels at a positive speed, which yields crossing estimates for tilted boxes; during runs of bad lines, we rely on the box-crossing property of Duminil-Copin, Tassion and Teixeira (2018); and the renormalized model dominates the oriented percolation with geometric defects of Hilário, Sá, Sanchis and Teixeira (2026).

Probability.title: Jump limits of continuous multiscale diffusions: Homogenization under heavy-tailed activity bursts
Probability.summary: We show that purely continuous microscopic diffusions can homogenize to a Markov process with genuine jumps. Consider a multiscale diffusion with time-dependent generator $\mathcal{L}_{0}+r_{t}^ε\mathcal{L}_{1}$ driven by a regenerative random environment. When the integrated activity over a regeneration cycle has a regularly varying tail of index $β\in(0,1)$, the cumulative operational clock converges to a $β$-stable subordinator, compressing finite activity-driven diffusion into vanishingly short physical time intervals. To overcome the noncommutativity of $\mathcal{L}_0$ and $\mathcal{L}_1$, we develop an extended-time parametrization paired with Khasminskii-type time discretization, establishing finite-dimensional convergence and strong semigroup convergence on $C_{0}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ toward a jump process with nonlocal generator $\overline{\mathcal{L}}=\mathcal{L}_{0}-κ(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$. Under uniform ellipticity of $\mathcal{L}_{1}$, the fractional power $(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$ is identified as a $2β$-stable-like nonlocal operator. We also clarify physical-time path-topology obstructions and apply the framework to Poisson resetting pulses, Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, and multiscale stochastic volatility.

Probability.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
Probability.summary: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.

Probability.title: The Odlyzko-Poonen Conjecture on Irreducibility of Random Polynomials
Probability.summary: The Odlyzko-Poonen conjecture states that a monic polynomial of constant coefficient $1$ and with remaining coefficients chosen independently and uniformly from $\{0,1 \}$ is irreducible over the rational numbers with probability tending to one as the degree tends to infinity. We prove the Odlyzko-Poonen conjecture unconditionally.
Probability.comment: 11 pages. Minor clarifications to previous version

Probability.title: Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise
Probability.summary: We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional càdlàg semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler-Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by $n$ converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative drift regularity conditions based on small-jump integrability or Lévy semigroup smoothing. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.

Probability.title: Fractional Navier-Stokes Equations with Caputo Derivative Driven by Hermite Noise
Probability.summary: We study time-fractional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations on a bounded domain of $\R^2$, driven by a cylindrical Hermite noise of order $k\ge1$ and Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$, built mode-by-mode on the eigenbasis of the Stokes operator. This class of noises generalizes fractional Brownian motion ($k=1$) and the Rosenblatt process ($k=2$) to arbitrary non-Gaussian order. Combining Wiener-chaos hypercontractivity with Hilbert-Schmidt estimates for the Mittag-Leffler operator, we establish the regularity of the associated stochastic convolution. A Da Prato-Debussche decomposition, carried out in a scale of Lebesgue spaces $L^q_σ(D)$ on which the bilinear term is controlled by a Calderón-Zygmund estimate, then yields existence and uniqueness of a maximal mild solution, and Hölder regularity of the time-frozen solution under the condition $\al+2H>2$ together with standard regularity assumptions on the initial datum. We further obtain moment bounds for the stochastic convolution and for the quadratic self-interaction of the noise, whose growth in the moment order is governed by $k$, and a functional non-central limit theorem giving a radially localised approximation of the solution by systems driven by functionals of Gaussian sequences with long-range dependence.

Probability.title: Sharp Weak-Trace Regularity of Stochastic Cross Integrals
Probability.summary: We prove a sharp spatial regularity theorem for the Itô and Stratonovich cross integrals of continuous semimartingales in separable Hilbert spaces. Without global moment assumptions, both integrals admit versions that are almost surely jointly continuous in the two time variables, with values in the little weak-trace ideal. This regularity is optimal even for Wiener processes with deterministic trace-one covariance. Given any positive sequence tending to zero, we construct such a process for which the singular values of its Lévy area, multiplied by their indices, tend to zero but have termwise ratios to the prescribed sequence tending to infinity almost surely. The same property holds simultaneously for both self-integrals. The upper bound follows from a rank-one cancellation in Itô's formula for a determinant, together with finite-rank approximation. For the lower bound, conditional Gaussian estimates and orthogonal time functions yield finite-dimensional spectral bounds, which are combined through a trace-one covariance to obtain lower bounds for all sufficiently large indices.

Probability.title: Entropic Inequalities and Limit Theorems in Boolean Probability
Probability.summary: We study Boolean entropy and Fisher information in information inequalities and the Boolean central limit theorem. We prove a fractional Stam inequality for the Boolean Fisher information associated with arbitrary fractional partitions of subset sums, and derive an entropy power inequality for sums of Boolean independent random variables and its weighted version. We then establish a Boolean analogue of Barron's entropy convergence result along the Boolean central limit theorem: Boolean entropy converges to the entropy of the Rademacher law if and only if the initial entropy is finite. Furthermore, under a finite fourth moment, in the Boolean central limit theorem, we obtain \[ Γ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b)= \frac{m_4(μ)-1-m_3(μ)^2}{2}\frac{\log n}{n} +o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \] with an explicit example showing sharpness. For symmetric laws with finite fourth moment and finite Boolean Fisher information, \[ Ψ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b) =2\bigl(m_4(μ)-1\bigr)\frac{\log n}{n} +o\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right). \] Our approach is based on the Nevanlinna representation of Cauchy transforms.

Probability.title: Simple repair policies and decompositions for semi-coherent systems with simultaneous failures
Probability.summary: We consider semi-coherent binary systems that are subject to simultaneous failures of its components. These are systems whose components can be either working or failed; the system can also be working or failed depending on the state of the components; and repairing a component cannot cause the system to fail. We consider that one or more components can fail simultaneously, allowing us to model external shocks and disasters. For this, we use the Lévy-frailty Marshall-Olkin (LFMO) multivariate distribution to model the failure times of the components. We aim to answer in which states of the system we should repair the components. This is a challenging question, as the number of repair policies grows super-exponentially in the number of components. To tackle this, we propose a simple family of repair policies, which we call $r$-out-of-$n$:R repair policies, where one repairs all failed components when the system fails or when there are $r$ or more failed components. Our main contribution is that we derive exact and simple expressions for key performance-evaluation quantities of the system operating under our proposed repair policies. That is, we give explicit expressions for the mean time-to-failure of the system, mean time-to-repair, probability of system-failure before repair, and component- and system-repair rate. We also give expressions for the expected cost and long-term average cost, when there are components' and system repair cost. The only relevant parameters involved in the derived expressions are the structural signature of the system, and the Laplace exponent associated to the LFMO distribution.

Probability.title: Metastability and Sharp Propagation-of-Chaos Thresholds for Mean-Field Interacting Diffusions on the Circle
Probability.summary: We study metastability and long-time propagation-of-chaos for mean-field interacting diffusions on the circle with multiple local free-energy minima. Working modulo rotations, we identify sharp exponential time scales for metastability and the validity and breakdown of the McKean-Vlasov approximation. Assuming finitely many critical rotation orbits and distinct local-minimum energies, we show that, for initial data in the attraction basin of a nonglobal minimum, metastability and propagation-of-chaos hold uniformly over deterministic times up to $e^{N(D-\varepsilon)}$ and fail at every deterministic sequence growing faster than $e^{N(D+\varepsilon)}$. Here $N$ is the particle number and $D$ the depth of the maximal Freidlin-Wentzell energy cycle having that minimum as its bottom. The same threshold governs running averages of the squared approximation error in a stronger pathwise sense, with corresponding metastability and propagation-of-chaos bounds for suitably aligned time-averaged empirical measures. When the global-minimum orbit is unique, we establish uniform-in-time propagation-of-chaos in its attraction basin without assuming finitely many critical orbits. The proofs develop the Freidlin-Wentzell cycle analysis for the empirical measure process and exploit Dawson and Gärtner's fixed-horizon large deviation estimates to analyze long excursions between metastable wells. We give a checkable Fourier criterion for finiteness of the critical orbits. We also investigate connections with phase transitions in the free-energy landscape, and discuss applications to the noisy Kuramoto and noisy transformer models. We provide, to our knowledge, the first sharp exponential-time analysis of the Dawson-Gärtner `tunnelling phenomenon' for general smooth interactions, with two-sided probability bounds and matching propagation-of-chaos thresholds.
Probability.comment: Minor typos corrected. Some additional comparisons to existing work and acknowledgements added. 78 pages

Probability.title: Drift parameter estimation for interacting particle systems with singular repulsion
Probability.summary: We study the estimation of the interaction parameter in singular interacting particle systems from continuous and discrete observations over a fixed time horizon. The singularity of the interaction drift prevents the direct application of standard likelihood and contrast-based methods, which rely on regularity assumptions that fail in this setting. Our approach exploits an exact reduction of the particle dynamics to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation for a quadratic empirical moment. By the symmetry of the interaction kernel, the singular terms cancel, yielding an explicit estimator in which the unknown parameter enters linearly. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality as the number of particles, \(N\), tends to infinity. Letting \(\varepsilon_N\) denote the microscopic noise scaling of the system, we obtain asymptotic normality at the rate \(\sqrt{N/\varepsilon_N}\) for strictly positive interaction kernels, under an additional condition on the limiting empirical information. We further extend these results to degenerate interaction kernels, achieving consistency and asymptotic normality at rate \(N\) under suitable structural assumptions and the canonical scaling \(\varepsilon_N=N^{-1}\). In both regimes, we provide conditions on the observation mesh ensuring that the statistical limits remain valid under discrete sampling, in high frequency. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our methodology through Dyson Brownian motion, the Dyson Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, and Wishart--Laguerre particle systems, alongside a numerical investigation of the estimators' finite-sample performance.

Probability.title: KPP type reaction--diffusion equations in narrow tubes with degenerating boundary and generalized second order operators
Probability.summary: We consider a reaction--diffusion equation with Kolmogorov--Petrovskii--Piskunov (KPP) nonlinearity and Neumann boundary conditions in a narrow tube $G^{\varepsilon,δ}\subset\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ of width of order $\varepsilon$. The tube is chosen from a family indexed by a second parameter $δ>0$, whose boundary $\partial G^δ$ is smooth for each $δ>0$ but degenerates as $δ\downarrow0$. In the iterated limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ followed by $δ\downarrow0$ the problem becomes a Cauchy problem on the line whose spatial operator is a generalized second order differential operator $D_{v}D_{u}$ in the sense of Feller, rather than a classical second order elliptic operator. Solutions of the limiting problem need not be differentiable in $x$, so they must be understood in a generalized sense. Using the Feynman--Kac representation, we prove that the limiting problem has a unique generalized solution. When the cross sectional volume is bounded above and below, we also prove that this solution is Hölder continuous in $t$ with exponent $1/2$, locally uniformly in $x$, whenever it is Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Under the same volume bounds, this Lipschitz condition holds when the initial function and the nonlinearity are Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Finally we prove that the solutions in the narrow tubes converge to the generalized solution uniformly on compact time intervals in the same iterated limit if the tube, the initial function, and the nonlinearity are periodic in $x$.

Probability.title: Minimax Binary Counting under Shuffle Privacy: Poisson Limits and Randomized-Response Optimality
Probability.summary: We study estimation of a deterministic binary count from the shuffled outputs of a common single-message local channel. Privacy is required for every neighboring composition at fixed global parameters $(\varepsilon,δ)$, and estimators may be biased. We obtain uniform critical Poisson and Skellam approximations and characterize the limiting minimax risk as an infimum over finite observed-mark Poisson experiments. Let $Λ$ be the noise intensity required by the boundary Poisson-shift profile and let $λ_{\min}$ be the intensity required by the full composition-maximized randomized-response profile. Binary randomized response is asymptotically minimax optimal if and only if $Λ=λ_{\min}$. When $Λ<λ_{\min}$, the minimax value lies strictly between $(Λ+λ_{\min})/2$ and $λ_{\min}$, and a randomized-response construction with observed rare marks strictly improves on binary randomized response. We give a finite-sample certified example. Binary randomized response is strictly suboptimal at $\varepsilon=0$ for every $0<δ<1$, and this persists for sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ at each fixed target. For every fixed positive $\varepsilon$, strict suboptimality also occurs along a sequence of fixed privacy targets tending to zero. The variational characterization permits approximation by finite marked channels; it does not assert that a finite optimizer exists.
Probability.comment: 39 pages, 1 figure. v2: complete revision with a new title and scope; it replaces v1 entirely. The two-dominant hybrid argument of v1 is withdrawn (see the Introduction). Ancillary files contain the certificate scripts for Proposition 10.1

Probability.title: Approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic hybrid systems with empirically observed ergodic behaviour
Probability.summary: Piecewise diffusion Markov processes (PDifMPs) form a versatile class of stochastic hybrid systems that combine continuous diffusion processes with discrete event-driven dynamics, enabling flexible modelling of complex real-world hybrid phenomena. The practical utility of PDifMP models, however, depends critically on accurate estimation of their underlying parameters. In this work, we present a novel framework for parameter inference in PDifMPs based on approximate Bayesian computation (ABC). Our contributions are threefold. First, we provide detailed simulation algorithms for PDifMP sample paths. Second, we extend existing ABC summary statistics for diffusion processes to account for the hybrid nature of PDifMPs, showing particular effectiveness for ergodic systems. Third, we demonstrate our approach on several representative example PDifMPs that empirically exhibit ergodic behaviour. Our results show that the proposed ABC method reliably recovers model parameters across all examples, even in challenging scenarios where only partial information on jumps and diffusion is available or when parameters appear in state-dependent jump rate functions. These findings highlight the potential of ABC as a practical tool for inference in various complex stochastic hybrid systems.

Probability.title: Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process
Probability.summary:
We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $α$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE).
  A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $α=α_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($α<\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $α= \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation.
  The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.

Probability.title: Hypocoercivity of Tempered Bouncy Particle Samplers for Heavy-Tailed Targets
Probability.summary: We introduce the Tempered Bouncy Particle Sampler, a state-dependently tempered generalisation of the Bouncy Particle Sampler. Adapting the hypocoercivity framework of Dolbeault, Mouhot and Schmeiser (2010), we establish explicit, non-asymptotic exponential convergence bounds for a broad class of heavy-tailed targets that need not be log-concave or radially symmetric, including distributions with polynomial tails. The convergence rate is linked to the spectral gap of a tempered Langevin diffusion with the same invariant distribution, making a weighted Poincaré inequality the key assumption. We give admissible tempering choices for polynomial and stretched-exponential tails and derive mixing-time bounds with polynomial dependence on the dimension.
Probability.comment: 42 pages, 2 figures; the revised version contains a new Appendix C exhibiting a measure where the weighted Poincare inequality does not hold; for short YouTube presentation discussing the main results, see https://youtu.be/HhlTlsyhhzY?si=S9ZTErX9NkR8Ctwj , and proofs, see https://youtu.be/tX93nqGz1WU?si=as1Pfu75ruAXv4A5

Probability.title: Interior smoothness and zero-variance geometry for finite-maturity Heston American puts
Probability.summary: We study finite-maturity American puts in the Heston model without the Feller condition. At positive variance, the exercise boundary is smooth and strictly decreasing in remaining maturity and variance. At zero variance, the endpoint is locally Lipschitz in remaining maturity, the boundary moves with bounded speed in maturity uniformly down to zero variance, and it extends continuously to the axis. Each boundary slice at positive maturity has a regular $C^1$ closure tangent to the zero-variance axis, its stock threshold has variance derivative tending to minus infinity, and both partial derivatives of the inverse boundary graph vanish along the slice. The continuation premium at the axis contact stock is of order variance, and as a consequence smooth fit fails in the variance direction at the axis. At expiry the whole boundary, including its axis edge, converges to the strike. We give quantitative boundary gap bounds, an exact limiting weighted boundary Hessian, and vertical identities retaining the maturity term. Exact boundary gap equivalents remain open.

Probability.title: Universality of the conformal anomaly
Probability.summary:
The sewing operation is the fundamental algebraic structure of the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces as the conformal cobordism category. We prove a universal property of local $\mathbb{R}_+$-extensions of the sewing operation, characterizing them by one real parameter: their central charge. Our result is an analogue of ``Mumford's theorem,'' that appeared in Segal's monograph [Seg88, Seg04], classifying complex extensions, also known as one-dimensional modular functors. Algebraically, the real extensions are characterized by real-valued cocycles on pairs of surfaces under sewing. We identify the disk-disk cocycle as the universal Liouville action, also known as loop Loewner energy.
  The real determinant line bundle encodes the trace anomaly of euclidean two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFT) and the restriction function of Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) loop measures. It serves as the guiding example in our setup and proof strategy, providing the universal $\mathbb{R}_+$-extension. Our results thus give a mathematical explanation for the appearance of the central charge in CFT and SLE, and prove the conjectured uniqueness of Brownian loop measures as the canonical restriction function for SLE.
Probability.comment: 70 pages, 3 figures; minor additions and improvements, renamed real one-dimensional modular functor to R+ extension

Probability.title: Angles and volumes of simplices, boxes, and crosspolytopes in constant curvature
Probability.summary: We determine, up to isometry, the Riemannian tangent and normal cones at arbitrary faces of boxes, acute orthocentric simplices, rectangular simplices, and asymmetric crosspolytopes in spaces of constant sectional curvature $κ\in\mathbb R$. Using these descriptions, we derive explicit one-dimensional integral formulas for their internal and external angles in arbitrary dimension. In particular, our results cover regular simplices, cubes, and crosspolytopes, the three families of regular polytopes existing in every dimension. We also establish a correspondence between regular simplices and cubes with isometric local cones at corresponding faces, provided their edge-length parameters are suitably matched. Combining our angle formulas with the Poincaré relation, we obtain volume formulas for simplices and crosspolytopes in even dimensions. For boxes, we derive volume formulas valid in every dimension. Among the new results are angle formulas for spherical and hyperbolic cubes and crosspolytopes, volume formulas for asymmetric crosspolytopes, and a one-dimensional integral representation for the internal angles of regular crosspolytopes that appears to be new even in the Euclidean case. The formulas involve the standard normal distribution function $Φ(x)$ and its values at purely imaginary arguments $Φ(\mathrm{i} x)$. For example, if $d\geq 2$ is even, then the volume of the ideal regular simplex in the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space of curvature $κ=-1$ is given by the absolutely convergent integral $$ \frac{π^{d/2}} {\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{i}^{d}\, Γ\left(\frac{d+1}{2}\right)} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \left[ Φ\left(\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} + Φ\left(-\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} \right] \mathrm{e}^{-y^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}y. $$
Probability.comment: 45 pages. Title changed; abstract revised; minor corrections

Probability.title: Efron type identities for stopping sets and Poisson hulls
Probability.summary: We consider a Poisson process $η$ on a general Borel space with intensity measure $λ$ and a stopping set $Z$ depending on $η$. Generalizing earlier results we prove a spatial Markov property for $Z$. In fact we establish this property for the larger class of finitely insertion tolerant random sets, which include pointwise limits of stopping sets. Using the spatial Markov property of $η$, we derive several distributional identities for the restrictions of $η$ and $λ$ to $Z$ and the complement of $Z$. An important special case in Euclidean space is the convex hull of a finite Poisson process. In this case our results generalize classical (and also more recent) identities connecting the number of vertices and the volume of the convex hull.

Probability.title: From smooth to discontinuous kernels: a variance transfer principle for hyperuniform processes
Probability.summary: We give a transfer principle for the fluctuations of linear statistics of finite particle systems around Lebesgue measure: if for a smooth kernel the variance decays polynomially with some exponent a compared to independent (non-interacting) particles, then the number variance over balls centred at almost every point decays with exponent min(1,a) times a log term if a=1, over a possibly reduced range of scales for non-periodic systems. We apply this principle to eigenvalues of random N*N Girko matrices, leveraging results of Cipolloni et al., and obtain the optimal perimeter-like number variance, on the microscopic and some mesoscopic scales range, after local averaging. We also apply the results to Coulomb gases, by transferring the results of Serfaty: we prove that 2D-Coulomb gases are 2-hyperuniform, i.e. they have surface order number variance, which is optimal, and that 3D Coulomb gases are 1-hyperuniform. In 2D, it allows to prove finite Coulomb energy and Wasserstein distance to Lebesgue measure.

Probability.title: Triggered urn models for frequently asked questions (FAQ)
Probability.summary: We investigate a nonclassic urn model with triggers that increase the number of colors. The scheme has emerged as a model for web services that set up frequently asked questions (FAQ). We present a thorough asymptotic analysis of the FAQ urn scheme in generality that covers a large number of special cases, such as Simon's urn. For instance, we consider time dependent triggering probabilities. We identify regularity conditions on these probabilities that classify the schemes into those where the number of colors in the urn remains almost surely finite or increases to infinity and conditions that tell us whether all the existing colors are observed infinitely often or not. We determine the rank curve, too. In view of the broad generality of the trigger probabilities, a spectrum of limit distributions appears, from central limit theorems to Poisson approximation, to power-laws, revealing connections to Heaps exponent and Zipf's law. A combinatorial approach to the Simon urn is presented to indicate the possibility of such exact analysis, which is important for short-term predictions. Extensive simulations on real datasets (from Amazon sales) as well as computer-generated data clearly indicate that the asymptotic and exact theory developed agrees with practice.

Probability.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
Probability.summary:
We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma.
  This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

Probability.title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $α$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
Probability.summary: Score-based generative models driven by $α$-stable L{é}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $α$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails. At any positive generation time, stable dynamics produces power-law tails with index $α$, whereas Brownian dynamics remains light-tailed. For a target with tail index $ν$, asymptotically correct extreme-quantile scaling is possible precisely when $α$=$ν$. These results identify tail-index matching as a principled mechanism behind the ability of stable generative models to capture extreme events.

Probability.title: Gaussian approximation for the integrated intensity of counting processes: application to Hawkes processes
Probability.summary: In this paper, we establish quantitative central limit theorems for the integrated fluctuations of the intensity of a counting process. Building on the work of Coutin and using the Clark-Ocone formula, we first derive a general upper bound on the Wasserstein distance between a Gaussian random variable and the normalized integral of the centered intensity. We then apply this result to subcritical linear Hawkes processes. In this setting, we prove that the integrated fluctuations of the intensity converge in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable, with a convergence rate governed by the tail behavior of the resolvent associated with the underlying Volterra equation.

Probability.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
Probability.summary: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.

Probability.title: Asymptotics and finite sample bounds for prediction and smoothing in Wright-Fisher hidden Markov models
Probability.summary: We study signal prediction and smoothing in hidden Markov models whose latent signal is a multi-type Wright-Fisher diffusion and whose discrete-time observations are categorical. We consider a repeated-sampling regime with finitely many inspection times and large within-time samples. Under parent-independent mutation, the Bayesian predictive and smoothing laws admit exact representations as mixtures of Dirichlet distributions. We show that the one-step predictive and local smoothing laws converge in total variation to the corresponding Wright-Fisher transition and bridge laws determined by the neighboring population frequencies, thereby justifying plug-in approximations based on empirical proportions. For prediction, we derive explicit finite-sample bounds for this approximation and for bounded predictive functionals such as diversity, together with a finite-sample concentration bound for the marginal smoother. The joint posterior at the inspection times concentrates at the target frequencies and satisfies a Bernstein-von Mises limit with distinct interior and boundary regimes, with Gaussian and Gamma limits on different scales. The results allow arbitrary dependence across inspection times. A key technical ingredient is a fixed-interval tail bound for the coalescent-based dual death process.

Probability.title: Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes
Probability.summary: We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.

Probability.title: Algebra of spectral duality structures
Probability.summary: This paper establishes the algebraic and categorical foundations of spectral duality structures (SDS). We show that the class of all SDS admits the structure of a graded symmetric monoidal category, where the degree $K$ is the fundamental invariant indexing the strata. We define operations of Cartesian product and disjoint union, morphisms preserving involution and weights, and prove that $C^\ast=1/(1+\sqrt K)$ is a functor constant on each stratum. We classify objects up to isomorphism by the combinatorial type $(k,f)$, the degree $K$, and a multiset of inversion classes $[r]=\{r,r^{-1}\}$. In each degree, skeletons are exactly the finite $C_2$-sets over the additive group of the reals with $C_2$ acting by $t\mapsto -t$, which explains the monoidal structure and identifies the classification with the decomposition into orbits. Furthermore, we prove that the response rank is the rank of an explicit matrix built from the amplitudes and the weights, and hence exactly the number of non-trivial pairs $k$ under the full-rank condition, and we connect the categorical structure with the Fisher--Rao geometry of Paper V. The SDS, originally discovered in stochastic resetting problems, is thus an autonomous mathematical object with a rich algebraic structure and a natural geometric realisation.

Probability.title: Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions
Probability.summary: We study the geometry that spectral duality induces on the simplex of reset distributions for absorbed Markov processes with geometric resetting. In the Fisher--Rao metric, selected by Čencov's theorem, the separatrix $Σ$ of reset-neutral distributions is rigid: under the square-root embedding $π\mapsto2\sqrtπ$ its interior is a totally geodesic subsphere of the positive octant, itself a lower-dimensional Fisher--Rao simplex. The reset response reduces to a finite structure: the response functionals span a subspace whose dimension $r$ equals the number of active orbits of the duality involution, and the local separatrix is its annihilator. At the vertices of the simplex we prove a sign theorem valid for every $r$, which recovers the two-zone phenomenon of the first paper of this series. The invariant $r$ also settles the question of global orientation: for $r=1$, under a scalar sign condition satisfied by the canonical realisation, the sign of the response is fixed by the side of $Σ$; for $r\ge2$ the orientation cannot stay constant, and we give the criterion under which no global sign law holds, with counterexamples due to T. Newton showing that it is met in the abstract class. The biased random walk with multi-site geometric resetting realises the whole picture explicitly.
Probability.comment: 46 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, v2: revised version

Probability.title: Eddy viscosity by Lévy transport noises
Probability.summary: We consider stochastic linear transport equations in dimension $d\geq 2$ and stochastic 2D Euler equations with $L^2$-initial condition, both driven by Lévy transport noise in the Marcus sense. Under a suitable scaling limit of the noises, we prove that the solutions to the stochastic linear transport equations converge to the solution of the deterministic heat equation, while weak solutions to the stochastic 2D Euler equations converge weakly to the unique solution of the deterministic 2D Navier--Stokes equation. These results show that small-scale jump noises generate eddy viscosity, extending the recent studies on Itô--Stratonovich diffusion limits to the discontinuous setting.
Probability.comment: 43 pages. We have added Lem 2.9 and Prop 2.10 on properties of convergence in Skorohod topology, Prop 3.2 on the existence of stochastic flow of Marcus SDE. We have also rewritten the convergence of stochastic integral in Step 3 of proof of Theorem 1.5

Probability.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
Probability.summary: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{ξ_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{ξ_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^α}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ α=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ α=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ α>-1/2 $ is also obtained.

Probability.title: Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
Probability.summary: In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate.
