We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $λ$, where the critical value equals $λ_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $λ_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<λ<λ_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $λ_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $λ_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.

Probability.title: Local Linearization and Exact Oscillations for the Nonlinear Stochastic Heat Equation with Spatially Rough Noise
Probability.summary:
Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear stochastic heat equation $$ \frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t} =
\frac{\partial^2 u(t,x)}{\partial x^2} +
σ(u(t,x))\dot W(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R, $$ where $\dot W$ is a Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1/2)$. Hu et al. ({\it Ann. Probab.} {\bf 45} (2017), 4561--4616) established existence and uniqueness of the solution under the assumptions that $σ$ is differentiable, both $σ$ and $σ'$ are Lipschitz continuous, and $σ(0)=0$. Hu and Wang ({\it Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat.} {\bf 58} (2022), 379--423) subsequently removed the technical condition $σ(0)=0$ by developing the well-posedness theory in a suitable weighted space associated with the weight $λ(x)= c_H (1 + |x|^2)^{H-1}$.
  In this weighted framework, which allows $σ(0)\ne0$, we establish temporal and spatial local linearizations: small increments of the nonlinear solution are approximated by the corresponding increments of the solution to the additive equation, multiplied by the local coefficient $σ(u(t,x))$. The main difficulty lies in handling the nonlocal fractional-difference structure induced by the rough spatial noise. We address this difficulty using weighted heat-kernel increment estimates. These approximations yield exact Lévy-type uniform moduli of continuity in both time and space, together with Khinchin and Chung laws of the iterated logarithm.

Probability.title: Polynomial mixing for stochastic viscous conservation law equation on the whole line
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of the viscous conservation law equation on the whole real line, subject to a white-in-time force and arbitrarily small damping and viscosity constants. We establish polynomial mixing rates in two settings: (a) a general super-quadratic flux with hyperviscous dissipation, where the growth of the nonlinearity is controlled by the order of hyperviscosity, and the force is sufficiently non-degenerate on a generic L2-basis; and (b) a general quadratic flux with standard second-order dissipation, and the force is non-degenerate on some unconditional basis. Both settings include the classical Burgers-type nonlinearity. The proof is based on an abstract polynomial coupling criterion developed in arXiv:2408.00592 and a Foiaş--Prodi estimate.

Probability.title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
Probability.summary: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.

Probability.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
Probability.summary: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.

Probability.title: Fluctuations in the Potts spin glass model at high temperature
Probability.summary: We study the fluctuations of the free energy of the Potts spin glass with $κ$ colors at high temperature. The disorder is symmetric with unit variance and finite fourth moment. For configurations with a balanced, or nearly balanced, color profile, the log-partition function satisfies a central limit theorem whenever $β^2<α_c(κ)$. Here $κα_c(κ)$ is the critical inverse temperature of the Curie-Weiss-Potts model. A comparison of color profiles transfers this limit to the unconstrained model for $β<β_{\max}(κ)$, an explicit threshold. In the same range, the magnetizations of two replicas and their overlap matrix satisfy a joint quenched central limit theorem with independent Gaussian limits. The fourth cumulant of the disorder enters the limiting mean and variance explicitly.

Probability.title: Crossing numbers of simplicial complexes
Probability.summary: This paper studies crossing numbers of $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes drawn in $\mathbb R^{2d}$ or $\mathbb S^{2d}$. We clarify and generalize a number of known results and conjectures from the graph case to higher dimensions: the crossing lemma (including the exceptional case of two-dimensional complexes drawn in dimension $4$), a generalized Harary-Hill conjecture (and evidence for it), existence of a midrange crossing constant (in a weak sense), and upper bound constructions based on stochastic geometry (related to Sylvester's problem) and the cyclic polytope. Some of our results are new even in the case of graphs: we give a simple proof of the Harary-Hill conjecture for antipodal drawings, and sharpen the threshold above which the rectilinear and spherical crossing numbers of the Erdős-Rényi random graph behave like those of the complete graph.

Probability.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
Probability.summary: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.

Probability.title: Dynamic models with $p$ parameters are identified by $2p+1$ random features
Probability.summary: A foundational principle in nonlinear dynamics is that the structure of a dynamical system can be recovered from a small number of generic measurements or coordinates. We develop an analogous principle for the identification of dynamic models for time series \textit{with noise}, which builds on previous identification results for noiseless dynamical systems. The noise is allowed to be non-iid, non-Gaussian, and dependent on the state. Our results cover noisily observed differential equations and discrete-time dynamical systems, as well as stochastic models with process noise. We illustrate the utility of this identification principle using a Lorenz-63 model and a Hénon map model, both with observational noise.

Probability.title: Competitive displacement in the grass-bushes-trees process on a scale-free network
Probability.summary: The grass-bushes-trees process is a two-type contact process in which the types face asymmetric birth mechanisms. Vertices of a graph can either be occupied by a tree, occupied by a bush, or empty (containing grass). The trees die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $λ_{\mathcal T}$ on any neighbouring vertex (possibly taking the place of a bush). Bushes die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $λ_{\mathcal B}$ on any empty neighbouring vertex; in particular, they are forbidden from taking the place of trees. We study this process on a power law random graph, namely the erased configuration model. We study which graph parameters lead to the possibility of coexistence versus the necessity of competitive displacement, i.e. joint metastability or fast extinction of the bushes.

Probability.title: $q_x$-Bass Martingales: Optimality, Existence and Convergence
Probability.summary: We introduce the class of $q_x$-Bass martingales, extending the notion of $q$-Bass martingales. These are martingale couplings with prescribed marginals whose transition kernels are closest to a given family of reference kernels $(q_x)_{x \in \mathbb R^d}$ in the sense of a suitable weak optimal transport problem. We show that $q_x$-Bass martingales are optimizers of this problem and establish a strong duality result. Building on this duality, we introduce an algorithm for their computation and, under compactness assumptions on the prescribed marginals, prove its convergence, thereby establishing existence. We then specialize to one-dimensional marginals and show that the algorithm reduces to a fixed-point iteration.

Probability.title: Infinite-variation Lévy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
Probability.summary: We prove that every real Lévy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a Lévy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.

Probability.title: The Q-process for the general mother-dependent multitype branching process
Probability.summary: The general mother-dependent neutral mutations model is a multitype branching process describing a population evolving in discrete time, in which mutations occur among a finite set of alleles: each mutant, independently of the others, acquires an allele different from its mother's, according to a prescribed distribution. We study the associated mutant and clone-mutant chains conditioned on extinction in the distant future, that is, their $Q$-processes, and we give an explicit description of their laws in the (sub)critical and in the supercritical regimes alike. Even under this conditioning, the clone-mutant process associated with the mother-dependent neutral mutations model is obtained from the corresponding infinite-alleles BGW process (studied in Bertoin (2010) and Blancas and Rivero (2018)) by an independent multinomial colouring with specific parameters. We also obtain the spine decomposition of the multitype mutant chain, from which we derive a Kesten--Stigum theorem in the supercritical regime and a genealogical construction of the Q-process in the (sub)critical one.

Probability.title: Third-moment cancellation and predictable representation in finite-state BSDE approximation
Probability.summary: We study finite-state approximations of Brownian-driven Markovian backward stochastic differential equations when the same one-step increment is used both for weak propagation and for martingale representation. For a centered isotropic state-independent increment with vanishing third moment, we prove first-order convergence of the Markov value field, its spatial gradient, and the predictable $Z$-field under suitable smoothness assumptions. The corresponding orthogonal martingale has maximal $L^2$ size $O(h^{1/2})$. We identify its quadratic representation defect and prove a joint functional limit theorem for the state process and the normalized orthogonal martingale, which in particular yields a mixed-normal terminal limit with path-dependent conditional variance. On the trace-free quadratic sector, the representation defect has the sharp universal operator lower bound $d/[2(d+2)]$; equality holds exactly for normalized laws that are weighted spherical 4-designs. In dimension $d\geq 2$, vanishing third moment is incompatible with exact scalar one-step predictable representation for any finite-state centered isotropic increment. Consequently, every such exact-representation law has a nonzero cubic direction, and a smooth Fourier terminal condition converts this direction into a sharp global $h^{1/2}$ weak error. For the centrally symmetric regular-simplex rule we also identify the leading quadratic GKW component, compute the exact first-order asymptotic of the accumulated orthogonal-martingale variance, and recover it from the general functional limit. Thus the same third-order tensor links weak accuracy and predictable representation, yielding an accuracy-representation tradeoff for finite-state BSDE approximations.

Probability.title: Derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics (after Y. Deng, Z. Hani, and X. Ma)
Probability.summary: Consider a microscopic system of $N$ hard spheres that are initially independent (modulo the exclusion condition on particle positions) and identically distributed in $\mathbb{R}^3$. When the number $N$ of particles goes to infinity and the diameter $\varepsilon$ of the particles goes to zero, and under the weak density assumption $N\varepsilon^2=1$, it has been known since the work of Lanford that the empirical measure for the particles converges to the solution of the Boltzmann equation in a short time interval. In particular, the particles remain dynamically independent, in this limit and in the short time interval where the correlations induced by their collisions remain under control. In a recent work, Y. Deng, Z. Hani and X. Ma successfully obtained the same convergence result in arbitrary large time; more precisely, the convergence result holds for any time interval on which the Boltzmann equation has a regular solution. In this note, we explain a few elements of their proof.
Probability.comment: 39 pages. Accepted manuscript for Séminaire Bourbaki, January 2026, Exposé no. 1247. To appear in Astérisque

Probability.title: Scaling limits for allelic subfamilies in a mother-dependent multitype branching process
Probability.summary:
The mother-dependent neutral mutations model describes the evolution of a population across discrete generations in which every individual carries one of $d$ alleles and each mutant child acquires a type different from that of its mother, chosen uniformly at random. We consider a critical population with finite offspring variance and analyze the genealogy of the allelic subfamilies, extending the framework of Bertoin (2010) from the infinite-allele setting to finitely many alleles.
  We study the Markov chain that records the sizes of the allelic subfamilies of each type together with the numbers of mutants that they beget, and we give a $d$-dimensional random walk representation of it. In a regime of large initial population and rare mutations, we prove that the rescaled chain converges to a discrete-time continuous-state Markov process driven by the masses of the mutant populations; from the first allelic generation onwards its clone component is a multitype Jiřina process whose branching mechanism is the Laplace exponent of a $d$-dimensional inverse Gaussian subordinator carried by the coordinate axes. Lifting this convergence to the genealogical level, we introduce a $d$-type tree of alleles and show that, in the scaling limit, it converges to a tree-indexed multitype Jiřina process, described by the ranked atoms of Poisson random measures with inverse Gaussian intensity.
Probability.comment: 35 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. v2: improved exposition and revised proofs in Section 5

Probability.title: Distributional Limits for Eigenvalues of Graphon Kernel Matrices
Probability.summary:
We study eigenvalue fluctuations of kernel and adjacency matrices in dense graphon-based random graph models, for modes associated with simple, isolated nonzero eigenvalues of the graphon integral operator. Our results require no smoothness or Lipschitz continuity. They include degenerate non-leading modes whose normalized eigenfunctions have constant modulus and change sign between $-1$ and $+1$ on measurable sets. Continuous graphons exclude this possibility: their nonzero eigenfunctions have continuous representatives, so constant modulus forces a constant eigenfunction, which corresponds to the largest eigenvalue of a nonnegative graphon. Nevertheless, non-leading degeneracy already occurs at the second eigenvalue of a two-block model with equal blocks.
  The limiting behavior is governed by the variance of the squared population eigenfunction. When this variance is positive, the empirical eigenvalue, divided by $n-1$ and centered at its population value, has a Gaussian limit under $\sqrt{n}$ scaling. When the variance vanishes, the first-order fluctuation disappears, and the centered unnormalized kernel eigenvalue converges to a weighted series of centered chi-square variables.
  For adjacency matrices, Bernoulli edge noise is negligible at the $\sqrt{n}$ scale of the unnormalized eigenvalues. In the degenerate regime, after the same deterministic centering used for the kernel eigenvalue, the adjacency eigenvalue converges to the same weighted chi-square series plus a deterministic shift and a Gaussian term independent of that series. The proofs combine spectral localization, exact Schur identities, finite-mode approximations, and Hoeffding decompositions.

Probability.title: Variance-Feedback Noise in Interacting Diffusions: Shape Dynamics and Mean-Field Limits
Probability.summary: We study a system of $N$ attractive interacting diffusions where the variance feeds back into the noise. That is the common and idiosyncratic Brownian forcing has amplitude $κ(S_t^N)^q$, with $S_t^N$ the empirical variance of the system, $κ>0$ and $q\geq 0$. With the interaction kernel given by $K(z)=|z|^p z$, for $p\geq 0$, feedback through the empirical variance gives the system critical homogeneity at $q=(p+2)/4$. For this exponent an intrinsic time change separates the variance from the normalized centered configuration: the latter evolves autonomously on a unit sphere and, when it is not purely driven by common noise and the sphere has positive dimension, is a reversible elliptic diffusion with an explicit invariant Gibbs measure. In this case, for $p>0$, the stationary averaged dissipation gives an exact finite-particle trichotomy between consensus, recurrent excursions through arbitrarily small and large variance scales, and finite-time explosion. At critical homogeneity we also derive an autonomous unit-variance mean-field equation and its constrained free-energy dissipation identity. Across the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes, we establish well-posedness and boundary classifications and prove conditional propagation of chaos on intervals where the limiting solution is unique and nonexplosive. We connect the sharp finite-particle coercivity constants to a mean-field variational problem. Finite-size Itô corrections enlarge the universal coercive consensus region. We solve the linear model, where $p=0$, completely, including invariant laws, explosion probabilities, noncommuting limits, and an $N^{-1/2}$ transition window.

Differential Geometry.title: All Serrin bands are unduloidal
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that any Serrin domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with two boundary components is a member of the canonical unduloidal family

Differential Geometry.title: Complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors in low dimensions
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify all complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors with complex Killing function $iμ-α$ on complete Riemannian surfaces, presenting an explicit list of all possible cases. We show that, contrary to previous statements in the literature, there exist complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors on Riemannian surfaces for which $αμ\not\equiv0$. We illustrate the classification by providing several explicit local, compact, and complete examples, including a complete example for which $αμ>0$ everywhere. We then move to three dimensions, proving that a spin-c Riemannian three-manifold admits a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor with complex Killing function $iμ-α$ if and only if it is a $μ$-exact trans-Sasakian manifold of type $(α,μ)$. In addition, we construct a geodesically incomplete Riemannian three-manifold equipped with a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor for which neither $μ$ nor $α$ vanishes identically, and then prove that this is not possible if the characteristic vector field of the associated trans-Sasakian structure is complete. These results settle a conjecture by Große and Nakad (Results in Mathematics, 2015) stating that on two- and three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds the complex Killing function of any complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor must be either globally real or globally imaginary.

Differential Geometry.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersection in flag varieties
Differential Geometry.summary:
We develop a root-theoretic localization formalism for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of flag varieties and of smooth zero loci of globally generated homogeneous vector bundles. The resulting invariants are expressed as finite sums over decorated trees whose contributions are determined by the root system of the ambient flag variety and by the torus weights of the defining bundle. We connect these computations with the Theory of Hodge Atoms of Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu via the matrix of small quantum multiplication by first Chern class.
  Let $X$ be a Fano fourfold with $h^{3,1}(X)=1$ arising as a hyperplane section of a suitable Fano fivefold. Its cohomology decomposes into a monodromy-fixed part and the middle vanishing cohomology. This decomposition is preserved by quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. Moreover, it acts by a scalar on the vanishing summand. We show, for the monodromy-fixed block, that (a) if every eigenvalue has algebraic multiplicity at most two and $X$ is Hodge general, then $X$ is irrational; (b) if every eigenvalue has Jordan defect at most one and $X$ is rational, then every weak factorization contains a smooth surface center whose minimal model is a projective K3 surface. Many applications are presented.
  Using the recently introduced quantum connection approach to irrationality, we obtain from the computations here presented the irrationality of the very general smooth complete intersection of a hyperplane and a quadric in $\operatorname{LG}(3,6)$; the very general smooth quadric section in $G_2/P_2$; and the very general smooth complete intersection of five hyperplanes and a quadric in the spinor 10-fold.

Differential Geometry.title: Proof of the Penrose Conjecture for Maximally Parameterized Initial Data Sets
Differential Geometry.summary:
We prove the spacetime Penrose inequality for asymptotically flat initial data sets $(M^n,g,k)$ in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, under the dominant energy condition, for data admitting the 'maximally parameterized form' defined in equation (4.7). In this case, the second fundamental form $k$ is locally parameterized by $n(n+1)/2$ functions, giving the same formal local functional degrees of freedom as an arbitrary symmetric $2$-tensor.
  The proof is based on a new 1-parameter family of generalized Schoen-Yau identities and their gauge-invariant specialization, inspired by the generalized Jang framework of Bray-Khuri [8, 9]. For maximally parameterized data, these identities produce a Riemannian comparison metric \[
  \bar g=g+β\otimesβ\] with nonnegative scalar curvature $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. Under a natural nondegeneracy condition (5.7) at the apparent horizon, the comparison metric admits a smooth minimal completion up to $\partial M^n$. Together with suitable asymptotic control, this reduces the Penrose inequality to its Riemannian counterpart. The all-dimensional conclusion uses the Riemannian Penrose theorem of Bi-Zhu [6], together with a minimizing enclosure argument that allows singular boundaries.
  More generally, in the spirit of [8, 9], we note that the Penrose conjecture follows whenever a certain system of PDEs (3.18) involving $k$ can be solved, in which case our new identity (3.15) immediately implies $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. A natural problem is thus to regularize our degenerate system to prove a general existence theory, thereby proving the Penrose conjecture. Essentially, we believe this is what the OpenAI paper [27] posted last week on October 6, 2026 claims to have done.

Differential Geometry.title: Inverse limits of locally convex Lie groupoids
Differential Geometry.summary: We study strict inverse systems of locally convex Lie groupoids and Lie algebroids. We show that strict inverse limits of Lie algebroids and Lie groupoids inherit natural Lie structures and establish a natural isomorphism of functors $\varprojlim\circ\operatorname{Lie}\cong\operatorname{Lie}\circ\varprojlim$. We then consider inverse systems of integrable Banach-Lie algebroids and their source-simply connected levelwise integrations. We give conditions under which these integrations form a strict inverse system of Lie groupoids and hence their inverse limit integrates the inverse-limit algebroid. Under additional hypotheses on the source-fiber inverse sequence, we describe the obstruction to source-simply connectedness of the resulting integration in terms of the derived inverse limit $\varprojlim^{1}π_2$ of the second homotopy groups of the source fibers. We illustrate the theory with several examples: inverse limits of jet groupoids, current groupoids, and gauge groupoids, including the corresponding inverse-limit Atiyah algebroids and a source-simply connected inverse-limit integration arising from the quaternionic Hopf bundle.

Differential Geometry.title: Flexibility of eigenvalues for graph Laplacians arising from genus 3 surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: It is known that the small eigenvalues of the Laplacian of a Riemann surface close to the boundary of the modular space can be well approximated by the eigenvalues of the discrete Laplacian on a certain graph coming from the pair of pants decomposition of the surface. In this paper, we provide a complete description of the sets of eigenvalues of the weighted graph Laplacian for all graphs on four vertices that correspond to a valid pair of pants decomposition of a surface of genus 3.
Differential Geometry.comment: v2: minor edits and improvements following referee report

Differential Geometry.title: On Meeks' conjecture on disjoint minimal graphs
Differential Geometry.summary: We study disjoint solution pairs $(u,D)$ to the minimal surface equation in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $u=0$ on $\partial D.$ A conjecture of W. Meeks states that at most two such pairs can exist in $\mathbb{R}^n.$ We confirm the conjecture in two complementary cases. For $n\in\{2,3,4,5,6\},$ we prove it under a superlinearity assumption. In dimension $n=2,$ we establish the result under a suitable sublinearity assumption. We also derive estimates on the asymptotic angle of domains supporting nontrivial solutions for $n\geq 3.$

Differential Geometry.title: Topology of tame contractible $n$-manifolds, $n=6,7$, with Positive BiRicci Curvature and Ricci lower bounds
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that if an open smooth $6$-manifold $M^6$ is the interior of a compact, contractible manifold with boundary $X^6$, such that $π_3(X,\partial X)=0$, and $M$ supports a complete metric with uniform positive BiRicci curvature and Ricci curvature bounded below, then $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^6$. Additionally, we show that if an open smooth $n$-manifold $M^n$, $n\in\{6,7\}$, is the interior of a compact, contractible manifold with boundary $X^n$, such that $π_3(X,\partial X)=0$, and $M$ supports a complete metric with positive BiRicci curvature with at most $C$-quadratic decay at infinity for some $C>C_n$ and nonnegative Ricci curvature, then $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$. Lastly, for each $n\geq6$, we construct a compact, contractible Newman $n$-manifold, $N^n$, based on a presentation of the Higman group such that $π_i(N,\partial N)=0$, $3\leq i \leq n-3$, and $\mathrm{int}(N)$ admits a complete metric with uniform positive scalar curvature and Ricci curvature bounded below.
Differential Geometry.comment: 18 pages, 1 figure. Statement of Theorem A has been corrected. Introduction has been expanded and improved. References were added

Differential Geometry.title: $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth approximation of mod $k$ integral cycles
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $Σ$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $Σ$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes. Moreover, we provide examples showing the impossibility of locally approximating minimizing cycles by smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifolds, even in homology classes with smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth representatives.

Differential Geometry.title: Cheng's Theorem in the Spectral Setting
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a maximal diameter rigidity theorem for closed 3-dimensional Riemannian manifolds under a spectral lower bound for the Ricci curvature. We show that if $0<γ<2$, $K>0$ and $λ_1(-γΔ+\operatorname{Ric})\geq 2K$, then the optimal bound $\operatorname{diam}(M,g)\leq\fracπ{\sqrt{K}}$ is attained if and only if (M,g) is isometric to the round 3-sphere of constant sectional curvature $K$.

Differential Geometry.title: An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
Differential Geometry.summary:
We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $α'$ with $α'=\partial_vα/\partial_vr$ and $α=\partial_v(rφ)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein.
  As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.

Differential Geometry.title: A Scale-Critical $μ<\frac38$ Extension Principle for Spherically Symmetric Einstein-Scalar Field System
Differential Geometry.summary: We present a new quantitative, scale-critical $C^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. We derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{O}$ of the center. Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $μ=2m/r$ satisfies $\supμ<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $μ$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $μ\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $μ<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.

Differential Geometry.title: Allen--Cahn and mean curvature flows from Clifford hypersurfaces to equators
Differential Geometry.summary: In this short note, using OpenAI's resolution of the Solomon--Yau conjecture, we extend our joint work with Pedro Gaspar to all dimensions $n\geq2$. We construct eternal Allen--Cahn flows on $S^{n+1}$ connecting approximations of any prescribed least-area Clifford hypersurface and equatorial sphere. We also construct infinitely many eternal integral Brakke flows from least-area Clifford hypersurfaces to equatorial spheres.

Differential Geometry.title: K-area bounds for smooth sphere bundles
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $E\to B$ be a smooth $S^n$ bundle with oriented Riemannian total space $(E,g)$, where $n\ge2$. We prove K-area$(E,g)\le4πn(n-1)/σ$ whenever every fibre has intrinsic scalar curvature at least $σ>0$, independently of the dimension of $B$. In particular, unit round fibres give K-area$(E,g)\le4π$. For arbitrary metrics on two-sphere fibres, K-area is bounded by the supremum of their areas. We also obtain stronger bounds from fibrewise scalar spectra.

Differential Geometry.title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
Differential Geometry.summary: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.

Differential Geometry.title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{λ,μ}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities ($λ\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $μ\in\mathbb{R}$).

Differential Geometry.title: CMC foliations on Euclidean spaces are minimal foliations
Differential Geometry.summary: In this article, we provide a complete answer to one of the most classical conjectures in differential geometry (of foliations). More precisely, we present a complete positive answer to the classical conjecture, due to Meeks III, Pérez, and Ros (2008), that states that every foliation on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by (possibly varying) CMC hypersurfaces is a foliation by minimal hypersurfaces. Moreover, if $n\leq 6$, such a CMC foliation must consist of parallel hyperplanes.

Differential Geometry.title: Holomorphic functions on a class of complete Hermitian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary:
In this paper, we prove a gradient estimate for holomorphic functions on complete Hermitian manifolds with nonnegative second Ricci curvature. As an application, we establish several Liouville-type theorems for holomorphic functions and mappings between complete Hermitian manifolds under suitable curvature assumptions. In particular, on a complete Hermitian manifold with nonnegative second Ricci curvature and Chern torsion of linear growth, any bounded holomorphic function must be constant. Moreover, we construct examples to show that both the gradient estimate and this Liouville theorem are sharp in a suitable sense.
  In the second part of the paper, we study holomorphic functions on simply connected complete Hermitian manifolds with vanishing Chern curvature and torsion norm of sublinear growth. Combining the gradient estimate with methods from sub-Riemannian geometry, we obtain a complete characterization of holomorphic functions of polynomial growth on such manifolds.
Differential Geometry.comment: In this version, we change the title and improve the exposition to highlight the main theorem (Theorem 1.1). We also add two examples (Examples 1.3 and 1.4) and update some references

Differential Geometry.title: On local minimality of Hausdorff dimension for round limit sets
Differential Geometry.summary: We address a question of Canary--Taylor and Canary--Minsky--Taylor for sufficiently symmetric compact hyperbolic $3$-orbifolds with totally geodesic boundary. We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.

Differential Geometry.title: Odd mapping cone Chern character
Differential Geometry.summary: Our previous work established the mapping cone Chern character on the even-degree side, using the powers of the mapping cone curvature associated with the given mapping cone connection. In this paper, we carry out the odd-degree version using a trivial mapping cone connection and an automorphism on a trivial complex vector bundle. This version is based on the related odd-degree transgression.

Differential Geometry.title: Geometric $C^1$-stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow
Differential Geometry.summary:
We prove stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow in the simply connected space forms under genuinely first-order geometric assumptions. The initial hypersurface is required to lie in a sufficiently thin annulus around a geodesic sphere and to have outward normal making a small angle with the radial direction. No convexity, mean convexity, initial curvature bound, or Hölder control of the normal is assumed.
  The main ingredient is a quantitative Alexandrov reflection argument that converts these initial assumptions into a strong reflection property preserved by the flow. The resulting radial and angular control allows us to derive estimates for the mean curvature and the full second fundamental form, and hence long-time existence, eventual convexity, and smooth exponential convergence to a geodesic sphere. In hyperbolic space, the eventual convexity can be strengthened to horospherical convexity. The reflection threshold also yields a quantitative estimate for the displacement of the limiting centre.
  For Lipschitz initial hypersurfaces, we develop a separate positive-time curvature estimate that is uniform along smooth approximations. This produces an instantaneously smooth evolution with the same eventual convexity and smooth exponential convergence.

Differential Geometry.title: Invariant complex structures on the Euclidean motion group as deformations of Calabi-Eckmann structures
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify, up to equivalence, all left-invariant complex structures on the three-dimensional Euclidean rigid motion group $SE(3).$ Our approach is based on the correspondence between complex structures on a real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(3)$ of the motion group and complex Lie subalgebras of the complexification of $\mathfrak{e}(3).$ The resulting structures form a one-parameter family $J_φ.$ We further establish a connection with the classical Calabi-Eckmann complex structures on $S^3\times S^3.$ More precisely, we construct a one-parameter deformation of Lie brackets connecting $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus \mathfrak{so}(3)$ to $\mathfrak{e}(3),$ for which each endomorphism $J_φ$ remains integrable. Consequently, every left-invariant complex structure on $SE(3)$ arises as a contraction limit of Calabi-Eckmann structures. The same family of endomorphisms also defines complex structures on $\mathfrak{so}(3,1).$

Differential Geometry.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_α$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $α$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.

Differential Geometry.title: Quantization of positive Lagrangians
Differential Geometry.summary:
A Lagrangian submanifold in an almost Calabi-Yau manifold is called positive if the real part of the holomorphic volume form restricted to it is positive. It is called $ε$-positive if the ratio of the restrictions of the imaginary and real parts of the holomorphic volume form is bounded by $\frac{1}ε.$ An exact isotopy class of positive Lagrangian submanifolds admits a natural Riemannian metric. We prove that the Riemannian metric restricted to the subset of $ε$-positive Lagrangians induces a path metric when the relative Kähler class of the ambient Calabi-Yau manifold lies on a line of rational slope.
  The proof relies on the construction of a sequence of quantization maps from a circle bundle over the space of positive Lagrangians to the dual of the space of holomorphic sections of powers of a prequantum line bundle. The rationality condition for the relative Kähler class allows us to reduce to the case of Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangians. Building on ideas of Tian and Nirenberg-Wells, Hörmander estimates are used to show that functions on a Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangian can be approximated by holomorphic sections of a sufficiently high power of the prequantum line bundle. Consequently, the quantization maps eventually separate fibers of the circle bundle.

Differential Geometry.title: On the generalized cohomologies of almost abelian solvmanifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Generalized complex structures give rise to generalized Dolbeault, Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomologies. We study these cohomologies for invariant generalized complex structures on almost abelian Lie algebras $\mathfrak g_A=\mathbb R e_0\ltimes_A\mathfrak h$, where $\mathfrak h$ is an abelian ideal of codimension one, and on almost abelian solvmanifolds $Γ\backslash G_A$. We first show that the invariant generalized Dolbeault cohomology can be identified with the Chevalley--Eilenberg cohomology of the complex Lie algebra $\mathcal L$, the $+{\mathbf i}$-eigenspace of the structure, with coefficients in a character determined by the canonical line. We prove that $\mathcal L$ is itself an almost abelian Lie algebra; thus the cohomology reduces to the kernel and cokernel of an explicit derivation. Assuming that $A$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R$, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the cohomology dimensions and compare with compact quotients. Other comparison results are discussed, noting that the cohomology of invariant forms always injects into that of $Γ\backslash G_A$.

Differential Geometry.title: The WKB Riemann-Hilbert Problem for the Painlevé I System
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we solve the direct monodromy problem for the Borel-summed $0$-parameter solution of Painlevé~I. Using the auxiliary time equation, we first construct formal WKB wave matrices whose amplitudes are regular at the double turning point. Rigorous Borel summation then yields exact WKB matrices in each Stokes region. Uniform estimates on moving action strips provide a common exact wave matrix in a full neighbourhood of the double point, proving that all four incident jumps are identities for consistent column normalisations. We formulate the resulting normalised Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its existence and uniqueness on the Borel domains of the construction. Finally, after Painlevé scaling, the five Borel-summed solutions coincide with the five rotated tritronquée solutions of Painlevé~I.

Differential Geometry.title: A note on the failure of Payne's inequality on manifolds with boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that Payne's conjecture on the comparison between Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues and buckling eigenvalues does not hold on flat and hyperbolic cylindrical surfaces and on (round) hemispheres.

Differential Geometry.title: Ball growth at all scales in universal covers of short metric graphs
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $Γ$ be a connected metric graph of first Betti number $b\ge 2$, and let $Γ_b$ be a trivalent graph of the same Betti number with all edges of unit length. We show that if $\text{length}(Γ) \le λ\, \text{length}(Γ_b)$, then the universal cover of $Γ$ contains a vertex around which, \emph{at every radius} $R\ge 0$, the ball is at least as long as the ball of radius $R$ in the trivalent tree whose edges all have length $3λ$. In particular, for $λ\le\frac13$, this ball is at least as long as the ball of the same radius in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, with no multiplicative loss. This improves an earlier theorem of the author, which gives the weaker lower bound $(1-3λ)$ times the ball in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, and only for $λ\le\frac16$. The proof rests on an elementary comparison principle. Among trees whose vertices have degree at least three and whose edges have length at most $c$, the trivalent tree with all edges of length $c$ has the smallest balls at every radius. As an application, we double the exponential growth rate in the author's earlier uniform lower bound for the area of balls in the universal cover of small-area surfaces of hyperbolic type, from $\ln 2$ to $2\ln 2$, beyond the hyperbolic rate. We also obtain explicit constants in the positive answer to Guth's question for surfaces. Finally, we conjecture the sharp, all-scale version of the minimal volume entropy inequality of Kapovich--Nagnibeda and Lim, and show that it would be optimal.

Differential Geometry.title: A semi-discrete scheme for horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
Differential Geometry.summary: The horizontal mean curvature flow is a geometric evolution associated with the horizontal perimeter in sub-Riemannian spaces. In this paper, we introduce a minimizing movement scheme for this flow in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}$, and prove the existence of a flat flow which is locally $1/2$-Hölder continuous in time, with respect to the $L^1$-distance. The construction applies to arbitrary bounded sets of finite horizontal perimeter and does not require smoothness or symmetry of the initial datum.

Differential Geometry.title: Algebraic and Symmetrized Affine star-Ricci Solitons for the Bott Connection on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We fix a spacelike two-dimensional left-invariant distribution and its associated almost contact structure on a three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie group, and investigate the star-Ricci contraction of the curvature of the Bott connection. We compute the complete tensor for seven standard bracket families and determine all real parameter solutions of the general algebraic equation and its self-adjoint subclass. Using the symmetric part of the tensor, we also define a Bott affine star-Ricci soliton equation and classify all left-invariant vector field solutions. Every affine solution is steady, while two non-unimodular families admit branches with a nonzero symmetrized tensor. The proofs provide complete component equations, treat all degenerate parameter branches, and establish sufficiency by explicit substitution. We also distinguish almost contact structures from contact metric structures.

Differential Geometry.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures III: Unfoldings
Differential Geometry.summary: We study unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We prove theorem of existence for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves for one-parameter families. We prove theorem of completeness for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We also present unfoldings of foliated nonsingular varieties defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves in the language of functors of Artin rings which is the algebraic version of unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures. We identify first-order unfoldings and obstructions.

Differential Geometry.title: Complex deformations of the circle: Group cohomology and Virasoro uniformization
Differential Geometry.summary:
We approach the question of complexification of the diffeomorphism group of the circle by considering real-analytic maps from the circle into the punctured complex plane with winding number +1. Such complex deformations form an infinite-dimensional manifold with partially defined inversion and composition operations, smooth in the sense of Frölicher structures, and with Lie algebra relations at the identity given by the Witt algebra. We compute their second group cohomology with real coefficients. It is generated by two cocycles: One cocycle extending the Bott-Thurston cocycle related to the Gelf'and-Fuks cocycle of the Virasoro algebra, and another Euler class cocycle combining mean rotation and conformal radius.
  Complex deformations act naturally on the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with enumerated and analytically parametrized boundary components, equipping them with smooth Fr{ö}licher structures. We prove a Virasoro uniformization theorem: The tangent spaces of the Segal moduli spaces are spanned by vector fields induced by the Witt algebra. Finally, we relate the actions of complex deformations to Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates and Schiffer variation on finite-dimensional moduli spaces of bordered hyperbolic surfaces with one marked point on each boundary component.
Differential Geometry.comment: 50 pages, 8 figures; changed rotation number to mean rotation and Euler class cocycle, see remarks 3.5 and 3.6

Differential Geometry.title: A parabolic flow approach to generalized Gauduchon metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: We give a parabolic proof of the Fu-Wang-Wu theorem for semilinear elliptic equations associated with generalized Gauduchon metrics. Fixing a Hermitian metric $ω$, we introduce a flow $\partial_t v-Δv=ψ(\vert\nabla v\vert^2)+\langle B,dv\rangle-c(t)-f(x)$ for the conformal factor, whose stationary points solve the semilinear elliptic equation of Fu-Wang-Wu. Under the growth condition $\liminf_{t\to+\infty}ψ(t)/t^μ>0$ for some $μ>\tfrac{1}{2}$, we prove that the flow exists uniquely for all time and converges; the limit solves the elliptic equation and is unique up to addition of a constant. Our convergence argument does not rely on a gradient-flow structure or a monotone energy functional. In particular, this recovers, by a flow method rather than the continuity method, the existence and uniqueness theorem of Fu-Wang-Wu on $k$-th generalized Gauduchon metrics, providing a new parabolic approach to their elliptic theory.

Differential Geometry.title: Coupled reciprocal-sum inequalities for Neumann eigenvalues in rank-one symmetric spaces
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $M$ be a rank-one symmetric space of compact or noncompact type and real dimension $m=kn$, where $k\in\{1,2,4,8\}$ is the real dimension of the underlying division algebra. Meng and Wang proved sharp isoperimetric inequalities for reciprocal sums of the first $p$ or $\ell$ nonzero Neumann eigenvalues, with indices strictly below $m$ in the nonconstant-curvature cases. We keep the whole $m$-dimensional transplanted first eigenspace of an equimeasurable geodesic ball and treat its mass and stiffness forms as a coupled generalized eigenvalue problem.
  For every bounded connected smooth domain in a noncompact rank-one symmetricspace we prove the full sharp estimate \[
  \sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{1}{μ_j(Ω)}
  \ge \frac{m}{μ_1(B)}, \] where $B$ is a geodesic ball with $|B|=|Ω|$; equality characterizes geodesic balls. The Hopf-direction contribution is encoded by a positive, unital, trace-preserving projection on symmetric matrices, and the finite-dimensional closure is supplied by a positive-projection Jensen inequality.
  In compact type, under the localization hypothesis of Meng--Wang, the same full estimate is obtained whenever $\cot^2 R\ge k-1$, where $R$ is the radius of the comparison ball, as well as in the isotropic endpoint cases and for Hopf-balanced angular second moment. Consequently the complete $m$-term inequality holds for all complex and quaternionic projective spaces under the original localization assumption, and for the Cayley plane when $R\le \arctan(1/\sqrt7)$. In the remaining admissible Cayley interval we exhibit a finite-dimensional obstruction showing that the affine tangent-matrix bounds alone cannot yield the full trace estimate. This obstruction concerns the proof mechanism and is not a counterexample to the unresolved spectral inequality.

Differential Geometry.title: Lin-Lu-Yau Ricci curvature on hypergraphs
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we introduce a unified framework for defining Lin-Lu-Yau (LLY) Ricci curvature on both undirected and directed hypergraphs. By establishing upper bounds and monotonicity properties for the parameterized curvature $κ_α$, we justify the well-posedness and compatibility of our definitions. Furthermore, we prove a Bonnet-Myers-type theorem for hypergraphs, which highlights the potential of LLY Ricci curvature in hypergraph analysis, particularly in studying geometric and structural properties. Our results extends the foundational definitions of graph Ricci curvature by Ollivier and Lin-Lu-Yau to the hypergraph setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Characterizations of weak almost ${\mathcal S}$-manifolds with curvature properties
Differential Geometry.summary: Weak metric structures, introduced by Rovenski and Wolak in 2022, extend Yano's $f$-structure and almost contact metric structure. In this paper, we investigate curvature phenomena of weak almost ${\cal S}$-manifolds (w.a.$\,\cal S$-manifolds) focusing on the $f$-$(κ,μ)$-nullity condition and its special case $R_{X,Y}\,ξ=0$. We establish several results that generalize known rigidity theorems for almost ${\cal S}$-manifolds. First, using the partial Ricci flow, we obtain dynamical characterizations of $\cal S$-manifolds: starting from a w.a.$\,\cal S$-structure satisfying the curvature condition of $\cal S$-manifolds or the $f$-$(1,μ)$-nullity condition, the flow evolves the structure exponentially fast toward an $\cal S$-structure. This extends results of Cappelletti Montano and Di~Terlizzi to the weak metric setting. Next, we identify conditions under which a w.a.\,${\cal S}$-manifold admits a bi-Legendrian structure with totally geodesic foliations. Finally, for w.a.$\,\cal S$-manifolds with $κ=μ=0$, we prove a splitting theorem in which one factor is flat and the another has positive constant sectional curvature, generalizing classical results for almost $\cal S$-geometry. These findings have consequences for the theory of Sasakian and $\cal S$- manifolds, the geometry of bi-Legendrian structures, and the behavior of weak metric contact manifolds under curvature constraints.

Differential Geometry.title: The Weil-Petersson diameter of moduli space for large genus
Differential Geometry.summary: We determine the large-genus order of the Weil-Petersson diameter of $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ for each fixed number of punctures: namely, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{M}_{g,n})\asymp\sqrt g\log g$. The main new ingredient is an integrated Ricci estimate for geodesics that minimize in moduli space and have thick endpoints, with no systole bound along their interiors.

Differential Geometry.title: Remarks on prescribed scalar curvature functions
Differential Geometry.summary: This short article is devoted to the study of the positive solution of Yamabe-type semi-linear equation with prescribed coefficient on general closed manifolds. Our main result is to provide some sufficient conditions for the existence of the positive solutions and give some examples to show that those conditions are sharp. An application to scalar-flat manifold settles a long standing question in prescribing scalar curvature problem in negative form.

Differential Geometry.title: The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Ampère potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.

Differential Geometry.title: Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $(X,ω)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. The complex $k$-Hessian equation identifies this space, modulo constants, with the space of smooth positive densities of fixed total mass. We compute the differential of the Hessian density map and use it to pull back the Fisher--Rao metric. The resulting Riemannian metric is \[
  G^{\HC,k}_{\varphi}(u,v)
  =\int_X
  \bigl(Δ_{\varphi}^{(k)}u\bigr)
  \bigl(Δ_{\varphi}^{(k)}v\bigr)
  \,ω_{\varphi}^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}. \] We then show that the square-root Hessian density map \[
  \varphi\longmapsto
  2\sqrt{\frac{ω_{\varphi}^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}}{ω^n}} \] is a global Riemannian isometry onto the positive part of the $L^2(X,ω^n)$-sphere of radius $2\sqrt{V}$, where $V=\int_Xω^n$. For $k=n$, this recovers the spherical description of the classical Calabi metric. We also derive the curvature, geodesic and diameter formulas, and prove a quantitative local comparison between adjacent Hessian--Fisher distances.

Differential Geometry.title: Kähler geometry on total spaces of vector bundles over elliptic curves
Differential Geometry.summary:
We study function theory and Kähler geometry on total spaces of vector bundles over an elliptic curve. Our main result characterizes the vector bundles whose total spaces admit complete Kähler metrics with nonnegative bisectional curvature ($BI \geq 0$ for short). We also obtain explicit expressions for all complete Kähler metrics with $BI \geq 0$ on the total space of a line bundle over a complex torus. These results are related to a general conjecture concerning the structure of complete Kähler manifolds with $BI \geq 0$.
  For rank-two vector bundles of degree zero over elliptic curves, we study holomorphic functions and automorphisms on the corresponding total spaces, and construct complete Gauduchon Hermitian metrics with vanishing Chern-Ricci curvature. These metrics are natural in the sense that the associated spaces of holomorphic functions of polynomial growth coincide with the ``polynomials'' on these total spaces.
Differential Geometry.comment: In the second version, we correct some inaccuracies in the first version and improve the exposition. Some references are added

Differential Geometry.title: A short open space curve of unit width
Differential Geometry.summary: In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.

Differential Geometry.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties I -klt Fano case-
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish the following Miyaoka-Yau inequality for any $n$-dimensional klt Fano variety $X$, possibly K-unstable, in terms of its delta invariant: \[\left(2(n+1)\widehat{c}_2(X)-n c_1(X)^2\right)\cdot c_1(X)^{n-2} \ge -n \left(1-\min\{1,δ(X)\}\right)^2 \cdot c_1(X)^n.\] Moreover, if equality holds in this inequality, then there exist a finite quasi-étale cover $\widehat{X} \to X$ and a positive integer $p$ such that $\widehat{X} \cong \mathbb{P}(1,\ldots, 1, p)$. We also discuss the relationship between Donaldson's conjecture and the Miyaoka-Yau inequality.
Differential Geometry.comment: v3: 31 pages; Major revision with improved and additional results. Split into two papers; the second will appear separately. v2: 66 pages; Minor revision. Theorem 1.1 and Theorem B.3 have been improved. v1: 64 pages; comments are welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Regularization and Hölder continuity for complex Hessian equations on Hermitian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(M,ω)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold, and let $Γ$ be a symmetric convex cone. We develop a quantitative regularization method for $Γ$-admissible functions. As an application, we prove Hölder continuity for every pluripotential solution of complex $m$-Hessian equations whose right-hand sides belong to $L^p$, for $p>\frac{n}{m}$. These results extend to a more general class of complex Hessian equations satisfying the structural condition used by Guo--Phong--Tong.
Differential Geometry.comment: 42 pages. We improve the Holder exponent in the statement of Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.1

Differential Geometry.title: Complete Self-Shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension with Positive Constant Scalar Curvature and $S\le 1$
Differential Geometry.summary: Let \(X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional complete self-shrinker in arbitrary codimension \(p\ge 1\). Suppose that the scalar curvature \(R\) is a positive constant and that the squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form satisfies \(S\le 1\). We prove that \(S\equiv 1\) and that \(X\) is isometric to either the round sphere \(S^n(\sqrt n)\) or the standard generalized cylinder \(S^k(\sqrt k)\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), \(2\le k\le n-1\). In particular, no new higher-codimension examples occur under these assumptions. The proof uses an algebraic lemma which yields a uniform positive lower bound for the Bakry--Émery Ricci curvature, together with the comparison theorem of Wei--Wylie, the equivalence of finite Gaussian volume and polynomial volume growth due to Cheng--Zhou, and the gap theorem of Cao--Li.

Differential Geometry.title: Quantitative Volume Estimate on Singular Sets of One-phase Free Boundary Problems in Ricci Limit Spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We study limit solutions of the one-phase free boundary problem on noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. We introduce a quantitative stratification $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$ of the singular set of the free boundary that simultaneously captures the approximate splitting of the ambient space and the approximate homogeneity and translational invariance of the solution. We also introduce a new truncated parabolic Weiss quantity that provides quantitative homogeneity via pinching across scales. Although this quantity may not be uniformly bounded across all small scales, it effectively shows that, among the first $j$ scales in a fixed decreasing geometric progression, at most $C\sqrt{j}$ scales fail to exhibit quantitative homogeneity. Such slow growth in $j$ enables us to adapt the covering argument of Cheeger and Naber [arXiv:1103.1819] to show, for every $η>0$, a $Cr^{n-k-η}$ upper bound for the volume of the $r$-tubular neighborhood of the $k$-th quantitative singular stratum, $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$. The same tubular-neighborhood estimate holds for the effective stratum $\mathcal S_\varepsilon^k$, and in particular we get the Minkowski dimension bound $\dim_{\mathcal M} \mathcal S_\varepsilon^k \le k$, from which the previously known sharp bound $\dim_{\mathcal H} \mathrm{Sing} \le n-3$ in Chan, Zhang, and Zhu [arXiv:2112.06962] follows. As another corollary, we prove that the free boundary admits a Hölder manifold structure away from a set of Minkowski dimension at most $n-3$.

Differential Geometry.title: Symplectic groupoid multiplication and Poisson integrators
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study the role of local symplectic groupoid multiplication in the construction of approximation methods for Hamiltonian flows on the underlying Poisson manifold. We show it can be used to construct a novel multiplicative type of approximating sequences for the relevant Lagrangian bisection. We describe the corresponding theoretical results, their practical implementation into approximation methods on coordinate charts via generating functions, and illustrative examples.

Differential Geometry.title: Stability of the catenoid for the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature equation in 4 spatial dimensions
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish the asymptotic stability of the catenoid, as a nonflat stationary solution to the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature (HVMC) equation in Minkowski space $\mathbb{R}^{1 + (n + 1)}$ for $n = 4$. Our main result is under a ``codimension-$1$'' assumption on initial perturbation, modulo suitable translation and boost (i.e. modulation), without any symmetry assumptions. In comparison to the $n \geq 5$ case addressed by Lührmann-Oh-Shahshahani arxiv:2212.05620, proving catenoid stability in $4$ dimensions shares additional difficulties with its $3$ dimensional analog, namely the slower spatial decay of the catenoid and slower temporal decay of waves. To overcome these difficulties in the $n = 3$ case, the strong Huygens principle, as well as a miraculous cancellation in the source term, plays an important role in arxiv:2409.05968 to obtain strong late time tails. In $n = 4$ dimensions, without these special structural advantages, our novelty is to introduce an appropriate commutator vector field to derive a new hierarchy of estimates with higher $r^p$-weights so that an improved pointwise decay can be established. We expect this to be applicable for proving improved late time tails of other quasilinear wave equations in even dimensions or wave equations with inverse square potential.
Differential Geometry.comment: 107 pages, 1 figure. Typos corrected, the rough statement of the main theorem streamlined, and some discussion in Section 4.3 moved to Section 5.4.1

Differential Geometry.title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
Differential Geometry.summary: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.
Differential Geometry.comment: 52 pages, comments welcome. Companion article to appear soon

Differential Geometry.title: $p$-Laplace Serrin problem on planar annuli
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove a rigidity result for the problem $Δ_p u=-2$ defined on a ring-shaped domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, when homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed and $p\in(1,2)$. This problem admits a natural physical interpretation, as it describes the steady laminar flow of a generalised Newtonian fluid exhibiting shear-thinning behaviour. Our symmetry result is obtained assuming that the set of maximum points, denoted by $Σ$, is a smooth closed curve, and there are no other critical points outside it; moreover, an appropriate asymptotic expansion of the solution near $Σ$ is required. Although our approach is inspired by the comparison strategy of [arXiv:2505.04458], the main ingredients used there are intrinsically linear and have no direct counterparts for the $p$-Laplacian. This requires the introduction of new ideas and techniques.

Differential Geometry.title: The \textsc{ABC}-equation revisited: missed integrable cases. Part I: classification and (quasi) integrable structures
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$, which was proved to be integrable in the case $A + B + C = 0$ (the Veronese web equation). Our study reveals ten more cases that admit integrable structures that, to the best of our knowledge, where not known before. The techniques is based essentially on the theory of the tangent and cotangent coverings.

Geometric Topology.title: Completely parabolic surfaces are Veech
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that completely parabolic translation surfaces are Veech, answering a question of Smillie-Weiss.

Geometric Topology.title: Minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ Complexes of Rational Tangles via the Fukaya Category
Geometric Topology.summary: We compute minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ complexes for oriented rational tangles, denoted $[\![τ_{u/v}^{O}]\!]_N$, in terms of the topological Fukaya category of the $3$-punctured disk. This demonstrates that the complexes stabilize, allowing us to define a HOMFLY-PT homology for rational tangles.
Geometric Topology.comment: 50 pages, many figures, 5 tables. Comments welcome!

Geometric Topology.title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $Γ_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ Γ_n(M)/K_n(M)\congπ_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.

Geometric Topology.title: On local minimality of Hausdorff dimension for round limit sets
Geometric Topology.summary: We address a question of Canary--Taylor and Canary--Minsky--Taylor for sufficiently symmetric compact hyperbolic $3$-orbifolds with totally geodesic boundary. We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.

Geometric Topology.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
Geometric Topology.summary: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_α$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $α$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.

Geometric Topology.title: The fundamental quandle of ribbon concordances
Geometric Topology.summary: We describe the fundamental quandle of a properly embedded surface $Σ$ (possibly with boundary) in $\mathbb{R}^{3}\times I$ and derive its presentation in terms of its motion picture. Our study is based on the topological definition of the fundamental quandle. We prove that a ribbon concordance $C$ from a classical knot $K_1$ to a classical knot $K_0$ gives rise to a quandle monomorphism $Q(K_0)\hookrightarrow Q(C)$ and a quandle epimorphism $Q(K_1)\twoheadrightarrow Q(C)$.

Geometric Topology.title: Mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds
Geometric Topology.summary: The goal of this work is to calculate the mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds. We introduce the dynamical commensurator group associated to an odometer action, and develop methods to calculate the mapping class group using the dynamical commensurator. Our results generalize the previous results of Odden for the mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a Riemann surface, and of Bering and Studenmund for the pointed mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a compact aspherical manifold. We include a selection of examples.

Geometric Topology.title: Property $(T)$ and nonlinearity of mapping class group quotients
Geometric Topology.summary: We give a general method for proving Kazhdan's property $(T)$ for quotients $G/K_{[c+1]}$, where $G$ is countable, $K$ is a normal subgroup and $K_{[j]}$ denotes its lower central series.
