Four unitary letters and four permutation letters attain these respective bounds, showing that a four-letter reversible alphabet reaches the static code-size orders in optimal quadratic and linear word length. In the fully dimension-limited regime, this yields \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=Θ(d^2)\) versus \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=Θ(d)\), establishing a quadratic quantum--classical separation in logarithmic code size. Low-overlap Grassmann and agreement-code packings supply the orbit endpoints, while exact inverse query words match each encoded state to its designated test. At the sharp boundary \(λ_2=0\), \(0\leqλ_1<1\), all four model classes satisfy \(\ln N=Θ(\min\{\ln d,T\})\). Thus any fixed positive false-acceptance tolerance activates the metric-packing regime, whereas zero false acceptance imposes an exclusive-witness constraint and yields the logarithmic-dimension boundary.

Information Theory.title: Z-Opt: A Near-Optimal Reduced-Complexity Two-Dimensional Grassmannian Constellation
Information Theory.summary: Grassmannian constellations achieve the capacity of noncoherent communications over Rayleigh fading channels at high SNR, yet their efficient construction remains challenging. In this paper, we present two construction methods for Grassmannian constellations on G(2,1), termed S-Opt and Z-Opt, and propose two low-complexity detectors. Both construction and detection are performed on the unit sphere, known as the Bloch sphere in quantum computing. Exploiting the proportionality between the chordal distance on the Grassmann manifold and the Euclidean distance on the Bloch sphere, we derive a theoretical upper bound on the minimum chordal distance from the Fejes-Toth bound. The S-Opt constellation is constructed from sphere-packing solutions and achieves the theoretical limit corresponding to the considered optimal Bloch-sphere packings. The S-Opt detector applies to arbitrary constellations on G(2,1) and requires a number of complex multiplications scaling linearly with the number of receive antennas and logarithmically with the constellation size, and a number of numerical comparisons scaling logarithmically with the constellation size, while achieving the same performance as the GLRT detector. Based on the insight from the S-Opt construction, we further propose the Z-Opt constellation, constructed by stacking regular polygons on the Bloch sphere, whose minimum chordal distance approaches the derived upper bound over the evaluated constellation sizes. The Z-Opt detector requires a number of complex multiplications scaling linearly with the number of receive antennas and a number of numerical comparisons scaling logarithmically with the square root of the constellation size, while achieving the same performance as the GLRT detector for the Z-Opt constellation.

Information Theory.title: Model-Driven Deep Learning for Distributed Detection with Low-Bit Quantization
Information Theory.summary: Distributed detection plays a fundamental role in communication-efficient collaborative inference over large-scale networks, where spatially distributed nodes must cooperate using severely quantized messages due to bandwidth constraints. While low-bit quantization is essential for reducing communication overhead, it can significantly degrade detection performance, particularly when prior knowledge of observation noise is unavailable. To address this challenge, we propose a model-driven deep learning framework for distributed detection with low-bit quantization. For fixed local quantizers, we first derive the exact finite-sensor maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection error and prove that, under conditionally independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations, independent local randomizations, and a common quantization-level constraint, identical quantizers preserve the supremum of the average network Chernoff information. Guided by these results, we develop a binary probabilistic quantizer with a trainable neural probability controller and design a tree-structured probabilistic quantizer for scalable multi-bit quantization. The exact finite-sensor MAP error provides the training objective for the binary quantizer, while we derive a computationally tractable Bhattacharyya surrogate objective for training the multi-bit quantizer. For both cases, we derive analytical MAP fusion rules based on the class-conditional probability mass functions (PMFs) of the quantized messages. When the observation statistics are unknown, these PMFs are estimated from held-out labeled data, yielding plug-in MAP detectors. Simulation results show that the proposed method approaches centralized-oracle performance at higher quantization resolutions and remains effective under changes in network size and test-time signal amplitude.
Information Theory.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. Accepted by IEEE JSAC

Information Theory.title: 3GPP-Compatible Long-Range Sensing for LEO-ISAC: A Window-Grid Processing Framework
Information Theory.summary: This paper addresses long-range sensing in bistatic low-Earth-orbit integrated sensing and communication (LEO-ISAC). Conventional OFDM sensing fails in LEO-ISAC because millisecond-scale propagation delays destroy the transmitter--receiver symbol alignment and, with multiple targets, make the receive window longer than the transmitted block. We propose a window-grid (WG) processing framework that exploits the known beam-intersection swath to resolve both problems purely at the receiver, leaving the 3GPP symbol structure unmodified: the swath delay span is folded into cyclic-prefix-sized slices, each handled by one WG. With 103.2 MHz bandwidth at bistatic ranges beyond 640 km, simulations demonstrate meter-level ranging of two targets, and 1000 Monte-Carlo trials over random target--satellite geometries show that, with an ephemeris-based satellite-selection rule, every target is detected with a 90th-percentile range error of 2.4 m.

Information Theory.title: Short-Boundary Signaling for Asynchronous Grant-Free Control-to-Control Communications
Information Theory.summary: In asynchronous grant-free access, receivers must detect variable-length transmissions and identify their start and end. Existing decoder-aided receivers use start and tail sequences which are as long as one codeword, causing substantial overhead for short commands. This paper treats the boundary (i.e., start and tail sequences) length as an independent design parameter and proposes a convolutional neural network that detects both boundaries from the received waveform and the decoder soft output. Its waveform input size decreases with the boundary length, while the decoder input keeps the codeword length, so the boundary can be shortened without altering the decoder. Analysis and simulations quantify the resulting tradeoff among payload efficiency, collision exposure, and boundary detection. The results show that the proposed receiver can exploit very short boundaries: in the considered setting, the shortest tested boundary, $L_{\mathrm{b}}=16$, yields the highest effective payload efficiency at all tested loads, whereas a correlation-based benchmark with the same sequences performs best with $L_{\mathrm{b}}=64$ at moderate and high loads.

Information Theory.title: Fisher Information and Support Complexity of Gaussian Mixtures
Information Theory.summary:
We study lower bounds on the Fisher information of Gaussian location mixtures and their applications to estimation problems. First, for a discrete mixing distribution, we derive a universal positive-semidefinite lower bound on the Fisher information matrix in terms of the Rényi entropy of order two. For a mixing distribution supported on $K$ points, this bound scales as $\log(K)/K^2$, improving by a logarithmic factor on the support-size dependence obtained from Stam's inequality. We then develop dimension-aware trace bounds using classical Sobolev inequalities. These bounds are expressed in terms of Sibson's $α$-mutual information and yield the scaling $K^{-2/n}$ in dimension $n$. A complementary bound involving the $α$-mutual information of order $1/2$ is obtained using the sharp Young convolution inequality.
  The derived inequalities are further specialized to rotationally invariant mixing distributions supported on discrete spherical shells. In this setting, an intrinsic-dimensional bound on Sibson mutual information leads to lower bounds on the Fisher information in terms of the number of occupied shells. As applications, we study least favorable priors for bounded Gaussian mean estimation. In the scalar case, we show that the least favorable prior on $[-R,R]$ has at least $Ω(R\sqrt{\log R})$ support points and that each of its probability masses is of order at most $1/R$. In the vector case, we show that the number of occupied shells grows at least linearly with $R$. Finally, Brown's identity and the I-MMSE relationship are used to translate the Fisher-information inequalities into upper bounds on the MMSE and mutual information.

Information Theory.title: Extreme Points of the $(0,δ)$-LDP Polytope with Small Input Size and Arbitrary Output Sizes
Information Theory.summary: The structure of locally differentially private (LDP) mechanisms can be understood through the geometry of the corresponding privacy polytope. While the extreme points of the \( (ε,0)\)-LDP polytope are well characterized (Kairouz {et al.}, 2014; Holohan {et al.}, 2017), comparatively little is known for the \((ε,δ)\)-LDP polytope with \(δ>0\). Recent work (Elangovan and Jog, 2024) has shown that even in the special case \(ε=0\), the \( (0,δ) \)-LDP privacy polytope exhibits fundamentally different behaviour. In this work, we provide complete characterizations of the extreme points for the low-input-alphabet regime \(k=2\) and \(k=3\) and with arbitrary output alphabet size \(m \). We also identify new extreme mechanisms for larger input alphabet sizes \(k\), of the star configuration type, as introduced by Elangovan and Jog (2024).

Information Theory.title: How Does Probabilistic Constellation Shaping Control Ranging Sidelobe Levels in ISAC?
Information Theory.summary: Probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS), originally designed to fill the gap between finite uniform constellations and continuous capacity-achieving input distributions, has recently emerged as a central tool in adjusting the expected integrated sidelobe level (EISL) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this paper, we show that PCS goes beyond EISL: A large class of PCS methods, termed as type-based PCS, are capable of providing precise control over codeword-wise integrated sidelobe level ratio (ISLR) for systems employing orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), thus yielding a stronger sensing performance guarantee than EISL control. We further show that OFDM is almost the only unitary modulation basis whose codeword-wise ISLR can be precisely controlled by type-based PCS. Based upon the analytical results, practical type-based PCS methods compatible with the probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) framework are conceived, which achieve higher communication rates than existing ISAC-oriented PCS methods under identical ISLR constraints.

Information Theory.title: Coverage Region Analysis and Optimization of FIRES-Assisted NOMA and OMA Systems
Information Theory.summary: Fluid integrated reflecting and emitting surfaces (FIRES) are investigated. In these metasurfaces, each subarea hosts an active element capable of simultaneous transmission and reflection, phase, and geometric positioning control within the subarea. We develop a coverage-centric system model for the two-user downlink scenario (one user per half-space) under spatially correlated Rician fading and imperfect phase control. First, we derive closed-form far-field line-of-sight (LoS) coverage bounds that reveal the effects of aperture size, base station (BS) distance, transmit power, energy-splitting (ES), and phase errors. Protocol-aware corollaries are then presented for both orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), including conditions for successful successive interference cancellation (SIC). Second, we formulate coverage maximization as a bi-level optimization problem consisting of (i) an outer search over FIRES element positions, selecting one active preset per subarea under minimum-spacing constraints, and (ii) an inner resource allocation problem tailored to the multiple-access scheme, which is one-dimensional for OMA and a small convex program for NOMA. The proposed framework explicitly accounts for target rate constraints, ES conservation, power budgets, geometric placement limits, and decoding-order feasibility. Extensive simulations demonstrate that FIRES, by jointly exploiting geometric repositioning and passive energy control, substantially enlarges the coverage region compared with a conventional simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) under the same element budget. Furthermore, NOMA yields additional coverage gains when feasible. The analytical coverage bounds closely match the simulation results and quantify the robustness of FIRES to phase-control imperfections.

Information Theory.title: Post-Quantum Secure Aggregation via Code-Based Homomorphic Encryption
Information Theory.summary: Secure aggregation lets a server learn the sum of inputs from multiple users without learning individual contributions. Recent single-server protocols achieve this with key- and message-additive homomorphic encryption (KAHE), but existing instantiations rely on lattice assumptions. We instantiate a KAHE from the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) assumption and analyze the challenges that arise with the Hamming metric. Decryption of the aggregate amounts to decoding over a q-ary symmetric channel whose crossover probability grows with the number of users. Security under leakage of the key sum reduces to LPN with a noise rate that is quadratic in the KAHE noise rate, and a matching attack shows that this loss is inherent when all but two users collude. Asymptotically, we characterize the optimal communication cost in closed form, showing that the overhead over the raw payload vanishes as the input length grows, and decouple the field size from the input range via the Chinese remainder theorem. In cross-silo settings, our protocol requires less communication than information-theoretically secure aggregation for moderate to high collusion.

Information Theory.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
Information Theory.summary: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

Information Theory.title: On the structure of polynomial ideal codes and additive Reed--Solomon codes
Information Theory.summary: We study structural properties of polynomial ideal (PI) codes and additive Reed--Solomon (aRS) codes in the folded Hamming metric (equivalently, the Hamming metric over a larger alphabet). We first determine the maximum possible length of PI codes, prove that the dual of every PI code is a generalized PI code, and deduce that PI codes are dually QMDS together with an explicit formula for their weight distribution. We then show that PI codes defined by irreducible polynomials correspond to aRS codes with pairwise nonconjugate evaluation points. For these aRS codes, the previous results on PI codes apply (duality, QMDS property and weight distribution). We show that, asymptotically, aRS codes with nonconjugate evaluation points achieve the same length as PI codes. We also compute the permutation group of such aRS codes. We also extend the family of PI codes to consider arbitrary polynomial modules (not necessarily pairwise coprime), and study when these and general aRS codes satisfy the QMDS and dually QMDS properties.

Information Theory.title: A Unified Two-Stage Generative Diffusion Framework for Channel Estimation and Port Selection in Multiuser MIMO-FAS
Information Theory.summary: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for next-generation wireless systems. However, practical multiuser multiple-input multiple-output FAS (MIMO-FAS) faces two inherently coupled challenges: acquiring accurate high-dimensional channel state information (CSI) from limited RF chains and solving the combinatorial port selection problem, where the effectiveness of the latter highly depends on the result of the former. In this paper, we propose a unified two-stage diffusion framework that formulates the joint task as a maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) inference problem equivalent to maximizing the posterior expected utility of the port selection, and approximates it through two sequential stages. For Stage I, we employ a continuous flow-based diffusion model as a powerful implicit prior for 2D FAS channels and perform approximate posterior sampling via a parallel guided generation scheme, enabling accurate multiuser channel recovery even under severely low sub-sampling ratios. For Stage II, we train a discrete diffusion model on optimal labels computed by exhaustive search to propose a pool of promising port selection candidates. The final selection is then determined by maximizing the empirical posterior expected utility over this pool, followed by a lightweight local refinement. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework simultaneously achieves accurate channel estimation and delivers over 90% of the deployed rate of the computationally expensive exhaustive search over the estimated channel, while substantially improving the minimum achievable rate relative to practical cascaded schemes.
Information Theory.comment: 16 pages, 9 figures. Revised version submitted to an IEEE journal for possible publication

Information Theory.title: Decoding Failure Biases IBLT Count Measurements: A Gaussian-Selection Law at the Peeling Threshold
Information Theory.summary:
In a self-sizing set-reconciliation protocol, a small first-round Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT) sketch attempts peeling decoding; after failure, the protocol estimates the difference count $d$ from the count energy and sizes the second round from a lower quantile of the measurement. This quantile must be computed conditionally on failure: the measurement and peeling success are determined by the same random mapping, so conditioning can shift the measurement law.
  In the ideal peeling model, inside the critical window where failure has nondegenerate probability, the standardized energy and a statistic of the unsigned mapping that governs the peeling outcome (the precritical score) have a joint Gaussian limit with correlation $η_kρ^2$, $ρ$ being the sign imbalance and $η_k$ a closed-form constant. The measurement conditional on failure is thus a bivariate normal truncated to a half-plane, which we call the Gaussian-selection law. Since $η_k$ changes sign between $k=4$ and $k=5$, under one-sided imbalance the unconditional threshold undercovers exactly when $k\ge5$ and is conservative for $k=3,4$.
  The key tool is a quenched CLT for a signed quadratic form on a random overlap graph; under asymptotically balanced signs, conditioning on any unsigned mapping event that is permutation-invariant and has probability bounded away from zero leaves the standard normal limit unchanged. After failure the protocol observes the total sign; inverting the selection law yields an upper confidence bound for $d$, asymptotically conservative in the critical window and, when $d/\sqrt M\to\infty$, along the whole load axis. The experiments use analytic constants, none fitted; the unconditional threshold carries a selection error that does not vanish with scale, while the corrected selection-law threshold matches per-configuration empirical quantiles.

Information Theory.title: Parallel Repetition for Entangled Games via Conditional Relative Entropy
Information Theory.summary:
We give a proof of the cubic parallel-repetition bound for finite two-player entangled games using quantum conditional relative entropy. For a game with entangled value $1-\varepsilon<1$ and answer alphabets $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, its $n$-fold repeated value is at most \[
  \exp[-Ω(\varepsilon^3n/L)],\qquad
  L:=\max\{1,\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|)\}, \] for every $n\ge1$. This recovers Song's cubic rate. We also prove a threshold bound: the probability of winning a fraction at least $1-\varepsilon+δ$ is at most $\exp[-Ω(δ^5n/(\varepsilon^2L))]$ for $0<δ\le\varepsilon$.
  Our information charge is the decrease in relative entropy when a question reference is discarded. Our comparison states preserve the original conditional question law. A chain rule bounds the coordinate charges using the cost of conditioning on checked wins and retaining checked answers. Our main lemma converts small charges into nearby pure-state descriptions and local corrections, each depending only on one player's question. Together with Song's sampler, these enable approximate local preparation of the conditioned workspace.

Information Theory.title: On the Power Distance Representation of Bregman Divergences
Information Theory.summary: We express Bregman divergences between parameters as power distances between corresponding weighted points, and investigate several applications of this representation. First, we show that the Bregman closest pair and diameter problems can be reformulated as bichromatic weighted point problems under the power distance. This reformulation enables Bregman nearest and farthest neighbor queries under power distances to be handled in practice through corresponding Euclidean neighbor queries in one additional dimension, after offsetting the weights. Next, we revisit the problem of computing minimum enclosing Bregman balls (Bregman MEBs) and establish their equivalence to double-sided weight power MEBs. We further show that Bregman MEBs can be approximated by relaxing the double-sided weight power MEB problem to its single-sided weight counterpart. We then present two approaches to solving general power MEB problems: An exact algorithm based on the LP-type framework and an arbitrarily accurate approximation scheme based on iterative Frank-Wolfe optimization. Finally, we show that the potential-function lifting transformations used to construct Bregman Voronoi diagrams can be reinterpreted as classical paraboloid lifting transformations applied to the corresponding weighted point sets. This establishes a direct connection between Bregman Voronoi diagrams and power diagrams, further illustrating how Bregman divergences can be represented as power distances.

Information Theory.title: Conditioning Strengthens Classical Entropy and Matrix Inequalities: A Submodular Approach
Information Theory.summary:
Dembo, Cover, and Thomas (1991) developed an elegant information-theoretic framework for proving determinantal inequalities for positive definite matrices, which relies on the structural inequalities of differential entropy. Submodular functions, which subsume entropy, inherently satisfy these structural inequalities because they obey generalized forms of the fundamental properties of entropy -- a chain rule and the property that conditioning reduces the function's value (under an appropriate definition of conditioning). Applying subadditivity, Han's inequality (1978), and partition subadditivity (i.e., subadditivity over a partition) yields Hadamard's, Szász's, and Fischer's inequalities, respectively. Furthermore, this framework recovers Ky Fan's inequality (1955), a strengthening of Hadamard's inequality. We highlight a previously unnoticed information-theoretic insight behind this improvement: conditioning yields a tighter upper bound on the joint entropy than the unconditional one.
  In this paper, we establish conditional strengthenings of Han's inequality and partition subadditivity in the general setting of submodular functions. We derive equality conditions for these strengthened bounds and characterize when they strictly improve their unconditional counterparts. We specialize these results to differential entropy and apply them to establish strengthened versions of Szász's and Fischer's inequalities. The strengthening of Szász's inequality recovers Ky Fan's inequality as a special case, and is strictly stronger than the classical Szász's inequality for any non-diagonal positive definite matrix. We also derive an inequality concerning eigenvalues, which generalizes and strictly strengthens a corresponding eigenvalue inequality of Ky Fan. We provide numerical examples to explicitly illustrate the tightness of our proposed matrix determinantal bounds.

Information Theory.title: Iterative Bounded Distance Decoding With 2-Bit Reliability Marker For Product-Like Codes
Information Theory.summary: We propose a novel soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product codes based on two-bit quantized reliability markers. In particular, one bit is used for a two-level tolerance miscorrection check to validate the bounded distance decoding (BDD) result, while the other identifies bits to be randomly flipped upon BDD failure and miscorrection. List decoding is incorporated to further facilitate the error performance. Density evolution is performed for the design of the quantization thresholds. Compared to iterative BDD, the proposed scheme requires only moderate increases in memory and computational overhead. Simulation results verify that our scheme outperforms several unquantized soft-aided decoders, while maintaining small memory costs and low BDD attempts.
Information Theory.comment: Accepted by IEEE Information Theory Workshop 2026

Information Theory.title: The Rate of the Delsarte Bound for Binary Codes and Spheres
Information Theory.summary:
We give the asymptotic rate of Delsarte's linear programming bound for binary codes and spherical codes. This extends previous work of the author which formulated and proved an analogue of the conjecture of Afkhami-Jeddi, Cohn, Hartman, de Laat, and Tajdini for binary codes, obtaining the rate of the Delsarte linear program at distance $1/2-1/π$.
  The lower bounds introduce ideas from potential theory into the study of Delsarte's bounds, whereby the measures underlying a system of orthogonal polynomials give an obstacle problem. We solve the resulting obstacle problem in the case of binary codes and spherical codes, obtaining a closed form for the lower bound in terms of elliptic integrals. For the upper bounds, we relate the $N$-qubit construction for binary codes used in previous work of the author to the constructions in OpenAI's Chapter 2 for spherical codes and observe that they both involve interlacing spectra. This leads to a variational problem involving measures constructed from these spectra under the Markov-Krein correspondence. This variational problem admits an exact solution and matches the lower bound.

Information Theory.title: Finite-History Outage Certification for Partially Observed Fluid Antenna Receivers
Information Theory.summary: Fluid antenna receivers can select a service position from partial port observations, but finite historical data leave uncertainty in the covariance used for that decision. We develop deployment-before-use reliability certification for a frozen partial-observation rule. A proper predictive density defines a history-based parameter region. Gaussian covariance envelopes, shared conditional-probability bounds and selector enclosures provide simultaneous risk bounds over continuous parameters and discontinuous port decisions. Separate history-coverage and integration budgets limit erroneous positive certification to 0.05 for a single qualification procedure under the stated stationary model and numerical assumptions. Confidence-set inclusion allows a new independent history to reuse the risk computation with the rule unchanged. In a structured Gaussian example with 32 candidate positions, five noisy probes and target outage 0.001, all 282 risk groups are qualified; the largest upper bound is 0.000999748. A separate coupled comparison gives a current-rule outage interval of $[7.6820,9.1266]\times10^{-4}$ and resolves lower outage than two observed-port controls using the same historical fit. One independently recalibrated history reuses the certificate without additional risk sampling. Unresolved and adverse-member controls delimit this reuse.

Information Theory.title: On the Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information
Information Theory.summary: We address an open problem raised by Polyanskiy and Wu in their textbook concerning the subadditivity of mutual \(f\)-information. We study two notions of generalized mutual information: mutual \(f\)-information, defined by \(\widetilde{I}_f(X;Y)=D_f(p_{XY}\|p_Xp_Y)\), and variational \((G,f)\)-information, obtained by minimizing an average of transformed \(f\)-divergences. For the first notion, we derive a sufficient condition on \(g(x)=x^2f''(x)\) that guarantees subadditivity under conditionally independent observations. This condition yields explicit families beyond the previously known examples generated by \(x\log x\) and \((x-1)\log x\). Our proof relies on the concavity of a generalized variance functional. For the variational notion, we extend existing sufficient conditions beyond the transforms \(G(x)\in\{x,\log(1+x),-\log(1-x)\}\). Using a comparison inequality for \(G^{-1}(G(A)+G(B))\), we obtain differential criteria for concave and convex transforms. Explicit constructions illustrate the resulting classes of subadditive information measures.

Information Theory.title: Antenna Placement for Movable Antenna-Enabled Near-Field Target Localization
Information Theory.summary: Movable antennas (MAs) have recently emerged as a promising technology to enhance the wireless sensing performance by exploiting additional spatial degrees of freedom. In this work, we consider an MA-enabled near-field target localization problem under a device-based sensing architecture, where the sensing target actively transmits signals and the sensing receiver estimates its location based on the received signals. We adopt the squared position error bound (SPEB) as the sensing performance metric and aim to minimize the target's SPEB by optimizing the antenna placement at the sensing receiver. The resulting optimization problem is highly non-convex due to the minimum antenna spacing constraints and the intricate dependence of the SPEB on the antenna locations and the intractable form of SPEB. To tackle this problem, we first relax the inter-spacing constraints and accordingly formulate an antenna position distribution problem in terms of degree-4 truncated moments. The reformulated moment-based problem admits an equivalent semidefinite programming formulation and can be optimally solved using standard convex optimization solvers. Using truncated moment theory, we then recover an optimal antenna position distribution supported on a finite number of locations and construct an efficient clustered placement policy. Numerical results demonstrate that the constructed optimal distribution exhibits a three-cluster structure with source-dependent weights. The proposed antenna placement method outperforms conventional array geometries and closely approaches the exhaustive-search benchmark scheme.

Information Theory.title: Four-Level Quantized Soft Information Aided Hard-Decision Decoder for Product-like Codes
Information Theory.summary: We propose a novel low-complexity soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product-like codes, termed iterative bounded-distance decoding (iBDD) with graded scaled reliability and bit-flipping (GSRF). This scheme operates on four-level quantized soft information. It incorporates a graded scaled reliability rule to assign decoding confidence to the bounded-distance decoding result, and employs a bit-flipping rule based on bit-level and component-code-level reliability. A selective re-decoding rule is designed to further facilitate the error performance while keeping the number of BDD attempts in reasonably low levels. The decoding parameter design of iBDD-GSRF is investigated for product codes and staircase codes, respectively. Simulation results on both codes verify that iBDD-GSRF achieves a gain of more than 0.4 dB over the conventional iBDD, comparable to several existing unquantized soft-aided decoders.

Information Theory.title: Explicit reduced APN permutations: ramification and optimal Galois-ring lifts
Information Theory.summary: Let $m\ge5$ be odd and $q=2^m$. For every odd $r$ with $3\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$ we give the reduced polynomial $P_{m,r}=\mathrm{red}((T_r^3)^{2^{m-2}})$, $T_r=\sum_{i<r}X^{2^i}$, explicitly: it has coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_2$ and exactly $3r-2$ terms, it is an APN permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$, and its formal derivative $1+X^{2^{r-2}}+X^{2^{m-2}}$ has no zero on $\mathbb{F}_q$ and is two-to-one. We determine the ramification of $P_{m,r}$ as a map of the projective line for all admissible $(m,r)$: there are $2^{m-r}$ finite ramification points, all wild, with index and different exponent $2^{r-2}$, all over the single finite branch value $1$. The $0/1$ lift of $P_{m,r}$ satisfies an identity in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ that evaluates it over every Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ with $m-1$ squarings, one general multiplication and $r+5$ additions or subtractions. For every quadratic optimal APN permutation $p$ of $\mathbb{F}_q$ (in particular $P_{m,r}$), every $k\ge2$ and every coefficient lift $F$ of $p$ to $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$, we determine the differential rows of $F$ exactly in the unit directions whose residue lies outside the kernel $\{0,ρ\}$ of the linear part of $p'$ (they are the residue rows of $p$; $ρ=1$ for $P_{m,r}$) and in the directions in $2^{k-1}\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)\setminus\{0\}$ (every nonzero entry equals $2q^{k-1}$). We also give a self-contained proof of the Li--Wang criterion for a Gold function plus a linearised polynomial, which explains why the inner map of $P_{m,r}$ is not a monomial, and record a two-word, two-layer transition that a simple linear layer forbids at the residue level.
Information Theory.comment: 15 pages. Submitted to Finite Fields and Their Applications. Code, Lean 4 formalization and blueprint: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23233173 (version 1.0.1; https://github.com/hirokifukui/residue-apn)

Information Theory.title: Optimal Reduced Representatives of Quadratic APN Permutations in Odd Dimension
Information Theory.summary: The formal derivative of the reduced polynomial representative of a map on a binary finite field depends on the coordinates, although its differential uniformity does not. This matters for lifting permutations to Galois rings: a polynomial over a Galois ring of characteristic a power of two greater than two permutes the ring exactly when its reduction permutes the residue field and the derivative of the reduction has no zero there. We prove that for every odd $n\ge5$, every quadratic almost perfect nonlinear permutation $Q$ of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ admits invertible binary-linear maps $L$ and $A$ such that the derivative of the reduced representative of $L\circ Q\circ A$ has no zero and each of its nonempty fibres has exactly two elements. The range is exact: this fails for $n=3$, as computed earlier, and for even $n$ there are no such permutations. For $n\ge9$, a linearization and a projectively injective cofactor map reduce the problem to counting binary matrices: more than 5% of the invertible inputs $A$ succeed, more than half for $n\ge15$, without any classification. For $n=5,7$ we use two independent classifications and finite certificates. Consequently every such permutation is linearly equivalent to a counterexample to the reduced critical-point conjecture of Bartoli and Stănică that lifts to permutation polynomials of optimal differential uniformity over every Galois ring with this residue field. For odd $n\ge9$ the existence proof is checked in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
Information Theory.comment: 22 pages. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. Code, certificates and Lean 4 formalization: https://github.com/hirokifukui/apnlift (Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23055799)

Information Theory.title: Shift-Invariant Permutations with Polynomial Composition: Construction and Algebraic Structure
Information Theory.summary: Shift-invariant permutations of $\mathbb F_2^n$ are particularly attractive in symmetric cryptography because of their regularity and implementation efficiency. Constructing such permutations with an explicit algebraic structure remains a challenging problem. In this paper, we study a family of shift-invariant transformations of $\mathbb F_2^n$ constructed from a recursively defined sequence of mappings $\{γ_j\}_{j\ge 0}$ associated with landscapes. First, we prove that, under an explicit dimension condition relating $n$ to the support of the landscape, the sequence $\{γ_j\}_{j\ge 0}$ has the polynomial composition property if and only if the corresponding landscape is quasi-conserved on $\mathbb F_2^n$ with a nonzero special index. Then, we determine the eventual zero or periodic behavior of $\{γ_j\}_{j\ge0}$, including the exact index at which the sequence either first vanishes or becomes periodic, together with the least eventual period, and establish linear independence until the first linear relation occurs. When the polynomial composition property holds, we establish an explicit isomorphism between the group of permutation elements in the monoid generated by these mappings and the unit group of a quotient ring $\mathbb F_2[z]/\langle p(z)\rangle$, where $p(z)$ is a monomial or a binomial determined by the landscape. This framework reduces the tasks of testing bijectivity, computing iterates, and determining compositional inverses and orders of permutation elements to polynomial computations. Finally, we apply the results to mappings represented by binomials and trinomials in the quotient ring, obtaining explicit criteria and formulas, and tabulate more than one hundred representative constructions of shift-invariant permutations, recovering and unifying several previously studied families.

Information Theory.title: A One-Sided McDiarmid-Type Inequality for Heavy Tails via Reverse KL Tensorization
Information Theory.summary: We revisit McDiarmid's inequality, a central tool in statistical learning theory and algorithm analysis. We show that large deviations above the mean are exponentially unlikely for functions of independent random variables that are almost surely bounded above and satisfy a conditional moment assumption of order $p\in(1,2]$. When $p<2$, the result applies even when the function has infinite variance. Our proof relies on a new tensorization inequality for the Kullback--Leibler divergence, termed reverse KL tensorization, which may be of independent interest. Applications include concentration of the sample mean and median-of-means estimator, and one-sided uniform risk bounds for unbounded losses.

Information Theory.title: Multiplicative Semidefinite Programming Upper Bounds on Quantum No-Signalling-Assisted Zero-Error Capacity
Information Theory.summary: We study zero-error communication and exact simulation of quantum channels assisted by quantum no-signalling correlations. For a channel with Kraus operator space $K$, we introduce a semidefinite programming parameter $Γ(K)$ that is exactly multiplicative under tensor products and upper-bounds $Θ_{\rm NS}(K)$, where $\log_2Θ_{\rm NS}(K)=C_{0,\rm NS}(K)$ and $C_{0,\rm NS}(K)$ denotes the asymptotic quantum no-signalling-assisted zero-error capacity. Among known upper bounds on $Θ_{\rm NS}$ given by semidefinite programs, $Γ$ is the tightest. We also prove that the previously introduced simulation lower bound $Σ^{-}(K)$ is exactly multiplicative and satisfies $Θ_{\rm NS}(K)\leqΓ(K)\leqΣ^{-}(K)\leqΓ(K)^2$. Using this multiplicativity, we show that neither $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)=\log_2Σ^{-}(K)$ nor its regularized extension $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)=\lim\nolimits_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log_2Σ^{-}(K^{\otimes n})$ holds in general. This answers an open question about the asymptotic simulation cost $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)$. For classical-quantum channels, we obtain sharp bounds. If $r$ is the effective output dimension, then $Θ_{\rm NS}\leqΓ\leq(1+r^{1/2})Θ_{\rm NS}/2$ and $Γ\leqΣ^{-}\leq(1+r^{1/2})Γ/2$. If $k$ is the minimum rank of the output support projections, then $Σ^{-}/Θ_{\rm NS}\leq[(1+r^{1/2})/(1+k^{1/2})]^2$, and this bound is sharp for every $1\leq k\leq r$. Thus, we obtain the sharp bound $S_{0,\rm NS}-C_{0,\rm NS}\leq2\log_2[(1+r^{1/2})/(1+k^{1/2})]$.

Information Theory.title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
Information Theory.summary: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.

Information Theory.title: Direction-Shift Keying for High-Mobility mmWave Communications: Geometry-Based Resilience to Short Channel Coherence Times and Phase Noise
Information Theory.summary: Communication reliability in high-mobility millimeter-wave (mmWave) systems is fundamentally challenged by rapid channel variations, manifested in short channel coherence times, and phase noise, which necessitate frequent channel estimation and phase tracking. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Direction-Shift Keying (DSK), a geometry-based modulation scheme that exploits the relative stability of propagation directions rather than the rapidly varying amplitude and phase of the wireless channel. DSK conveys information through distinguishable directions of arrival (DoAs), enabled by a distributed antenna system (DAS), thereby shifting the communication principle from channel-dependent to geometry-dependent signaling. We first derive the structure of the optimal DSK detector for a mobile device equipped with an arbitrary number of antennas. We then establish the fundamental law governing the temporal stability of propagation directions, termed Direction Coherence Time (DCT), and show that DCT scales as $d/v$, where $d$ is the transmitter--receiver distance and $v$ is the relative velocity. In contrast, conventional Channel Coherence Time (CCT) scales as $λ/v$, where $λ$ denotes the wavelength, revealing a coherence-time advantage on the order of $d/λ$, potentially exceeding four orders of magnitude in mmWave systems. Furthermore, we establish the inherent invariance of DSK to common phase rotations, providing resilience to common oscillator phase noise without explicit phase tracking. Numerical results corroborate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the potential of geometry-based signaling for reliable high-mobility mmWave communications.

Information Theory.title: Efficient Agnostic Learning of Univariate Densities Under Local Differential Privacy
Information Theory.summary: We propose a general framework for non-interactive locally differentially private (LDP) learning of structured univariate distributions that can be approximated by piece-wise polynomials. This gives the first sample-efficient LDP learners for several distribution classes, including mixtures of log-concave distributions, such as Gaussian mixture models (GMMs). These learners also provide agnostic guarantees and are computationally efficient. We also prove a lower bound for learning GMMs under LDP, improving on the standard pure-DP packing lower bounds of Bun et al. [BKSW19]. To obtain our general learning framework, we develop an efficient non-interactive LDP algorithm for synthetic data generation over large domains, which may be of independent interest. We then use it together with a deterministic adaptation of the non-private piecewise polynomial learner of Acharya et al. [ADLS17].

Probability.title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
Probability.summary: In this paper, we consider a discrete-time pull-based remote estimation system involving an information source and a remote monitor where the information source is a finite-state irreducible discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) process. In this system, the remote monitor sends a pull request towards the source which responds by sampling its process so as to transmit the sampled values towards the monitor through a delay channel, encapsulated in information packets. We consider i) zero delay (ZD) and ii) unit delay (UD) channels, where the packet transmission times are zero and one slot, respectively. For remote estimation, we use the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, and for quantifying its performance, we use the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) which is a recently proposed freshness and mismatch metric that penalizes an incorrect estimation along with its duration. Our goal is to obtain pull policies so as to minimize MAoII under a long-run sampling rate constraint. For the ZD model, we propose a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) formulation of the problem, which allows us to find the optimum observation-dependent pull policy. On the other hand, the UD channel prevents the monitor from possessing perfect information on the actual AoII process at any given time, and the SMDP formulation of the ZD channel cannot readily be used for the UD model. For the system with the UD channel, we first provide a numerical algorithm to calculate the MAoII and the average sampling rate for a given observation-dependent pull policy. For the optimization of the underlying remote estimation system, we use the joint distribution of the age and source processes to be obtained from the history of all observations, termed as belief. Subsequently, we propose a belief-dependent policy obtained via the belief-MDP formulation and a constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) algorithm.

Probability.title: Efficient sampling of the unlabeled structure of uniform random mappings and surjections
Probability.summary:
This article deals with the sampling and statistics of uniform random mappings and surjections from $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ to $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. More precisely, we focus on statistics that are invariant under relabeling of the domain and codomain. The structure of a mapping or surjection up to relabeling is captured by a compact representation called its profile. The profile records, for each occurring preimage size, the number of preimages of that size.
  We provide a complete set of algorithms that directly sample the profiles of uniform random mappings and surjections, covering the full parameter space. Their expected running times match the expected length of their outputs up to logarithmic factors. It is important to note that we make no assumption about the relationship between $n$ and $k$; in particular, we do not assume that $n/k$ is constant. All our guarantees are uniform in $n$ and $k$. Achieving this uniformity substantially complicates the analysis. Our algorithms are based on exact-size Boltzmann samplers, which we accelerate by optimizing the cost of each sampling round and increasing the acceptance probability.
  As spin-off results, we answer, up to a logarithmic factor, an open question of Devroye and Los~25 on sampling profiles of random mappings when $n>k\log k$, and obtain a sampler for uniform random surjections with expected running time $O(n\log k)$, valid across the full parameter space.

Probability.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
Probability.summary: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output. Anari et al. (2026) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token. We propose the Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al. (2026). Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping. We show that the KL-divergence between the data distribution and the SIRS output is bounded by a clipping term plus the model's training error. With exact scores, parallel decoding pays the full within-block dependence, whereas SIRS pays only the part beyond the clipping range.

Probability.title: Per-State Signatures and Mean Time-to-Failure: An Algorithm for Systems With Simultaneous Failures
Probability.summary: We present an algorithm that computes the structural signature and the mean time-to-failure (MTTF) of a monotone binary system at every one of its states, rather than only at the state in which all components work. It makes no assumption on the structure function and evaluates it exactly once per state, as many times as needed for the signature of the complete system alone, so computing the MTTF everywhere costs only a factor polynomial in the number of components over computing it once. As a by-product, it identifies all minimal path sets. We assume exchangeable component failure times whose survivor count is a continuous-time Markov chain. This setting admits simultaneous failures, as in the Lévy-frailty Marshall-Olkin, binomial failure rate and lethal-shock models, where the simplifications available for single failures do not apply. We use the per-state MTTF to define threshold repair policies. We show that the per-state signature is a strictly finer decision criterion than the MTTF: signature dominance at a common failure count implies MTTF dominance, but not conversely. Under the Lévy-frailty Marshall-Olkin model the MTTF is monotone in the state, which yields the long-run cost rate of every threshold policy in a single pass. Experiments on 22 benchmark networks with up to 30 components and 31 failure models show that the best MTTF-threshold policy has a median excess cost of 0.36% over the optimal state-based policy, and that it is never worse than the best policy that repairs after a fixed number of failures.
Probability.comment: The manuscript has been submitted to IEEE Transactions on Reliability

Probability.title: A quadratic ancestor inequality for spanning trees
Probability.summary: We introduce a quadratic ancestor inequality for weighted spanning trees on finite undirected graphs and give two applications. First, for every finite $n$-vertex transitive graph, the expected distance in its uniform spanning tree (UST) between two independent uniform vertices is at least $\sqrt{n}-1$, resolving a conjecture in [Benjamini--Kozma, Comm. Math. Phys. 259 (2005), 257--286]. Second, we prove that the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) is at least 3/2.

Probability.title: Segal's semigroup, Virasoro structure, and Ward identities in Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory
Probability.summary: Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory (CILT for short) is a probabilistically constructed Conformal Field Theory (CFT), expected to have connections to minimal models, Coulomb gas integrals, and loop models. In this paper, we study the quantization of Segal's semigroup given by CILT. Each element $\mathbf T_f$ in the quantized semigroup corresponds to a conformal annulus: the unit disk $\mathbb D$ with $f(\mathbb D^\circ)$ removed, where $f:\mathbb D\to f(\mathbb D)\subset \mathbb D^\circ$ is a contracting biholomorphism. This semigroup encodes the local conformal structure of the CFT, in particular the Virasoro symmetry with central charge $<1$ for CILT. We first relate the quantized Segal's semigroup to Segal's amplitudes of annuli and recover the Virasoro generators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\geq0$) of CILT as generators of this semigroup. Compared to the real Liouville CFT, the main difficulty here is the absence of positivity, which we address through estimates for the imaginary Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos and non-self-adjoint operators. Using Segal's gluing axiom as in the real case, we differentiate the amplitude and use conformal covariance to derive the Ward identities in terms of all Virasoro operators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$). We also outline the parallel theory for Boundary CILT (BCILT), concerning Segal's semigroup of semiannuli. These results provide essential tools for the conformal bootstrap program of (B)CILT, boundary BPZ equations, boundary structure constants, and the global construction of conformal blocks.

Probability.title: Spectral comparison on Specht modules and mixing of the interchange process
Probability.summary:
We characterize the cases in which the minimal eigenvalues of interchange-process Laplacians on two Specht modules can be compared up to a positive multiplicative constant, independent of the edge rates. In the comparable cases, we establish an inverse-polynomial lower bound for this constant. We conjecture that the constant can always be taken to be 2/3.
  We apply these ideas to the mixing times of the interchange and exclusion processes. Using the comparison method of Hermon, Kozma and Salez, we prove that our conjecture implies a conjecture of Oliveira on the mixing time of the interchange process. We also obtain unconditional mixing-time bounds for both processes.

Probability.title: Gamma Expansions of Level Two Large Deviation Rate Functionals for Metastable Diffusions
Probability.summary: Consider the diffusions $dX_t^\varepsilon=b(X_t^\varepsilon)dt+\sqrt{2\varepsilon}σ(X_t^\varepsilon)dB_t$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $b$ and $σ$ are smooth coefficients and $B_t$ is an $r$-dimensional Brownian motion, with $r\le d$. We allow nonreversible dynamics and a degenerate diffusion matrix. Let $\mathcal{I}_\varepsilon$ be the level-two large deviation rate functional of the empirical measure. Under our assumptions, including a complete metastable hierarchy described by resolvent convergence, we establish the full $Γ$-expansion $\mathcal{I}_\varepsilon=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\mathcal{J}^{(-1)}+\mathcal{J}^{(0)}+\sum_{p=1}^{\mathfrak{q}}\frac{1}{θ_\varepsilon^{(p)}}\mathcal{J}^{(p)}$ in the sense of successive $Γ$-limits in the weak topology on probability measures. Here $θ_\varepsilon^{(p)}$ are the metastable time scales, and each $\mathcal{J}^{(p)}$, $p\ge1$, is the lift of the level-two rate functional of the corresponding finite-state Markov chain. We establish the pre-metastable $Γ$-limits for generalized overdamped, underdamped, and third-order Langevin dynamics. For the generalized overdamped model, existing metastability results yield the full expansion under additional conditions. For the underdamped and third-order models, the full expansion remains conditional on verification of the complete metastable hierarchy.

Probability.title: Convexity, the spectrum of free Laplacians and geometric consequences: a free KLS bound
Probability.summary: We establish a compactness theorem for the resolvent of free Laplacians. More precisely, let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ be a self-adjoint tuple admitting Lipschitz conjugate variables in the sense of Dabrowski (2014). Under the non-commutative curvature--dimension condition $CD(c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, introduced in our previous work (2026), we prove that the free Laplacian $Δ:=\partial^*\bar\partial$ is proper, that is, has compact resolvent. Our argument is non-perturbative and uses a spectral variant of the free Bochner method based on Dabrowski's almost-commutation formulas. A further stochastic argument gives a normal unital trace-preserving embedding of $M=W^*(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ into $L(\mathbb F_2)$. Together, the compactness and embedding theorems gives several operator-algebraic consequences, including the Haagerup approximation property, the CMAP, and strong solidity. We also obtain proper proximality and bi-exactness. We finally obtain several geometric consequences. We prove a free analogue of Klartag's improved log--Lichnerowicz inequality (2023), together with rigidity in the equality case. More surprisingly, under $CD(0,\infty)$, we prove a dimension-free Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits (KLS) bound in the free setting. As a consequence, we obtain a free thin-shell estimate for isotropic tuples. We conclude with further questions on spectral comparison with the canonical semicircular model.

Probability.title: Barrier Log-Concavity of Large Forests
Probability.summary: We prove that the independence sequence of every sufficiently large forest is strictly barrier log-concave: whenever $i_{k+1}>i_k$, one has $i_k^2>i_{k-1}i_{k+1}$. Consequently, every common downward coefficient tilt is unimodal, with one order threshold valid simultaneously for all $0<t\le1$. As an application, we prove that every sufficiently large well-covered tree has a strictly log-concave independence polynomial. More generally, the latter conclusion holds for well-covered forests with sufficiently large matching number. Every sufficiently large forest with a palindromic independence polynomial is also strictly log-concave, with its modes at the central ranks. The proof establishes local coefficient-curvature estimates uniformly over forests of unbounded maximum degree and over activities tending to zero. Combined with the fixed-density theorem of Fang, Lu, Nevo, Yao, and Zheng, these estimates complete the strict log-concavity interval down to rank one through $\lfloor17α/25\rfloor$; the terminal fraction is inherited. The classical decreasing tail then yields the barrier property. A cumulative-coefficient corona theorem transfers barrier log-concavity of the base forest to full strict log-concavity of its leaf corona.
Probability.comment: 26 pages, 2 figures; optional 16-page quantitative supplement and verification code/data in ancillary files

Probability.title: Strong invariance principles in deterministic systems
Probability.summary: We show that in every aperiodic, probability preserving dynamical system there is a function whose associated time series satisfies the almost sure invariance principle with rate asymptotically smaller then $\sqrt{n}$ and the almost sure weak invariance principle of Brosamler and Schatte.

Probability.title: Poincaré's Inequality on Sliding-Window Occupation Count Kernels and the Optimal Normalized Spectral-Gap Constant
Probability.summary:
Let $P$ be an irreducible reversible Markov kernel on an $m$-state space $Ω$, and denote its right spectral gap by $\Gap(P) =1-λ_2(P)$. From a stationary trajectory, let $K_t$ be the occupation-count vector of the length-$n$ window beginning at time $t$. The stationary pair $(K_0,K_1)$ defines a reversible projected count kernel $\widetilde P_n$. For each fixed $m\ge2$, define \[
  c_m^\star=
  \inf_{\substack{|Ω|=m,\ P\ \mathrm{irreducible\ and\ reversible}
  n\ge2}}
  \frac{n\Gap(\widetilde P_n)}{\Gap(P)}. \] We prove \[
  \frac1{1080m}\le c_m^\star\le q_{m-2},
  \qquad
  q_0=\frac14,\quad q_{r+1}=q_r(1-q_r). \] We also show $q_{m-2}=(m+\log m+O(1))^{-1}$, which implies that $c_m^\star=Θ(m^{-1})$. Thus, the reciprocal optimal comparison cost $C_m^{\mathrm{opt}}=(c_m^\star)^{-1}$ has order $m$. In the two-state case, we determine the exact values $c_2^\star=1/4$ and $C_2^{\mathrm{opt}}=4$. %the exact constants for $m\ge3$ remain open. The lower bound also holds for $n=1$ and is uniform in $P$, including sparse and periodic kernels. The proof combines short-window decorrelation with an averaged anchor-excursion decomposition, a Green-kernel hitting estimate, and a stopped Carleson--Hardy inequality. A nested rare-state construction produces finite $m$-state witnesses whose normalized Rayleigh quotients approach $q_{m-2}$ through an ordered sequence of limits. For every fixed finite irreducible reversible aperiodic kernel on at least two states, $\Gap(\widetilde P_n)=Θ_P(n^{-1})$.

Probability.title: Partial Localization and Multifractality in Heterogeneous Population Growth with Resetting
Probability.summary: We study a model of heterogeneous multiplicative growth with mean-field redistribution and independent local stochastic resetting. The model describes populations or wealth distributed over sites with quenched growth-rate heterogeneity, while resets represent random local extinction or bankruptcy events. At large redistribution or resetting rate, we find a delocalized phase and we compute the growth rate as well as the stationary distribution of the population of a given site. We show that reset-free growth episodes generate power-law stationary tails with site-dependent exponents. For weak resetting and redistribution, favorable sites can undergo long reset-free episodes and localize. This produces a partially localized phase, in which a finite fraction of the total population is carried by a small set of sites whose identity changes on an $O(1)$ time scale within a subextensive pool of $N^{u^\star}$ favorable candidates, with $0<u^\star<1$. We derive the corresponding growth rate from a saddle point analysis, and show that the averaged stationary fractions display multifractal behavior.

Probability.title: Quality control in sublinear time: a case study via random graphs
Probability.summary:
Many algorithms are designed to work well on average over inputs. But when such an algorithm is run on an arbitrary input, the question arises: Can we trust the algorithm on this input? This question is especially relevant in network science, where algorithms for theoretical random graph models are often applied to individual real-world networks.
  We identify a new class of algorithmic problems addressing this, which we call "Quality Control Problems." These problems are specified by a "quality function" $ρ$ and a distribution $D$ such that, with high probability, a sample drawn from $D$ is "high quality," meaning its $ρ$-value is near $1$. The goal is to accept most inputs $x \sim D$ and reject potentially adversarially generated inputs $x$ with $ρ(x)$ far from $1$.
  In this work, we consider the sublinear version of the quality control problem, where $D \in Δ(\{0,1\}^N)$ and the goal is to solve the $(D,ρ)$-quality problem with $o(N)$ queries and time. As a case study, we consider random graphs, i.e., $D = G_{n,p}$ (and $N = \binom{n}2$), and the $k$-clique count function $ρ_k := C_k(G)/\mathbb{E}_{G' \sim G_{n,p}}[C_k(G')]$, where $C_k(G)$ is the number of $k$-cliques in $G$. In suitable parameter ranges, worst-case approximate $k$-clique counting requires $p^{-Ω(k^2)}$ queries. In contrast, we show that the quality control problem for $G_{n,p}$ (with $n\geq p^{-ck}$ for some constant $c$) with respect to $ρ_k$ can be tested with $p^{-O(k)}$ queries and time, showing quality control is provably superpolynomially more efficient in this setting. More generally, for a motif $H$ of maximum degree $Δ(H)$, we show that the corresponding quality control problem can be solved with $p^{-O(Δ(H))}$ queries and running time.

Probability.title: Convergence Rates for Lasserre's Upper-Bound Hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with Gaussian Measure
Probability.summary: We establish quantitative convergence rates for Lasserre's measure-based upper-bound hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ using the standard Gaussian measure as the reference measure. For any polynomial $f$ attaining its global infimum $f_{\min}$, we prove that the order-$r$ upper bounds satisfy $$ λ_r-f_{\min}=O\Big(\frac{1}{r}\Big), $$ yielding, to the best of our knowledge, the first explicit convergence rate for this hierarchy on a noncompact domain. We further show that the rate is sharp by proving an $Ω(1/r)$ rate for $f=x^2$, while demonstrating that, without attainment of the infimum, convergence can be arbitrarily slow: for every $m\ge0$, we construct a polynomial whose upper bounds converge at rate $Θ(r^{-1/(m+2)})$.

Probability.title: On the asymptotic shape of quantile surfaces
Probability.summary: This article is concerned with the asymptotic shape of quantile surfaces, defined as the set of quantiles at a given level $α$ generated by a controlled one-dimensional distribution. Specifically, when the distribution arises as a linear combination of log-normal random variables and the control is a vector of positive coefficients, we prove that quantile surfaces are globally concave in the left tail ($α\to0$) and globally convex in the right tail ($α\to1$). Moreover, these surfaces exhibit asymptotic separation of scale and shape.

Probability.title: Fluctuations from a random fractional averaging limit
Probability.summary: We consider a system of multiscale stochastic differential equations whose slow component is drivenby a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H greater than 1/2. Under ergodic assumptions ensuring the applicability of the fractional averaging and fractional homogenization theorems of Hairer and Li (arXiv:1902.11251, arXiv:2109.06948), we establish a fluctuation result. The deviation of the slow motion, scaled by epsilon^{1/2-H}, from its effective, time-dependent random limit converges, as the time-separation scale epsilon tends to zero, to the solution of a stochastic differential equation driven by a fractional Brownian motion and influenced by an additional space--time Gaussian field. Since the averaging principle and the fractional homogenization hold in different modes of convergence, obtaining the required joint convergence is a delicate matter. Moreover, neither the continuity of the Ito--Lyons solution map nor the martingale method is directly applicable for our purposes, so the proof requires several innovations. To establish the fluctuation theorem, we combine cumulant methods with a residue lemma and formulate the enlarged system as a rough differential equation in a suitable space.
Probability.comment: Accepted version, to appear in Annales de lInstitut Henri Poincare

Probability.title: On Stopping Sets and Continuous-Time Decision Trees
Probability.summary: We study stopping sets and continuous-time decision trees (CTDTs) for Poisson point processes. We first give a proof of the spatial Markov property without assuming that the stopping set contains finitely many points or admits a finite approximation. The proof uses the multivariate Mecke formula on the complement of the stopping set. We then prove that every $μ$-continuous CTDT has an explicit exploration representation: between successive discoveries, the explored set grows according to a deterministic rule depending on the points already observed. If $μ$ is diffuse, the points are revealed one by one almost surely; this need not be imposed as a separate assumption. We also allow atoms of $μ$, in which case all points at one location are revealed together. Finally, for diffuse $μ$, we prove that a locally bounded stopping set revealing at most one point is attainable by a $μ$-continuous exploration. More generally, an increasing sequence of locally bounded stopping sets, each revealing at most one additional point, can be attained by a single exploration at successive stopping times.

Probability.title: Random walk on the small-world network model in 3 or more dimensions
Probability.summary: We study the mixing time of a simple random walk on the small-world network defined by adding edges to $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ as follows: for each pair $\{x,y\}$ we add an edge with probability $Z_n/\|x-y\|^{d}$ with $Z_n$ chosen so that the average number of added edges to every vertex is $1$. When $d\geq 3$, we show that with high probability the mixing time is of order $\log n$ and that the random walk does not exhibit cutoff.

Probability.title: Finite Cumulant Towers for Small-System-Noise Expansions in Nonlinear Filtering
Probability.summary: We study asymptotic expansions for nonlinear filtering in the small-system-noise regime. Our main result is that the expansion coefficients of conditional cumulants satisfy a closed finite-dimensional system that can be solved recursively. At each expansion degree, the evolution of a coefficient introduces a coefficient of the next higher cumulant rank, while a high-rank vanishing property terminates this hierarchy, yielding a finite triangular tower. The first layer is the Kalman--Bucy filter, and subsequent layers satisfy linear equations once the lower layers are known. To derive these equations, we establish generalized Zakai and Kushner--Stratonovich equations for observation-dependent random variables and obtain explicit coefficient equations in arbitrary dimension. The conditional cumulant expansion also determines the expansion of the conditional characteristic function. We further obtain an explicit bound on the number of scalar variables in terms of the state dimension and expansion degree. When the observation function vanishes, the construction reduces to ODEs for unconditional cumulant coefficients. Comparisons with existing asymptotic-expansion algorithms illustrate the resulting reduction in the number of ODE variables.

Probability.title: Mixing time of the lazy and simple random walk on a randomly twisted hypercube
Probability.summary: We consider a randomly twisted hypercube on $N$ vertices and study a simple or lazy random walk on this graph. We show that for both walks the mixing time is of order $\log N$, and the model does not exhibit cutoff. We also establish that both walks have cover time of order $N\log N$, and we show that the chromatic number of the graph diverges.

Probability.title: Sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation bounds for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums
Probability.summary: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables with zero mean and variance $σ^2\in(0,\infty)$. In this paper, we establish a sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums under a finite $p$-th absolute moment, $2<p\le3$. In particular, we show that $\mathbb{P}(M_n\ge xV_n)=2(1-Φ(x))\{1+O(1)β_{n,p}(1+x)^p\}$ for $0\le x\leβ_{n,p}^{-1/p}$, where $M_n=\max_{1\le k\le n}\sum_{j=1}^kX_j$, $V_n=(\sum_{j=1}^nX_j^2)^{1/2}$, $β_{n,p}=\mathbb{E}|X_1|^p/(n^{(p-2)/2}σ^p)$, and $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. This proves a conjecture of Shao2010. More precisely, we bound the relative error by the same truncated-moment quantity as for self-normalized sums. The proof compares the maximum with the absolute sum while preserving their common denominator, through a reflected-walk representation and Fourier estimates with distribution-adapted smoothing.

Probability.title: Conditioning diffusions on a terminal bearing
Probability.summary: We study sampling of a diffusion on $[0,T]$ conditioned on its terminal position lying on a prescribed ray, i.e. on an exactly observed bearing. For a linear drift we derive closed-form expressions for the Doob $h$-function and its gradient. For a broad class of tracking models admitting a Kronecker block structure, the guiding term is obtained from a single row of a matrix exponential, and the conditioned process decomposes into independent radial and angular components. For a nonlinear drift, we construct a guided process using the $h$-function of the linear model and prove absolute continuity of the law of the true conditioned process with respect to the law of the guided process, with an explicit likelihood ratio. This result is used to devise an auxiliary particle filter for bearings observed sequentially in time without noise. Numerical experiments show that the proposed filter approximates the filtering distribution and estimates the log-likelihood considerably more accurately than the shifted Rayleigh filter, at the cost of a higher computing time.

Probability.title: Cutoff Phenomenon for the Glauber-Misanthrope process in a perturbative regime
Probability.summary:
We investigate the Glauber--Misanthrope process, obtained by superposing a Misanthrope dynamics with finite site capacity and a Glauber dynamics which creates or annihilates particles one at a time at each site. In a perturbative regime around the diffusively scaled partial exclusion process, we prove the cutoff phenomenon and identify the limiting mixing time.
  Our approach relies on the information percolation framework developed by Lubetzky and Sly and extended by Tran, which we adapt to accommodate multiple occupancy per site and account for the two distinct correlation mechanisms generated by the Misanthrope and Glauber dynamics. Our lower bound on the mixing time holds under assumptions more general than those required for the matching upper bound.

Probability.title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
Probability.summary:
The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falcón-Cortés, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $ξ_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $ξ>ξ_0$ anywhere else.
  We prove that, for all $ξ_0\in (0,1)$, if $ξ$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $ξ= ξ_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses").
  Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour Pólya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued Pólya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

Probability.title: An inductive approach to stochastic estimates for the $\varphi^{4}_2$-equation with correlated coefficient fields
Probability.summary: We develop an inductive approach to obtain stochastic estimates for singular SPDEs when the coefficient field is correlated with the driving noise. We implement our method, in the whole space, on the example of the $\varphi^{4}_2$-equation. Our approach is based on (infinite-dimensional) integration by parts with respect to Wick products of Gaussian random variables (more precisely, mollifications of space-time white noise) together with an inductive scheme over the moment's exponent.

Probability.title: Feeling the generalised rough SABR boundary
Probability.summary: We provide an in-depth analysis of a generalised rough version of the SABR volatility model, widely used in the financial industry. We specifically focus on its behaviour at the origin, whether it can reach it and how fast it may do so.

Probability.title: Hydrodynamic limits of finite range exclusion processes
Probability.summary: We consider variants of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) where particles are 'large'; while in the SSEP, each lattice point is either occupied or not occupied by a single particle, in our model each particle is represented by a fixed shape, and the dynamics is so that shapes cannot overlap. In one dimension, this reduces to a finite range interaction that prevents particles from coming closer to each other than a certain distance. In this case, we prove the existence of the hydrodynamic limit, and identify the relevant macroscopic PDE, which is a porous medium equation. In two dimensions, we have no rigorous results, but instead rely on numerical simulations to approximate the diffusion matrix. Under the assumption that the hydrodynamic limit exists in two dimensions, we derive properties of the diffusion matrix based on the shape of the particles.

Probability.title: Localization induced by Sinai disorder in mass-exchange models
Probability.summary: We introduce a conservative continuous-mass-exchange model with quenched disorder in the splitting laws on the bonds of a finite segment. Although the dynamics is generically irreversible, its stationary mean mass profile remarkably turns out to be exactly solvable through an associated birth-and-death chain and has a Gibbs representation in terms of a simple random-walk potential. If $N$ is the number of bonds and $β$ measures the strength of disorder, the parameter $β\sqrt N$ separates an asymptotically flat profile, a Brownian crossover, and a profile localized near the global minimum. We characterize the fluctuations of macroscopic masses and identify arcsine laws for the localization centre, the competition between left and right valleys, and the disorder-averaged mass measure. Furthermore, for the extremal masses, we discuss the emergent limiting random variable in terms of the literature linking finite RW paths seen from its minimum to infinite-horizon walks conditioned to stay positive. Finally, in proximity of the localization transition point $β=0$, we show that the inverse participation ratio for the extremal masses give rises to a scaling with decay of order $k^{-3/2}$ consistent with the scaling limit of the latter conditioned walk. In the same limit, the inverse participation ratio shows a scaling form.
